# trust-cg limitations

trust-cg implements native multi-target compilation, a substantial Trust Rust
bridge, JIT publication and bounded independently checked proof routes. Version
0.7.0 retains a research-preview release tier because full replacement and
platform qualification remain incomplete. A usable implemented path and its
proof/qualification status must be assessed separately; the
[source audit](ARCHITECTURE.md#source-audit-and-capability-boundaries) maps them.

This file records the user-facing limits and detailed path contracts. The maintained
inventories in [`rustc-mir-coverage-inventory.md`](rustc-mir-coverage-inventory.md)
and [`trust-cg-full-replacement-ledger.md`](trust-cg-full-replacement-ledger.md)
contain the conservative engineering detail. If a broad statement conflicts
with one of those inventories or with a fail-closed runtime check, the narrower
claim wins.

## Correctness and proof scope


The explicit `compile_for_installation` Core continuation requires the existing
default body license and replayed source-island-bound certificates. It retains
the exact Core/LIR through publication; a previously produced address-free
artifact, whose source was released, cannot be made callable by joining it to
caller-supplied bytes or a new source graph. The current installation domain is
ARM64/macOS, no imports, no runtime catalog entries, no symbolic fixups, and
text alignment at most4096 bytes. ADR/ADRP and PC-relative literal
load/prefetch classes refuse pending an explicit placement contract; an empty
fixup inventory alone is insufficient. This conservative byte scan can also
refuse embedded data. Direct relative branches must stay inside the same
function. Entire unsupported inventories refuse,
including unused entries. Installation returns the existing installed-image
owner and the finalized manifest, whose actual native-payload digest and
checked-proof-bundle identity are required by checked symbol lookup. It adds
no provider resolver, proof credit, source authority, or default-policy change.

The ordinary positive is an independently authored Clean declaration returning42
and its matching source-bound Core body, executed through that owner. A
source-less recorded-comparand identity certificate remains insufficient for
this continuation even though the existing default Core license accepts that
legacy F-008 case. Neither run licenses original E1. Its retained complete-machine
probe returned zero artifacts; this component does not requalify that probe. See the
scoped implementation and retained losses.


The separate owned source-peer continuation
admits one actual zero-argument scalar call/return, or a direct one-U64
forwarding call/return, beside its genuine defined callee. The
one-word continuation
authenticates the sole zero-byte X0 self-copy and seals invocation arity. Complete original-request/source/LIR/machine/frame/final-target replay
stays conditional and non-promotable until the opaque consumer owns actual
private writable entry storage. The ordinary `compile_for_installation` and
forced-object-frame refusals above remain. This bounded framed source42 gains
no external-memory/provider, generalized control-flow, unwind, original-E1 or
complete-model authority. Runtime allocation/signal/adapter and macOS
RecordedOnly permissions remain distinct from the conditional Formal statement.


Every per-function proof the backend produces takes as its source the LIR
that instruction selection receives: the x86-64 source-bound body theorem,
the AArch64 source-bound obligations and whole-body theorem, the
per-instruction lowering proofs and translation-validation gates on every
target, and the JIT certificates. At O1 and above two shared LIR passes can
run before that point, and neither is validated. The module inliner
(`trust_cg_opt::ir_inline`) checks only structure: the opcode multiset, CFG
well-formedness and fresh values. A wrong argument-to-parameter mapping
passes that check. Unsigned-range simplification
(`trust_cg_opt::lir_unsigned_range`) has no check at all; from its own
interval facts it deletes `Assert`s and folds branches, selects, compares and
checked arithmetic. So a compile that claims proofs runs neither pass, on
every target (ruling OD-225, `docs/decision-record.md`), and the source of
its proofs is exactly the adapter's LIR, as at O0. The rule covers:
- `emit_proofs`, which is the rustc bridge's default (`no-proof-certs`
  turns it off);
- a verifying JIT validation mode, either `CachedVerified` (x86-64's JIT
  default) or `AlwaysVerify`;
- a raw lane's shared LIR step under `InlineOnlyAdmission::Withhold`.

A compile that claims nothing keeps both passes. Consequences:
- A proof-claiming O1+ compile can be slower than the same compile without
  the claim, wherever inlining or range simplification would have paid.
- It splices no inline-only body, authenticated or not.
- A function whose `Assert` the range pass used to delete keeps it. The
  x86-64 body theorem does not model a LIR `Assert`, so that function is
  refused as it is at O0.
- Credit can also be gained. In `tests/proof_claim_lir_passes.rs`, a checked
  add whose trap branch the range pass folded away was refused at x86-64 O2
  and O3; with the branch kept it promotes.

Each pass can return to proof-claiming compiles only with a validator of its
own: an inlining validator, or V-range, a theorem whose source is the
pre-range LIR and which proves each deleted `Assert` and each folded edge
infeasible.

TrustIR v63 runtime `MakeClosure` retains a physical target and ordered live
captures. Native lowering constructs the environment directly from those SSA
values when a coherent declared capture layout supplies the physical offsets.
The descriptor must match the native carrier's total size and alignment and,
on x86 SysV, its register classes;
missing, ambiguous, malformed or incompatible layouts remain refused before
optimization, including unused constructors. Runtime pointer captures and
reordered constant environments execute on AArch64/macOS at O0-O3 in the
focused regression. WebAssembly and Core retain their explicit constructor
refusals. Bounded fsym admits pure construction with flat scalar/thin-pointer
captures and an exact target signature. It tracks capture values through copy,
extraction and update, including pointer lifetime/escape facts; closure calls,
Char/handle/nested captures remain outside that model. Memory operations
still require a modeled reference layout. Structural merge checks target/type identities and capture order. Neither
bounded diagnostics nor native execution supplies a source-refinement or
machine-code proof claim.

TrustIR v60 records physical ABI claims in `FuncTy.abi`, separately from the
carrier vectors. Module batching preserves these records and refuses
conflicting recorded/unrecorded declarations. Native and WebAssembly entry
points refuse every `Some` record with `[TCG-SIGNATURE-ABI]`, including unused
and indirect-only signature rows: existing LIR does not implement that record's
source placement, extensions or hidden-result claims. `None` is the legacy
unrecorded state, not evidence that hidden transport is unnecessary. Carrier
promotion refuses recorded signatures rather than erase their claims. Source
custody and this refusal floor do not qualify a new native ABI or a frontend.

Defined-body effect-frame violations receive TrustIR's typed coverage refusal
on native and WASM compiler entry points. This is the existing shared syntactic
over-approximation, not a new optimization or proof that an external callee
honours a declared frame. Retained proof-formula identities distinguish entry,
exit and legacy unqualified worlds; identity custody alone proves no effects.

The October 1 v52 cohort refuses all source `Inst::Assert` on native and
WebAssembly paths until faithful panic-runtime lowering exists. The old
canonical bounds fusion and source-Assert trap routes did not preserve Rust
panic identity, payloads, hooks and caller locations. Their former native
coverage, including the wide-bounds post-index guard fixture, is not retained
as current execution credit. Original source fixtures and recorded failed
positives remain available in the
migration record.
The diagnostic interpreter's structured panic agreement is not native
execution or proof. Existing explicit panic calls/cleanup blocks, internal
checked traps and Assert-free native controls are separate, bounded routes.
The separate rustc-private bridge now has an exact kind-specific MIR panic
route: fourteen assertion forms execute on ARM64/macOS at O0–O3 and both
abort/unwind strategies, with payload, location, hook, Drop and catch checks.
Its diagnostic native record
uses certificates off; it does not establish certified EH, another target,
the general TrustIR panic runtime contract or a complete sysroot.

Some panics the bridge raises for calls it lowers itself now call the entry
that std's optimized MIR reaches, with std's payload and Location, so a hook
observes what it observes under LLVM (OD-170). These are an intercepted std
call's failure edge, a formatted panic in a compiled body, a diverging std
`#[track_caller]` helper and a `-Cdebug-assertions` precondition check. On
aarch64-apple-darwin, `std_panic_payload_differential` matches LLVM on 1680 of
1680 rows, with certificates off. A route that cannot be derived from std's
MIR is refused by name (`[TCG-STD-PANIC-ROUTE]`).

Two gaps are still open:
- On x86-64 under `panic=unwind`, two cases still unwind through a frame that
  must abort: an ordinary call with a `Terminate` edge into a std body that
  panics, and an untracked diverging helper inlined at -O2/-O3. Call lowering
  there keeps no terminate edge for any call.
- The x86-64 and wasm32 routes and `panic=immediate-abort` have not been run.
  The measuring host has no Rosetta and no wasm32 std.

One divergence from LLVM's binary is deliberate. A panic that reaches a
Rust-defined `extern "C"` fn under `panic=unwind` runs that fn's cleanups and
then aborts with "panic in a function that cannot unwind", as MIR states.
LLVM's binary does the same unless its search meets a gap before a handler.
That gap can be in the caller's call-site table or, above O0, where LLVM
infers `nounwind` for the caller itself, in the table of a frame above it.
There the search fails, and the process aborts ("failed to initiate panic,
error 3") before any cleanup runs. Where those gaps fall depends on the
caller's shape and on LLVM's inlining, `nounwind` inference and range
merging.

A cleanup that only the bridge runs can therefore also change the outcome, if
it exits, loops or blocks. Ruling OD-NOUNWIND-CALLEE-EDGE-20261011 keeps MIR's
behaviour. `terminate_panic_differential_aarch64` measures it on
aarch64-apple-darwin: of 152 cells, 127 match LLVM exactly, and in the other 25
the bridge runs the pinned cleanups where LLVM's search fails.

TrustIR v53 non-propagating call boundaries (`Inst::CallCannotUnwind`,
`Inst::CallIndirectCannotUnwind`) are refused by name on the adapter's shared
floor (every native and WebAssembly lane), in the closed-JIT Core census and by
the bounded fsym scanner. TrustIR states the boundary as enforce-or-refuse, not
as a no-panic fact; no lane emits the abort-on-unwind call-site range that would
enforce it, and lowering one as an ordinary call would let an unwind cross it.
Each adapter translation also runs that body floor on the function it is
handed (detached, inline-only and body-template entries included); the Core
JIT plan's source-call replay, the standalone WebAssembly ABI model and the
pre-layout wasm policy refuse them too, and module merge's identity lockstep
also compares each boundary's operands, indirect callee, callee identity and
indirect signature/convention (it already refused a boundary rewritten to an
ordinary call by its variant check).

TrustIR v54 panic sites (amendment P: an `Inst::Assert` carrying a `site`, and
the `Inst::AssertInvoke` terminator) are refused by name on the same floor,
before the check's kind is consulted, in the closed-JIT Core census, by the
bounded fsym scanner and by the diagnostic interpreter. A sited failure calls
its panic entry with the kind's operands and the location record (and an
`AssertInvoke` may enter its landing pad); no lane lowers that call, and a trap
would compile a different program. Module merge remaps a site's entry and
location global so no splice misdirects one.
The wasm lane's own per-function scan refuses both by name as well, so
`wasm::lower_function` refuses one in a function its module does not hold.

TrustIR v55/v56 (amendment D: the module drop-glue table, the
`Inst::DropInvoke` and `Inst::InvokeIndirect` terminators, and the
`PanicStrategy` under which unwinding is an exit) are not modeled. Both
terminators are refused by name on the same floor, in the closed-JIT Core
census, by the wasm lane's scan and by the bounded fsym scanner: no lane lowers
a drop (resolved, a drop is a call of its type's glue), and none routes an
indirect callee's unwind to an in-frame landing pad. The drop-glue table is
carried inert, since every drop site is refused; trust-ir's own verdicts on a
malformed row and on a glue reached by a direct call refuse the module, and
module merge refuses a module carrying a table rather than drop it. fsym's run
model is the panic=abort projection (`PanicStrategy::Abort`, the interpreter's
default); a run under `PanicStrategy::Unwind` is outside it.

The October 1 real-source sysroot audit
binds each replay to its exact source and backend. That audit's completed full
graph, candidate 21, retains 441 required refusals with CG core/alloc outputs.
Its latest completed std-body diagnostic is candidate 17, with 114 refusals
and 13 explicit LLVM dependencies; candidate 21's newer std-body replay times
out. The completed std count improves
from candidate 16's 116 after the checked raw-pointer cell retry. Earlier
repairs remove three undefined-value loop functions and one projected
scalar-borrow branch mismatch. Full CG-built `std`, `proc_macro`, `test` and
self-hosting remain open. Independent native O0–O3 controls cover memory-only
loop headers, typed projected scalar borrows, live cleanup cells and genuine
caught panics. f16/f128 transport, unsupported aggregate/layout/reference
shapes and ABI/lowering barriers remain required work. These diagnostics
disable frontend verification and backend certificates and supply no proof credit.

Map-containing owning dyn conversions require an exact local construction
receipt. The receipt follows CFG paths and fully known scalar joins; user calls,
unknown loop back edges, loads and incoming values cannot establish it. Linux's
pointer-wrapper route checks the same receipt before vtable publication.
Independent LLVM-created real maps retain exact origin refusals at O0–O3,
while 52 heap-glue native comparisons pass on sealed candidate26. This is
bounded representation admission, not arbitrary map ABI interoperability.
On merged candidates27 and28, the unchanged owning test failed because `dyn_vec`
at O2/O3 reached the then-unsupported canonical bounds-panic route. Their 34
partial owning matches and 16 passing borrowed matches remain dated failures.
Fresh source30 (`b422f87fd`, TrustIR `dee0ab3b`) passes all four dyn methods,
including 36 owning and 16 borrowed LLVM/CG native comparisons. The genuine
MIR panic route restores those mandatory cells; this does not admit general
TrustIR assertions or establish every failing bounds payload on Linux.
Modeled `Vec::IntoIter` requires its actual allocator argument to be the
compiler's genuine Global lang-item type. `Custom<Global>` receives
`TCG-VEC-INTOITER-LAYOUT`; source30 checks two independently compiled LLVM
custom-allocator controls and two required CG refusals. The two collection
ownership defects this paragraph recorded on 2026-10-01 (the
source audit has the state before the
fixes) are fixed:
- A by-value iterator terminal frees the `vec::IntoIter` it consumes
  (b0d6c8924; `real_program_runtime_aarch64`
  `consumed_vec_into_iter_frees_its_buffer`), also when its payload, `Sum`'s
  checked add or an allocation raise unwinds out of it, and a `collect` then
  frees the `Vec` it was building (`vec_compact_user_trait_differential_aarch64`
  `vec_into_iter_terminals_free_the_buffer_when_a_payload_unwinds_aarch64`,
  against LLVM at -O0..-O3 under both strategies; the -O2/-O3 cells of shapes
  refused before the drive are pinned by code and reason).
- Zero-length repeat and from-element allocate nothing
  (`vec_from_elem_capacity_aarch64`, and `real_program_runtime_aarch64`
  `slice_repeat_zero_total_and_large_fill_match_llvm`).

Re-measured on main 72a46f7ed (2026-10-09) with a counting global allocator
against LLVM at -O0..-O3 under both panic strategies, in every cell the
bridge compiles (the rest are named refusals):
- over a `vec::IntoIter`, `sum`, `count`, `fold`, `last`, `max`, `any`,
  `all`, `position`, `nth`, a partial `take(2).sum()` and a `for` loop each

The source26 live AY stride-one slice assertion still fails: its queries return

Linux's separately dated bound-memory checker qualification replays 72 exact
committed queries and passes 53 focused certificate/authority tests.
It retains Darwin's authorization and all certificate bytes. The formal-only
integration credits 72 form queries and refuses 621 wrong queries; its live

Candidate28 adds exact full-word binding for admitted AArch64 scalar-immediate
and pair memory forms, and rejects a row when a decomposed effect part is

The Rust bridge now rejects unresolved shared trait-object referent storage
with `[TCG-DYN-REF-IDENTITY]`, unsupported required Fn* call-shim bodies through
the failed-root diagnostic. ARM64/macOS now models direct nonvariadic foreign
may-unwind calls under `panic=abort` using the actual instance FnAbi and only
the live source cleanup domain. Unsupported targets, foreign function pointers,
variadic calls, disabled EH and abort-body exception escape still refuse with
`[TCG-EH-FOREIGN-ABORT]`. Darwin Abi/InCleanup termination resolves the actual
reason lang item and FnAbi; its original 48 native diagnostic controls pass.
The mixed-strategy extension has a separate mandatory 32-run denominator and
source-boundary controls; incomplete runs do not receive that credit. These
diagnostics do not establish certified EH, which still refuses at TB-12.
(`extern "rust-call"` callables are declared untupled since round 10, F2: the
aggregate-passing section below.) Ordinary canonical-address coercions retain
their routes.

The source audit also found an LLVM-input contract gap:
[`parser.rs`](crates/trust-cg-llvm-import/src/parser.rs) ignores LLVM
`target datalayout`. It reads the compile target (the triple a caller
passes, else the module's `target triple`) only for the rules that depend
on it: the object format (the `\01` asm label and `.L` name rules, L02-P15;
the `@llvm.used` function declaration rule, L02-P13), the RISC-V calling
convention and `memset_pattern` (L02-P15), and, with the relocation model a
caller passes, the `dso_local` rules (L02-P13). Pointer layout is fixed at
64 bits with eight-byte alignment. The importer implements substantial LLVM text
lowering, but does not source-bind arbitrary LLVM layouts. Inputs needing a
different pointer or ABI layout have no supported contract; explicit refusal
of incompatible stated layouts remains work to do. This is a source-derived
finding, not a new native mismatch measurement.

Direct LIR `Load`/`Store` and volatile accesses cannot carry a whole `Struct`,
`Array` or `Enum` value on AArch64, x86-64 or RISC-V. The shared
[`Type::whole_aggregate_memory_access_refusal`](crates/trust-cg-lower/src/types.rs)
contract refuses them before instruction emission, including small and
zero-sized aggregates. Producers must use exact byte copies or address-based
access. The TrustIR adapter's aggregate-copy and native ABI lane marshallers
have separate routes; this refusal does not establish complete aggregate ABI
support. Scalar aggregate-constant fields also reject composite carriers
instead of constructing a scalar value with an aggregate type.

Bounded source-bound theorems, structural translation validation, solver
certificate replay and published-image hashing establish different facts.
In particular, x86 body proofs cover pre-allocation ISel; the final-byte ABI
envelope excludes relocation patching/veneers. AArch64 Core affine checking
covers its admitted final-byte domain. None establishes arbitrary frontend
lowering or a universal compiler theorem. AY is build-digest-pinned; Clean is
capability-probed and bound to the actual checker bytes. Ordinary builds
discover a capable Clean; local overlay builds additionally require the
manifest's build-recorded Clean digest and forbid checker fallback. The
unsigned manifest's source labels do not prove tool correctness. The Rust
checkers, frontend premises and the Lean model's assumptions (the faithfulness
of its source and machine definitions, `bv_decide`'s native axioms) stay in the
trusted boundary. The Lean capstone now has an inhabited program-indexed
model witness, but still does not prove production compilation or observable
machine behavior
([formal/lean/SOUNDNESS.md](formal/lean/SOUNDNESS.md)).

Composed transition records (L09-P3) chain the AArch64 stage checks of one
function instead of leaving them disjoint. A preparation on a proof-grade
route (the sealed Core, the verifying JIT, `--emit-proofs` objects) records
legalization (TrustIR to LIR) and selection (LIR to raw MachIR) from the
affine check, one link per optimizer pass or scheduler run that changed the
function's interface, the post-allocation value-flow comparison and a
proof-grade, relocation-free encoding (ENC-5 enforced with undecoded words
refused, the CFG-bound final-layout cross-check, the switch binding). Every
link names its relation, its check, its model and the SHA-256 interface of
the program at both ends; the record composes only when every required link
is present and established and each adjacent pair shares one interface, so
a dropped link, a swapped digest, a rewrite no validator saw and a byte
changed after the last link are each refused by name
([`trust_cg_verify::composed_transition`](crates/trust-cg-verify/src/composed_transition.rs)).
A pass-manager or scheduler run is validated for the record by its dedicated
validator or the generic symbolic region check even where the
pass-validation scope runs none. CEGIS and the extended loop rotation have
no validator: a run of either that changes the interface is an uncovered
link, so an opt-in CEGIS budget on a proof-required route refuses every
in-domain function CEGIS rewrote. The machine-IR interface digest covers
the function's name, signature, stack-protector and stack-limit state,
every field the pass validators read and the side tables a later check or
the encoder reads (trap expansions, call ABI facts, incoming stack
arguments, target features, `noalias` claims, fusion edges, profile order);
it leaves out the derived predecessor/successor lists, ID counters, proof
annotations, the lowering-provenance sidecar, debug metadata and the
code-alignment hint, so "no unchecked mutation between links" holds modulo
those fields. Recording changes the pass validation an in-domain function
runs under where the route did not already select it: on the verifying JIT
and `--emit-proofs` objects (already proof-grade) the record's extra
verdicts go into the record only and the pass-validation counters and
refusals are unchanged; the sealed Core does not select proof-grade
publication, so for an in-domain function it now runs the dedicated
validators and the post-allocation comparison under the enforce policy,
whose refusals (`PipelineError`) are the ones composition would make
(their cost on the Core route is unmeasured); `record` raises an in-domain
function to the diagnostic policy and the dedicated scope, which refuses
nothing more but adds those runs to the counters. The routes refuse
(`CompileError::ComposedTransitionRefused`) a function the legalization check
covers unless its record composes at exactly-decided strength or better,
checked right after preparation and before any certificate is generated or
promoted, and unless the bytes they publish for it are the chain's
terminal: the sealed code; the JIT buffer's whole installed range (bound
before the certificate gate); the object's bytes read back by an
independent reader as the symbol's whole extent (ELF `st_size`; Mach-O up
to the next symbol, `NOP` padding only) with no relocation inside.
`CompilationMetrics::composed_publications` counts the bindings that ran.
What a composition establishes (carried as the composition's `claim`, with
every link's strength): the published code bytes are reached from the
module-owned TrustIR function through those checked transitions with no
unchecked mutation of a digested field between them, so, under the
conjunction of the links' models, they compute the source's result on every
input where the source is defined. Each link is decided exactly over its own
model by trusted Rust (the affine checker, the pass validators sharing the
optimizer's operand-role and memory-effect tables, the post-allocation
comparison's model, the A64 decoder); the chain is as strong as its weakest
link, is never upgraded, and is not a proof. The legalization check covers
only the affine domain (one block or one diamond of homogeneous
I32/U32/I64/U64 values: constants, copies, wrapping add/sub, comparisons and
flat selects, at most eight register parameters, no calls, memory, loops or
Boolean arguments). Every other function keeps a record saying why no chain
exists and is published on the route's other gates alone, with no
TrustIR-to-bytes claim. Measured with the compile corpus's census lane
(`compile_corpus --lane composed-census`), which classifies each record with
the requirement the routes apply (object entries compiled under
`TRUST_CG_COMPOSED_TRANSITION=record` with certificates off, JIT entries
prepared at proof grade) and holds each composing object function to the
object publication binding; it runs no route's own check and installs no
JIT buffer: at `2a42547f4` (merged with `origin/main` `dfb0c3e4a`;
2026-10-14, Apple M4 Max) 3 of the 5,449 AArch64 functions the corpus
prepares are in the domain at their production levels, and at each of
O0-O3 all 3 compose, none is refused and each composing object function's
symbol extent is exactly its terminal. 5,446 are not covered (the
whole-body owner's 22 families are all outside the domain); 5 preparations
fail before a record exists (the variadic aggregate ABI; a sixth at O3 is a
LICM pass-validation refusal of a loop outside the domain); 657 of the 1,587
modules are refused before any function is prepared. At `a1a807fd0`
(merged with `c84acf0c3`) the same lane found 101 of 6,085 functions in the
domain, all composing; the trust-ir validation merged since then refuses
244 more rustc-bridge modules before preparation, among them the 98
`rustc_allocator_shim` modules that held 98 of those functions (on
`origin/main` alike: the identity check below compares every lane's verdicts
and error texts). The proof-required JIT census
(`jit_proof_coverage_census`, 398 compiles, Trust package 9192's AY and the
managed Clean; at `a1a807fd0`, every per-family pin holding) publishes 21
compiles, all memory-family load/store leaves
outside the domain; its in-domain compiles (the arith family's 160 add and
subtract shapes among them) are refused at proof promotion because the frame
theorem is not replayed. So on this host no in-domain function is published
by a proof-required route: the record-level requirement is reached by real
compiles on both routes (the floor row refuses real AOT instrumentation
there by composition), and the byte bindings after publication are reached
only by the crate's unit tests, which waive proof promotion (test-only) to
drive both routes to them. Recording costs +0.17% instructions retired on
the corpus's proof-grade lane `aot-proofs` at `2a42547f4` (per entry -1.8%
to +6.3%, within run-to-run noise; +1.57% at `a1a807fd0`, whose corpus held
101 in-domain functions; that lane's compiles end refused at proof promotion
or before preparation on both sides) and nothing measurable on the default
lanes (lane totals 0.9989 to 0.9994), whose emitted bytes are unchanged:
Identity PASS on all 534 entry/lane pairs of `2a42547f4` against
`dfb0c3e4a` (load average 1.9 to 5.2).
`TRUST_CG_COMPOSED_TRANSITION=record` builds records on any route for
measurement; no setting lowers a proof-grade route. Relocated words, the
installed image beyond the function's range, the TrustIR frontend and dialect
legalization (original to admitted TrustIR) are outside every chain; the
LIR-bound source-bound owners (frame, whole body) still have no TrustIR
endpoint and are not links of it.

The Lean development's forward simulation and capstone are x86-64 only. For
AArch64 it has an A64 instruction-word model with proved encode/decode round
trips over the 27 integer encoding classes the emitter writes
([`formal/lean/Trust/A64/`](formal/lean/README.md#aarch64-instruction-word-model-and-integer-semantics))
and the start of a machine model whose condition certificates are proved, but
no AArch64 forward simulation, refinement theorem or capstone (ledger
X-LEAN-P1). The Rust emitter is bound to the model only on the 831 generated
golden rows `lean_a64_encode_golden_binding` checks, and the model's
semantics only on the 1,165 recorded Apple M4 Max executions in
`Trust/A64/SiliconChecks.lean`: both are tests. SIMD&FP, atomics, exclusive
accesses, system registers, exceptions, alignment faults and the weak memory
model are outside the Lean A64 model.


The [September 25 complete Linux regression run](reports/perf/2026-09-25-linux-required-floor/README.md)
passes all 167 required integration targets and 1078 Rust tests on clean
source `443ed769f`, with zero failed, ignored or filtered tests. This
establishes the required regression baseline; complete compiler acceptance and
every L01–L14 requirement remain open. The root-workspace floor does not
qualify the separate private ABI bridge, and the scoped
[kernel](reports/perf/2026-09-25-linux-kernel-fixtures/README.md) and
[frontend](reports/perf/2026-09-25-linux-frontend-fixtures/README.md) fixture
qualifications (exact Trust compiler `ae9c2c1da`) do not update the floor's
source revision. AY's
scoped proof reconstruction
covers authenticated solver scope selectors only; user assumptions remain
outside that reconstruction domain. Earlier floor runs and the AY/Clean repair
history are in the dated records under `reports/` and
`docs/archive/session-reports/`.

The root-workspace test matrix has per-host required sets
(full-test-matrix.md); its
first complete Darwin run
(clean `f89656f9e`, Trust package 9192) is not green: 717 of the 752
Darwin-required suites pass, and the strict proof gate verifies 477 of 2,503
obligations with the installed AY and 2,294 with a development AY/Clean
overlay, with no counterexample, so it stays a named host residual. The

repository executes the 53 `other-lane` tests (`wasm-ld`/`node` link legs,
x86-64 execution, RISC-V cross tools) or the 13 `opt-in` tests of required
suites, and the matrix runs every suite except the `trust-cg-verify` library
with one test thread, so it does not exercise races between a suite's tests.
The Linux
required set is classified statically and has never been executed.

Downstream consumers run in the Darwin
consumer lane (`L13-P8`), a required stage of
that matrix: trust-cg's TY and AY contract targets, abi-xback at O0-O3 in both
directions through ld64, and the TY repository at a pinned commit re-pointed

corpus); see its first and
second records.
It is testing evidence for those consumers' current domains, and its records
are not green. abi-xback declines 50 of the 160 trust-cg-caller
combinations at O0 and O1 (no mismatch). Since 2026-09-28 (`2fe7332ff`) the
bridge refuses, under `[TCG-RET-ABI]`, a Rust-ABI return of a padded
single-scalar `BackendRepr::Memory` value that rustc returns through the

`A16 { i128 }` argument, which the generated caller passes through the

residual (strict proof promotion refuses its frame opcodes, the residual
behind the floor's `jit_fail_closed_proof_policy` reds), listed by its full
refusal and kept red. Since the
store-form `insertfield` refusal (WS7.1, `6e72c7034`), TY's native BFS-level
and next-state compilation is refused: 18 TY library tests and the native

failures that are TY's own (a self-audit of the pins the lane substitutes, a

listed by exact name; the lane runs TY's PowInt test with TY's `0^0`
semantics as its own target, so the assertions after that point execute.
Five tests whose bodies need an environment variable (three replay-bundle
readers, TY's linked trust-ir probe and its FFI-abort child entry) are

The [September 20 private ABI bridge gate](reports/perf/2026-09-20-linux-bridge-checkpoint/README.md)

The Darwin AArch64 bridge
runner record is a
failing run. At `ae3f0c539` it builds the bridge on the Apple M4 Max with Trust
package 9192 and runs all 13 Darwin bridge test targets (80 tests). It credits a
test only when the test's own output carries a positive-evidence marker whose

are credited and 6 targets pass; 17 of the 29 are proofs-off diagnostics
(`no-proof-certs`). All 51 failures are certificates-on compiles refused at
proof promotion (`[TCG-PROOF-465]`), including `hello_loop`, every
`overflow_asserts` oracle and all 26 corpus rows. Three of them, among them the
fixed-cost bound, passed before `main` `5ff639bc2` and fail on `main` too. The
runner sees only compiler output a test echoes: a certificates-on compile that
exits 0 can still leave out an unreachable Rust-internal function. That every
knob argument comes from the traced constructor is checked by a source scan of

The bridge's differential corpus and x86 feature suites now also run natively
on AArch64 (record,
`L06-P3`), against LLVM, with every cell pinned in a census. On
aarch64-apple-darwin 432 of 462 proofs-off corpus cells and 1403 of 1538
proofs-off feature-suite cells match (the Darwin gate's pinned markers,
2026-10-10, and 2026-10-13 for the feature suites). The rest refuse by
name, except 8 cells (4 programs) that LLVM cannot build alone. Since OD-170, no cell differs from LLVM in its panic
message: the 16 `panics_unwind` cells that did now match. With certificates
on, none of the 154
-O2 corpus cells builds (`L07-P2`). The lanes have not run on an aarch64 Linux
host, and the feature lane runs only the table programs of 48 suites: another
81 x86 suite files (394 tests: fragment-built `no_main` programs,
`format!`-built programs, x86 ABI cross-backend and object-inspecting cases)
still run only on an x86-64 host.

The bridge lowers `for_each`, `fold`, `sum`, `count`, `collect`,
`sort_by_key`, the in-place `Vec::retain`/`retain_mut`, `dedup_by` and
`resize_with` models and their kin as synthesized loops. A loop must account
for every value it consumes. There is no exemption for drop glue that only
frees `Global`-allocator memory: an allocation-only capture needs destruction
just as an environment holding a user `Drop` or an `Rc` does. This supersedes
the resource-leak admission in OD-171; see
DR-CONSUMED-CLOSURE-RESOURCE-ADMISSION-20261014 in the decision record.

`for_each` and supported `fold` consumers use rustc's actual closure layout,
mutable environment slot and drop-glue instance. They drop the closure after
the drive and on its modeled callback-unwind edges, before releasing a
consumed iterator. `fold((), f)` uses the void callback driver, with Rust unit
elided according to the actual FnAbi. Shapes outside those contracts still
refuse. Other synthesized callback loops refuse any environment that needs
drop as `[TCG-CLOSURE-DROP]`; their owning-argument accounting uses
`[TCG-INTERCEPT-OWNED-DROP]`. Borrowed environments without drop remain eligible.
The adapter check can still over-refuse a move closure owned by the caller
when a consumer only borrows its iterator (`any`, `all` or `position`).

Projected `Box` fields with a drop-free payload use the existing allocator
shim on Linux AArch64, Linux x86-64 and Darwin AArch64. Projected Box
payloads needing their own destructors and nested unwind cleanup retain the
Darwin AArch64 boundary (`L06-P8`). On x86-64 Linux under `panic=abort`,
where no nested cleanup pad can exist, the same payload-glue lane is admitted;
under `panic=unwind` x86-64 Linux still refuses
(`SLICE-CAP-BOX-PAYLOAD-ABORT-20261115`). Shape-specific bare-local Box-drop paths
have their own admission. Under `panic=unwind`, a normal-exit closure destructor
that panics now enters the consumed iterator's release pad before caller
cleanup. The
Linux allocation regression
requires a real buffer free for `for_each` and scalar `fold` at O0–O3;
the old backend leaks in all eight CG cells. Droppable source elements under
unwind remain refused. These native tests do not close L06-P6 or prove
arbitrary cleanup.

The unchanged
October 14 foreign-observer reproducer
records the original missing free and the repair separately. Its C observer
requires the concrete allocation to occur, measures its release, and preserves
direct-drop controls. Allocator call counts alone are not a general Rust
language-soundness oracle. Admission no longer depends on whether a
`#[global_allocator]` is visible, so an allocator defined only in a downstream
binary does not grant permission to skip cleanup in its library.

A `fold`'s initial accumulator is not checked as a value the callee drops:
it becomes the result. The carry rule (`[TCG-ITER-UNWIND-CARRY]`) refuses
a droppable accumulator that the drive carries across an adapter closure
which can unwind under `panic=unwind` (measured: refused at -O0/-O1, matching
LLVM's drop count at -O2/-O3; ruling OD-171). `try_fold`'s initial
accumulator is still checked (`[TCG-INTERCEPT-OWNED-DROP]`); whether main
builds a `try_fold` that check refuses was not measured. An intercepted
`Vec::insert` of a needs-drop element drops it when its out-of-bounds check
panics, as std does; whether it drops it when the grow step's allocation
failure unwinds (a panicking allocation-error hook: `-Zoom=panic` or an
unstable `set_alloc_error_hook`) was not measured on the merged code, which
no longer has the unwind guard that covered that edge (ruling OD-173).

Since LA-11 (2026-10-16) one bounded scalar-cell caller shape has a
source-bound owner on Linux AArch64 only: a C caller with one or two F32/F64
parameters, one escaped scalar stack cell and exactly one direct call
`void S(T *, T)` (the six families `aliased_{f32,f64}_{read,write}` and
`local_cell_read{,_f32}`, and any caller whose TrustIR is the same). Its frame,
SP, cell-address, argument-copy, constant, call and chain-branch rows are
credited only through a whole-call theorem replayed in parts, each part an AY
proof Clean independently checked, and only where a changed row value
falsifies the theorem. The theorem rests on a trusted AAPCS64 callee contract
and stack-window premises (ruling LD-89);
callee identity, order and count are paired in Rust; the theorem claims nothing
about CFI/unwind tables, SVE/SME state, signal handlers or threads. Darwin is
neither ruled nor run, more than one call is refused, and the AOT
`--emit-proofs` route cannot export the theorem (it refuses such rows by proof
name, L09-P11) (LA-11 record).
Every other scalar-cell caller's evidence is diagnostic, not proof. Machine-code
admission still refuses those callers' unproved calling frames
([source binding](reports/perf/2026-09-20-scalar-cell-source-binding/README.md)).
The [conditional callback-memory model](reports/perf/2026-09-25-callback-frame-obligations/README.md)
grants no instruction proof credit; independent proof replay and callback
environment authority remain open. The
[static linked-image checker](reports/perf/2026-09-25-scalar-cell-linked-image/README.md)
treats callback bodies as unproved endpoints and adds no calling-frame
admission, callback contract or native execution evidence. The
[PIE](reports/perf/2026-09-25-scalar-cell-pie-images/README.md) and
[native ABI runtime](reports/perf/2026-09-25-scalar-cell-native-runtime/README.md)
runs use diagnostic emission with verification or CG certificates disabled;
the proof-enabled calling-frame refusal, callback semantics, loader authority
and the production calling-frame proof requirement remain open.

- There is no complete, machine-checked end-to-end theorem from arbitrary
  trust-ir input to every emitted machine-code byte.
- The default verifier exhaustively evaluates small-width obligations but uses
  edge cases and pseudorandom samples for many 32/64-bit obligations.
  Statistical success is regression evidence, not proof over all inputs, and
  is never credited: an instruction whose obligation discharged only by
  sampling is reported as unverified and blocks proof promotion. A sampled
  sweep in which no point satisfies the obligation's preconditions reports
  `Unknown`, not success.
- Per-instruction credit requires an obligation built from that instruction
  (a complete-domain reconstruction or a source-bound replay). A registry
  theorem selected by a name query (for example `"load"`, which selects an
  I32 LDP pair theorem) is about a representative form, so on every ISA it is
  reported as unverified and never discharged for the instruction. Most
  emitted instructions therefore block `--emit-proofs` and proof-required JIT
  promotion today.
- The AArch64 source-bound frame and arithmetic replay binds only a body inside
  the sixteen-byte FP/LR envelope. The zero-storage leaf policy keeps that
  envelope for ADD/SUB/LSL leaves and constant/copy returns on ELF targets, and
  on `aarch64-apple-darwin` in every proof-required or verifying compile
  (`--emit-proofs`, a verifying JIT, a sealed-Core address-free compile), where
  it takes precedence over the red zone. Ordinary Darwin compiles keep the red
  zone, so there the same leaves are frameless; frameless bodies have the
  whole-body owner below, which admits no memory access, and the memory-leaf
  checker binds the loads and stores of a straight-line frameless leaf to its
  LIR source, crediting nothing but those accesses (`L07-P2`). Inside the
  envelope
  the ALU owner binds ADD/SUB/LSL. The owner's source domain observes one
  integer width. A parameter no instruction reads, such as the context pointer
  of `fn(*mut T) -> i32 { 0 }`, may have the other width: its register is seeded
  at its own width, so no machine read narrows or widens it. A parameter that is
  read at another width stays outside the domain. A single `MOVZ`/`MOVN` can also receive
  credit from an owner binding the actual LIR Iconst's coordinates, digest,
  value and width, with an independently replayed ground theorem. Wrong dead
  constants are refutable even when they leave the return unchanged. Multiple
  move-wide words sharing one source stamp (including MOVK sequences) remain
  uncredited. Live register copies can receive OD-35's independently replayed
  raw source/result theorem; dead or overwritten copies receive no credit.
  The existing sealed body owner also constructs homogeneous I32/I64 integer
  comparisons with canonical B1 returns from actual source operands and
  allocated CMP/reaching-NZCV/CSET. Their live dependencies can receive credit
  only after both exact frame and body replay, never by a representative
  theorem citation. On the October 5 ARM64/macOS checkpoint, required positive
  comparison replay fails with the installed AY's incomplete certificate;
  construction and passing byte/mutation controls supply no formal credit.
  Source/frame binding remains the Rust checker, not an implementation proof.
  See the raw-comparison record,
  the body-credit record, the
  constant-credit report
  and the earlier E0.2 report.
- The AArch64 source-bound whole-body owner (`source_bound_a64_body`)
  binds a FRAMELESS final allocated body (the FP/LR envelope stays the frame
  owner's) to its exact LIR source with one theorem: the machine's X0 (W0 for
  an `I32` or `B1` result, a `B1` being exactly 0 or 1 in W0, stronger than
  AAPCS64's byte) equals the source's result for every input on which the
  source is defined. The source domain, decided by the LIR alone, is an
  acyclic CFG of at most 16 blocks of `Jump`/`Brif`/`Return` (256
  instructions), up to eight `I32`/`I64`/`B1` parameters and one such result,
  over `Iconst`, `Copy`, `Iadd`, `Isub`, `Ineg`, `Band`, `Bor`, `Bxor`,
  `Bnot`, `BandNot`, `BorNot` (bitwise on integers, the connectives on `B1`),
  `Ishl`, `Ushr`, `Sshr`, `Icmp` and `Eq`/`Ne` `Select` (nested, on any
  admitted type), with general block arguments (the simultaneous-substitution
  rule) and every use dominated by its definition. A shift follows trust-ir's
  `ShiftInRange` rule: executing one whose amount is not below the width is
  undefined, and the theorem quantifies over the inputs on which no executed
  shift is out of range (one Boolean domain premise, omitted when every amount
  is provably in range: a constant, or Rust's `y & (w - 1)`). A `B1`
  argument is bit 0 of an AAPCS64 byte whose bits 1..7 are zero; nothing is
  assumed about the bits above, so a body that reads them is refuted.
  Value-carrying or conditional loops,
  `Switch`, `Trap`, calls, memory, stack slots, EH, guard-bearing comparisons
  (`InBounds`/`GuardBoundsCheck`), explicit two-result overflow,
  `I8`/`I16`/`I128`, extensions between widths and FP stay refused by name.
  A separate pure-jump domain admits at most sixteen reachable blocks, each
  containing only one argument-free `Jump`, with no function parameters or
  results. The final body must have the same block identifiers and entry,
  one resolved `B` per block, and matching complete predecessor/successor
  lists. Its theorem equates every source next-PC with the independently
  decoded branch displacement for an arbitrary image base; only independent
  replay supplies Formal credit. This is a control-step theorem under the
  trusted Rust binding and Arm model, not a general loop or compiler theorem.
  The machine side is the meaning of the words the encoder emits for the
  admitted rows (ADD/SUB in every admitted form, NEG, AND/ORR/EOR/BIC/ORN and
  the logical immediates, LSLV/LSRV/ASRV modulo the width, immediate shifts,
  UBFM/SBFM, the fixed-width extends, shifted-register EOR/ADD/SUB, CMP/TST,
  CSET/CSEL/CSINC/CSINV/CSNEG with every condition read from NZCV, MOVZ/MOVN/
  MOVK and the copies, B, B.cond, CBZ, CBNZ, TBZ, TBNZ, RET); only X0-X17 may
  be written (a write to X18-X30 is a mismatch) and an SP operand is refused.
  ENC-5 and the final-layout cross-check, not the theorem, bind those rows to
  the bytes on a proof-grade route; each row's word semantics is trusted
  translator code, tested (not proved) by unit fixtures with a refuted
  mis-model for every row but `RET` and by a CPU differential on this host
  (566 probe bodies over all 58 rows, 201,496 calls, every result equal to
  the theorem's machine term). A concrete evaluation of both sides on a
  fixed input set (corner values, the source's constants, a deterministic
  stream) can only refuse (the `SourceBoundA64BodyMismatch` precondition
  failure under Enforce); it also refuses a theorem whose domain premise
  disagrees with the evaluated definedness on any sample. Credit comes only
  from AY's proof of the exact theorem replayed by Clean, and only to the
  returned value's backward slice and the body's direct transfers. Since
  2026-10-12 (`L11-P11`) the register copies and wide-move constants of that
  slice are credited by the same replay, under OD-35's route C: the theorem
  composes each from its own allocated operands, so a wrong register route,
  immediate, halfword or width changes the returned value it equates. They
  never count as the computing row a body needs, so an identity or
  constant-only body stays refused; dead rows, dead O0 folded constants
  (route A2, the LIR-bound constant owner, exists only inside a bound frame
  envelope) and `RET` get nothing from this owner. On this host the overlay
  AY/Clean pair certifies 50 of the 53 distinct theorems of the 176
  qualification bodies (22 families, O0-O3, the AOT and JIT preparations) and
  AY refutes all 305 corruption theorems; the proof-required JIT and AOT
  routes each publish 67 of 88 compiles (55 before route C), the rest refused
  at O0 on a dead folded `MOVZ` (17) or on the two-join DAG (4), whose AY proof
  carries a `hole` step (`printer-rule-without-external-spelling`) that Clean
  cannot check. With pack 9192's own AY (build 9624) the 2026-10-01 record
  certified 11 of the 53 and published 12 compiles on each route, but on
  trees descended from `main` `1359b3bca` the same AY binary certifies none:
  a qualification re-run on 2026-10-12 gives 36 `unknown` (an incomplete
  certificate or a rejected self-check) and 17 AY errors (it refuses to write
  an unverifiable proof, `and_pos`), so neither route publishes any of the 88,
  as in the census record's two runs with that AY. Whether the theorem text
  changed since 2026-10-01 or AY's strict self-check nondeterminism is
  responsible is not isolated, so package-tool counts are per-tree
  measurements
  (record;
  route-C census).
  The floor target has not run on a Linux host. The Rust translators, the CFG
  walk and the serializer are trusted.
- Proof-required AArch64 JIT coverage (`L11-P11`) is measured on this host by
  the opt-in census `jit_proof_coverage_census` (`TCG_JIT_PROOF_CENSUS=1`) over
  the repository's corpora: 398 compiles of the whole-body families, the
  source-bound arithmetic matrix, the custody fixtures, the memory leaves, trap
  bodies, calling frames and every beat-llvm leaf. With the overlay AY/Clean
  pair 273 publish and run; with Trust package 9192's tools 21 (the
  copy-free memory leaves) do. Every other compile is refused by name: calling
  frames (0 of 16 publish) on their `BL` (an instruction-derived row) and the
  arithmetic around it, since no source-bound owner admits a call; division and
  remainder bodies on `UDIV`/`SDIV`/`MSUB` rows with only statistical evidence
  (the frameless owner admits no `Udiv`/`Sdiv`/`Urem`/`Srem`, and an unproven
  LIR division TRAPS at a zero divisor, so a sound theorem must equate the trap
  conditions, not exclude them); memory leaves on the copy that moves a loaded
  value to the return register, on address arithmetic or on an O0 constant
  (the memory-leaf checker credits accesses only); dead O0 constants; and the
  beat-llvm `FnOnce::call_once` shims, which return nothing (no non-vacuous
  theorem) and keep an `ADD` with only statistical evidence. No publication in
  these corpora contains a relocation, since every call is refused
  (record).
- A verifying AArch64 JIT publication (`JitConfig::verify`: `AlwaysVerify`,
  `CachedVerified`) is replayed at the installed-artifact boundary (`L11-P2`)
  before any function pointer exists: the sealed, cache-walked MAP_JIT mapping
  is re-read; every installed word of a certified range must equal the word
  of the publisher's image buffer whose digest that function's certificate
  records (on the publisher's own path both hashes come from one buffer, so
  the digest check only ties the compared baseline to the certificate and
  cannot fail there; the independent content is the re-read and the decoder
  checks); every `BRANCH26` site is decoded by the verifier's independent A64 field
  decoder and must reach the function entry or veneer its relocation names at
  the mapped address; each reached veneer must decode as `LDR X16, <+8>;
  BR X16` holding the resolved address; profile literals must hold their
  values; any other relocation inside a certified range is refused by name
  (`JitError::InstalledArtifactReplayRejected`). The proof-required compiler
  route refuses a buffer without a replay covering every function. This is a
  byte- and relocation-level check of what will execute against the
  certificate-bound words, not a re-proof of the certificate's semantic claim
  or of an external symbol's identity; it reads memory, not the instruction
  cache, and binds nothing outside certified ranges and their veneers beyond
  the read-back hash. The tamper controls (a flipped byte, a branch
  re-encoded to a valid wrong target and a moved veneer literal, each after
  the seal and the cache walk) are crate unit tests; a mutant replaying the
  heap copy instead of the mapping fails them. They need the publisher's
  test-only tamper hook, so they run in the `trust-cg-codegen` library suite,
  which the Darwin floor does not run; the floor target
  `jit_installed_artifact_replay` checks faithful replays only. Linux has not
  run them.
- The x86-64 source-bound body lane (slices 1-15, `x86_source_bound_body`)
  credits the PRE-REGISTER-ALLOCATION ISel stream the x86 certificate lane
  verifies, not the emitted bytes; crediting that subject is an owner decision
  (2026-09-27). One theorem per function states that the ABI-observable
  result of that stream equals its exact LIR source's result for every input
  (since slice 14, on which the source's run is defined up to the point
  observed, below). That source is the LIR instruction selection receives,
  which in a compile that claims proofs is the adapter's own (OD-225: no
  shared LIR pass runs there). AY refutes the negation and Clean/Carcara checks the
  Alethe proof. The
  observable is the return bits every caller the backend meets reads: RAX for
  an I64 or pointer result; EAX, AX or AL for I32, I16 or I8 (the backend's
  own callers copy AL/AX with `MOVZX`, and LLVM callers re-extend from
  AL/AX/EAX, measured with LLVM 22.1.2 on x86_64-apple-darwin); and EAX
  holding 0 or 1 for a B1 (`bool`) result. The psABI `_Bool` rule and an
  LLVM caller (`movzbl %al, %eax`, no mask) read only AL, but the backend's
  own B1 contract is a clean 32-bit boolean: the width its own results are
  held to and the width it passes a B1 argument at, which an LLVM callee
  relies on (LLVM compiles `fn(b: bool) -> u32 { b as u32 }` to
  `movl %edi, %eax`), so a B1 result with EAX bits 8..31 set is refuted. A
  trust-cg caller of another function's `bool` result relies on AL only and
  re-extends it with `MOVZX` (slice 3 below).
  Residual: LLVM's Darwin callee convention also extends `i8`/`i16` return
  values to 32 bits for legacy callers that relied on clang's old behaviour
  (PR26665). Neither the backend's narrow-return contract nor this theorem
  promises that, so a legacy or hand-written Darwin C caller that reads EAX
  of a trust-cg `extern "C"` `i8`/`i16`-returning function is not covered.
  An argument register defines only its parameter's own low bits (rustc's
  Rust ABI marks no extension on `i8`/`i16`/`i32`, and an LLVM caller passes
  them unextended). A B1 parameter has bit 0 as its value; a psABI caller
  clears only bits 1..7, while the backend's own callers and LLVM callers
  (`zeroext i1`) pass a clean 32-bit bool. A function that takes and returns
  a B1 is walked under both views and must return EAX = 0/1 to clean-bool
  callers and AL = 0/1 to psABI callers; every other function is walked once
  under the psABI view. No caller's extension is assumed that the caller
  does not provide. The callee-saved registers and RSP are not part of the
  observable: the machine walk refuses any write to RBX, RBP, R12-R15 or RSP
  before a theorem is built, so their preservation rests on that trusted
  Rust walk, not on the replayed proof. That one replayed whole-body theorem
  credits every value row it covers, including copies, constants and
  dead-but-harmless rows; its certificate names it a whole-body theorem. A
  refuted theorem fails the covered rows; an inconclusive solve, an
  uncertified UNSAT or a refused replay leaves them unverified. Register
  allocation, the two-address fixup, spills, the `push rbp; mov rbp, rsp`
  frame, branch resolution and encoding are checked only by the
  TV-4/TV-5/ENC-3 validators, which are not proofs. Trusted: the Rust
  LIR-to-SMT and x86-to-SMT translators, including the width rules they take
  from the encoder (a 32-bit write zero-extends into bits 32..63;

  shared with the machine's `lea r, [rip + symbol]` (direct) and `mov r,
  [rip + symbol@GOT]` (GOT) respectively; the theorem assumes nothing about
  the address (alignment, non-null, distinctness), a load or store through
  it is an incoming-memory access under the slice-4 rules, and a machine row
  naming a symbol or form the source does not reference is a named
  mismatch (the two forms differ under interposition). A two-symbol swap is
  refuted by the theorem. `Icmp` (a `bool` that is returned, stored, passed
  or widened) is exact LIR semantics on the source side and, on the machine
  side, `cmp` (`CmpRR` of one width or `CmpRI` with a sign-extended `imm32`)
  through the shared x86 EFLAGS model (CF, ZF, SF, OF, PF of `lhs - rhs`),
  `setcc` of the x86 condition over those flags, and the selector's `movzx`;
  no table maps a LIR condition to an x86 one, so a wrong condition,
  signedness, operand order or operand extension is refuted. `setcc` writes
  only its low byte and register allocation treats its destination as a pure
  definition, so bits 8..63 are a free input (a `bool` returned without the
  `movzx` is refuted); RFLAGS is undefined at entry and after a call (a
  `setcc` of it is a named undefined read) and every other admitted ALU row
  rewrites it (a `setcc` after one makes no claim). A compare that feeds a
  branch stays outside with all control flow, and so does a signed order of
  two `bool`s (LIR orders a 1-bit value as signed). Trusted for slice 5, in
  addition: the System V return-register table, the shared EFLAGS model and
  condition evaluation (`x86_64_eflags`), the flag-writer table, and the
  symbol binding (a `LeaRip` is the address a `GlobalRef` names and a
  `MovRipRel` the one an `ExternRef` names; the relocation encodings and the
  loader's GOT are outside this theorem, covered only by the per-row
  relocation proofs and the linker). Host qualification (toolchain AY
  0.27.0 build 10530, Clean 5f09e36c, the replayer pair above): every one of
  the 40 slice-5 fixture shapes (sixteen pair, eight symbol and sixteen
  compare bodies; five of the pair shapes use a pair call's `bool` lane,
  widened, forwarded, passed and stored) and three alternative machine
  forms (`cmp r, imm32`, a mirrored compare, a `lea` field offset)
  certifies through the real builder, and AY refutes with counterexamples
  eighteen wrong lowerings (swapped pair halves, RDX holding lane 0, a u64
  lane returned through a 32-bit move, swapped call lanes, a pair call's
  `bool` lane used unmasked when widened and when forwarded, swapped
  symbols, a wrong global field offset, a signed order for an unsigned
  compare at 64 and 32 bits, an unsigned order for a signed one, a negated
  equality, a zero extension for a signed `i8` compare, `setcc` without
  `movzx`, swapped compare operands, and a u64 `x == 5` made at 32 bits by
  a truncating copy against a register or an immediate and by `cmp edi,
  5`). The last three differ from the source only when bits 32..63 of `x`
  matter, which the test-only sampled oracle missed until its boundary
  values carried each 64-bit constant of the theorem with bit 32 set; AY
  and the verifier refuted them before and after.
  Measured through the rustc bridge (Darwin `core`, O0, proofs required,
  `reports/perf/2026-09-29-darwin-x86-64-census-slice5/`), as a controlled
  A/B of the merged tree after review (`7ad4cee62`) against its `main`
  parent (`a77f920dc`), same host, compiler, flags and replay tools: 2708 ->
  2115 failed roots (`[TCG-PROOF-465]`, and on both sides 14
  `[TCG-DYN-REF-IDENTITY]`), 593 promote (359 pair returns, 125
  symbol addresses, 83 compares, 26 pair calls, including the four panic
  helpers whose first instruction is a `GlobalRef` to a `.const.alloc`),
  none newly fails, no `[TCG-SOURCE-BOUND-X86-MISMATCH]`; 1270 bodies replay
  Valid (677 before). (The first measurement, against `main` at
  `db6c150ee`, 230 commits before the branch's parent, gave the same 2115
  roots and the same 593.) The replay checker in both rows is the one the
  bridge's default discovery resolves first, the stage-1 toolchain's
  `bin/clean` (built from Clean `faf434b73`), not the Clean `5f09e36c` of
  the library-test qualification. 165 bound bodies do not certify, their rows stay
  Unverified: 162 because AY rejects its own proof in strict certification
  (`strict UNSAT proof validation failed: step t1 uses unverified trust
  rule`, or `... uses unsupported hole rule`, / `unknown` /
  `(:reason-unknown (incomplete self-check-rejected))`; mostly theorems
  with seven or more observed items, and multiplies) and 3 on an incomplete

  a counterexample or a timeout. A proof-required bridge build of a
  seventeen-function slice-5 crate promotes at O0 and agrees with LLVM in
  all four rlib x bin cells over 1282 values; at O1/O2 its pair bodies make
  no claim, because the optimizer's two-operand `xor r, r` zeroing idiom is
  a row form no slice admits (only three-address ALU rows are). The census
  wall time rose from 2073 s to 4398 s on single runs (the harness's
  default 3600 s timeout killed a first run), and from 2597 s to 4726 s in
  the controlled A/B (single runs on a shared host). That is the cost of the bodies

  finds it in the process's proof memo, but AY's `(:reason-unknown

  memo below (it is not a function of the query bytes), so each of the 162 self-check
  rejections is solved in full by the batched compile, again by the
  fallback, and again for every byte-identical body (the 165 non-certifying
  queries are 95 distinct texts; replayed alone they take 717 s per pass,
  252 s of it on repeats, measured in review). A
  three-function probe crate (`u32::overflowing_mul`, a pair swap and a
  compare; `no_std`, O0, proofs required) compiles in 6.2 s through the
  `db6c150ee` bridge and in 148.6 s through the slice-5 bridge: the

  `core`'s local copy) goes to AY four times, 22.0 s each, and ends
  `incomplete self-check-rejected` every time, while each Valid body is
  solved once. The replayer's outcome on identical query bytes
  is not deterministic: the slice-4 `SlotFoldedOffset` fixture query
  certified on 9 of 10 direct replays on the qualification AY (`--strict-proofs`)
  and was otherwise rejected by AY's own strict certification (`step t1
  uses unverified trust rule`), and on 2 of 3 replays under load; so a

  qualification test that pins the certified set can fail without a code

  Cost: admission is not free when the replayer cannot certify. A
  straight-line memory body that slice 3 refused at the source gate is now
  replayed, and when AY times out (30 s) or rejects its own proof the
  function still fails `[TCG-PROOF-465]`, only later; a codegen unit whose
  batched compile fails is recompiled per function (the rustc bridge's
  CT-BATCH fallback), which solves every theorem AY did not certify again
  (a certified one is a memo hit). Measured in the review of fd126a8ad
  (single-function crates through the rustc bridge, interleaved min-of-3
  against the slice-3 bridge, same outcome under both): four field stores
  through `*mut Mixed` 3.45 s -> 37.56 s (AY timeout), a slot-spilled store
