  NEGATIVE MEMO (owner decision, 2026-09-30;
  `crates/trust-cg-verify/src/source_bound_negative_memo.rs`). A source-bound
  replay that ends in one of the outcomes measured to be properties of the
  query is remembered, and a later identical replay returns the same
  non-credit outcome without running AY: AY's strict self-check rejecting its
  own proof (`(:reason-unknown (incomplete self-check-rejected))`), a
  disclosed incomplete certificate, the working checker rejecting the exact
  proof, and a timeout of a solve that used its budget. Every other `unknown`
  (AY's memory, resource, interrupt, internal-error and split-limit answers,
  which describe the host; a bare `unknown`; AY's model gate) and every error
  is solved again at its next occurrence. A timeout is remembered only on
  evidence that the QUERY ran out, not the host (since 2026-10-01, schema v3):
  the replay's budgets are wall-clock deadlines, and on 2026-09-30 a host at
  load 40-80 made the solves of bodies that certify at rest time out, each
  timeout was recorded, and later processes were answered `Timeout` without
  solving for the entry's retry budget, so proof-required builds and six
  `trust-cg-codegen`/`trust-cg-cli` proof-promotion tests failed on that busy
  host. The subprocess supervisor now measures, immediately before it kills
  a child whose deadline expired, the CPU time (user + system) its whole
  process group used under that deadline (AY solves in a worker it forks
  into the group; the resident route measures one query's exchange,
  subtracting the group's total when the exchange began), and a `Timeout` is
  remembered only when the replay saw at least one deadline expire and every
  expiry used at least 90 % of its budget in CPU time
  (`BUDGET_EXHAUSTING_CPU_PERCENT`). A starved expiry, an unmeasured one (a
  platform other than macOS and Linux, a group member that could not be
  read, a resident deadline spent before the query reached the server), and
  a `Timeout` no supervised deadline produced (AY printing `timeout`; the
  checker's capability probe running out of its deadline is, since OD-223,
  the uncredited "Clean checker unavailable" outcome) record nothing and
  leave an existing entry for
  the key as it is; the entry of a remembered timeout carries the CPU time
  that justified it (`cpu-ms`). The measurement counts CPU time, not work: a
  solve that ran on a slower core (an efficiency core under load) for its
  whole budget counts as having used it, and a solver that computes on
  several threads or processes at once can reach the share in less wall time
  than an idle host would give it; the retry policy below still bounds such
  an entry. The certification failures vary with load too, because AY's
  strict certification has its own wall-clock bound (3 s per
  proof-producing bit-blast in the toolchain AY 0.27.0 build 10530):

  - On 2026-10-01 at load 45-60 it rejected its own proof of the AArch64
    leaf FP/LR frame theorem after 24.7-26.8 s, with about 65 % of that
    time on a processor. A later process was answered from the entry
    (`reports/2026-10-01-negative-memo-load-timeouts/`).
  - A Darwin x86-64 `core` census at load 16 on four cores lost two bodies
    that replayed `Valid` at rest.

  Since schema v4, a certification failure is remembered only when at
  least one fresh solve of the replay completed and every such solve held
  the processor: process-group CPU time of at least 90 % of the solve's
  wall-clock time (`PROCESSOR_HELD_CPU_PERCENT`). The supervisor reads it
  at the exit while the exited leader is still unreaped, so AY's reaped
  worker is counted (`subprocess::run_measured`). A starved or unmeasured
  completion, or none at all, records nothing and leaves an existing entry
  as it is. For calibration, the toolchain AY's genuine rejections of
  eight census queries ran at 98-99 % CPU share at load 7 with a processor
  each, so they are still remembered. An outcome that follows a SAT
  verdict is never remembered,
  and deletes the key's entry, so no hit can stand in for a known SAT (a model
  query that timed out after AY answered SAT ends `Timeout`, and before this
  rule was recorded as one). It can only withhold credit: an entry stores the
  outcome kind and AY's reason text, never an `AYResult`, and a stored reason
  that does not classify as its own label is a miss; a hit becomes only
  `Unknown` (the recorded text) or `Timeout`, never `Verified`, `SolverUnsat`
  or a counterexample, and never carries a reuse receipt. It is consulted
  inside the exact-query funnel after the in-process `Verified` memo and the
  per-box Alethe certificate store, so a proof any process has minted is still
  consumed first (tested in a fresh process, where only the per-box store
  holds it), and a live `Verified` or counterexample deletes the entry. The
  key hashes the exact query bytes, the v2 query key (AY's content digest over
  those bytes), AY's recorded identity (build banner, digest, overlay), the
  positive-reuse authority (AY path, Clean path and digest, the sanitized
  verifier child environment, including its working directory), the Clean
  digest, the solve budget, the Clean check's own deadline (ruling OD-223,
  below), the model option, whether the resident AY route is
  live, the replay protocol (rendered from the command builders the replay
  uses: the resident, fresh, SAT-model and Clean command lines, plus the
  split-assert retry and the fresh replay of a resident candidate; a test ties
  it to the real commands) and the verifier's build identity
  (`VERIFIER_SOURCE_SHA256`, which `build.rs` records as the SHA-256 of this
  crate's manifest, build script and `src/` and of `trust-cg-process-env`'s
  manifest and `src/`, so an entry never crosses builds whose replay or
  verdict code differ; a build that cannot record it runs without the memo);
  any difference misses. `TRUST_CG_AY_TIMEOUT_MS` is not in the key: it
  budgets only the checker's capability probe. Tiers: an in-process map (it
  answers the CT-BATCH per-function fallback's second replay and
  byte-identical bodies across codegen units), and one file per key under
  `source-bound-negative-v6/` in the per-box certificate store (the earlier
  namespaces are never read: a v2 timeout may be a starved one, a v3
  certification failure a starved one, a v4 timeout a resident deadline
  alone, and a v5 timeout a Clean check that overran the solve budget it
  then shared, OD-223). Every per-box
  read-modify-write and delete holds the namespace's advisory lock (`flock` on
  `.lock`), so a concurrent `Verified` delete is never undone by a reuse count
  written back (a stress test of overlapping reuse and delete rounds; without
  the lock an entry came back); an entry is published by a fresh temporary
  file renamed over it; only a regular file is opened, without following links
  or blocking, so a FIFO or other non-regular file at an entry or lock path is
  a miss (before, a reader-less FIFO hung the compile); a missing, truncated,
  corrupt, oversized, foreign-schema or foreign-key entry is a miss; and each
  recording prunes a bounded window (32) of expired or unreadable entries and
  stale staging files, so the store does not only grow. Retry policy (the
  default, `RetryPolicy::DEFAULT`): per box, reuses are counted per process
  (the first occurrence of a key in a process that reads the per-box entry is
  one reuse), a first failure is reused by at most 2 later processes, and each
  further consecutive failed re-solve doubles that up to 32; in one process,
  an entry answers at most 64 hits within 60 minutes of entering the process,
  then the next occurrence solves again (a long-lived verifying process, such
  as the JIT, which replays through the same path, therefore retries); and no
  entry older than 24 hours is honoured in any tier. The next occurrence after
  any bound solves again and refreshes the entry. Justification, measured on
  this host (AY 0.27.0 build 10530;
  `reports/2026-09-30-ay-strict-selfcheck-nondeterminism/`): occurrences
  inside one compile are not independent retries (in 18 Darwin `core` censuses
  no body's batched and per-function replays ever differed, and the one
  load-dependent query found fails whenever the host is loaded), so one
  compile solves each key once however many byte-identical bodies it has (the
  slice-5 `core` gaps are 95 texts for 165 bodies, up to 13 bodies per text,
  each replayed twice); that query certified 18 of 20 times one at a time
  (both rejections as the load rose past 5) and 0 of 34 times at load 7.6 or
  with four copies running, always rejected at 9.07-9.13 s, so a failure
  recorded under load is retried by the third compile after it or within a
  day; and the 95 texts the bridge fails on never certified in 475 replays
  (load 2.9-3.3) nor in 18 censuses, so each further failed re-solve halves
  how often such a text is re-solved. In one process: the most frequent
  uncertified key of that census occurs 26 times in one compile (13
  byte-identical bodies, each judged by the batched compile and its fallback),
  and the longest compile with the memo took 47 minutes (2824 s), so 64 hits
  within 60 minutes let one compile solve each key once, while a long-lived
  process retries each failing key at least every hour or every 64
  occurrences. It serves every source-bound owner (the x86-64 body and
  envelope parts and the AArch64 frame and ALU theorems), because they share
  the one replay path (`verdict_db::live_source_bound_replay_explained`). It
  is off under `TCG_NO_PROOF_CACHE`, while the tier-0 recorder is armed and
  without a capable checker; the per-box tier follows `TCG_NO_CERT_STORE`; the
  tracked bridge knob `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=source-bound-no-negative-memo`
  (`TCG_SOURCE_BOUND_NO_NEGATIVE_MEMO` outside the bridge) bypasses it
  entirely, reading and writing nothing. `x86-body-trace` and `solve-trace`
  name every hit (`replay negative-memo hit tier=… kind=… reuses=…
  process_hit=…`). The cost of the memo is the nondeterminism it can pin:
  while an entry is honoured, a retry that would have certified is not run, so
  those rows stay Unverified, refused, never credited, until a bound of the
  retry policy expires or the knob re-solves; a compile that meets an unlucky
  outcome keeps it for the entry's budget in later compiles that use the same
  per-box store (the library host-qualification tests replay fresh and are
  unaffected). A bounded DIAGNOSIS suppression follows from remembering
  timeouts: when the lowering is genuinely wrong but AY's search for the
  refuting model ran out of its budget once, later occurrences replay that
  `Timeout` instead of searching again, so their rows stay Unverified (the
  compile is refused) rather than Failed with a counterexample. Acceptance
  does not change (a timeout and a refutation both refuse, and neither
  credits); only the counterexample that a retry might have produced is not
  reported until the entry's budget expires (at most 64 hits or 60 minutes in
  one process, 2 or more later processes, 24 hours) or the knob re-solves. A
  SAT verdict itself is never masked (above). Measured through the rustc
  bridge on a shared host with the first version of the memo (before an
  adversarial review's fixes: the build identity, the stable classes only, the
  in-process budget, the SAT rule, the locking)
  (`reports/perf/2026-09-30-darwin-x86-64-negative-memo/`, single runs): the
  slice-5 three-function probe crate compiles in 146.5 s and 148.0 s without
  the memo (its uncertified 3180-byte body query occurs four times at about 34
  s each: a resident `unsat` candidate after 22 s, then the fresh
  proof-bearing replay AY rejects), in 45.0 s and 44.7 s with an empty per-box
  namespace (solved once) and in 8.7 s and 9.6 s once that entry exists; with
  the bypass knob 147.5 s. The Darwin `core` census (O0, proofs required) took
  3994 s on the base `73e5a69f5`, 2824 s with an empty namespace (each of the
  95 non-certifying texts solved once, 235 occurrences answered in process)
  and 1031 s warm (none solved; 95 per-box reuses, 235 in process), with 2114
  failed roots, the same 165 bodies without an independently checked proof and
  the same 1271 Valid bodies on all three rows; no root differs. The one
  difference is the outcome KIND of the three `core::fmt::num::imp::*::_fmt`
  bodies (an incomplete certificate on the base row, a strict self-check
  rejection on the cold row's live solves), which AY varies with load on
  identical bytes. After the review fixes (this branch merged with `main`
  `f2ba63226`, bridge sha256 `fe294f80…`), the probe crate compiles in 145.0 s
  and 145.0 s through the `73e5a69f5` bridge, in 43.8 s and 43.0 s with an
  empty per-box namespace, in 7.8 s and 8.1 s warm, and in 145.0 s with the
  bypass knob, every run ending in the same refusal and body trace. The census
  was not re-run after the fixes: for its keys they change nothing but the
  key's build component (every uncertified census body ends in a recorded
  class, a strict self-check rejection or an incomplete certificate; its most
  frequent key's 26 occurrences per compile are within the 64-hit budget and
  the 47-minute compile within the 60-minute window), so the only difference
  is that the previous build's entries are not read.
  Slice 6 admits acyclic control flow. The LIR CFG may be any DAG of at
  most sixteen blocks whose terminators are `Jump`, `Brif` on a scalar
  (`then` when it is not 0), `Switch` on a scalar (each case the adapter's
  normalized constant of the selector's carrier, every edge to a different
  block), `Return` and `Trap`; a loop (slice 12's), another terminator, an
  unreachable block, more than sixteen entry-to-end paths or more than 256 instructions
  on one path stay outside (named in `x86-body-trace`). Each source path is
  admitted as a chain under the slice 1-5 rules (a join's block parameters
  are the values the predecessor's copies defined on that path) and paired
  with the machine path it must run through a one-to-one correspondence of
  machine and LIR blocks found from the rows' TV-1 lowering provenance, not
  from block ids (at O1+ `renumber_blocks_contiguous` renames the surviving
  blocks to `0..n` after a pass deletes some, so an id can name another LIR
  block): a machine block lowers LIR block B when every source-attributed
  row in it is stamped with B, each LIR block needs exactly one such block
  and no other block may be laid out, and each machine block's successors
  must be, through what they lower, its LIR block's successors. A `jcc` is
  taken exactly when its target lowers the source path's next block, a `jmp`
  or a fallthrough reaches that block, and the last block ends in its `ret`
  or, for a path that traps, its `ud2`. Every step is a real machine
  transfer, so the pairing only chooses which machine path each source path
  is judged against; soundness never rests on it. The theorem states, for
  each source path P, `(or (not C_P) (and M_P O_P))`: C_P the source's
  branch literals on P,
  M_P the machine's `jcc` conditions on the paired path through the shared
  EFLAGS model (every condition code, from a `cmp` or `test` of the same
  block), O_P that path's observed items; the conditions partition the
  inputs, so a machine that branches on another condition or code, swaps
  its successors, traps where the source returns (or the reverse) or takes
  the other arm's value is refuted. A machine CFG without the
  correspondence makes no claim, never a named mismatch: a block merged
  (except a chain of single-entry `Jump`s, which slice 24a states over its
  exact contraction, below), if-converted (except a single-entry region one
  machine block lowers, which slice 24c states over its segments, below),
  split, duplicated, added (a
  switch search tree of five or more cases until slice 20, below, an
  `Assert`'s trap edge, a dead block) or deleted (an arm an
  O1+ pass proved unreachable), a transfer retargeted, or a machine path the
  source does not have; so do a jump table and a `jcc` whose fallthrough
  also reaches its target. (The first version paired blocks by id, and the
  review found a correct O2 body, an inner compare repeating the outer one,
  named a control mismatch after its trap arm was deleted and the survivors
  renumbered; `a_renumbered_optimized_body_is_never_a_mismatch` and
  `renamed_machine_blocks_are_paired_by_provenance` fail on that version.)
  A one-path source whose machine has no conditional jump is the slice 1-5
  machine chain, whatever its blocks, as before slice 6. The exact affine
  refusal names a return-value, call-argument or memory mismatch only for a
  one-path body: it compares the two sides over all inputs, while on a path
  of several a value is observed only where the path condition holds (a
  machine returning 7 where the source returns `x + 7` on its `x == 0` path
  is correct); there the theorem judges it. The review found the first
  version naming that correct machine a mismatch
  (`path_conditioned_values_are_judged_by_the_theorem`). Flags reach only
  readers in the block that wrote them, a call leaves them undefined (a
  named undefined read),
  and a flag writer other than `cmp`/`test` between a compare and its
  reader makes no claim; register allocation inserts only moves and treats
  a `cmovcc` destination as tied, which is what the walk assumes. `test r,
  imm32` is admitted on a 64-bit register only: the encoder emits the REX.W
  form whatever the register class, so a 32-bit one makes no claim (nothing
  emits `TestRI` today). Slice 6 also admits `Select` on a nonzero test (the
  selector's `mov; cmp; cmovne`,
  64- or 32-bit) and a path's read of a private stack byte no store on it
  wrote (an `Option::None` payload built on one arm): that byte is the
  slot's initial value `f_k`, shared with the machine's read of the same
  frame byte, which is stronger than the source needs (trust-ir reads it as
  poison), so a machine that zeroes the slot instead, also correct, is
  refuted rather than credited. Encoding, chosen by host qualification
  (AY 0.27.0 build 10530, Clean 5f09e36c), per shape: one `or`/`not` claim
  per path (spelled `=>`, AY prints its proof with a `hole` step,
  `ay.proof.decline mechanism=printer-rule-without-external-spelling`,
  which Clean rejects as holey, on every fixture), no name defined for a
  copy, and only the definitions the claims depend on. On the Darwin
  `core` census's 345 several-path theorems (offline, the O0 `dump-trust-ir`
  modules of `main` 73e5a69f5), AY and Clean certify 281 with that encoding
  and 162 with copies defined (none that certifies with copies fails
  without), 104 of the first 244 with every definition stated and 125 with
  the cone alone; the nested `ite` case split certifies 4 of the 119 the
  canonical claims did not; 64 do not certify (44 AY rejects its own proof
  in strict certification, `step tN uses unverified trust rule` / `(:reason-
  unknown (incomplete self-check-rejected))`, 20 on an incomplete
  certificate, `unproved_steps=1`), and none is refuted. A design with one
  obligation per path would certify 28 more of the first 119 failures (each
  path certifies alone) and is not built: the lane replays one theorem per
  function. All 25 slice-6 fixture shapes and three alternative machine
  forms (the O1+ fused `cmp; jb`, a branch laid out as a fallthrough, a
  `test r, r` zero test) certify through the real builder, and AY refutes
  20 wrong lowerings with counterexamples; the merged `ite` of the
  observable, the case split and every-definition spelling certify on the
  fixtures too and are recorded as rejected spellings. Each walk rule of the
  first version has a control that fails when the rule alone is disabled
  (the census report's `fails-before/mutants.txt`). The real x86 optimizer's
  output of the 25 fixtures at O1, O2 and O3 is judged too: 13 build a
  theorem that holds on samples at each level (the fused
  compare-and-branch, the inverted branch layout, switch chains, trap and
  call paths, selects), 12 make no claim (merged or if-converted arms, a
  block without the provenance correspondence, or a row form outside the
  slice; measured at slice 6, before slices 24a and 24c state merged chains
  and if-converted regions), and none is a mismatch. The branch-layout pass inverts a `jcc`
  and swaps its fallthrough without reordering the block's recorded
  successors, so the
  owner compares recorded successors with the transfers as a set; the first
  bridge build compared them in order and named every such correct O1/O2
  body a mismatch (found by the cross-backend matrix, fixed with a
  fails-before test). Trusted for slice 6, in addition: the path
  enumeration, the machine walk's control semantics (a taken `jcc`
  continues at its target, an untaken one at the next row, a block without
  a final transfer at the next block in layout), the flag-block rule, the
  EFLAGS model of `test`, the `cmovcc` tie, the meaning of an admitted
  `Switch` constant, and the frame-byte rule; the pairing (provenance, the
  successor and fallthrough rules) only chooses the machine path a source
  path is judged against. An independent library-level credit attack on
  the first version (6,643 mutants of 18 fixtures, plain and O1-O3 and the
  variant forms, judged against a concrete x86 interpreter) found no wrong
  machine function credited; its completeness notes: 7 correct mutants are
  refuted because the theorem requires the source's path (`setb` for
  `setbe` where the operands are equal), and 7 correct synthetic mutants
  were named mismatches (a `ret` after a diverging call where the source
  traps, and a branch past a block that computes an equal value, which the
  provenance pairing now leaves without a claim). On the
  Darwin `core` census (O0, proofs required,
  `reports/perf/2026-09-30-darwin-x86-64-census-slice6`) slice 6 takes the
  failed roots from 2114 (the `main` 73e5a69f5 bridge) to 1816 (a bridge of
  slice 6 on 915fff712, which also carries e6288b598, the LEA-writeback
  collapse turned on by default; the verdicts were recomputed by the
  review): 298 promote (284 control flow, 7 partially written slots, 7
  selects), none newly fails, and no
  mismatch is named. Of the baseline's 766 control-flow functions, 345 are
  bound and 284 of them replay Valid (61 do not certify: AY rejects its own
  proof or leaves an incomplete certificate; none is refuted); 76 have more
  than sixteen blocks, 64 a loop, 23 a path over 256 instructions, and the
  rest stop at an instruction outside the lane on some path (a private
  slot's address escaping into a call, a call result with no scalar type,
  `Checked*` arithmetic, `GuardDivZero`, `AtomicLoad`, ...). The census's
  wall time rose from 3994 s to 7054 s on single runs of a shared host: the
  first solves of the newly bound bodies about 1.3 ks, the per-function
  fallback's second solve of the 79 newly uncertified ones about 0.5-0.7 ks
  (which the negative memo above now answers without AY), and about 1 ks is
  not attributed (host load, and e6288b598 in the measured tree). The owner
  changed after the census bridge only in ways that accept no less at O0:
  the set comparison of recorded successors, the provenance pairing (on the
  census's O0 modules, offline, it binds exactly the functions the id
  pairing bound, with byte-identical theorems), the one-path affine refusal
  (the census named no mismatch) and the 64-bit `TestRI` rule (nothing emits
  it).
  Slice 7 admits calls through memory. A direct call may receive a private
  stack slot's address (a `StackAddr`, copied or offset by a constant or a
  `StructGep`, as for a load) as an ordinary 64-bit argument: a `&mut`/`&`
  out-parameter, or argument 0 of a callee in `Function::sret_arg_callees`,
  its hidden return buffer (the selector places it in RDI; such a call must
  have no result; the frame condition "an sret-arg callee" no longer
  refuses; an indirect return-buffer callee still does). The slot then
  escapes to that call and every later call on the path, and slice 3's
  Ackermann-reduced call model extends to it exactly: a call's observable
  inputs are its scalar arguments and the contents, at the call, of every
  slot that escaped to it or earlier (in 8-byte chunks from offset 0, each
  chunk one store's value when it is exactly that store's bytes, else the
  concatenation of its bytes; a chunk both sides spell alike, initial bytes
  or the bytes an earlier call left, is not stated), and its outputs are
  its scalar result and every byte of every escaped slot after it, the free
  input `d{site}s{slot}o{offset}` shared by the two sides at that call
  site. So a Valid theorem means each call meets equal arguments, equal
  escaped bytes and an equal world on both sides, and leaves equal bytes
  and an equal result; nothing is assumed about which bytes the callee
  writes (an LLVM callee may write every byte of a return buffer or of
  `*out`, padding included, or leave any of them), and a `&T` argument is
  no read-only promise. A private address is no SMT term: the walk checks
  that the machine's argument register holds exactly the paired slot and
  offset (another slot or offset, or a private address where the source
  passes a value, is a named `CallStackAddress` mismatch; a value the walk
  does not track as a private address makes no claim). Retention: once a
  slot escaped, what a call returns, what an incoming load reads and what a
  call left in a slot may be an address derived from it, and so may every
  value computed from one; an incoming load or store through such an
  address was outside the domain until slice 15 (it could touch the slot
  behind the byte model; slice 15 observes the escaped slots at it), while
  one through an address computed only from parameters,
  symbols, constants and what loads and calls produced before the first
  escape is incoming memory as in slice 4. Storing (until slice 13,
  below), returning or computing with a slot's address stays outside. A `bool` read of one call-defined
  byte is trust-ir's `Load Bool`, `byte != 0`, which the selector computes
  for every bool load. Not checked: that the slot is as large or as aligned
  as the callee's pointee (LIR states neither; the frame layout that honours
  the slot table is outside this theorem, as for every slot). Trusted for
  slice 7, in addition: the extended callee contract (a callee reads and
  writes incoming memory and the escaped slots' bytes only, and its result,
  next world and new slot bytes depend only on its register arguments, the
  world and those bytes), the walk's private-address check and the
  provenance rule behind the retention refusal (since slice 15, behind the
  escaped-slot observation that replaces it). Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-01-darwin-x86-64-census-slice7/`): 15 fixture
  shapes over real selector output (return buffers of a 3-word struct, a
  `(u64, u32, bool)` read at its widths, two buffers, a forwarded incoming
  buffer, an sret call on one branch arm, an `Option<(u64, u64)>` buffer
  whose tag is branched on; `&mut` out-parameters, two calls sharing one
  slot, a call that reads the slot it is given, a field address into the
  slot, a later call that is not given the slot, an `Option<u64>`
  out-parameter) all certify on the qualification host (AY 0.27.0 build
  10530, Clean 5f09e36c), AY refutes 6 wrong lowerings with
  counterexamples, the solver-free library gate
  (`x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice7::`, golden digest
  `slice7_snapshots.smt2`) holds every control, each of five walk rules
  disabled alone fails a control (`fails-before/`), and the real optimizer's
  O1-O3 output of 14 of the 15 fixtures builds a theorem that holds (one
  makes no claim, a `bt` row), none a mismatch. A mutation probe
  (`robustness/`) of 757 mutants of those 23 distinct streams, judged
  against an independent concrete interpreter whose callees overwrite every
  buffer they ever received, credits no wrong stream: AY refutes every
  wrong mutant the owner binds, and the 14 credited mutants are correct.
  The library gate's sampler now refutes each of those too. On the Darwin `core`
  census (O0, proofs required) slice 7 takes the failed roots from 1817 (the
  `main` 336a49f14 bridge) to 1634 (a slice-7 bridge on 65e3818dd with
  `main`'s bridge build fix eaa5d9ca8): 183 promote (131 whose slot escaped
  into a call, 52 with an sret-arg callee), none newly fails, no mismatch
  is named, and every body Valid before is Valid after. Of the 423
  sret-callee functions 52 now replay Valid and 131 are bound without a
  certified proof; the rest stop at a later refusal (65 more than sixteen
  blocks, 46 a non-scalar parameter, 45 a path over 256 instructions, ...);
  of the 185 escape-into-call functions 131 replay Valid and 20 are bound
  without one. The 151 newly bound bodies that do not certify end, like the
  baseline's, in AY's strict certification rejecting its own proof or an
  incomplete certificate (a few attempts at AY's 30 s budget; none
  refuted); they are larger (median 131 bound rows) and stay Unverified,
  the encoding unchanged for them. Replayed offline one at a time, 13 of
  150 certify and 126 are still rejected; respelling their call-defined
  bytes as 64-bit words changes none, and by size they certify like the
  baseline's bodies. A cross-backend matrix with LLVM-compiled callees (sret buffers,
  `&mut`/`&`/`&mut Option` out-parameters) and a proof-required rlib of
  exactly the credited callers matches the LLVM oracle in all four rlib x
  bin cells at O0-O3.
  Slice 8 admits aggregates in general-purpose registers. A parameter, the
  result, a direct call's argument or its one result may be a LIR `Struct`
  or `Array` that System V passes in general-purpose registers: 1 to 16
  bytes under the verify-owned C layout, every leaf a `B1`/`I8`/`I16`/
  `I32`/`I64` field inside one eightbyte and every eightbyte holding a
  field, so each eightbyte is INTEGER (psABI §3.2.3) and travels in the low
  bytes of one register (the next argument register; RAX, then RDX, for a
  result). The classification is verify-owned (`classify_aggregate`); a
  unit test sweeps 45 admitted aggregate types (integer arrays of every
  size from 1 to 16 bytes, structs with interior and tail padding, nested
  aggregates, `bool` fields) through the real adapter and selector as
  `fn(x: T) -> T { g(x) }` and finds the selector's own argument and result
  registers and widths equal to it (42 build a theorem that holds; the 3
  with a 3-byte eightbyte, which the selector moves through a register of
  another width, make no claim) and 6 refused types refused by name, and
  every call row's declared registers and widths are compared with it per
  compile. Refused by name: an enum, MEMORY class (over 16 bytes), an SSE
  eightbyte, an `i128` or vector field, an aggregate result beside another
  result, parameters needing more than six argument registers, and `i128`
  and floating-point scalars. LIR carries an aggregate by its address, and
  the model is byte-exact: an aggregate parameter is the private copy the
  selector makes at entry, whose bytes are the caller's (byte `b` of
  eightbyte `k` is byte `b` of the `k`-th argument register's entry value,
  only the eightbyte's own bytes); a returned aggregate's bytes at the
  return are observed against exactly the low bytes of RAX and RDX a caller
  reads; an aggregate argument's bytes at the call against exactly the low
  bytes of its argument registers (its slot does not escape; its address in
  the register is a named `CallStackAddress` mismatch); and a callee
  defines each eightbyte of an aggregate result and nothing above it (RAX
  after the call is `g_c ++ r_c` with `r_c` as wide as the eightbyte's
  bytes), its slot holding those bytes, which slice 7's retention rule
  taints once a slot escaped. Padding bytes inside an eightbyte are
  observed like the rest (on both sides they are the same bytes, so this is
  stronger than a caller needs, never weaker). Two machine forms the
  selector's eightbyte moves use are admitted: the tied two-operand `shl d,
  imm`, `shr d, imm` and `or d, s` (`d = d op x`), and a byte or word load
  into, or store from, a physical register's 8- or 16-bit alias, whose bits
  above the loaded ones are a free input (every other two-operand row,
  among them the optimizer's `xor r, r` zeroing idiom, stays outside, as the
  first version's O1 regression test caught). The machine's slot table must
  be the source's plus the copies at each aggregate's size and alignment;
  which machine slot holds which copy is not a soundness premise, because
  the source defines every byte of a copy and the machine every byte it
  walks. Trusted for slice 8, in addition: the classification and its
  layout, the callee contract for an aggregate result (it defines each
  eightbyte's bytes and nothing above them), the LIR meaning of an
  aggregate-typed value (the bytes at its address when it is passed or
  returned; the bridge's mapping of a Rust `PassMode` to that LIR type is
  the bridge's), the tied two-operand rule and the narrow physical alias
  rule. Evidence (`reports/perf/2026-10-02-darwin-x86-64-census-slice8/`):
  measured first, on the slice-7 census's own dumped `core` module, the
  class is 275 functions refused for a non-scalar parameter (191 an
  integer aggregate of at most 8 bytes, 5 of 9 to 16, 3 over 16, 56 an
  `i128`, 20 a float), 223 for a non-scalar result (197, 0, 0, 14, 12), 62
  for a call result with no scalar type (58 aggregates, 4 `i128`), 27 for
  the inconsistent type hint of a by-value aggregate argument, and 13 for
  more than six (all scalar) parameters; offline, a development build of
  the slice-8 owner bound 418 more functions (2147 to 2565: 163 of the
  parameter class, 182 of the result class, 50 of the call-result class,
  23 of the type-hint class), bound none less, and every theorem it built
  held on 2000 samples; every in-scope function it did not bind stopped at
  an unrelated later refusal.
  22 fixture shapes over real selector output all certify on the
  qualification host (AY 0.27.0 build 10530, Clean 5f09e36c; 131-3114 ms)
  and AY refutes 14 wrong lowerings with counterexamples (swapped halves, a
  wrong register, offset or width, a sign extension, swapped result
  registers, a narrowed or widened result, a dropped `or`, a call result
  used past its bytes, a byte loaded into AL and used wider, a `bool` field
  read as bit 0); the solver-free library gate
  (`x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice8::`, golden digest
  `slice8_snapshots.smt2`) holds every control; each of twelve rules
  disabled alone fails a control (`fails-before/`); the real optimizer's
  O1-O3 output builds theorems that hold and no false mismatch; and a
  mutation probe (`robustness/`) of 2383 mutants of 40 streams, judged
  against an independent concrete interpreter with its own eightbyte
  placement, credits no wrong stream (1795 wrong: 62 no claim, 1014 named,
  719 refuted by both the sampler and AY; every theorem AY refutes the
  sampler refutes too). The Darwin x86-64 `core` O0 proof census on the
  slice-8 bridge has 1276 failed roots against slice-7 `main` `90ccb1b0b`'s
  1626. Of the 350 promoted roots, 341 name a function slice 8 now binds
  and AY certifies. The other 9 are solver variance: scalar-only bodies
  whose strict AY self-check rejected the proof on the baseline. No root
  newly fails, no mismatch is named, no bound body is refuted, and no
  function that replayed `Valid` on the baseline fails to now. Of the 604
  functions the baseline refused in the slice-8 classes, 420 are bound:
  341 certify; 79 do not (the AY strict-certification and word-level
  class, fail-closed). Refused by name: 79 `i128`, 38 floating-point and 3
  MEMORY-class functions. Another 5 stop at a mixed-width `MovRR` that
  assembles a 3-byte argument; the rest stop at later refusals of other
  classes.
  Slice 9 lifts the control-flow bounds of slice 6. A several-path source
  of more than sixteen blocks, more than sixteen entry-to-end paths or a
  path of more than 256 instructions is stated over its DAG, in size linear
  in its blocks, with no bound on its paths; a one-path source keeps the
  slice 1-5 chain at any length. A source stated as one query has at most
  128 blocks and 1024 LIR instructions, and its machine at most 128 blocks
  and 512 rows (no theorem of more rows certified offline); a larger one is
  stated in parts (slice 16, below), else refused by name; a loop is slice
  12's. Each block is admitted once in a topological
  order from the state the paths into it share: its one predecessor's, or
  at a join the merge of its predecessors' (a value every incoming edge
  defines alike is kept, a private byte the edges leave differently is a
  merged byte, an unwritten one the slot's initial byte). A slot that
  escaped on some path into a join is escaped after it (slice 12; slice 9
  refused such a join). A `Switch` of two cases of one value, a redefinition of a value some path into a block
  defined and a register that the paths into a join leave holding different
  kinds of value (read later) are outside the domain. Each machine block,
  the one that lowers the LIR block under the slice-6 correspondence, is
  walked once per outgoing source edge over the rows that run on the way to
  the edge's target, from its entry state (at a join, the incoming states
  merged by the SOURCE edges' guards; flags never cross the boundary,
  whether a compare, a test or a slice-10 ALU row wrote them). The
  theorem defines 1-bit guards (the entry block's 1, a join's the `bvor` of
  its incoming edges', an edge of a conditional block its block's guard
  `bvand` the edge's slice-6 test), joins each differing value, register and
  private byte by `(ite (= G_e #b1) ...)` over the incoming edges' guards,
  and states in topological order each block's observed items under its
  guard, `(or (not (= g_B #b1)) O_B)`, and each conditional edge's machine
  `jcc` literals under the edge's guard, `(or (not (= G_e #b1)) M_e)`. It is
  EQUIVALENT to the slice-6 per-path conjunction input by input: the edge
  tests partition the source's runs, so exactly one path's guards hold,
  every joined value is that path's on both sides, and the claims state
  exactly that path's M_P and O_P. A wrong branch condition, a swapped,
  retargeted, extra or missing edge, or another arm's value is refuted or
  breaks the correspondence (no claim), as in slice 6. A several-path
  source within the slice-6 bounds keeps the per-path theorem byte for
  byte. Trusted for slice 9, in addition: the topological admission and
  walk, the merge rules, the guard definitions and the partition of a
  block's runs by its edges' tests. The DAG's theorem, and a one-path chain
  past 256 instructions, define no name for a copy, state only the
  definitions their claims reach and substitute every definition used at
  most once into its use, dropping each claim equation the substitution
  makes an identity (true on every input), all satisfiability-preserving;
  on the qualification host (AY 0.27.0 build 10530, Clean 5f09e36c) AY's strict
  certification rejects its own proof of a theorem with many definitions
  within 0.1 s (`step t0 uses unverified trust rule`, or a `hole` step),
  even a certified slice-6 theorem padded with twenty unused definitions.
  Evidence (`reports/perf/2026-10-02-darwin-x86-64-census-slice9/`):
  measured first on a fresh dump of `core` (the `main` `ac0481810` bridge),
  the baseline's 271 control-flow roots name 183 functions refused for more
  than sixteen blocks and 88 for a long path (and one for more than sixteen
  paths); of the 171 such functions in the dump, the slice-9 owner binds 52
  (5 of the block class, 47 of the path class), and the rest stop at a loop
  (63), a join of different escapes (24), checked arithmetic (7), a bound
  (9) or another instruction outside the lane. Offline, AY 0.27.0 certifies
  1 of the 52 with every copy and definition stated, 6 trimmed and 22
  trimmed and inlined (no theorem of more than 511 bound rows certifies; an

  qualification host with AY build 10530 (conditional calls, conditional

  (`KNOWN_UNCERTIFIED_SLICE_NINE`); all 14
  wrong lowerings are refuted with counterexamples on both. The solver-free
  library gate (`x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice9::`, golden digest
  `slice9_snapshots.smt2`) holds every control and checks the equivalence

  control (`fails-before/`); the real optimizer's
  O1-O3 output builds theorems that hold and no false mismatch; and a
  mutation probe (`robustness/`) of 2299 mutants of 37 streams, judged
  against an independent concrete interpreter, holds no wrong stream: of
  1887 wrong, 960 make no claim, 288 are named and 639 are refuted by the
  sampler. Replayed (728 mutants), AY certifies no wrong stream and refutes
  none the sampler misses. The probe found a sampler gap (a fixed stride
  missed a third switch's wrong case), now closed and controlled. The Darwin
  `core` O0 census on the slice-9 bridge (merged with main `cffb7e876`) has
  1166 failed roots against main's 1198: 32 promote, none newly fails, no
  mismatch is named, no bound body is refuted, and no function Valid on main
  loses that verdict. Of the 32, 28 are slice 9's: 23 with a path over 256
  instructions, 3 with more than 16 blocks, 1 with more than 16 paths, and 1
  over main's 256-row machine bound. The other 4 have byte-identical
  theorems on main and certify only at a lower host load. Of main's 272
  control-flow refusals, 63 are now bound (27 certify). The rest stop at: a
  loop (100); a join of different escapes (31); 512 machine rows (26); a
  `Switch` with two edges to one block (14); the slice-9 size bounds (10);
  and instructions outside the lane (28). The 76 newly bound bodies certify
  at 37%. The rest are AY rejecting its own proof, and none is refuted.
  Slice 10 admits more instructions. LIR checked arithmetic of two `I64`
  operands (`CheckedUadd`/`Usub`/`Umul`/`Sadd`/`Ssub`/`Smul`, the adapter's
  lowering of a 64-bit trust-ir `Overflow`; a narrower one is ordinary
  arithmetic and compares in LIR, and a checked op of another carrier is
  refused by name) has the results `[value, overflow]`: the wrapping
  result, and the `bool` that the mathematical result is outside the
  carrier's unsigned or signed range (trust-ir `eval_int_overflow`),
  computed exactly at `w + 1` or `2w` bits. The walk now models the flags
  of exactly the register-register `add`, `sub` and `imul` of a value and
  of the one-operand `mul` (Intel SDM: `add`/`sub` every status flag, CF
  the carry or borrow; `imul` and `mul` CF = OF only, "the product does not
  fit", SF/ZF/AF/PF undefined, so reading one of those is a named undefined
  read of `rflags`); `mul src` reads EAX/RAX and writes EDX:EAX/RDX:RAX at
  the width `src` names. `Bnot` and `Ineg` of an integer (`not`/`neg dst,
  src`), `CtPop` (`popcnt`, a narrow operand first masked by the tied `and
  d, imm`, admitted as `d = d & imm`) and `CallIndirect` through an `I64`
  function pointer (`call r64`: slice 3's Ackermann-reduced call model with
  the callee pointer observed like an argument, all 64 bits of the call
  register at the call; an indirect source call pairs only with `call r64`
  and a direct one only with `call symbol`, else a named `CallTarget`
  mismatch) are admitted, and so are shifts by a variable amount of the
  value's own carrier (`shl`/`shr`/`sar` by CL, the low byte of RCX masked
  to 5 or 6 bits). At an amount below the width that shift is trust-ir's;
  at the width or above trust-ir has undefined behavior
  (`interpret::shift_amount`), and the theorem states one refinement of it,
  the amount reduced modulo the width (what the selector's masked lowering
  computes), so a lowering that differs only where trust-ir is undefined
  (an unmasked narrow count) is refuted rather than credited. A shift by
  an out-of-range constant stays outside. Population count and the
  variable shift are each stated once for both sides (`count_ones`, a
  balanced tree of narrow adds; `shift_modulo_width`, a barrel shifter of
  extracts), the spellings chosen by host qualification: on the
  qualification host AY rejects its own proof of a 32- or 64-bit count
  spelled as a chain of full-width adds and prints a variable `bvlshr`/
  `bvshl`/`bvashr` with an unproved step. On a target without POPCNT (the
  Darwin x86-64 baseline) the pipeline expands the `popcnt` row into a
  SWAR sequence after this theorem's subject; that expansion is checked
  only by its own pass validation (widths 8 and 32 on every compile, 64 by
  a dedicated proof test). Trusted for slice 10, in addition: these
  trust-ir meanings and the stated shift refinement, the Intel SDM flag,
  width, implicit-operand and count-masking semantics of the admitted rows
  (and the rule that an undefined flag is never read), the two shared
  statements above, the tied `and` rule, the indirect-call pairing and the
  callee contract for any callee a pointer names. Division (`Udiv`/`Urem`,
  and the magic-number multiply of a constant divisor), the `GuardDivZero`
  trap carrier and atomics stay outside: a division traps where its source
  is undefined, which needs a definedness condition in the path claim, and
  every atomic body in `core` also dispatches through a jump table.
  Evidence (`reports/perf/2026-10-02-darwin-x86-64-census-slice10/`):
  measured first on `main` `ac0481810`'s Darwin `core` O0 census (1272

  arithmetic, 23 `CallIndirect`, 17 `Bnot`, 15 `CtPop`, 11 variable shifts
  and 1 `Ineg`, every one of them inside the control-flow bounds and with

  real adapter and selector output: 22 certify on the qualification host
  (AY 0.27.0 build 10530, Clean 5f09e36c), and the three 64-bit multiply
  shapes are recorded gaps there (AY's strict
  certification rejects its own proof, `step t1 uses unsupported hole

  checked multiply that panics certifies too, leaving the wrapping one
  (`KNOWN_UNCERTIFIED_SLICE_TEN`). AY
  refutes 19 wrong lowerings with counterexamples (a signed flag
  for an unsigned one and the reverse, an inverted flag, swapped or
  replaced operands, the product's high half as its value, a dropped
  complement, an overflow word compared with -1, which differs at one
  input only, a negation as a complement, a narrow popcount operand
  unmasked or masked short, a logical shift as arithmetic, a narrow shift
  count masked short, a narrow arithmetic shift of a zero-extended
  operand, a count loaded from the value, a call through the argument);
  the solver-free library gate
  (`x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice10::`, golden digest
  `slice10_snapshots.smt2`) holds every control; each of fifteen rules
  disabled alone fails a control (`fails-before/`); the real optimizer's
  O1-O3 output builds theorems that hold and no false mismatch; and a
  mutation probe (`robustness/`) of 1230 mutants of 29 streams, judged
  against an independent concrete interpreter that treats an out-of-range
  shift as undefined, credits no wrong stream (1041 wrong: 10 no claim,
  551 named, 480 refuted, and AY refutes none the sampler misses). The
  Darwin `core` O0 census on the slice-10 bridge has 1198 failed roots
  against `main` `ac0481810`'s 1272: 74 promote (39 checked arithmetic,
  12 `Bnot`, 8 `CallIndirect`, 7 variable shifts, 7 `CtPop`, 1 `Ineg`),

  Of the 164 functions the baseline refused in these classes, 157 are

  Replayed offline, the 83 are the AY certification class: 74 strict
  self-check rejections (among them all 24 multiplies), 8 proofs with an
  unproved step, 1 timeout, none refuted.
  Slice 11 admits `I128` register pairs and float bit patterns. An `I128`
  is two System V INTEGER eightbytes: a parameter or argument takes the
  next two integer argument registers, low half first (with one left,
  System V passes it on the stack, outside the lane), and a result is
  RAX:RDX, the only result. The source states every `I128` operation at
  128 bits with trust-ir's meaning (an `Iconst { ty: I128 }` is its `i64`
  immediate sign-extended, `Iconst128` both halves); the machine computes
  it on halves with the rows the walk models plus `adc`/`sbb` (`a + b +
  CF`, `a - (b + CF)`, CF from the flags of a modelled row of the block,
  undefined flags a named undefined read) and the tied one-operand
  `shl`/`shr`/`sar d, cl`. An incoming 16-byte access is two 8-byte
  accesses, the low half at the address and the high half 8 bytes above
  (a non-atomic, non-volatile little-endian access reads or writes exactly
  those bytes); an `I128` field filling a 16-byte aggregate is two INTEGER
  eightbytes. Every name a theorem defines stays 64 bits wide (a 128-bit
  value is named as its halves). An `F32`/`F64` is the bit pattern in the
  low 32 or 64 bits of an SSE register: XMM0-XMM7 numbered apart from the
  integer registers, a result in XMM0 (XMM1 for a second float lane), every
  XMM register changed by a call. It is admitted only where it is moved,
  stored, loaded or reinterpreted by a `Bitcast` to or from the integer of
  its width (`movss`/`movsd`, `movd`/`movq`, SSE loads and stores; a
  `movss` destination's bits above 32 are a free input, register
  allocation's pure definition). Refused by name: every floating-point
  operation but the slice-15 constants, `Fneg` and `Fabs` and (since slice
  21, OD-198) the rounding events (ruling OD-73 in
  `docs/decision-record.md`: on the
  qualification host AY's strict certification rejects its own proof of
  every `QF_FP`/`QF_BVFP` query tried, however trivial), a shift of an
  `I128` by a variable amount (the selector's register-pair lowering
  reduces no amount modulo 128, so it computes neither trust-ir's undefined
  behaviour nor OD-57's refinement), a branch on an `I128`, an `I128`
  beside another result, an aggregate with an SSE eightbyte (the selector
  passes `{f64, i64}` and `[f32; 2]` in XMM registers) and an f16 or
  vector value. Two spellings were chosen by host qualification: a shift
  by CL whose count the walk's exact constant folding knows is the shift by
  that constant, masked as the hardware masks CL (slice 10's barrel shifter
  left the constant `I128` shifts uncertified); and every arithmetic shift
  right by a constant, on both sides, is the sign extension of the bits it
  keeps (`bvashr` by a constant made AY print a `bitblast_ashr` step Clean
  rejects), which also certifies slice 1's two arithmetic-shift shapes.
  Trusted for slice 11, in addition: the System V class assignment of
  `I128` and float values (`argument_roots`, `result_roots`; swept against
  the selector's real output, and every call row's declared registers
  compared per compile), the callee contract for an `I128` result (all of
  RAX and RDX) and a float result (the low 32 or 64 bits of XMM0/XMM1,
  nothing above) and for the SSE registers (all caller-saved), the LIR
  meaning of `I128` constants and the split of a 16-byte incoming access,
  the Intel SDM semantics of `adc`, `sbb`, the one-operand shifts by CL and
  the SSE moves (and register allocation's pure definition of a `movss`
  destination), that a float `Bitcast` keeps the bits, and the constant
  folding that decides a CL count. Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-03-darwin-x86-64-census-slice11/`): measured first
  on the slice-10 census, the slice-11 classes are 60 roots first refused
  for an `i128` parameter, 15 for an `i128` result, 20 for a float
  parameter and 18 for a float result; in their bodies the only machine
  rows outside slice 10's lane are `adc`, `sbb`, the tied shifts and the
  SSE moves, and the float bodies that compute are the OD-73 class. 36
  fixture shapes over real adapter and selector output: 35 certify on the
  qualification host with AY build 10530, and `u128::wrapping_mul` is a
  recorded gap (AY times out at 30 s); with build 12713 34 certified and

  The qualification's outcomes are recorded per host triple, each compared
  only under that host's own pair, measured there; a host with no recorded
  pair refuses (DR-PER-HOST-QUALIFIED-PAIR-20261015). Every lane that
  reads that record checks the pair before it compares with it (since
  2026-10-17; before, slice 1's lane and every credit lane compared under
  any pair), and the compiler holds it to that: the record is private to
  the check's module, and every reader a lane can call takes the check's
  witness. The per-slice tables of recorded gaps and encodings are not
  gated that way; each lane compares with them after its check. Since
  2026-10-17 a lane that finds no AY or no checker fails, naming what is
  missing and how to provide it; before, each of the 40 tool-gated lanes
  printed a `SKIP` line and libtest counted it as passed. Since 2026-10-18
  the checker must be the one the build's proof authority accepts: under a

  accepted proof had still passed. The witness also refuses a lane the
  qualification command's filter (`--lib _qualification`) does not select,
  so such a lane fails wherever it runs (slice 1's and slice 4's credit
  lanes were outside the filter), and the command checks that it ran the
  record's 36 lanes and the explicit one.

  Slice 12 admits loops. A source with back edges is admitted when its CFG
  is reducible (every back edge's target, a loop header, dominates its
  source) and no loop is headed by the entry block; an irreducible cycle
  stays a named refusal. The theorem is translation validation by
  simulation over cut points, the entry block and the loop headers. Each
  region (the blocks a run reaches from a cut point before it reaches one
  again, a DAG) is stated with slice 9's machinery from its cut point's
  assumption, and on every cut edge into a header the theorem states,
  under the edge's guard, the cut-point relation: each header parameter
  (a loop-carried value, defined by the adapter's copies before the `Jump`
  into the header, run in order) equals the low bits of its machine
  register, and each private byte the loop may change (some edge into the
  header leaves it other than the entry edge does) equals the machine's
  byte. The register is the one the machine's copy of the parameter on the
  header's single entry edge writes (named by that row's TV-1 stamp: a
  pairing the theorem checks, never assumes); the relation states the
  parameter's own bits, a `bool` as the clean 32-bit carrier under the
  clean-bool walk and as its byte under the psABI walk, where a `bool`
  argument's register holds the caller's bits 8 and up; a register every
  edge into the header leaves zero above the parameter (judged from the
  term's shape) holds exactly the zero-extended parameter there, a greatest
  fixpoint checked on every edge. At a region's start
  both sides share one free input per parameter and per such byte; every
  other value, register and byte the region assumes is what the entry edge
  brought, and is checked unchanged on every edge into the header (a source
  value is defined once; a machine register some edge changes and no
  parameter pairs is unreadable, so the machine's loop-carried registers
  are exactly the source's parameters; a private byte only the machine's
  loop changes makes no claim). The assumptions are a fixpoint over every
  edge into each header. A slot that escaped on some edge into a header,
  or on some path into a join, is escaped after it: every later call
  observes its bytes and redefines them, the same on both sides, an
  over-approximation of what a callee may touch that only adds claims.
  The claim (OD-84 in `docs/decision-record.md`): for every run,
  terminating or not, the machine runs the paired path of each region
  instance with an equal world trace and ends the same way, and a source
  run that never ends (trust-ir defines it, an outcome of its
  `behaviour_refines`) is matched by a machine run that never ends with the
  same trace. By induction over a run's region instances: the relation
  holds at an instance's start, so the instance is an instance of the
  theorem's free inputs and its claims hold of it. Outside, by name: a
  header entered from more than one edge outside its loop, an `I128` header
  parameter or one an edge gives a private stack address, a byte a loop
  changes that holds a stored private address (slice 13's addresses are
  tracked, never assumed: as at a join; slice 17 leaves such a byte out
  when it is dead at the header), a machine edge into a header with
  an outgoing argument area open, and a fixpoint of more than 64 rounds.
  A header's escaped slots are closed under the addresses its slots hold
  (slice 13's transitive rule). Trusted for slice 12, in addition: the natural-loop
  analysis and the regions, the meaning of the edge copies, the checks that
  what a region assumes is unchanged on every edge into its header (term for
  term), that a run between two visits of a header runs only its loop's
  blocks, and the escape over-approximation. Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-05-darwin-x86-64-census-slice12/`): measured first
  on the slice-9 census, 161 failed roots (163 functions) stop first at a
  loop; every one of the 163 is reducible, 144 have one loop and 7 nest,
  and 179 of their 196 loops call a function and 179 access a private slot
  (52 keep every loop-carried value in one). 19 fixture shapes over real
  adapter and selector output (counting, accumulating, swapping, `bool`
  and `u8` carried values, a call, a load and a store per iteration, a
  slot counter, nested and sequential loops, an early exit, a `Switch` in
  the loop, a do-while, an escaping iterator slot, a trap in the loop, a
  slot-held bound and a `bool` passed to a call each iteration): 18 certify
  on the qualification host (AY build 12713),
  and the early exit was the recorded gap: its body multiplies by 3, which
  the selector computes with a scaled `lea` (the multiply class, not the
  loop), and it timed out at 30 s (it certified with 200 s); on build 10530
  it and the store loop kept one unproved step in AY's certificate. Since
  slice 18's folded spelling (OD-188) it certifies in 4.6 s and slice 12
  records no gap (`KNOWN_UNCERTIFIED_SLICE_TWELVE`).
  AY refutes 20 wrong lowerings with counterexamples (loop-carried
  registers swapped on a back edge, a back edge carrying the old value, a
  stale value carried, a cycle of copies run in place, a missing first
  iteration, an extra one, the exit taken on the wrong condition, a wrong
  increment or step, a counter not advanced, an inner loop started wrong or
  not carrying its sum in, a wrong call argument, the next element loaded,
  a slot counter advanced wrongly, a slot read after the loop as its value
  before it, an early exit returning the bound, an inverted bounds check,
  an `or` for the `xor` of a carried `bool`); the solver-free library gate
  (`x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice12::`, golden digest
  `slice12_snapshots.smt2`) holds every control; each of 19 rules
  disabled alone fails a control (`fails-before/`); and a mutation probe
  (`robustness/`) of 3337 mutants of 75 streams (O0 and the optimizer's
  O1-O3 output), judged against an independent concrete interpreter that
  runs the loops, credits no wrong stream (2251 wrong: 1434 no claim, 174
  named, 643 refuted; 69 the interpreter cannot decide within its bounds,
  none of which holds), and with the AY replay (before the merges) AY
  refutes none the sampler misses and certifies only result-preserving
  rewrites. The 16 correct
  mutants it refutes take another path to the same result (most swap the
  registers of two carried values that start equal, which the stamped
  pairing refutes by design). On the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census
  (O0, AY build 12713, merged onto main `f6dcad152`), failed roots go from
  447 to 373: 74 promoted (73 of them loops whose bodies now replay Valid),
  none newly failing, no named mismatch and no refuted body. Of the 170
  loop functions the baseline refused, 75 replay Valid, 5 are bound without
  a checked proof, and 90 stop at another refusal: 31 over 512 machine rows,
  29 a private stack address offset by a non-constant amount, 13 a division
  or its guard, 8 over 1024 LIR instructions, 6 an `I128` loop-carried value
  and 3 others ([census record](reports/perf/2026-10-05-darwin-x86-64-census-slice12/README.md)).

  Slice 13 admits more of the memory and value domain. A private slot's
  address may be stored as data, by an 8-byte store of the pointer: its
  value is one free 64-bit input per slot, `slot{x}`, plus the offset, on
  both sides (the slot binding by index makes it the same slot; nothing is
  assumed about it, and it is only ever data: the walks still decide which
  bytes a private access touches, without the solver). Stored to incoming
  memory, the slot escapes at the store (slice 7's model from there on:
  every later call reads and redefines its bytes, and the retention rule
  refuses an incoming access through an address that may derive from it,
  which slice 15 admits with the escaped slots observed);
  stored into a slot that escaped already, likewise; stored into one that
  has not, it stays private until that slot escapes, which takes along
  every slot whose address it holds, transitively. A DAG join takes the
  union of its edges' escaped slots (slice 9 refused a join of different
  escapes). Read back whole by an 8-byte load it is the address again (an
  access through it is private); any other read of its bytes, an aggregate
  argument or result holding one, and a join of paths that leave different
  bytes where one holds an address are outside the domain. At every call
  the slots the machine lets escape must be the source's, else no claim.
  An `I8`/`I16`/`I32`/`I64` parameter past the six argument registers is
  the low bits of its eightbyte of the incoming argument area, a free input
  `e_stack{16 + 8k}`, which the pre-RA stream reads as `[rbp + 16 + 8k]`
  (the frame the post-allocation prologue builds; any other access through
  RBP makes no claim). An argument of those types or a private address past
  the argument registers is observed at its return bits as the bytes the
  outgoing argument area holds at its eightbyte when the call runs (`sub
  rsp, n`, stores to `[rsp + 8k]`, the call, `add rsp, n`): an unwritten
  byte is a named undefined read, a return with the area open is a named
  write of RSP, and any other RSP adjustment or access makes no claim. LIR
  `Memcpy`, `Memmove` and `Memset` are calls to `memcpy`, `memmove` and
  `memset` by symbol under the slice-3/7 call model (an uninterpreted
  callee on both sides, observed at the routine's C signature; a private
  address operand escapes to it), so nothing about what they copy is
  assumed. A `bool` load of a private byte another integer store wrote is
  trust-ir's `byte != 0`. Scalar atomic loads (any load ordering) and
  `Relaxed` or `Release` stores of incoming memory are their plain-memory
  counterparts, a single-threaded claim (ruling OD-83 in
  `docs/decision-record.md`): each pairs only with one machine access of
  its width carrying the selector's atomic origin, and a plain access never
  with such a row. That the x86 `mov` gives each ordering its inter-thread
  meaning under x86-TSO is the hardware's and the selector's, not this
  theorem's. Refused by name: a sequentially consistent `AtomicStore` (the
  selector now lowers it to `mov; mfence`, the C++11 x86 mapping, and the
  body lane does not model the `mfence` row; until 2026-10-05 it was a
  plain `mov`, which x86-TSO may reorder with a later load; the rustc bridge
  emits such a store as an exchange instead),
  read-modify-write, compare-exchange, fences, `I128` atomics, an atomic
  access of a private slot, and a `bool`, float or aggregate parameter or
  argument on the stack (slice 15 admits an `I128` there). Trusted for
  slice 13, in addition:
  that the frame puts the `k`-th incoming stack eightbyte at `[rbp + 16 +
  8k]` and the callee reads its `k`-th stack argument at `[rsp + 8k]` when
  the call runs (the verify-owned placement is swept against the
  selector's formal-argument bindings); that `memcpy`, `memmove` and
  `memset` are the C runtime's routines (OD-217, the guard of OD-210 and
  OD-216: a theorem whose function under proof is the routine, or whose
  module or crate defines it, is refused; a definition in another crate of
  the link stays trusted); trust-ir's single-threaded meaning
  of the admitted atomics; and the transitive escape rule. Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-05-darwin-x86-64-census-slice13/`): measured
  first on the `main` `6b108b81d` census (1095 failed roots), the slice-13
  classes are 49 roots first refused for a stored private address, 35 for
  a join of different escapes, 26 for more than six register parameters,
  11 for more than six register arguments, 14 for an atomic access (all
  `atomic_load`/`atomic_store`, which dispatch on the ordering through a
  jump table, outside this slice), 5 for `Memcpy`/`Memset` and 4 for a
  `bool` read of another store's byte; every stored address of the class
  goes into another private slot that a call then receives. 20 fixture
  shapes over real adapter and selector output all certify on the
  qualification host, and AY refutes 15 wrong lowerings with
  counterexamples (another stored offset; two slots' addresses swapped; a
  value kept in a register across a call its slot escaped to; a narrow read
  through a reloaded address; swapped or widened stack eightbytes; another
  stack argument; swapped `memcpy` operands; a copied word read at another
  offset; an atomic load from another address; an atomic or private `bool`
  byte returned raw; the pointer stored for the value); the solver-free
  library gate (`x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice13::`, golden digest
  `slice13_snapshots.smt2`) holds every control; each of 19 rules disabled
  alone fails a control (`fails-before/`); the real optimizer's O1-O3
  output builds theorems that hold and no false mismatch; the end-to-end
  proof-required compile promotes five slice-13 functions Formal on Darwin
  and Linux; and a mutation probe (`robustness/`) of 1111 streams (24
  base streams and their mutants), judged against an independent concrete interpreter that
  models escape by reachability, credits no wrong stream (849 wrong: 116
  no claim, 609 named, 124 refuted, and AY refutes none the sampler
  misses). Building the probe found a credit hole, fixed before landing: a
  return with the outgoing argument area still open (RSP not restored)
  built a theorem that held. The Darwin `core`
  O0 census on AY build 12713 (the lane's qualification AY since the same
  day; slice 13 certifies every fixture on it too) has 493 failed roots on
  the slice-13 bridge against 573 for the requalification's row of `main`
  `6b108b81d`: 80 promote (a stored private address 41, a join of
  different escapes 14, parameters on the stack 10, arguments on the stack
  9, `Memcpy`/`Memset` 5, a `bool` read 1), none newly fails, no mismatch
  is named and no bound body is refuted. Of the 144 class functions, 89
  are bound (80 certify; 9 do not, replayed offline: 7 run out the
  resident route's 30 s deadline, 1 is a strict self-check rejection and 1
  a proof AY cannot render, none satisfiable) and 55 stop at later
  refusals (14 atomics, 11 of them at the ordering's jump table; 12 machine
  bodies over 512 rows; 7 LIR bodies over 1024 instructions; 4 stack
  parameters other than integers; 4 forwarded `bool` arguments; 4 the
  retention rule; 3 loops; 7 others).

  Slice 15 closes the value, call and observable refusals that a real
  proof can close. LIR `Fconst` is trust-ir's `float_bits_from_f64`
  (`imm.to_bits()` at `F64`, `(imm as f32).to_bits()` at `F32`; an `F32`
  NaN constant stays outside by name, since Rust leaves its narrowed
  payload unspecified), and `Fneg`/`Fabs` are trust-ir's `-x` and
  `x.abs()`, IEEE 754's sign-bit `negate` and `abs` (ruling OD-112 in
  `docs/decision-record.md`): exact bit operations, which the lane's
  bit-pattern model of floats (OD-73) states in `QF_BV`. The selector's
  constant-pool `movss`/`movsd` loads (exactly the entry's bytes, the rest
  of the register zeroed) and three-operand `pxor`/`andps`/`andpd` are
  modelled; every other floating-point operation stays outside (until
  slice 21's rounding events, below). A `mov` or
  ALU row of mixed 32- and 64-bit registers (encoded with REX.W) defines
  the low 32 bits of its operation and leaves the bits above a free input.
  A function that takes a `bool` may pass one: the argument is observed as
  the clean 32-bit bool under every caller view, and the x86 selector now
  defines a System V `bool` register parameter as `movzx` of the
  register's low byte, because a psABI caller defines only bits 0..7 of it
  (ruling OD-113; it copied the 32-bit register before, which forwarded a
  psABI caller's bits 8..31 to the callee). A load or store through an
  address that may derive from an escaped slot (refused by slice 7's
  retention rule until now) observes every escaped slot's bytes at the
  access, and a store leaves them as fresh inputs on both sides, as a call
  does (ruling OD-114); the machine must let exactly the source's slots
  escape by then. An `I128` parameter or argument without two registers
  left takes two eightbytes of the stack argument areas, the first 16-byte
  aligned, and a later scalar still takes a register left over. A body
  with no result, no call and no incoming-memory access stays outside
  (ruling OD-115): every effect it has on its caller is checked by the
  trusted walk, and an observable stating them would be an identity on
  both sides. Still outside: floating-point arithmetic, compares and
  conversions; aggregates over 16 bytes by value; a private address offset
  by a non-constant amount (slice 17, below, admits one used by a load, a
  store or a call argument); more than 64 stack slots. Trusted for slice 15,
  in addition: that a constant-pool entry is emitted read-only, with its
  bytes, at the address its RIP-relative load resolves to (the encoder's
  and linker's, as for a symbol); the encoder's REX.W rule for mixed rows;
  and the derived-access congruence (an address that may derive from an
  escaped slot reaches only incoming memory and the escaped slots, the
  provenance rule behind the retention rule). Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-06-darwin-x86-64-census-slice15/`): measured first on the slice-13 census row (493 failed roots), the
  slice-15 classes are 12 roots first refused for a forwarded `bool`, 15
  for an access through a derived address, 8 for a float constant, 4 for
  `Fneg`/`Fabs`, 6 for a mixed-width row and 5 for an `I128` on the stack
  (14 more have no observable and stay refused). 22 fixture shapes over
  real adapter and selector output all certify on the qualification host,
  and AY refutes 14 wrong lowerings with counterexamples (another constant
  or NaN payload, a sign mask of another bit, `xor` and `and` swapped, a
  dropped `abs`, an aggregate byte dropped, the `bool` register forwarded
  raw, a slot written behind a derived load, a value kept across a derived
  store, another derived offset, swapped `I128` stack eightbytes or
  halves); the solver-free library gate
  (`x86_source_bound_body::tests::slice15::`, golden digest
  `slice15_snapshots.smt2`) holds every control; each of 14 rules disabled
  alone (13 of the owner's and the selector's entry `movzx`) fails a
  control (`fails-before/`); the real optimizer's O1-O3 output builds
  theorems that hold and no false mismatch; the end-to-end proof-required
  compile promotes the six slice-15 functions Formal on Darwin and Linux
  (with slice 9's three functions left out of the module: beside a census,
  `dag_stores`, whose theorem is unchanged, misses the replay deadline);
  and a mutation probe (`robustness/`) of 1341 streams (24 base streams and
  their mutants), judged against an independent concrete interpreter,
  credits no wrong stream (969 wrong: 144 no claim, 408 named, 417 refuted,
  and AY refutes none the sampler misses). The Darwin `core` O0 census on
  AY build 12713 has 466 failed roots on the slice-15 bridge against 499
  for `main` `cf982f936`: 29 promote in the slice-15 classes (a forwarded
  `bool` 12, a derived access 5, `Fneg`/`Fabs` 4, a float constant 4, an
  `I128` on the stack 3, a mixed-width row 1) and 4 more are the baseline
  run's replay noise; none newly fails, no mismatch is named and no bound
  body is refuted. Of the 50 class functions, 38 are bound (29 certify; 9
  do not, replayed offline: 4 certify off the loaded host, 2 are AY
  certification rejections and 3 run out the resident deadline, none
  satisfiable) and 12 stop at later refusals (more than 512 machine rows
  3, the machine-function refusal 3, a join of different slot values one of
  which is an address 2, an `Fcmp` 2, a `Udiv` 1, unmatched blocks 1).

  Slice 14 admits definedness and dispatch (rulings OD-178..OD-181 in
  `docs/decision-record.md`). LIR `Udiv`, `Urem`, `Sdiv` and `Srem` of an
  `I8`/`I16`/`I32`/`I64` are trust-ir's `eval_int_binop` (pin `cf33f748`):
  the unsigned or truncating signed quotient and remainder, undefined
  behaviour at a zero divisor and, signed, at the minimum divided by -1 (for
  `Srem` too). The undefined case is a per-path domain premise: each point of
  a run (every event, every block end) has a stop term, 1 once an executed
  division on the way there was undefined (0 at the entry and at each loop
  header; at a DAG join the incoming edges' terms joined by their guards, so
  a division on an untaken path adds nothing), and every claim there is
  waived where it is 1. Claims before the undefined division keep their
  force, which is more than trust-ir's `behaviour_refines` asks (it
  constrains nothing of a run with undefined behaviour). The machine's
  `div`/`idiv` is Intel's (the double-width dividend, quotient to RAX,
  remainder to RDX, every status flag undefined) and #DE stops it when the
  divisor is zero or the quotient does not fit: wherever the source has not
  stopped, the theorem requires the machine not to have stopped either, so
  a fault on a defined input is refuted. The dividend is exact for any high
  half (stated at double width, and at the width when the high half is the
  selector's `xor edx, edx` or `cqo`/`cdq`). A canonical machine
  division's value is restated as the source division's where their
  operands are equal, and a signed division states its divisor's unit
  cases first, and an unsigned division by a constant power of two (and
  the selector's magic multiply by one) is stated as the shift it is:
  exact spellings that keep the query within the solver's reach. A
  division by any other constant, through the magic-number multiply, is
  past the qualified AY (recorded gaps `UdivConst`, `UremConst32`). A division by a constant
  other than 0 (signed, other than -1) is defined for every dividend and
  adds no stop. The divide-by-zero guard
  (`GuardDivZero`, which the adapter emits before a division annotated
  `DivNonZero`) is a defined trap and an observable, never a premise: where
  it fires, the machine's first stop before the next event must be its
  `TrapDivZeroExact` carrier, which the pipeline expands after this
  theorem's subject to `test d, d; je -> ud2` (a #DE in its place, a dropped
  or misplaced carrier, is refuted); a guard bound to a discharged
  obligation stays outside. A `Switch` several of whose cases (or a case and
  its default) reach one block is one source edge whose test is their
  disjunction (the adapter gives a case with block arguments its own copy
  block, so such cases pass none), stated against the disjunction of the
  machine's routes to the block (each `je`, the default's `jmp`); a
  several-path source with such a switch or a division is stated over its
  DAG. The selector's jump-table dispatch (`ja default; jmp d; d: lea b,
  [rip + table]; mov e, [b + n*8]; add e, b; jmp e`) is stated from the
  function's own pre-RA table: the indirect `jmp` reaches a target exactly
  when the index is one of its entries. (It refuted the selector's former
  dispatch of a 32-bit selector, a 64-bit `mov` of the selector's `Gpr32`
  vreg, whose bits above 31 the pre-RA stream does not define, into the
  index; the selector now zero-extends it, OD-181. Natively the former form
  returned the right values in both contexts measured: a hardening of the
  stream the theorem judges, not a fixed miscompile.) The machine-function refusal of
  slices 1-13 is now one refusal per cause (EH tables, guard obligations,
  an outgoing call area, a constant-pool entry other than slice 15's loads,
  a jump table outside the dispatch idiom). Trusted for slice 14, in
  addition: trust-ir's meaning of division as stated (a unit test checks it
  and its undefinedness against the pinned interpreter), the LIR meaning of
  `GuardDivZero`, the Intel SDM semantics of `div`, `idiv`, `cqo`, `cdq` and
  `xor r, r` (a unit test sweeps the double-width and simplified forms
  against a direct computation), the exactness of the division spellings
  (a signed division's unit-divisor cases and the power-of-two shifts,
  swept by unit tests against the stated division and Intel's `mul`; the
  pairing's restatement holds by construction, `pair_divisions`), the
  carrier's expansion (checked by its
  guard-carrier canary, outside this theorem), the stop bookkeeping that
  waives claims and orders a trap before a fault, the adapter's copy blocks
  behind a shared target, and the jump table's emission (the codegen writes
  it into the function's `.text` after the body, entry `i` the delta of
  `targets[i]` from the table, and patches the `lea` to it). OD-57's
  refinement of an out-of-range variable shift is unchanged. Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-09-darwin-x86-64-census-slice14/`): 28 fixtures
  over real selector output, of which 26 certify on AY build 12713 with
  Clean; the two divisions by a constant other than a power of two (the
  magic-number multiply) time out, also at 300 s, and are recorded gaps
  (`PENDING(solver-capacity)`, no credit); 24 wrong lowerings are refuted
  with AY counterexamples; each slice-14 rule disabled alone fails a
  control (22 mutants; the constant fold, a simplification, fails only the
  golden digest); the codegen end-to-end compile promotes slice 14's
  functions on both x86-64 triples. Of the 71 Darwin `core` functions
  first refused in these classes, 44 now build a theorem (the rest are
  `i128` divisions, bodies past the 512-row cap, an `i128` loop value or
  a switch search tree) and 35 of those certify offline; the others are
  the magic-number and 64-bit multiply classes. On the Darwin x86-64
  `core` proof census (O0, AY build 12713, on main `a902ea9ef`), failed
  roots go from 377 to 342: 35 promoted (17 jump tables, 8 `Udiv`, 6
  `GuardDivZero`, 2 `Urem`, 2 bodies now certifying), none newly failing,
  no named mismatch and no refuted body.

  Slice 16 states a function past the single-query bounds (more than 128
  LIR blocks, 1024 LIR instructions, 128 machine blocks or 512 machine
  rows; at most 1024 blocks and 8192 instructions and rows) as one theorem
  replayed in parts (ruling OD-182 in `docs/decision-record.md`); every
  function within the bounds keeps its theorem byte for byte (the golden
  digests of slices 1-15 are unchanged). Such a function is cut at its
  entry, at every loop header and at program points a deterministic plan
  chooses so that each region has at most 256 machine rows, 1024 LIR
