  instructions and 128 blocks, and the function at most 32 regions (a
  planned cut whose interface refuses is banned and the plan made again, at
  most four times): block
  starts, and instruction boundaries inside a block where its machine rows
  split cleanly by their TV-1 stamps (no transfer or open outgoing area
  before the split; no physical register or flag read after it before a
  write). A cut inside a block makes two blocks of it on both sides (the
  LIR jumps to a new block with the rest; the machine block falls through
  to a new block laid out right after it); the cut stream is checked to be
  the original's rows in the original order, each at its walk ordinal. At
  every cut point but the entry, every LIR value live there (and every
  parameter of the cut block) and every private byte some edge into it
  wrote and the cut does not leave dead (slice 17, below) is an item of
  the cut's interface, one free input both sides share, unless it is
  fixed for the run: an `Iconst`, a parameter of the function, a
  symbol's address, a private address, or a byte stored from such a
  constant or parameter, of an aggregate parameter's register or
  holding a stored private address, which is carried exactly and checked
  to be the same term on every edge into the cut. An item that is no
  `i128` and that no edge taints is no free input either when its source
  term on every edge into the cut, forward and back, resolves to one term
  over the run's fixed inputs (OD-233: entry registers and incoming stack
  eightbytes, parameter bindings, symbol addresses, frame bytes' initial
  values and `bool` caller views, no slot address; at most 64 nodes, with
  the statement's definitions and the other defined inputs inlined, after
  the parts' bit identities and exact fold): the theorem DEFINES it as that
  term and, on every edge into the cut, in that edge's part, under its
  guard and where the source runs, claims the item's source term equal to
  it (a claim that is no observable); a defined term that names anything
  else, or an edge that does not carry the claim, makes no claim (by name).
  On EVERY edge into a
  cut, under the edge's guard and where the source has not stopped, the
  theorem states each value item equal to the low bits of its machine
  register (the one the last row stamped with its definition writes; for a
  parameter of the cut block, its edge copy's) and each byte item equal to
  the machine's byte at the same frame address; the bits above a value are
  free unless every edge leaves them zero. Every other machine register
  starts as the term every edge leaves in it when that term is a function
  of the run's fixed inputs alone (an entry register, a symbol, a
  constant), else unreadable; the flags start unmodelled, no outgoing
  argument area may be open, and a slot the machine lets escape or a byte
  it writes where the source does not makes no claim. Each region's claims
  (its observed items, its edges' `jcc` literals and the relation on each
  of its cut edges) mention only its own definitions and the run's fixed
  inputs: each region with a claim is one PART, one AY query with its own
  30 s budget and one Clean check, over the cone of definitions its claims
  reach, value-numbered (a definition that renames a name, is a constant,
  or repeats an earlier definition's term after three exact bit-vector
  identities, is that term or name) and spelled as slice 9 spells a
  theorem; a region whose claims all become identities is no part, unless
  every region's do, when every region is stated without the
  substitutions. The function's theorem is the conjunction of its parts,
  equivalent to the single theorem with the same claims, and the claim is
  OD-84's, by the same induction over region instances. Its rows are
  credited only when every part replays Valid (serially, stopping at the
  first that does not; a refuted part fails every covered row), and the
  part inventory is re-derived from the statement and checked before any
  replay and before any export; the proof emitter publishes the parts,
  never the statement. Outside, by name: a value of type `i128` live
  across a cut, a value whose definition no row writes into a virtual
  register, two items in one register, a point that is no clean stamp
  boundary, a plan that cannot fit a region within the bounds, more than
  32 parts or 8192 machine rows, and a function whose every part states
  nothing (OD-115). Trusted for slice 16, in addition: the region
  construction over the cut points (every cycle passes a loop header), the
  cut of a block into two (checked stream identity, and the walk's
  fallthrough), one cut interface used for both the relation on every edge
  into a cut and the start of its region, the closed-term, escape and
  machine-byte checks at a cut (term for term), every register and byte
  outside the interface starting unreadable, the part inventory check, the
  value numbering, bit normalization and identity dropping of the parts'
  spelling (as slice 9's identity rule), and the meta-argument that the
  parts' conjunction is the one theorem (OD-233: with defined cut inputs,
  each supplied at a crossing by that crossing's claims), with OD-233's
  check that a defined term names only the run's fixed inputs, its check
  that every stated edge into a cut claims each defined input in each
  region that states the edge (a block two regions hold states its edge
  into a later cut once in each), and that each claim takes its edge's
  source term from OD-182's relation on that edge (a run's whole store
  read as the concatenation of its bytes, slice 7's reading). Not
  trusted: the pairing (the relation states it on every edge), the cut
  plan (any cut set with the loop headers is sound; a bad one refuses or
  refutes more), the liveness (a value left out is undefined after the
  cut, and a read of it refuses) and OD-233's choice of the inputs to
  define (a wrong term is refuted by its edge's claim). Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-14-darwin-x86-64-slice16-parts/`): five control
  shapes and five size shapes over real selector output, their parts
  certified on AY build 12713 with Clean except `LongChain`'s three (30 s
  and 300 s timeouts, recorded gaps: its machine spells the source's
  ninety steps step for step, so its theorem is stated plainly); ten of
  eleven wrong lowerings refuted with AY counterexamples (an inverted
  branch, never credited, timed out in the live replay's resident AY; since
  slice 18 spells each part again, OD-189, it is refuted in 0.7 s and all
  eleven are);
  each of 11 rule mutants fails a control; the cut-everywhere sweeps over
  the 368 fixtures of slices 1-15 name no mismatch. Of the 121
  size-refused functions of main's `core` census, 106 are stated in parts
  and 86 have every part certified offline within 30 s (496 of 563
  parts). On the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census (O0, AY build 12713,
  on main `2854ce3e3`), failed roots go from 813 to 763: 50 promoted (35
  past 512 machine rows, 11 past 1024 LIR instructions, 4 bodies now
  certifying), none newly failing, no named mismatch and no
  refuted body. That main's census is 813, not 342, because its bridge
  now spells array-element addresses as `ArrayGep`, which the lane did
  not admit before OD-185 (below).
  OD-233's evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-11-05-darwin-x86-64-od233-defined-cut-inputs/`):
  fixtures from real O2 output (O1 for the loops), the
  `core::wtf8::slice_error_fail` reduction among them, one over the
  merged-chain quotient, and slice 25's three slot fixtures hold on samples
  in parts with their inputs defined, where the reduction, three variants
  and the slot fixtures are refuted on samples in parts at slice 25's base;
  their parts replay `result=Verified` on AY build 13556 with Clean
  (35 parts); six wrong lowerings are refuted with AY counterexamples;
  ten free-input controls keep byte-identical statements, each candidate
  input still free; thirteen rule mutants each fail every control they
  name with its stated text; the cut-everywhere sweep (1102 statements)
  loses no region on samples, and every statement in it that defines
  nothing has the digest it has at slice 25's base; ten of slice 25's
  eleven `lea; mov [t]` decompositions refuted on samples hold on samples
  (ByteMerge's undemanded bits stay free, OD-233b), none replayed. A
  definition claim on an unguarded edge deepens the statement by one
  conjunct, and 14 swept statements are cut into a different number of
  parts, ten of them with the definition claims stated unsubstituted. On
  the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census (2026-11-07, AY build 13556) the
  O2 failed roots go from 254 to 253: `core::wtf8::slice_error_fail`,
  refuted in one part before, is stated in three parts and replays Valid,
  with no root newly failing, no named mismatch and no refuted body; at O0
  the 20 roots, the failed-root and refusal records and every emitted
  object are unchanged.

  OD-185 admits LIR `ArrayGep { elem_ty }` of `(base, index)` with the one
  meaning the selector gives it (rulings OD-185 and OD-186 in
  `docs/decision-record.md`): `base + index * size(elem_ty)` at 64 bits,
  wrapping, where `size` is the element's natural-C size under the
  verify-owned layout (a unit test sweeps it against the selector's
  `Type::bytes`) and the index is the `I64` value itself, unextended (the
  adapter extends a narrower trust-ir index with an explicit `Uextend` or
  `Sextend` before the opcode, which the lane models as such, and emits
  `ArrayGep` only where the natural-C stride is the authority, writing any
  other stride out as `Iadd`/`Imul`). An index of another type, an element
  type outside the layout model (an enum) and a zero-sized element are
  refused by name. Over an incoming pointer, a symbol, a call result or an
  address derived from an escaped slot (OD-114) the element address is
  that value, spelled as the machine's scaled `lea` is, and accesses
  through it are incoming or derived accesses as before. Over a private
  slot it is, at an `I64` index that is a constant `k` of the chain, the
  exact offset `k * size` (overflow refused), and at any other `I64` index
  slice 17's indexed address (below). The machine rows are the selector's:
  a scaled `lea` for a size of 1, 2, 4 or 8, a scaled `lea` and an `add` of
  the index for 3, 5 or 9, and an `imul` by the size and an `add`
  otherwise; a scaled `lea` of a private address at an index the walk
  knows as a 64-bit constant is that exact offset (at any other index,
  slice 17's indexed address), a 64-bit `imul` of a known constant by an
  immediate is a constant, and a scaled `lea` at a constant index has an
  exact affine value. OD-186: a slot's own address (`StackAddr`) the LIR
  types as a by-value aggregate, the adapter's copy of an aggregate `Load`
  into a fresh slot, is that aggregate when returned or passed by value, as
  slice 8's `Copy` of a slot address so typed already was (the selector
  types the address at its hint); an element or field address typed as an
  aggregate stays refused, since the selector passes it as a pointer.
  Every earlier golden digest is unchanged. Trusted in addition: the LIR
  meaning of `ArrayGep` above (the adapter's choice of the opcode and its
  explicit index extension), the verify-owned stride, and that the
  selector types a `StackAddr` at its hint. Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-15-darwin-x86-64-arraygep/`): eighteen fixtures
  over real selector output, all certified on AY build 12713 with Clean;
  seventeen wrong lowerings (an index scaled by the wrong element size, the
  wrong base, a missing and a wrong index extension, an off-by-one element,
  a load or store of the wrong element, and three of the OD-186 copy)
  refuted with AY counterexamples; sixteen rule mutants each failing a
  control. Of the 476 functions census-s14 credited and main's census
  (`2854ce3e3`) did not (354 stopped at `ArrayGep`, 109 at the `StackAddr`
  type hint, 13 otherwise), the probe on a fresh dump of main's bridge
  builds a theorem for all 476, each holding on samples, and 469 certify
  offline within 30 s (7 time out: 3 are past 512 rows and replayed in parts
  by the census); the 2633 functions census-s16 credits all still build
  one, and no function is named a mismatch. On the Darwin x86-64 `core`
  proof census (O0, AY build 12713, on main `cb390e657`), failed roots go
  from 743 to 235: 508 promoted (394 refused at `ArrayGep`, 112 at an
  inconsistent type hint, 2 at a machine row of its lowering), none newly
  failing, no named mismatch and no refuted body.

  Slice 17 admits a private stack access at a non-constant offset (ruling
  OD-183 in `docs/decision-record.md`): an `Iadd` of a private slot's
  address and an `I64` index that is no constant, and an `ArrayGep` of one
  at such an index (OD-185's element size `s` the stride), is an indexed
  address with the 64-bit offset term `o = c + d * s` (`s = 1` for
  `Iadd`; spelled as OD-185 spells the product), used only as a scalar
  load's or store's address or a direct call's argument (anything else, a
  second non-constant offset, or a C memory routine on it refuses by
  name). An access of `w` bytes into a slot of `n` bytes has the candidate
  offsets `k <= n - w` congruent to `c` modulo the power of two the
  variable part `d * s` is a multiple of (from `d`'s constant stride and
  `s`; at most 256 per access and 1024 per function, since slice 20 1024
  and 4096). A load reads a select over the candidates of what a load at
  each constant offset reads (each candidate's bytes judged by the
  constant-offset rules: a stored private address, a dead byte or an
  unreadable `bool` among them refuses): the low-bit select, a balanced
  `ite` tree on the offset's bits above the stride's power of two, which
  are the candidate's index where the offset is one; a store updates each
  byte a candidate covers by an `ite` chain over the candidates covering
  it, a new private byte joined and carried like any other; a call
  argument is observed as `slot{s} + o` on both sides and the machine must
  pass an address of the same slot. The machine's offset is whatever its own rows compute (`add` of a frame register and a
  value, `lea` with a scaled index, constant offsets of either), a term,
  never matched against the source's; its candidates are those of the
  source access its row's TV-1 stamp names, else every offset in the slot.
  The claim is OD-84's and: on every run on which the source is defined,
  every indexed access the source performs, and every one the machine
  performs before the source stops, lies inside its slot at a candidate
  offset; each side states it for its own offset (`bvule o (n - w)` and the
  congruence), as a claim AY proves, never a premise (trust-ir's
  `IntToPtr` resolves provenance by address and LIR lowers a GEP and
  integer pointer arithmetic alike, so a premise could waive a defined
  run). By induction over a run, the first access off its candidates would
  meet every earlier term exact and falsify its own claim, so a Valid
  theorem makes every select and update the memory. Admission needs a bound
  the access's own region holds (a dominating guard on the index, or the
  index's own range); it decides admission only (an unbounded index refuses
  by name), and a slice-16 plan never cuts between a guard and its access.
  With it (ruling OD-184), a private byte that no path from a cut point (a
  slice-12 loop header or a slice-16 cut) reads before a store overwrites
  it, by one backward byte liveness that counts every load, indexed access,
  call, C memory routine, untracked access and other address use as a read,
  is left out of that cut's relation on both sides and starts unreadable
  (a source read refuses, a machine read makes no claim): no observable can
  depend on it. Every body without an indexed access keeps its theorem byte
  for byte unless a byte is dead at one of its cut points (one slice-12
  fixture, `ByteBoolCarried`, whose header byte is overwritten before every
  read). Trusted for slice 17, in addition: the slot of an indexed address
  from its frame base, the candidate set and the one select/update spelling
  both walks call (unit-swept against a concrete byte array for every slot
  to 64 bytes and of 100, 128, 255 and 256 bytes, width 0 to 8, modulus to
  16 and residue), the per-candidate byte metadata (the constant-offset
  rules applied per candidate), the machine walk's indexed register, the
  same-slot check of an indexed argument, and, for a theorem with an
  in-bounds claim, slice 16's part spelling (as for parts) after the
  substitution of every definition that only moves bits of variables
  (unit-swept against evaluation), and the stride's offset spelling and
  modulus (unit-swept). Not trusted: the bound finder and the byte
  liveness (each only refuses). Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-15-darwin-x86-64-slice17-indexed/`): 20
  fixtures (four of them `ArrayGep`s of strides 8, 3 and 12 and a store)
  and two machine variants over real selector output, every one certified
  on AY build 12713 with Clean, selects of up to 256 arms among them; 17
  wrong lowerings refuted with AY counterexamples, three of them (out of
  bounds on the source only, a machine access past its slot, a misaligned
  machine read) by one in-bounds claim alone; each of 15 rule mutants
  fails a control; no wrong stream credited among 254 robustness mutants
  (before the `ArrayGep` merge). The load's select is the low-bit select,
  and a theorem with an in-bounds claim is value-numbered as one slice-16
  part after its bit-moving definitions are substituted, each chosen by
  host qualification (AY rejects its proof of a 256-arm linear chain,
  multiplies a constant stride behind a definition name out as a variable
  product, and keeps a stored value's byte claims alive when the two sides
  name the value differently). Of the design's 51 `core` functions, 43
  build a theorem and 39 certify offline within 30 s, on main a902's dump
  and on main 2854ce's after the `ArrayGep` merge (where
  `parse_decimal_seq` stops at the candidate cap); no `ArrayGep` of that
  dump has a variable index over a private slot. Slices 12 and 16
  re-qualify with the dead-byte rule, whose 327 changed queries over the
  crate lose no certification. On the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census
  (O0, AY build 12713, on main `6191f3621`), failed roots go from 232 to
  191: 41 promoted (39 refused at a non-constant private stack offset, 1
  at a cut entered with different stored slot addresses, 1 bound body now
  certifying), none newly failing, no named mismatch and no refuted body.
  Outside, by name: a second non-constant
  offset, an indexed address stored, returned, compared, joined to a
  different address or carried by a cut, a C memory routine on one, more
  than 256 candidates per access or 1024 per function, an index no fact
  of its region bounds, and, on the machine, a memory operand with a
  scaled index over a frame register (O1 and above; slice 25 states it,
  below).

  Slice 18 (ruling OD-187 in `docs/decision-record.md`) makes slice 17's
  value-numbered spelling canonical for every single-query theorem whose
  source side is `true`, whether or not it states an in-bounds claim: the
  definitions that only move bits are substituted, the rest value-numbered
  and inlined, every claim that becomes an identity dropped. The cascade is
  fixed in advance: a theorem whose claims would all drop, or whose spelling
  fails the structural check, takes slice 16's part spelling (no bit
  moves), and only if that also empties or fails keeps the plain spelling
  (never stated by identities alone). A spelled theorem is checked as a part
  is: one claim suffices. A one-path theorem `(= S M)` and every part keep
  their bytes. Trusted for slice 18, in addition: nothing new in kind; the
  domain of OD-182's and OD-183's spelling grows to every conjunctive
  single-query theorem, swept against an exact evaluator over every fixture
  and every wrong-lowering family (`slice18::`). Of the 386 golden fixture
  theorems, 184 change (163 in slice 17's spelling, 21 through slice 16's,
  57 of them left with one claim), 74 conjunctive ones keep the plain
  spelling and the 128 one-path ones keep theirs; every changed theorem is
  proved equivalent to its old one by z3 in both directions and a 256-input
  evaluation sweep, and a test-only legacy spelling re-renders every old
  golden byte for byte. On census-s17's 91 bound but uncertified single
  theorems, re-dumped through the builder, AY build 12713 with Clean
  certifies 52 within 30 s one-shot and 51 by the resident route (none
  before); `is_power_of_two`, a one-path theorem, keeps its spelling and
  Clean's 30 s overrun.
  Every slice's AY 12713 qualification ledger was re-run one test per
  process on the Darwin x86-64 pair: nine recorded gaps certify now (seven
  slice-9 DAG fixtures, slice 10's `MulPanics`, slice 11's `SlotU128`), none
  joins, and every wrong lowering stays refuted with a counterexample (slice
  16's inverted branch stays the recorded unrefuted part until OD-189,
  below). The other hosts' records (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`,
  `aarch64-apple-darwin`) were measured on the spelling before slice 18 and
  are re-qualified only by a run on their own host. The cascade's first step (ruling OD-188) folds every
  right-hand side and claim first: an operator whose operands are all
  constants is its value (each operator written from its SMT-LIB
  definition, division by zero included, never an `ite` or a Boolean
  connective) and `(= (bvsub x y) 0)` is `(= x y)`; trusted in addition,
  unit-swept against the exact evaluator over every operator at widths 1 to
  128 and over 4000 random terms. Ruling OD-235 adds one more pair, also
  trusted: an unsigned division or remainder by a constant power of two
  `2^k` is its shift by `k` or its mask `2^k - 1` (unit-swept at ten widths
  from 1 to 128 against the same evaluator; no golden moves), since a
  divisor OD-233 makes constant would otherwise reach the solver as a
  division circuit. OD-188's fold moves 104 golden theorems again (z3 in
  both directions and the sweep: equivalent), takes census-s17's single
  theorems from 52 to 64 certified one-shot (63 by the resident route, at
  load 6; a twelve-copy query that takes 24-30 s makes it 72 on a quieter
  run) and slice 12's early exit from a recorded gap to 4.6 s. Each
  slice-16 part is then spelled a second time as slice 17 spells a theorem
  (ruling OD-189: the bit moves substituted, value numbering, inlining and
  identity dropping over the part slice 16 spells; a part that empties is no
  part, one that fails the part check keeps its first spelling): nothing new
  in kind is trusted, and the part inventory check re-derives the parts the
  same way. 9 of census-s17's 34 bound but uncertified bodies stated in
  parts then have every part certified on AY build 12713 (none before); of
  the goldens, only the one pinning the slice-16 size shapes' parts (added
  with OD-188) moves, 4 of its 13 parts, each proved equivalent. On the
  Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census (O0, AY build 12713, on main
  `4a65bc3cf`), failed roots go from 187 to 114: 78 promoted (bound
  bodies that now certify), 5 newly failing, no named mismatch and no
  refuted body. The 5 are AY timeouts of re-spelled theorems, never a
  credit: `i128::wrapping_sub` (the `SubU128` shape) times out at 120 s on
  build 12713 and certifies in 1.9 s on build 13556; a part of
  `TypeId::as_u128` needs 37 s on 12713 and 25 s on 13556; a part of
  `Big32x40::clone` certifies offline in 0.45 s, a load timeout the
  negative memo repeated; two `EscapeDebug` chain functions were not
  replayed offline.

  Slice 20 (rulings OD-191 to OD-194 in `docs/decision-record.md`) admits
  the domain refusals of the Darwin x86-64 `core` census (census-ay13556)
  that need no new trust; `I128` division (slice 20a) stays outside, by
  name. A `Switch` the selector lowers as a balanced binary search (five or
  more distinct cases in `[0, i32::MAX]` and no jump table) is admitted with
  its search blocks (OD-191): a block of `cmp r, imm` and `jcc` rows ended
  by a `jmp`, every row stamped with that `Switch` and reached only from the
  switch's other machine blocks, lowers no LIR block of its own; a route to
  a target runs through the tree, every compare and branch walked with its
  Intel SDM meaning, so the solver judges the search, and a source whose
  switch the selector may search is stated over its DAG. A private byte a
  DAG join's paths leave holding different values, one of them a stored
  private address, is left out on both sides when no path from the join
  reads it before a store overwrites it (OD-192, OD-184's liveness at
  joins): unreadable after the join, so a read refuses. An `I128`
  loop-header parameter or slice-16 cut item is two free 64-bit inputs, its
  halves (OD-193), paired with the two 64-bit registers its copy's or
  definition's rows leave as their result, the lower virtual register the
  low half, both halves related on every edge. And (OD-194) a variable
  `I128` shift whose amount its own definition bounds below 128 is slice
  10's shift modulo 128 (an unbounded one refuses by name); a byte any store
  wrote is `bool`-readable past a join, loop header, cut or indexed store as
  a direct read takes it (`byte != 0`); undefined bits a machine row outside
  every loop introduces are a closed leaf at a cut, one per row for the run;
  private slots are bounded by their bytes in all (262,144) instead of their
  count (64); and an indexed access may have 1024 candidate offsets (4096
  per function). Trusted for slice 20, in addition: nothing. Not trusted:
  the search-block recognizer, the register pairing, the join liveness and
  the shift bound finder (each only chooses what the theorem then judges, or
  refuses). Evidence (`reports/perf/2026-10-26-darwin-x86-64-slice20-rules/`):
  19 fixtures over real selector output and 8 variants; 20 wrong lowerings
  (among them a wrong pivot, an `I128`'s halves swapped across a cut and on
  a back edge, a dead temporary's target holding another value) refuted
  with AY counterexamples; 22 rule mutants, each failing a control; every
  earlier golden theorem unchanged. On the qualification pair (AY build
  13556 with Clean 5f09e36c) 25 of the 30 fixture theorems and parts
  certify; the three variable `I128` shifts need about the whole 30 s
  deadline (28-38 s of AY offline) and are deadline-bound on this host, and
  the one-query production theorems of two `I128` cut fixtures, whose parts
  certify, are recorded gaps (Clean rejects an `equiv_simplify` step of the
  proof AY prints; both certify since slice 19's spelling). Over census-ay13556's 33 domain refusals, this owner
  builds a theorem for the 19 that need no `I128` division and refuses the
  14 that do, by name; 16 of the 19 certify offline within 30 s. The x86-64
  selector's `I128` division libcall now declares its four argument
  registers (no emitted byte changes); slice 20a would make the division a
  call of the runtime routine, a contract this slice does not trust. On
  the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census (O0, AY build 13556, on main
  `bf5d4b2c9`), failed roots go from 108 to 90: 18 promoted (4 `I128`
  loop-carried values, 3 past the slot count, 3 binary-search switches, 2
  stored-address joins, 6 singletons and bounds, 1 bound body now
  certifying), none newly failing, no named
  mismatch and no refuted body.

  Slice 19 (ruling OD-195) spells every value-numbered single-query
  theorem, every one-path theorem `(= S M)` (as its one claim) and every
  part again, after slice 18's spelling, with the whole exact normalizer:
  slice 18's "v18" identities (extension and extract, folding, Boolean
  constants, the one-bit encoding of a Boolean, the widening product's
  overflow test, the `bvsub`-zero identity, unit and zero laws), ten more
  identity groups (the low bits of a product or sum are those of its
  operands' low bits, a shift by a constant is an extract, one comparison
  operator per direction, the overflow test of a zero- or sign-extended
  product, a product by `2^k` is a shift, an `ite` of two equal extensions,
  a subterm equal to a kept definition's right-hand side is its name, an
  extract of a kept name looked through) and `peel` (the low bits of a name
  defined as an extension are its operand), repeated to a fixpoint. A
  theorem the spelling empties keeps slice 18's spelling (never stated by
  identities alone); a part it empties is no part; a sign test whose
  all-ones constant needs more than 64 bits is left as it is. Trusted in
  addition: about thirty identities with no side condition, each checked
  exhaustively at small widths and swept over random terms, random
  definition lists, every fixture and wrong lowering and every part against
  an exact evaluator. Of the 410 golden theorems and part shapes, 172
  change (30 one-path, 18 of slice 20's 19); every one is proved equivalent
  to its slice-18 spelling by z3 in both directions and a 256-input sweep,
  and a test-only switch (`with_normal_groups`) re-renders every slice-18
  golden byte for byte. On census-ay13556's 41 bound but uncertified roots, re-dumped
  through the builder (byte for byte the design's measured Python spelling
  but for one part the builder keeps in slice 18's spelling because the
  Python spelling breaks its claim skeleton, and unused argument
  declarations), AY build 13556 with Clean certifies 20 within 30 s,
  one-shot and by the resident route alike (none before). In the
  qualification ledger, slice 1's `Mul/commuted` (0.07 s), slice 10's
  `MulU64` (2.9 s) and slice 20's `U128LiveAcrossCut` (3.8 s) and
  `U128CutParam` (0.2 s), whose proofs Clean rejected before, certify and
  leave their tables, and the commuted add with slice 1's preserved tail
  certifies (it published no proof before). One measured departure
  from the design's spelling: a name defined as bits of a term wider than
  64 bits that holds no product stays a name when used once, since
  `i128::wrapping_sub` (the `SubU128` shape), whose only claim left is the
  high half of a 128-bit difference, times out at 30 s with it inlined and
  certifies in 1.8 s with it named (2.3 s on main); a half of a 128-bit
  product is inlined (kept, it held five roots' 128-bit products in their
  queries after `magic`, and they timed out).

  Slice 19's second stage (ruling OD-196) rewrites a constant-divisor
  multiply-high (`extract[hi:lo]((zero_extend x) * C)`, and the "add" shape
  compilers emit when the magic constant needs `N + 1` bits) to the
  quotient `(bvudiv x d)` it computes, only when the Granlund-Montgomery
  inequality holds for the instance's own constants: with `d = ceil(2^k /
  m)` and `e = m d - 2^k`, `(2^N - 1) * e < 2^k`, checked per instance in
  128-bit integers (`magic_divisor`), the product never wrapping its width;
  unsigned only (no pattern matches a sign-extended operand, so a signed
  multiply-high is never rewritten). Two companions: an extension of the
  quotient's low bits that the quotient fits, and `(bvurem x C)` as SMT-LIB
  defines it. Trusted in addition: the pattern match and that integer check.
  On the 41 roots, with the wide-bits rule as finally committed, 31 roots
  certify whole (20 at stage 1). Slice 14's `UdivConst` and `UremConst32` empty
  under it (every claim an identity once the quotient is in place), so
  they keep slice 18's spelling (never stated by identities alone) and stay
  recorded AY gaps.

  Slice 19's third stage (ruling OD-197) changes two routes, both
  fail-closed. A theorem or part whose whole replay is neither Valid nor
  refuted is replayed again claim by claim: one obligation per distinct
  claim over the cone of definitions it reaches (a one-path theorem, a
  single claim or more than 64 claims are not split), replayed in order
  and stopping at the first without a Valid replay; the obligation is
  credited only when every claim's AY proof is accepted by Clean, and the
  export publishes the claims in its place, which every consumer re-derives.
  And for the x86-64 body owner only, a resident AY deadline is followed by
  one one-shot replay with a new budget instead of ending the replay. The
  source-bound negative memo moved to schema v5 with it: a `Timeout` is
  recorded only when every deadline the replay saw used its budget in CPU
  time (for a body query, the resident one AND the one-shot retry's), and
  no v4 entry, recorded under the resident-only policy, is read. Trusted
  in addition: nothing new in kind (the claim split is the part rule one
  level finer, under the same structural check; the retry changes which
  route answers, not what credits). Of the 41 roots, 39 certify one-shot
  claim by claim and 39 by the census route with the retry (37 without it:
  the resident route times out on two claims of `i64::from_ascii_radix`,
  and `isize`'s, that the one-shot route certifies); `align_offset::<u8>`
  and `u64::overflowing_pow` each keep one claim AY does not certify within
  30 s. The cost is time: a theorem or part that times out whole now pays
  the resident deadline, the one-shot retry and its claims (14 such queries
  on the 41 roots, 134 claim replays with a median of 1.1 s).

  The replay budget is the AY solve's, and the Clean check has its own
  (ruling OD-223, `obligation_cert_store::proof_check_timeout_ms`). The
  30 s budget (`TCG_RECON_SOLVER_MS`) bounds each AY process of a replay:
  the resident solve, the one-shot solve, the SAT model query. Every Clean
  check of a proof runs under the checker's own deadline. That covers the
  check of the proof AY just emitted on the one-shot route (the resident
  route's candidates included), on every part and claim replay, and on the
  export's re-check (`--emit-proofs`). It also covers the certificate
  store's re-check of a stored proof and its prefetch, the mint's check
  and a composed closed-definition proof's check. The deadline is 180 s of
  wall-clock time, never less than the solve budget and never unbounded: a
  solve budget of 0 still leaves the check bounded.
  `TCG_CLEAN_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` overrides it, within (0, 1 h], outside the
  rustc bridge: trustc refuses `TCG_*` variables, so a bridge compile takes
  the default. Before
  the ruling, every check shared the solve budget, and the outcome of a
  check that ran out of it read "AY TIMEOUT".
  `core::num::<u64>::leading_zeros` (census s23final) is the measured case:
  AY 13556 answers `unsat` in 7.6-8.0 s (2.3 s resident), and Clean 5f09e36c
  needs 41-53 s of CPU time to check the ~11 MB proof. The certificate
  store's re-check of its stored proof failed the same way, on every
  occurrence. Now a checker outcome is labelled as one ("Clean check
  timeout", "Clean check refused", "Clean check did not complete", "Clean
  checker unavailable"), and "AY TIMEOUT" means an AY deadline. The
  negative memo records a checker timeout as `checker-timeout`, never as a
  solver `timeout`, judged on the checker's own expiries (90 % of the
  checker deadline in CPU time). Its key names the checker deadline, so a
  longer deadline is not answered by an entry recorded under a shorter
  one. This changes completeness and compile time only: Clean accepts the
  exact proof or nothing is credited. The cost is time: a check that never
  ends now holds its replay for up to 180 s instead of 30 s, once per key
  until the memo records it. 180 s is 3.4 times the worst measured check.
  A proof whose check needs longer than that still fails, now labelled as
  a checker timeout.
  On the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census (O0, AY build 13556, on main
  `5d732f441`), slice 19's three stages take failed roots from 89 to 48:
  41 promoted (bound bodies that now certify), none newly failing, no named
  mismatch and no refuted body; the census dumped 2 uncertified bodies.

  Slice 21 (rulings OD-198 to OD-201 in `docs/decision-record.md`) admits
  floating-point operations as paired rounding events and the remaining
  atomics. `Fadd`, `Fsub`, `Fmul` and `Fdiv` of `F32`/`F64`, `FcvtFromInt`/
  `FcvtFromUint` of an `I64` and the in-range value of `FcvtToInt` of an
  `F64` to an `I64` are events of the world trace, like calls (OD-198): the
  SSE row of the same operator key (operation, format, rounding direction)
  whose TV-1 stamp names the operation pairs with it, the theorem observes
  the row's operands against the source's, and both read the result as one
  free input (an FP leaf); a rounding row no event pairs gets a leaf of its
  own, and a source event with no partner refuses. No side states what an
  operation computes, so the claim is refinement: the source run in which
  each paired operation returns the machine's result is one trust-ir
  permits (its operations are IEEE 754's at the operand's format, round to
  nearest even, any NaN), and no NaN payload is claimed. An unsigned
  conversion pairs with the signed `cvtsi2sd` only with its operand's bit
  63 claimed clear. `Fcmp` and `ucomisd`'s ZF/PF/CF are exact over the
  bits. `FcvtToInt` means the saturating conversion (OD-199), exactly
  trust-ir's `FPToSISat` and a refinement of `FPToSI`; `cvttsd2si` returns
  the integer indefinite outside the range. A theorem with a rounding event
  or row is FP-abstract (OD-200): a satisfying model of its negation (a
  pairing's operands differing, a leaf no IEEE unit computes) is no
  counterexample, so its rows are left uncredited, never failed, and the
  trace reads `Unknown (FP abstraction)`; an abstraction cannot prove a
  lowering whose correctness is a rounding theorem (the unbounded `u64 as
  f64`'s round-to-odd halving: stated, satisfiable, uncredited), nor one
  that canonicalizes NaNs or commutes a NaN-propagating operation. An `I128`
  `AtomicLoad` is its two halves paired with the `AtomicLoadCmpxchg16b`
  pseudo row alone (RAX the low, RDX the high, RBX and RCX zero, memory
  unchanged), and `AtomicRmw { op: Xchg }` of an `I32`/`I64` an incoming load
  and store at one address paired with the CAS-loop pseudo of kind 5 alone,
  both with OD-83's single-threaded meaning (the loop runs once) (OD-201).
  Narrower conversions, `Fsqrt`, `Fma`, `Fmin`/`Fmax`, rounding, `FPExt`/
  `FPTrunc`, `FcvtToUint`, other read-modify-writes, compare-exchange, fences
  and an `I128` atomic store stay outside by name. Trusted for slice 21, in
  addition: the Intel SDM transcription of the SSE rounding rows and of
  `ucomisd`'s flags and `cvttsd2si`'s indefinite (T1), that MXCSR holds its
  default control state `0x1F80` (round to nearest even, no FTZ/DAZ,
  exceptions masked) whenever a body runs (T3; code that changes MXCSR voids
  it), trust-ir's meaning of the admitted operations (T2; the compares and
  the conversion are checked against the pinned interpreter), that the frame
  saves and restores RBX around a body with the `cmpxchg16b` pseudo (T4: the
  save and restore rows are emitted after register allocation, outside the
  pre-RA stream this theorem walks, so the walk cannot check them; every
  other RBX write stays a mismatch), that the 16 bytes an `I128` atomic load
  reads are writable (T5: the pseudo writes them back and faults on a
  read-only page; Rust makes a 16-byte atomic load of read-only memory
  undefined behaviour, trust-ir is silent, and the lane's plain incoming
  stores already rest on the same writability), and the pseudo rows'
  single-threaded meaning (T6). Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-26-darwin-x86-64-slice21-fp-atomics/`): 35
  fixtures over real selector output, every one certified on the
  qualification pair (AY build 13556 with Clean 5f09e36c, 0.1-1.2 s); 16
  wrong lowerings as unit fixtures (the roots' own theorems cannot see
  several of them): `une` without `setp`, `olt` without `setnp`, `oge` as
  `seta`, an exchange returning the new value and an `I128` load's halves
  swapped refuted with AY counterexamples; `divsd`'s operands swapped, the
  saturating conversion without its NaN `cmovp` or with `cmova`, and `u64 as
  f64` as the signed `cvtsi2sd` alone satisfiable and left uncredited
  (OD-200); `mulss` or `divsd` for `mulsd`, a row stamped with another
  instruction, `cvtsd2si` for `cvttsd2si` and the atomic pseudo rows paired
  with plain rows (or the reverse) refused by name; 16 rule mutants, each
  failing a control; the compares and both conversions checked against the
  pinned trust-ir interpreter and `ucomisd`, `cvttsd2si` and MXCSR against
  this host's hardware; every earlier golden unchanged. The 12 census roots
  this slice targets (the four `Mul`/`Div` impls, two
  `already_rounded_value_should_use_exponential`, two `Lemire::from_u64`,
  `pow2_to_pow10`, `atomic_load::<i128>`/`<u128>` and `atomic_store::<*const
  OsFunctions>`) build a theorem through the real builder and certify
  offline in 0.1-0.8 s each (measured on the census-s20 `core` dump).
  On the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census (O0, AY build 13556, on main
  `c4885af82`), failed roots go from 48 to 36: all 12 targets promoted (6
  floating-point operations, 3 conversions, 3 atomics), none newly failing,
  no named mismatch and no refuted body.

  Slice 22 (rulings OD-202 to OD-204 in `docs/decision-record.md`) admits
  the `i128` division class. An `I128` `Udiv`/`Sdiv`/`Urem`/`Srem` is the
  call of its runtime routine (`__udivti3`, `__divti3`, `__umodti3`,
  `__modti3`) under the call model of slices 3, 7 and 13 (OD-202): its
  operands are the call's arguments (RDI:RSI, RDX:RCX), its result the
  call's one `I128` result, a free input both sides share, so no division
  and no undefined stop is stated; the argument placement, the symbol each
  opcode calls and the result's use are checked. An `I128` divide-by-zero
  guard is slice 14's guard at 128 bits (`or d, lo, hi; TrapDivZeroExact
  d`). Trusted for slice 22, in addition: that the routine the link binds
  to each name (for a Rust program the sysroot's `compiler_builtins`; for a
  C link the platform's compiler-rt, libSystem's on macOS 13.7.8, an
  OS-version-dependent binding; or a definition in another module of the
  link) returns trust-ir's `udiv`/`sdiv`/`urem`/`srem` of its two System V
  `I128` arguments on trust-ir's defined domain, and (OD-211) writes no
  memory the caller observes, has no effect on the world and returns, which
  is more than the call model assumes of a callee (it lets one rewrite the
  escaped slots and the world) and is not tested. OD-210 refuses a theorem
  whose routine the module under proof defines (the AOT lane and the JIT
  name the module), or which is the function under proof, and OD-216 one
  whose routine another compile unit of its link unit defines: the rustc
  bridge compiles a crate one codegen unit, or one function, at a time, and
  names to every module the trusted routines any codegen unit of the crate
  defines (the symbols of rustc's mono items; a `global_asm!` block counts
  as all of them), so a crate defining `__udivti3` anywhere gets no theorem
  that trusts it. A definition in another crate of the link (the sysroot's,
  the platform's) still binds and stays trusted, and a frontend that names
  no link unit (every other one) has OD-210's module-level guard only.
  Every walk names the module: each verifier entry that takes an ABI
  requires it, and a theorem built where none is named is refused (until
  2026-11-01 the AOT lane's request-free walk named none, and refused so a
  body stated in parts that the whole-body admission refuses: a lost
  credit, never a false one; OD-210, amended). The
  x86-64 vectorizer's fill tier (O2 and above) rewrites a write-only fill
  of a local of 1024 bytes or more into `call memset` after the LIR the
  theorem reads; no body theorem credits that call, it binds to a crate's
  own `memset` if one exists (`#![no_builtins]` is not read), and OD-218
  withholds the route from a function named `memset` (its fill would call
  itself). The value contract is tested, never proved: a
  native differential of both bindings against an independent bit-serial
  reference (15.6 M checks per binding, 0 mismatches, a wrong routine
  caught; `slice22::the_i128_division_routines_match_an_independent_
  reference` repeats it against the test binary's own binding). trust-ir's
  interpreter (its `u128 /` compiles to the very routine) and
  `e2e_x86_64_i128_div` (both sides link one routine) are no independent
  reference: the latter is evidence for the lowering only. A 128-bit product
  is spelled by its 64-bit limbs (OD-203: `limb`, `addhi0`, a structural
  addend order of a 64-bit sum with a product leaf, and a guarded claim whose
  guard's double negation was folded keeps its skeleton), and bit moves have
  a normal form (OD-204, `catnf`); all identities on every input
  (exhaustive at small widths; `limb` also in integer arithmetic at 128 bits
  by z3), adding no trust. A theorem whose one claim the limbs make an
  identity keeps slice 18's spelling (slice 11's `MulU128` stays a gap).
  Evidence (`reports/perf/2026-10-27-darwin-x86-64-slice22-i128-division/`):
  on a fresh `core` dump from the census-s21 bridge, 13 of the 14 targeted
  roots certify offline on AY 13556 with Clean 5f09e36c (5 with OD-202 alone,
  12 with OD-203); `wide_mul_u128::scalar_mul` stays open (AY bit-blasts a
  multiplier its claim needs only as an atom). OD-203 and OD-204 change the
  theorems of 142 census-certified `core` functions, every one still
  certifying. 17 fixtures, 12 wrong lowerings refuted (5 of them wrong
  128-bit multiplies) and 16 rule mutants, each failing a control; the
  hostile review of the slice added controls for `catnf`'s same-term merge
  and zero extensions and for the zero constant of the `I128` guard, and
  OD-210's, 6 more mutants each failing a control.
  On the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census (O0, AY build 13556, on main
  `20649afe9`), failed roots go from 36 to 23: 13 promoted (9 `Udiv`, 3
  `Sdiv`, 1 divide-by-zero guard), none newly failing, no named mismatch
  and no refuted body.

  Slice 23 (rulings OD-205 and OD-206 in `docs/decision-record.md`) targets
  the census's three AY-capacity roots. On the Darwin x86-64 `core` proof census (O0, AY build 13556, on main
  `1fb7620a5`), failed roots go from 23 to 20: 3 promoted (`ptr::align_offset::<u8>`,
  `u64::overflowing_pow`, `wide_mul_u128::scalar_mul`), none newly failing, no named
  mismatch and no refuted body; all 20 left are OD-115's no-observable bodies. OD-205 pairs a machine arithmetic
  row (a product's low half, an unsigned widening product, an unsigned
  quotient or remainder, a 32- or 64-bit shift by a count the walk does not
  know; an 8- or 16-bit `shl`/`shr`/`sar r, cl` masks its count modulo 32,
  not log2 of its width, and is refused by name) with the
  source operation its TV-1 stamp names, when the two have one operator key
  (operation, width and signedness) and the row's own transcription is
  `K(c, d)`: the row is spelled as the source's `K(a, b)` and the theorem
  claims `a = c` and `b = d` unconditionally (a shift: the counts' low
  log2(w) bits). The pairing admits nothing (the theorem without it is built
  first, and its refusal is the body's), is kept only where the theorem's
  spelling does not absorb it, and never refutes: a paired theorem's
  refutation is decided by the theorem without the pairing. No `idiv` row is
  paired (the selector's divisor fixup would make a correct lowering's
  divisor claim fail). OD-206 replays an obligation whose exact replay is
  neither Valid nor refuted once more with every arithmetic node a fresh
  free input; only a Valid replay credits (a satisfying model is no
  counterexample), an exact refutation is never generalized, and every
  consumer re-derives the generalization. Trusted for slice 23, in
  addition: nothing. A paired theorem carries its pairing record (each
  paired row's key and operands, each paired name's walk definition, and
  the theorem before its spelling with the spelling's choices); the
  verifier, before it replays a paired theorem, and every export, before it
  is published, re-derive from it that each paired name's walk definition
  is its part of `K(c, d)`, that its definition is the same key's `K(a,
  b)`, that the operand claims of the bits `K` reads are unconditional
  conjuncts, and that the statement is the recorded theorem's spelling; a
  record that does not re-derive, or none, and the paired theorem is never
  replayed or published (the theorem without the pairing decides). What
  stays trusted is slices 1 to 22's: the walk's and the source's
  definitions and claims, and the spelling. The stamp that chooses the rows
  is not trusted. A lowering whose operands agree with the source's only on
  the path that uses them loses its paired theorem to the one without the
  pairing (incompleteness). Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-10-27-darwin-x86-64-slice23-arith-pairing/`): on a
  fresh `core` dump from this branch's bridge (byte for byte census-s22's),
  the three roots certify offline on AY 13556 with Clean 5f09e36c
  (`align_offset::<u8>` paired, 4.7 s; `u64::overflowing_pow` and
  `wide_mul_u128::scalar_mul` by their generalizations, 0.8 and 4.5 s); the
  theorems of 15 census-certified `core` functions change, every one still
  certifying; 5 earlier golden theorems move, each reviewed equivalent.
  13 fixtures, 11 wrong lowerings refuted (a wrong operand, a 32-bit product
  for a 64-bit one, a wrong divisor, `idiv` for `div`, `sar` for `shr`, a
  count from another register, a stale high half, the high half the divisor
  minus one, a wrong shifted value at 64 and 32 bits and in a clean-bool
  function), forged, absent and unbound pairing records refused, and 20
  rule mutants, each failing a control.

  OD-224 (`docs/decision-record.md`) makes x86-64's 128-bit checked multiply
  division-free: the adapter emits the value `Imul` and, for the flag, the
  limb check of two `I64` `CheckedUmul`s, a carry compare against the
  product's high limb and a both-high-limbs test; for `i128` the same core on
  the magnitudes (computed as `I64` mask arithmetic) and a sign check; for a
  multiply by a constant `C` the compare of the other operand with `floor((2^128
  - 1) / C)`. AArch64 keeps the guarded division (`__udivti3`/`__divti3`)
  byte for byte, so OD-202's routine contract still covers AArch64's checked
  multiply and every program division. Trusted in addition: nothing; the 11
  census roots that were this check (both types' `checked_mul` and
  `overflowing_mul`, `u128::overflowing_pow`, both `from_ascii_radix`,
  `div_rem_1e16`, `carrying_mul_add`, `full_multiplication`,
  `wide_mul_u128::scalar_mul`) no longer trust a routine. The body theorem's
  `mul` row reads its CF/OF off the upper-half name it defines (an identity),
  so OD-205's pairing carries the flag. AY 13556 rejects its own proof of the
  exact theorem of a full-operand limb check in its strict certification;
  those theorems are credited through OD-206's generalization, which
  certifies (fixtures 0.2-2.8 s; on the census-s23 `core` dump all 11 changed
  theorems certify by the census's route, as on main; the division form
  states every other function's query byte for byte as main). The adapter
  step (L04-P10) stays statistical: its three x86-64 forms are discharged by
  the sampling evaluator with a native-oracle battery and 19 refuted
  controls; on AY each times out whole, and the structured attempt reduces
  the flags formally to two multiplier lemmas (a 64x64 product's bound, the
  `Imul` high limb as its limb chain) AY does not decide. The limb check's
  scaled analogs (8 bits with 4-bit limbs, 16 bits with 8-bit limbs) are
  swept exhaustively over the adapter's actual output: evidence for those
  widths only. The two spellings that depart from the design have their
  128-bit lemmas proved by z3 4.15.4 alone, composed by hand and never
  replayed by AY/Clean (solver-backed, not formal): the constant form for
  every constant, and the signed mask spelling lemma by lemma. The whole
  signed spelling as one query is undecided
  (`reports/perf/2026-11-02-darwin-x86-64-i128-mulo-divfree/`).

  OD-226 (`docs/decision-record.md`, slice 24a) states a machine block the
  x86-64 block merge made out of a chain of LIR blocks as one block. A link
  `x -> y` is an argument-free `Jump` from `x` that is the only edge into
  `y` from any block, reachable or not, `y` neither `x` nor the entry; a
  chain is a path of links whose absorbed members declare no parameter,
  whose last member does not branch to its head and whose last member's
  edge copies into a loop header do not begin in the member before it. The
  stamps of each machine block that lowers rows of several LIR blocks (then
  of each naming one, for a stamp-silent member) choose which chain to
  contract; the theorem is the slices 1-23 theorem over the quotient (each
  chain's instructions concatenated under its head, the machine's stamps
  renumbered into its coordinates, the original source's encoding) and
  binds the original pair, its audit coordinates mapped back.
  `Quotient::check` re-derives the quotient from the original pair in every
  build, and a quotient it does not re-derive is a construction refusal (no
  claim). Trusted in addition: no assumption (such a `Jump` transfers
  control and does nothing else, the model `admit_blocks` already applies
  to every `Jump`; stamps have no machine semantics), but the theorem
  generator's trusted code grows by `Quotient::check`, on which `⟦Q⟧ = ⟦L⟧`
  rests. On the parts route the quotient admits exactly what its pieces
  state, which can be more than the original pair's own region admission
  would (flags across an old seam, a header copy or a join's edge copies
  found in the merged block): wider in what is stated, never in what a
  statement means. Only a pair whose block
  correspondence fails and whose walk needs one is stated over a quotient;
  every other theorem is byte for byte as before. Declined by name (`; not
  contracted: …`, no claim): a member another edge enters (live or dead), a
  link over a `Brif`, `Switch`, `Return` or `Trap` (one a machine pass
  folded), the entry inside a chain, a member off the chain (an if-converted
  arm, moved header rows, LICM: the 63 census-o2-7ee0 roots whose members are
  not one chain keep their refusal; slice 24c states an if-converted region
  over its segments, below), an absorbed member with parameters, a
  tail that branches to its head, a row stamped with a removed `Jump` or
  past a member's end, a cycle of single-entry `Jump`s, and a latch whose
  edge copies would begin in the previous member. A function with a laid-out
  dead block is stated but exports nothing, with or without a merge: no
  theorem claims the dead rows, so its opcode inventory is not promotable.
  Evidence (`reports/perf/2026-11-04-darwin-x86-64-slice24a-chain-quotient/`): 21
  fixtures from the real selector (19 merged by the real `X86BlockMerge`,
  one cut by `split_lir`, the merge's inverse, one merged by hand), 2 stated
  in parts and 3 further pairs (an entry behind a dead `Jump`, a 141-block
  chain the production planner cuts, a `u128` division chain stated in its
  module), each refused on `7ee0def54`; all 26 replayed units Verified on
  AY 13556 with Clean 5f09e36c (17 distinct theorems in the golden); 8 wrong
  lowerings, each refuted on samples, a named mismatch (W5a) or making no
  claim, three of them refuted by AY with counterexamples; 20 named
  refusals; 33 configurations of 27 rule mutants, each failing its
  controls. The `core` proof census at O2 falls from 582 to 378 failed
  roots (204 promoted, none newly failing, no named mismatch, no refuted
  body; one more function binds with no independently checked proof), and
  at O0 every function's trace is unchanged (20 roots). The 2026-10-01
  stamp campaign is not re-run over merged chains.

  OD-227 (`docs/decision-record.md`, slice 25) states the scaled-index load
  and store rows and the memory-destination `add`/`xor` rows that
  `X86Peephole`'s address folds and read-modify-write fusion produce at O1
  and above. `MovRMSib`, `MovRM32Sib`, `MovRM8Sib`, `MovzxRM8Sib`,
  `MovsdRMSib`, `MovssRMSib`, `MovMRSib`, `MovMR32Sib` and `MovMR8Sib` with
  a virtual value register and an address `[b + i*s + d]` (the base a
  virtual 64-bit register or a declared stack slot, the index a virtual
  64-bit register, `s` 1, 2, 4 or 8, no proof origin) are their base-only
  row's access, through the unchanged code, at the address `LeaSib`
  computes, by `LeaSib`'s own code: a slot base is the slot's address; a
  private base at an index the walk knows as a constant is the exact
  checked offset (OD-185), at any other index slice 17's indexed address
  (whose candidates the TV-1 stamp sizes, never chooses); at scale 1 only, a
  value base over a private index is the same sum; otherwise `b + i*s +
  sext(d)` mod 2^64. `AddMR`/`XorMR [v + d], r` and `AddMRSib`/`XorMRSib [v
  + i*s + d], r` (every register virtual and 64-bit) into incoming memory
  are the next two incoming events of the world trace, a plain 8-byte load
  and a plain 8-byte store of `old + r` or `old ^ r` at the one address,
  each paired as a `mov`'s; `add` defines `AddRR`'s flags, and `xor` leaves
  them unmodelled. A `MovRMSib` not of that virtual form, or whose base
  holds a jump-table value, is slice 14's dispatch load, read as a table
  entry at scale 8, displacement 0 and in the table's own dispatch block
  only (a read of a table in any other block is refused by name). The
  stack-slot scan exempts a
  slot that is a scaled-index access's own base over an index that names no
  slot. Outside (no claim, by name): a physical component (an RBP or RSP
  base included), scale 3, a 32-bit index, a proof origin, a private index
  at any other scale, two private components, a slot as an index, on
  `LeaSib` or on a read-modify-write row, an undeclared slot, a
  read-modify-write of private memory, a mixed or carried component (an
  undefined one is a named mismatch), an indexed access past 1024
  candidates, `MovsxdRMSib`, `MovdquRMSib`, `ImulRMSib` and every other
  scaled-index opcode, and a read of `xor`'s flags. Trusted for slice 25, in
  addition: the SDM meaning of `ADD`/`XOR r/m64, r64` (`REX.W 01 /r`,
  `REX.W 31 /r`); the SIB effective address was already trusted for
  `LeaSib` and the dispatch load (every SIB row shares
  `emit_sib_mem_operand`); and the post-theorem lowering a credited body now
  exercises, unchanged in kind and with no per-compile check of its own:
  frame-index elimination of a slot SIB base, slot prune and remap of SIB
  uses, register allocation's use-only classification of SIB stores and
  read-modify-write rows, and the SIB presequencing replay. The per-compile
  `decode_check` compares each emitted instruction's bytes with that same
  lowered row, so it re-checks only the encoding of the integer SIB and
  read-modify-write rows (it cannot see a fault in those transforms), and it
  does not decode `MovsdRMSib` or `MovssRMSib` at all (allowlisted: ENC-2's
  offline lane only). `e2e_x86_64_sib_rmw` executes those transforms' output
  for eleven O2 fixtures against clang references: execution evidence on
  chosen inputs, not a check of any other compile. Not trusted: the peephole's folds and their hand proofs, the fusion and its
  admission gate, TV-1 stamps (the fused row carries none, and a row with
  no stamp is never given a site). Evidence
  (`reports/perf/2026-11-04-darwin-x86-64-slice25-sib-rows/`): 32 fixtures,
  30 from the real selector and O2 pipeline and 2 synthetic (a merging byte
  load no selector path emits, and an `AddMR` whose carry is read, which the
  fusion declines), each refused on `6c036f1de`; all 81 replayed units
  Verified on AY 13556 with Clean 5f09e36c (the 32 fixtures, the 7
  qualified edits and the 42 parts of the fixtures that hold in parts;
  27 distinct theorems in the golden's 39 entries); 25 wrong lowerings refuted on samples or named,
  each refuted by AY with a counterexample; 7 wrong widths and slots never
  credited; 15 neutral and 7 qualified edits holding; 47 named refusals; 17
  rule mutants, each failing a control, and one neutral mutant. Every real
  displacement is 0 at O2, so the displacement controls fold a constant
  into it by hand. Stated in parts (OD-182), 21 fixtures hold, 7 are
  refused and 4 are refuted on samples, each exactly as its `lea; mov [t]`
  decomposition is (no credit; OD-233). On the `core` census at O2 the
  failed roots go from 378 to 254 (124 promoted, none newly failing, no
  named mismatch); one root that failed before still fails, its theorem now
  stated in parts and refuted in one part by the same cut-interface gap
  (`core::wtf8::slice_error_fail`, no credit; OD-233, above, promotes it);
  at O0 every record and trace is unchanged (20 roots).

  OD-228 (`docs/decision-record.md`, slice 24c) states a machine block that
  lowers a single-entry region of LIR blocks (a diamond or two-way switch
  `X86IfConvert` folded into its head's block) over its segments. A segment
  is a head `h` and members `S` one laid-out machine block `m` lowers: every
  member but `h` is live, is neither the entry nor a loop header and is
  entered only from `S`; `S` is acyclic and no member branches to `h`; every
  member ends in `Jump`, `Brif` or `Switch`; no exit enters a loop header;
  `m` reaches no jump-table or binary-search block; every call, incoming
  access, rounding operation, stop and indexed access of `S` lies in one
  member every run through `S` passes; `m`'s stamps name `h` and only
  members, and segments are disjoint. The stamps choose the segments, and
  `segment::check` re-derives the rule from the LIR and the machine's stamps
  in every build. `lowering` stays one to one (`h` to `m`); `m`'s
  successors must be exactly the segment's exit targets; `m` is walked whole
  once per exit target from `h`'s entry state against the effect member's
  program, each exit claiming its machine edge under the source guard;
  members walk no rows and state no items (re-checked where the theorem
  consumes the walks, every build, with the effect member re-derived there);
  per path, consecutive members take no machine step; the parts route never
  cuts inside a segment, at an exit target with parameters, or where a
  value only non-head members define is live. Trusted in addition: no
  assumption, but the theorem generator's trusted code grows by
  `segment::check`, the segment branch of the block correspondence, the
  segment walk and its effects rule, the internal-join rule, the region
  walk's member arm, the per-path member skip, the member guard and the
  choice of the segments it guards, the DAG claim floor over segments, the
  parts bans and the pieces' segment-equality guard. Not
  trusted: the stamps, the chooser, `X86IfConvert`, `X86CmovSwap`, their
  inversion admission and every machine pass. Declined by name (no claim):
  a member entered from outside, the entry or a loop header as a member, a
  named block the head does not reach inside the set, a member ending in
  `Return` or `Trap`, overlapping segments, a machine block whose
  successors are not the exits (an exit the machine cannot take included:

- Solver-backed paths prove supported encoded obligations. They do not
  automatically prove that the encoding covers an entire compiler pass, ABI,
  object writer, runtime, or unsupported semantic surface.
- Proof coverage is not uniform across targets, opcodes, optimizations,
  register allocation, object relocations, debug/unwind data, and JIT
  publication.
- `--emit-proofs` is intentionally stricter than ordinary compilation. It can
  reject a module that compiles without proof emission when any required
  opcode or relocation lacks promotable authority.
- Emitted `.cert` and function-level sidecars record evidence and provenance;
  emission alone is not independent certification. Current unsigned exports
  do not cross the trust-cg/AY trust boundary merely by existing.
- Selected SAT-blasted obligations and canaries have independent `drat-trim`
  replay. That checker path does not cover every compiler obligation.
- The Lean development proves selected models and forward-simulation/encoding
  results. It still contains classified proof gaps and explicit trusted axioms.
- Differential and triple-oracle tests cover named corpora. Passing them does
  not prove the absence of miscompilations outside those corpora. The correspondence is read from the TV-1 lowering stamps, which the owner
  trusts (TV-2 checks digests and op classes only afterwards and accepts a
  restamp onto another compatible instruction); soundness does not rest on
  them, since the theorem requires the paired path's `jcc` conditions to hold
  whenever the source path's do. Forged stamps can make a correct body fail
  closed (refuted, or a named control mismatch when a trap block's and a return
  block's stamps are swapped under equal successor sets) but never credit a
  wrong one: 17,669 stamp-perturbation x mutation cases (2026-10-01), every
  credited case correct by an independent interpreter. Slice 24a (OD-226)
  reads the stamps for one more choice, which chains of a merged machine
  block to contract, and trusts them no more: a forged merge, a member
  restamped into another chain, a row stamped with a removed `Jump` or past
  a member's end, or a dead or foreign member is declined by name (no
  claim), breaks the correspondence over the quotient (no claim) or is
  refuted (the slice-24a refusal controls and wrong lowerings); the
  2026-10-01 campaign itself was not re-run over merged chains. Slice 25
  (OD-227) reads a scaled-index access's stamp only as slice 17 reads a
  load's, to size an indexed access's candidates (with the stamp of an
  indexed slot byte load removed or pointed at another instruction, its
  theorem still holds); the fused read-modify-write row carries no stamp,
  and a row without one is never given a site. Slice 24c (OD-228) reads the
  stamps for one more choice, which LIR blocks one machine block lowers as a
  segment, and trusts them no more: `segment::check` re-derives the rule
  from the LIR and the stamps in every build, forged chooser outputs are
  refused by name, and a block whose head no stamp names keeps its refusal;
  the 2026-10-01 campaign was not re-run over segments.

Unsupported input is intended to fail closed, but trust-cg is alpha software:
bugs, crashes, hangs, and wrong-code defects may still exist. Do not use its
output for safety-, security-, financial-, or mission-critical systems.

Fresh AY execution, AY version probes and Lean replay require complete stdout
and stderr before accepting a result, with finite capture deadlines where
configured. AY timeout zero explicitly remains unlimited. Bounded cleanup is
not a guarantee that an OS-blocked or escaped child terminates; Windows cleanup
targets only the direct child. This increment is runtime-tested on macOS ARM64,
not Windows or Linux. It does not bound OS spawn/syscall scheduling or total
output memory. Resident AY polls both I/O directions under a solver deadline
that starts when the query is admitted to the resident server; time queued
behind other queries is not charged to it. Queueing is bounded separately: a
waiter is refused by name only when the query holding the server has run past
its own budget plus a 10 s allowance, so a waiter behind a holder under the
unlimited (zero) timeout policy waits without bound. The protocol frame does
not itself authorize a proof. On macOS the first start of a new private AY
copy (which the host holds until it has assessed the new executable: up to
32.2 s measured for the 158 MB toolchain AY on a busy host) is made, or
waited for, before any solver deadline starts, at most once per process. It
is bounded only by its own 120 s allowance, a hang guard rather than a
budget; a start stopped there counts as made in that process, so a later
start may pay the rest of the assessment inside a solver deadline. What a
per-query deadline still measures is wall time: the start of an assessed
file, the solve, the proof-bearing re-solve and the Clean check, each under
its own budget. None of these budgets is a deterministic fuel, so a query
near its budget can still time out on a loaded host.
Clean capability probes/replay and AY proof-cache minting now honor the same
per-process timeout policy. This is not a whole-query deadline: optional cache
replay, solving, proof checking and minting can each consume a separate budget;
staging and executable hashing are not bounded by the subprocess timer.
Certificate publication never replaces a competing entry, but does not promise
crash durability or removal of every temporary hard link on every platform.
The cache directory must not be attacker-controlled. Missing or timed-out proof
evidence cannot justify acceptance or switching away from AY.

Shared codegen test supervisors request termination without blocking on
reaping and report whether a child exit was observed. That does not establish
that a host whose supervisor timed out is safe for further EH or Rosetta
execution. Panic-count checks and source-bound manual reviews are separate: a
passing panic-count ratchet does not establish panic freedom.

AY runs only from its private copy under `<user cache>/trust-cg/ay-exec`, and
only when no ancestor of that directory is writable by group or others without
the sticky bit. `<user cache>` is an absolute `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, else an
absolute `HOME`'s `.cache`, for every trust-cg cache root and the gate
scripts alike (`private_fs::user_cache_base`, `private_cache.user_cache_base`):
an empty or relative `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is ignored (a leading space makes a
value relative; an absolute value is used exactly as given, a trailing
space included), and with a
relative or empty `HOME` and no absolute `XDG_CACHE_HOME` there is no cache,
so AY is refused (`TCG-AY-IDENTITY-UNMATERIALIZED`), the certificate store
and solver-identity memo are off, the JIT caches miss and the CEGIS cache
uses its temp-directory fallback. trust-cg creates each cache directory `0700` and each cache
file `0600` (the AY copy `0500`) whatever the umask. The gate scripts that
write under `<user cache>/trust-cg` follow the same rule through
`scripts/private_cache.py`, and the builds they run there write under umask
077: `soundness_check.sh` (`soundness-deps`, its pinned checkouts, and the
Clean lane's builds and checks), `check_x86_icmp_certificates.py` (`ay-cli`
and `clean-cli` and their builds, binaries `0500`), and `soundness_remote.sh` on the x86-64
executor (the clone, the x86-64 legs run in it, and the bundles). Nothing
changes a directory that already exists. `soundness_check.sh` refuses, never
repairs, a `soundness-deps` directory that another user could rename entries
in, by the rule the icmp gate holds `ay-cli` to, and a pinned checkout with
any entry another user could write: each checkout is judged as a whole tree
(`private_cache.py require-private-tree`: every directory and file this
user's, with no group/other write bit, a symlink only when every hop of its
literal target stays in the tree, LD-71) before it is used and again after
the Clean build, and the Clean binary before it runs (LD-65). An attested
run checks trust-cg's own proofs (`proofs/*.lean` and `formal/lean`) only in
a private export of the attested commit below its log directory, refused
when a `TMPDIR` another user could write lies above it (LD-70). The export
is read from the object store by hash, with no system or global git
configuration and no attributes, and read back against the blob hashes, so
the filters of a git configuration reach none of it (LD-70's correction of
2026-10-15; `git archive` had applied them). The user's own toolchain
installs (rustup/cargo, elan/lake, the Trust package), git and its
configuration, and the candidate checkout are the host's trust boundary
(LD-73): no tool can defend a build against a user who can rewrite the
compiler, and everything else an attested run reads from the candidate
checkout it reads in place. An attested run still fails closed there:
before it starts any program but bash and python3,
`scripts/host_boundary.py` judges every PATH directory and every command in
it, `TMPDIR`, `CARGO_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME`, `ELAN_HOME`, the Trust package,
the island twin rustc's install, python3's user site-packages, node's global
module folders, the candidate checkout (its `target/` included), the
git directories of it and of the Clean, AY and aterm sources, git's
configuration, and ssh's configuration and the program each fetch
transport setting names (in every run), and refuses (FAIL with
the path and the remedy, nothing else run, no attestation) any that another
user can write: world-writable, group-writable by a group with a member
other than this user (`/etc/group` members and every account's primary
group), owned by another account (a system account's file in a root-owned
directory excepted), or writable through a POSIX ACL. A group-writable path
in a group with no other member passes; on this host the `ayates` group has
none, so its `0775` tool directories and checkout pass. Since LD-75 the
check also judges, as whole trees, the alternate object stores a judged git
directory borrows objects from (refusing an alternates file it cannot read
or parse, an entry naming no directory, an `http-alternates` file and a
`GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` or `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` in its
environment); refuses a directory whose default ACL would open what is
created in it and a `core.sharedRepository` other than `umask` or false; and
refuses a candidate checkout, `SOUNDNESS_DEPS_DIR`, user cache, `CARGO_HOME`
or `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` below a directory in which another user can create
the `.cargo` Cargo reads, sticky or not, so an attested run's checkout,
given as an absolute path, cannot live below `/tmp`. Since LD-75's repair
of 2026-10-16 the check also refuses `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`,
`RUSTUP_HOME`, `ELAN_HOME`, `SOUNDNESS_DEPS_DIR` or `ATPKG_BIN` set to a
value that is not an absolute path (an empty one included), naming the
variable (Cargo, rustup, elan and the gate resolve such a value against
their working directory, which the check does not judge; it had skipped
them), an empty `TMPDIR` (Rust's `std::env::temp_dir()` returns the empty
path, so temporary files would land in the unjudged working directory), and
a program a git configuration key names by a relative path with a slash
(git runs it from its working directory, a work tree no rule judges). The
check judges the running python3's own `-I` import path (the standard
library and site directories), never the caller's working directory, so
since ruling OD-XHOST-GATE-CWD-20261025 (2026-10-25, the sixth closure
audit's F1 and F3) an attested run starts nothing there: it works in `/`
until the check has passed and in the judged candidate checkout from then on
(where the landing train and the pre-push hook start it), and every inline
python3 the gate and its helpers start (`python3 -c`, `python3 -`) runs with
`-I`. Before it, a run started in a `0777` directory holding a `0666`
`json.py` passed the check, imported that module through the gate's own
`python3 -c` and `python3 -` and `gate_env.sh`'s `python3 -`, and wrote its
record, and a `lean-toolchain` there chose the record's `toolchains.lake`.
Its repair round 2 (two verifiers, the same day) closed what that left: a
plain `cd` of the gate's own directory looked it up in an exported CDPATH, so
`scripts/soundness_check.sh --attest` with a CDPATH naming another user's
directory ran that directory's `soundness_attestation.py` before the check
and attested; a relative PATH entry found the scrub's python3 relative to the
working directory before the check could refuse the entry; and the record
had said that a python3 script run without `-I` adds only its own directory
and the user site-packages, while a `.pth` file there also puts every
directory it names on the path (a `0777` one included) and runs its `import`
lines. The gate now finds its own directory with `CDPATH= cd`, refuses one
that does not hold the script bash runs, refuses a relative or empty PATH
entry before its first program, and starts every python3, scripts too, with
`-I`; the check judges each directory a user-site `.pth` file names, as a
tree, and refuses the startup code a python3 run without `-I` (a leg's)
would execute from there. Its repair round 3 closed two older fail-opens
(present since `fa2d651e8`): the check's own python3 was found by name after
`gate_env.sh`'s prelude had put `$HOME/.elan/bin` first on PATH, so a python3
in a directory not yet judged ran the check and was not the interpreter the
earlier checks saw; and an `--attest` run whose script bash read from
standard input or a `-c` string had no `BASH_SOURCE`, so a
`soundness_attestation.py` in the caller's directory ran before the check and
the run attested. The gate now pins one python3 by its canonical path before
the prelude (`SOUNDNESS_PYTHON3`), starts every python3 by it (the scrub, the
check, every tool, and the helpers it starts), and the check judges exactly
that file and refuses it unless it is the interpreter running the check; an
`--attest` run that bash does not read as a script from the candidate's
`scripts/soundness_check.sh` file (standard input, a `-c` string, a sourced
script, another file) refuses before any program; and the check refuses a
user-site `.pth` file holding a character `str.splitlines` breaks a line at
besides `\n` and `\r`, since CPython 3.13 reads its lines that way and 3.12
does not. Its repair round 4 closed what round 3 left open: the legs start
python3 by name on the prelude's PATH, while the check judged the pinned
interpreter's import path alone, so a python3 the prelude put first (a
wrapper running a virtual environment's interpreter, its site-packages
writable by every user) or a virtual environment's `bin/python3` first on
the caller's PATH (a symlink to the very file pinned) was the legs' and the
run attested. The check now refuses the run unless the first python3 on the
legs' PATH is the pinned file, reached by a name around which python3 reads
no other `pyvenv.cfg` (each it would read judged as a path no other user may
create), refuses a pin that is a `#!` script or, on Linux, not the file
`/proc/self/exe` names, and the scripts the run starts before the check are
named by the gate's own directory, never by a caller's `TRUST_CG_DIR`. Still
outside the check, as stated: the outer bash and the python3 PATH finds,
which run before it (that python3 only to print its canonical path, with
`-I -S`, once in each of the run's two bash runs); the import path of an
interpreter a leg starts by another name than `python3`; on macOS, which
has no `/proc/self/exe`, a compiled launcher that runs another binary under
its own `argv[0]`; the remote probe phase of `soundness_remote.sh`; and the
identities step's `toolchains.lake`, elan's default. Since
ruling OD-XHOST-FETCH-TRANSPORT-20261016 (2026-10-16) it judges, in every run
and not only with an x86-64 executor (a pinned checkout's `git fetch origin`
may use ssh), `~/.ssh` and `/etc/ssh` and the program each of
`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_SSH` and `GIT_PROXY_COMMAND` in the environment and
`core.sshCommand` and `core.gitProxy` in a judged repository's
configuration names, every one that is set: its first word (split where the
shell splits words, not at U+00A0, as for every key's program) is the
program; an absolute or `~/` program is
