resolved, a bare name is found on the judged PATH, and a relative path with
a slash refuses, as do a value that is empty, holds a character the shell
gives a meaning beyond separating words, begins with an assignment, or (a
program git runs without a shell) holds whitespace; every later word of an
ssh command that names a path was judged the same way (an absolute or `~/`
path resolved, a relative one with a slash refused; a clause the next ruling
replaced); and a
`protocol.allow` or `protocol.ext.allow` other than `never`, or a
`GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` listing `ext`, refuses, since git's `ext::` transport
runs the command a remote URL names. Before it, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` was
judged only with an executor and only when its first word was absolute, so
a program in a `0777` directory, or one named relative to the Clean source's
work tree, ran as the gate's user and the run attested (the fifth closure
audit). Since ruling OD-XHOST-TRANSPORT-WORDS-20261024 (2026-10-24: the
round-5 verifier's three fail-opens and three lows; in a second repair
round, five git-command-key shapes two verifiers ran to an attestation at
`9352c20f1`; in a third, a source git used from a directory other than the
one judged, a `core.worktree` naming an ancestor of the Clean source and a
`CLEAN_SOURCE_DIR` that is a subdirectory of Clean, each run to an
attestation at `f7919800a` and at `4a0668957`, and a Unicode-whitespace `!`
prefix `9352c20f1` had let pass; in a fourth, an alias a judged command key
runs, `remote.origin.uploadpack = git x` with alias x `!sh <program>` or
`-c uploadpack.packObjectsHook=<program> upload-pack` (a program in a `0777`
directory), each run to an attestation at `a6cbba41b` and at `4a0668957`,
and an alias `!! <program>`, which `4a0668957` refused and `a6cbba41b` let
run) the check also: refuses any judged path
whose canonical
resolution enters `/proc` or `/dev/fd` (they name the checking process's
own view, not the view git's child has from its working directory, so
`GIT_SSH_COMMAND=/proc/self/cwd/tools/evil` would run elsewhere than it is
judged), in every lookup, every tree, the Cargo ancestry search and an
atpkg shim's exec target; for `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` and `core.sshCommand` (shell
commands) accepts the program alone and refuses ANY later word (the remedy
is `~/.ssh/config`, which it judges); judges each `--git-repo` WORK TREE
(the Clean, AY and aterm sources, where the fetch, its lazy fetches and
`git worktree add`'s parent run) as a whole tree; asks git, for the
candidate, each `--git-repo` and each Cargo git database
(`$CARGO_HOME/git/db/*`, whose configuration it now lists too), which work
tree and git directory it uses (`git rev-parse`), and refuses unless they
are the directory itself (a bare repository: as its git directory) and the
git directories judged as trees, so a `core.worktree` naming an ancestor or
any other directory, a subdirectory of a repository, a directory with no
`.git` of its own, a `core.bare` on a work tree's `.git` and a `GIT_DIR`
naming another repository refuse; and judges `$SHELL` (absolute or refused),
`/bin/sh`, and `~/.ssh` of the passwd home as well as of `$HOME`. The gate
asks git the same of each pinned checkout before its first `git status`
and refuses one whose work-tree top or common git directory git reports
elsewhere (a `core.worktree` in its per-worktree `config.worktree`). Every
other git command key, `alias.*` included, is read by the TEXT of its words:
a judged command can run git with an alias (`uploadpack = git x`), so every
alias is judged, whatever runs it. git strips exactly one leading `!` from an
alias or a credential helper, and none from any other key; after it only
blanks and newlines are skipped, as by `/bin/sh`, so `!<U+00A0>/x` refuses as
the relative program it is. A shell command (every value but an alias
without `!`) refuses a shell metacharacter; a first word the shell reads as
reserved (`!`, `if`, `time`, `[[`, ...) or that begins with `!` (`!! /x` is
`! /x` to the shell, which runs /x); a first word holding `=` (an
environment assignment, `PATH=.. prog`; `LESS=FRX less` is over-refused); a
word naming git (`git`, `.../git`) followed by a git option (`git -C <dir>`,
`--git-dir=`, `-c`: that git could read the configuration of a repository
other than the judged ones; an alias such as `!git -C <dir> status` is
over-refused); and a later word that sets the environment, holds `..` (`../x`, `-C ..`,
`-C..`), holds a `/` or `~` without being exactly an absolute or `~/` path or
a plain `--option=` followed by one (`-S/x`, `tools/x`, `~user/x`; a sed
script such as `s/a/b/` is over-refused: name a script file or a wrapper by
an absolute path instead), names such a path holding `:`, `,`, `=`, `%` or
a later `~`, or holds a character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_.,:@%+=-]`. An alias
without `!` is the argument list git runs itself after `git`, whose options
can run a program: its first word refuses when it is a git option (`-c`,
`-C`, `--exec-path`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--config-env`, ...), and
every word is read as a later word is (`fetch --upload-pack=<path>` judges
the path). An absolute or `~/` later word is resolved, and judged as a whole
tree when it is a directory; a plain later word passes. A plain word's text names nothing
outside git's working directory and PATH, and, per the ruling's inventory
of the gate's own git commands and Cargo's git fetch, git starts a
configured program only in a directory the check judges as a tree and
verifies is the one git uses (a `--git-repo` work tree, the candidate,
`CARGO_HOME`'s git databases; a pinned checkout, judged by
`require-private-tree` and verified by the gate) or in
the new pinned checkout `git worktree add` creates under umask 077 in the
private deps directory (its filters and hooks run there;
`require-private-tree` judges it right after, before anything else runs in
it); the check's own `git var` and `git --exec-path` (run in `/`, in no
repository) start none, and since OD-XHOST-GATE-CWD-20261025 no git the run
starts runs in the caller's working directory. A path git reads from a key
(`core.hooksPath`, `core.attributesFile`) is judged as git reads it, not
whitespace-stripped.
This host's `!/usr/bin/gh auth git-credential` keeps passing (a root-owned
program, two plain words).

Since ruling OD-XHOST-GIT-PROGRAM-KEYS-20261024 (2026-10-24: the round-4
verification confirmed the transport-words repair but REFUTED a PRE-EXISTING
class — a judged command key reaches a program-valued key the check never
listed, `remote.origin.uploadpack = git web--browse -b <tool>` running
`browser.<tool>.cmd`, and `diff.external` and the `difftool`/`mergetool`
`.cmd` keys the same shape (R1); git passes a local-path remote's path to a
configured upload-pack command as its last argument, so `uploadpack = sh`
runs a script such a remote names (R2); and `exec-scrubbed` ran PATH's git
before the boundary judged PATH (R3, finding (7))) the run's git reads only
JUDGED configuration. The set of keys that name a program git, a git helper
(web--browse, difftool, mergetool, ...) or a git extension runs is open and
cannot be listed completely, so every git the gate starts runs with
`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and, as its global configuration, only a file the
host trust boundary writes on a pass: it carries the credential helper(s) the
https origins need, the commit identity, and `core.excludesFile` — the keys
it judged from the user's system and global configuration — and nothing else
(no alias, pager, editor, filter, diff, merge, browser, `url.*.insteadOf`,
`http.*` or include). It reads that file back with git and refuses if it does
not read as written; the run removes the file when it exits. And it judges
the repository-local (and worktree) configuration of every repository the
gate runs git in COMPLETELY: every key refuses unless it is on a short
allowlist of keys that name no program (data keys such as `core.filemode`,
`remote.<n>.url`, `branch.<n>.merge`, `submodule.<n>.url`, `advice.*`, plus
the five path keys judged above). Those repositories are the candidate, each
`--git-repo`, each Cargo git database and checkout, each pinned checkout
(before its first `git status`), each local repository a remote names, each
submodule git directory below `<git-dir>/modules`, and, since the round-2
repair of 2026-10-24, every repository NESTED in the work tree of one of
them, recursively: every directory there holding a `.git`, and every gitlink
path of the index holding one, a symlinked path included. Both verifiers of
the first repair showed that the gate's `git status` enters a populated
submodule whose git directory is embedded in its path (a plain clone, or
Cargo's checkout submodules) or named by a `gitdir:` file elsewhere, runs git
there with that repository's own configuration, and that the check had
judged only `<git-dir>/modules`: a `core.fsmonitor` naming a program in a
`0777` directory ran during the preflight and the run attested. A nested
repository is now judged as a tree with its git directories, git's view of
it must give its own path as the work-tree top (a `core.worktree` elsewhere
refuses), and its configuration is held to the allowlist; the same then
covers Lake's packages and any clone inside a judged work tree. Since the
round-3 repair of 2026-10-24, each kind of judgement of a repository (its
configuration, its nested walk, as a nested repository, as a local remote)
is made once per repository and never stands in for another: the round-2
regression verifier showed that a submodule the candidate also named as a
local remote (`remote.mirror.url = <candidate>/vendor/sub`) had its identity
recorded by the local-remote judgement, which does not ask git's view of a
work tree, so the nested judgement returned early and a `core.worktree`
naming a `0777` directory passed, from which the gate's `git status` ran a
program a nested repository there configured. That repository is now judged
as a nested one too and refuses. A
`remote.*.uploadpack` or `remote.*.receivepack` refuses outright in every
scope (R2). A `remote.*.url`/`pushurl` (and `submodule.*.url`) that names a
local path or `file://` repository is judged as a repository the run uses git
in (its tree, git directories, alternates and configuration); a relative,
`~`, `ext::` or non-plain `file://` location refuses. A local
`branch.<n>.remote`, `branch.<n>.pushRemote` or `remote.pushDefault` naming
neither `.` nor a configured remote is judged as a location, a file in a git
directory's `remotes/` or `branches/` (a remote defined outside the
configuration) refuses, and the preflight's `git fetch origin` (now with
`--no-recurse-submodules`) refuses when the source's own configuration
defines no `remote.origin.url` (git would read such a file or use `origin`
as a path). A new git key, or a key a git helper or extension would run, is
refused until it is reviewed and added to the allowlist, the fail-closed
direction. `isolate_git_environment` in `soundness_attestation.py` no longer
runs `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` before the boundary (R3): it drops a
fixed superset of git's repository-local variables, checked against the
installed git's list by a test, so no program runs before the boundary.
`EDITOR`, `VISUAL`, `PAGER`, `LESS`, `GIT_EDITOR` and `GIT_PAGER` (each names
a program git or a helper runs) are dropped from an attested run's
environment, and one that reaches the legs past the scrub refuses the run.
That is the writer scrubbing more than the `allowlist-v1` rules allow: under
those rules, which the record verifier re-derives row by row, the six stay
`inert` (round 3 restored them; the first repair had changed their verdict
under the same policy name, and its verifier refused 25 of the 26 local
records), so every earlier record verifies as before and a record this
writer makes, which has no row for them, is judged alike by main's verifier
and this one. The user's system and global files are still READ AND JUDGED by
the command, transport and path rules above: the check's own git reads them,
and Cargo's built-in libgit2 ignores `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and
`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` and reads them itself (the only programs Cargo runs from
them are its credential helpers, which are judged). The default files
libgit2 reads (`/etc/gitconfig`, the XDG git config and `~/.gitconfig`, with
their includes) are judged even when the caller's `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` names
another file, which had hidden them from the check (round 2). So a global key those
rules refuse still refuses the run, as before the ruling (for example a
global alias holding a quote, `log --pretty=format:'%h %s'`), and a global
`remote.*.uploadpack` now refuses too. A Mac host's ordinary configuration
(`credential.helper=osxkeychain`, a `core.editor` or `core.pager` naming a
program, plain aliases without shell syntax) passes those rules and is not
carried into the run's file (the helper is), and only a repository's own
local configuration is held to the allowlist; an ordinary clone's is data
keys and remote URLs.
`scripts/private_cache.py`'s tree rule refuses a POSIX access
ACL, or a directory's default ACL, that lets anyone but this user or root
write anywhere in a pinned checkout, so the check of an existing checkout before
anything is built in it refuses one (it had judged mode bits only, and the
default ACL opened what the build created until the post-build check).
After the check passes, the rest of the attested
run, every leg included, runs under umask 077. The check still judges the
state when it runs: a mode a program sets explicitly past that umask (a
build script's `chmod`) is not judged. Not judged: what a
judged program loads from outside those trees (gcc's own helpers, shared
libraries below root-owned directories), including what a judged program
makes of a plain later word of a git command key by its own rules (an option
that selects a file or directory of the program's choosing, such as a login
shell's `-l` reading `~/.profile`, or a credential helper's own
configuration under `$HOME`: the check reads the words' text, not each
program's grammar), such as a git a judged program starts by its own option
in a directory outside every judged work tree (`env -C /abs/dir git ...`:
the directory is judged as a tree, but the configuration of the repository
git finds from there is not held to the allowlist) or under another name, or
in a bare repository nested in a judged work tree that is no `.git` (`env -C
<word>.git git ...`; neither git status nor Lake uses one); the keys of a
repository holding another directory with a `.cargo` Cargo reads (the Cargo
configuration check runs `git ls-files` there, now with `core.fsmonitor` off
on its command line, so it runs no configured program; `$HOME` is no
repository on this host); a git another tool starts in a repository none of
the rules above reaches (Lake's in a package outside a judged work tree, for
instance); what an ssh configuration names (its programs, such as
`ProxyCommand`, an `Include` from outside `~/.ssh` and `/etc/ssh`, and a
relative name in them, resolved in ssh's working directory: git's, or the
candidate checkout for `soundness_remote.sh`'s own ssh in a full-scope run),
which is out of the check's scope by ruling OD-XHOST-GATE-CWD-20261025, not a
gap it claims to close: ssh's configuration files are judged as files, and a
program they name is the user's own choice inside LD-73's host trust
boundary, not one of the programs git or a configured command runs that the
attested gate claims to judge;
an absolute program a judged `--git-repo`'s git starts from outside the
judged trees; the `core.worktree` of a local remote and of a submodule git
directory no populated path uses (git uses no work tree there during the
run; a local remote that is also a populated submodule, or any other
repository git uses a work tree of, has it judged as that one's); a
repository-local `GIT_*` variable a git newer than the supported
versions adds, outside an attested run (the attestation tool's subcommands
clear the fixed list; an attested run refuses every other `GIT_*`
variable); an import hook that root-owned site code installs, and where it
loads from; the working directory of a python3 a leg starts with `-c` or
`-`; macOS extended ACLs, group
membership granted outside the account databases, and the bash and python3
that started the run, which ran before any check (with the caller's
environment as bash read it before its first line: `BASH_ENV`, `SHELLOPTS`,
exported functions, which the scrub refuses for the re-executed run). A
host whose `soundness-deps` an earlier run left `0775` fails
the attested gate's preflight until its owner runs `chmod go-w` on that
directory; a checkout created before the umask-077 rule is refused until it
is removed (`git worktree remove --force`), since a `chmod` cannot undo what
another user may have written into it while it was open. Owner and mode
bits cannot show such an earlier write in a tree its owner has since made
private entry by entry. That rule judges canonical paths, so each script resolves a checked
path once and then uses only the canonical path it checked, as trust-cg's
own AY copy does: the soundness gate's checkouts and Clean binary, the icmp
gate's slots and binaries, and the AArch64 arithmetic runner's AY copy, which
it also holds to the ancestor rule itself. A cache reached through a symlink,
even one in a directory others can write, is therefore used where the
symlink led when it was checked, and re-pointing the symlink afterwards
changes nothing that runs (before 2026-10-15 the soundness gate ran Clean,
and the icmp gate its tools, by the symlinked name, so another user could
substitute them). `soundness_remote.sh` enters the executor's clone once,
by its physical path; it does not judge that clone's privacy (the executor
is trusted to run its legs; SOUNDNESS_CHECK.md). `soundness_remote.sh`
refuses a `SOUNDNESS_X86_REMOTE_DIR` (or any remote argument) with a
character outside `[A-Za-z0-9 ~/._+,:@=-]`, because the executor's login
shell may be a POSIX shell that reads bash's `$'...'` quoting differently.
The umask does not govern two
cases. First, a file a build step copies keeps its source's mode: Clean's
build copies three zstd-sys headers into its `target/` as `0644` (measured
2026-10-03), and trust-cg's own lock, which the x86-64 legs build, has the
same crate. Such a copy carries no write bit its source lacks and sits below
`0700` directories. Second, in a directory with a default POSIX ACL, what
git, tar or Cargo create directly follows the ACL. The scripts' helper
removes the default ACL that each directory it creates inherited (Linux
only; it removes no macOS ACL), but a directory that already has one keeps
it. Neither case makes an ancestor of `ay-exec` writable by another user.
Unit tests
of `trust-cg-verify` write no solver-identity memo unless
`TCG_PROOF_CACHE_DIR` names one. The memo is read only from an owner-private
canonical directory and an owner-private (`0600`) file; a memo another user
could write (this host's legacy `solver-identity-v1` is `0664`) is ignored,
not trusted, and the identity is hashed afresh (LD-68). The opt-in JIT
IR-text disk cache (`TRUST_CG_JIT_DISK_CACHE`) is used only from an
owner-private canonical directory, and an entry counts only when its HMAC
under that directory's owner-private seal key verifies (LD-67); the key
reaches its name only whole, so concurrent first openers share one key
(LD-72). A `trust-cg` cache
directory that an earlier build or script created under umask `0002` (`0775`),
or a cache placed under any group-writable directory, refuses AY in every
process until
its owner runs `chmod go-w` on the directory the refusal names or selects
another `XDG_CACHE_HOME`. Proof-required compiles then fail closed, and when
the build records an AY (a Trust toolchain build) their refusal carries
`TCG-AY-IDENTITY-UNMATERIALIZED`: the refusal of the function-verification
request the refused evidence came from, resolved once when that request was
captured, never resolved again at the refusal (LD-66). A compile request
that demands Formal strength is refused before any function is verified,
with `proof_strength_unavailable`; since ruling OD-XHOST-STRENGTH-NOTE-20261016
(2026-10-16) that refusal, and the no-solver disclosure
(`trust-cg.assumption.no_solver_available`) of the request's evidence
summary, carry the AY refusal of the one resolution of the proof route that
decided them (`the proof route was resolved with no AY admitted, ...`, with
the code, the directory, its mode and the remedy); before it, both named no
cause (the fifth closure audit). When no capable Clean checker is found, the
route is refused before AY is resolved, and those two name no AY refusal. A
CEGIS-enabled
compile's `CegisIncomplete` refusal still carries a resolution made when it
refuses, and CEGIS's own solver calls resolve AY per call, so with a cache
path another user re-points in between, that note can differ from what the
calls saw. A stock build records no AY and its refusal text is unchanged. A host where AY was refused this way also skipped the
solver-coupled `trust-cg-verify` unit tests; once AY runs, 62 of them fail on
AY capability gaps (mostly AY's own strict-certification refusal,
`(incomplete self-check-rejected)`), as they do on any host where AY runs, and
one (`test_ay_batch_verify_all_categories_comprehensive`) exceeds a 600 s
bound. Only the Linux root floors (AArch64 and x86-64,
`--require-proof-tools`) ask the rule before their
targets; the rustc-bridge lanes and the Darwin floor still learn of it only
from their failing targets.

The installed Trust pack 9192 ships AY build 9624 and a `bin/clean` built
without `carcara-verify`. That pack cannot pass `proof_gate_strict`'s formal
tests. A local overlay toolchain (`scripts/assemble_trust_overlay.py`, see
SOUNDNESS_CHECK.md) can stand in until a pack ships newer tools. All figures
below were measured on one arm64 Mac on 2026-09-29, with the gate's argv
(`test --locked -p trust-cg-verify --test proof_gate_strict -- --show-output`,
`TRUST_CG_RUN_FORMAL_PROOF_TESTS=1`) and a fresh cache per run. Each overlay
is pack 9192 plus a local AY and Clean, both built unverified from local
branches that are not upstream, except the last four rows, all at trust-cg
origin/main: in the first (2026-10-08), AY and Clean are built unverified from
the upstream commits Trust main pins (T8); the second (2026-10-08) keeps that
AY and takes Clean main a5d3fe0df (the `drup` fix below), which Trust main
does not pin yet; the third (2026-10-09) keeps that Clean and takes AY main
8aeefcb214 (the coroutine paragraph below); the fourth (2026-10-09) keeps that
AY and takes Clean 425bf736d, the commit Trust main pins since c2f0c1b312
(Trust's pin 08084daa0 plus cherry-picks of a5d3fe0df and 1077d4058; its
`third-party/carcara` is byte-identical to Clean main 1077d4058's).

| Overlay (AY build / Clean) | Tests passed | Formal tests | `full_database` |
|---|---|---|---|
| AY 57a37e513 (11377) / Clean 5390f432b, the pair Trust main pins | 34 of 36 | 14 of 16 | 2296 of 2503 |
| + AY 0b670d840 (11378), `bvashr` fill | 35 of 36 | 15 of 16 | 2307 of 2503 |
| + Clean bb955d2c9 (AY 11379), `and`/`or_simplify` | 36 of 37 | 15 of 16 | 2315 of 2503 |
| + AY c66287d91 (11380), bit-vector `poly_simp` judge | 36 of 37 | 15 of 16 | 2381 of 2503 |
| the same overlay, branch rebased onto origin/main 6ce36a21b | 36 of 37 | 15 of 16 | 2397 of 2503 |
| + AY 6baa59c94 (11381), complete-blast transport, branch rebased onto origin/main 48e674d51 | 37 of 38 | 16 of 17 | 2415 of 2503 |
| + AY 26cb9b455 (11383), `bvurem` blast up to 32 bits, branch on origin/main abd26b65e | 37 of 38 | 16 of 17 | 2415 of 2503 |
| AY 01b5801207 (12775) / Clean 0c59422f6, the pair Trust main pins, trust-cg origin/main 0215f1ab5 | 36 of 39 | 15 of 17 | 2503 of 2504 |
| AY 01b5801207 (12775) / Clean a5d3fe0df (main, drup fix), trust-cg origin/main b4da4cb65 | 38 of 39 | 16 of 17 | 2504 of 2504 |
| AY 8aeefcb214 (13028) / Clean a5d3fe0df, trust-cg origin/main 1cb64760a | 39 of 39 | 17 of 17 | 2504 of 2504 |
| AY 8aeefcb214 (13028) / Clean 425bf736d (Trust main's clean pin), trust-cg origin/main 1cb64760a | 39 of 39 | 17 of 17 | 2504 of 2504 |

In each of the first seven runs, the one failing formal test is
`full_database`. In the first run, `wired_checked_overflow_bindings` also
failed (Clean rejected its CheckedSmul_I64 row at `bitblast_ashr`). The 37th
test, `overlay_build_checks_proofs_only_with_its_own_clean`, was added in the
third run, and the 38th, `a_real_proof_check_records_the_tools_that_ran`, in the
sixth. Each fix moved exactly the rows of its class, and no other row changed
class. `AtomicRmwCasLoop_Or_I64 updates memory` went from `incomplete
self-check-rejected` to Verified in the third run because of Clean's
`or_simplify` fix. The gate first sends the obligation's array-lowered QF_BV
query (`generate_lowered_queries`), and falls back to the exact QF_ABV query
only when that query fails. AY 11378 proves the lowered query. Clean
5390f432b rejects its certificate at an `or_simplify` step, and Clean
bb955d2c9 fully verifies the same certificate. The fallback query is the one
the corpus dump holds. AY 11377-11381 all answer `unknown` for it
(self-check-rejected: a `trust` step), and that answer was the one the gate
reported until the lowered query verified.

- **`bvashr` overshift fill** (11 rows, fixed in AY): AY spelled the fill as
  `false`, but Clean's Carcara checks the sign bit.
- **`and_simplify`/`or_simplify`** (7 rows, fixed in Clean): the one argument
  left was itself an `and`/`or` application equal to the result, and Carcara
  compared it against the result's arguments. Clean now accepts that form. It
  is a completeness extension, sound because the rule only drops identities
  and duplicates.
- **Bit-vector `poly_simp` judge** (66 of the 113 `incomplete proof-trusted`
  rows, fixed in AY): the complete bit-blast rendered these rows, but AY's
  printed-arithmetic judge read a `poly_simp` between two of the blast's own
  bit-vector definitions as distinct atoms and turned the lemma into a hole.
- **Rebase** (16 `incomplete proof-trusted` rows, the WebAssembly narrow i8
  and i16 rows): main's 8d85bf68f retries a query the checker cannot replay
  with its derived bit-vector operators spelled by their SMT-LIB definitions.
- **Complete-blast transport** (18 `incomplete proof-trusted` rows, fixed in
  AY 6baa59c94): 13 products by a power of two and the subtractions around
  them (`x * 4/8/17/31`, the `MUL #4`/`#8` peepholes, `Sub_Lsl_Shift` I32 k=1
  and 16 and I64 k=1, 24, 32 and 40, `ConstMul_Shift_Sub_I64 a=5`), and 5
  extract, insert and shift rows at 32 and 64 bits (UBFM extract w32 and w64,
  the BFM Wd insert, WebAssembly `i32.shr_s` and `i64.shr_s`). Input clauses
  that print a literal under two `not`s
  forced the transported refutation onto binary steps, and for
  `x * 4 == x << 2` the document crossed AY's 76 MiB budget. Those clauses are
  now re-spelled once, with `contraction` and `not_not`, and the chains are
  `:args` steps. Separately, AY's SAT engine answered `unknown` for some blasts
  because its `backbone` pass emitted a hint-less LRAT step. That case is now
  retried without inprocessing. For the 31 rows of the previous run, the
  corpus harness now renders 13 certificates (it rendered 1), and Clean
  bb955d2c9 fully verifies all 13. The gate resolved 18: the harness reads
  only the dumped exact query, and the gate's own path verified 5 rows whose
  dumped query the harness refuses.

On the pair Trust main pins, every one of the 88 rows the AY 11383 run left
open verifies: the 13 `incomplete proof-trusted` rows, the 71
`incomplete self-check-rejected` rows and the 4 timeouts. That run had no
counterexample, no hole, no self-check rejection and no Clean rejection. The
host's load average was 44 to 94 on its 18 cores (other builds) for the whole
run, and its three failures are:

- `x86_64: BSR_I64 (nonzero) == width-1-Ctlz` timed out at the 120 s budget,
  the one row of 2504 not verified. Alone with a fresh cache it timed out again
  at 120 s, and verified in 168.8 s with `TRUST_CG_AY_TIMEOUT_MS=1800000`,
  under the same load.
- `aarch64_eh_coverage_proofs_are_formally_verified`: the LSDA partition row
  timed out at that test's own 60 s budget. It verified inside
  `full_database` at 120 s, and alone in 111.2 s with a larger budget.
- `solver_capacity_pending_allowlist_is_narrow_unique_and_live`: the corpus
  had 2504 obligations and the test pinned 2503. 00bfd0bc6 added the ADDP
  (scalar, .2D) row without moving the pin; a name-by-name inventory diff
  across that commit shows it is the only change, and the pin is 2504 now.

Neither of that run's timeouts was the solver's, and neither was load: the
time went to Clean's check of AY's certificate. Measured per subprocess in CPU
time, with a fresh cache, `BSR_I64` was 9.3 s in AY and 148.6 s in `clean cert
verify-external` (a 17.6 MB certificate), and the LSDA partition row was 3.3 s
in AY and 106.0 s in Clean (10.4 MB). The cause was Carcara's `drup` rule, which
Clean vendors (`third-party/carcara/carcara/src/drup.rs`): its reverse unit
propagation rescanned the clause list from the first clause after every literal
it propagated, so a `drup` step whose N premises form one implication chain
cost O(N^2). Since AY d39838422a (2026-09-30) a transported resolution chain of
8 or more links prints as one `drup` step over the chain's clauses (the
`BSR_I64` proof has 63 such steps, of up to 16,769 premises), which is why the
LSDA test passed on 2026-09-29 and not after. Clean a5d3fe0df propagates
through occurrence lists in linear time, with the same verdicts. On the same
certificates it checks `BSR_I64` in 0.69 CPU-s (9.6e9 instructions retired,
against 1.49e12 for Clean 0c59422f6) and the LSDA partition in 0.48 CPU-s
(5.7e9 against 1.04e12).

Measured 2026-10-08 with that Clean (the table's 12775 / a5d3fe0df row: pack
9192, AY 01b5801207 build 12775, Clean a5d3fe0df built with `carcara-verify`,
fresh cache, the gate's argv, host load average 100 to 270 on 18 cores),
`full_database` verified all 2504 obligations in 2587 s (3620 s before the
fix): no counterexample, hole, self-check rejection, Clean rejection or
timeout, and `STRICT PROOF EVIDENCE: checked=2504`. The LSDA test passed. 38 of
the 39 tests passed. The one failure, `coroutine_frame_proofs_are_formally_verified`
(1 of its 2 rows), is the solver's budget at that test's own 60 s, not Clean's,
and not a counterexample (the test's soundness assertion passed). Measured alone
per subprocess with a fresh cache, its state-save row verifies in 3.4 s. Its
value-independence row (`CoroSuspend: state store preserves the yielded value
(disjoint slot)`) first sends the array-lowered QF_BV query, which AY decides
UNSAT in 73.7 CPU-s and then refuses at its own strict self-check (`step t1 uses
unsupported theory lemma kind Generic in strict mode`, answer `unknown
(incomplete self-check-rejected)`). The gate then sends the exact QF_ABV query,
which AY proves in 51.6 CPU-s with an 18.6 MB certificate that Clean fully
verifies in 0.48 CPU-s. At 60 s the lowered query runs out its deadline, and the
exact query fits only when AY has a whole core: alone (load average 57 to 71)
the row verified in 114.9 s, and under the gate's load the test verified one
row. Inside `full_database`, at 120 s per query, both rows verified. With
Clean 0c59422f6 this test passed in the run in the table and failed (1 of 2) in
a rerun at trust-cg 6a4088ea2. Measured 2026-10-09 (the table's last row: AY
8aeefcb214 build 13028, the same Clean, fresh cache, the gate's argv, host load
average 38 to 74), this test passed and so did all 39: `full_database` verified
all 2504 obligations in 2153 s, with `STRICT PROOF EVIDENCE: checked=2504` and
nothing holey, rejected or pending. AY now encodes an equality between two
offset words through one shared difference (AY's DR-30), so the
value-independence row's lowered query verifies and the exact query is no
longer sent: AY answers `unsat` in 1.9 to 2.1 CPU-s with a 25.4 MB certificate,
and Clean fully verifies it in 0.9 CPU-s (two runs each, load average 52 to
74; AY 43c531aead took 1.6 and Clean 0.6 at load average near 10). AY
43c531aead, with DR-30 alone, passed this test but lost one `full_database`
row (`NEON UdotV.4S lanewise-intent == D-pair per-lane u8-dot-accumulate
(faithful)`, 2503 of 2504) to AY 562aac51de's charge on the checker's sweep
envelope, which AY's DR-31 reverts.

Trust main still pins Clean 0c59422f6, which does not contain the fix, so a
toolchain built from Trust main reaches this result only after its Clean pin
moves to a commit that contains a5d3fe0df.

Registry Tier-0 and live-promotion memos bind favorable results to the owned
query and solver/checker environment used for their discharge. Portable DRAT
results retain separate checker authority and do not acquire AY reuse receipts.
Whole-function JIT cache consumers now pass one captured request through worker
verification and require an immutable matching request/input report at lookup
and insertion. This binds cache attribution, not source-to-installed-bytes
correctness or certified publication (the separate installed-artifact replay
of `L11-P2`, above, re-reads each published mapping, warm hits included). Executable identity checks also do not
pin an image against an arbitrary filesystem replacement-and-restoration race.
On AArch64 the same-process CachedVerified warm hit, function-name binding,
raw-versus-source-bound separation, a source-swapped report and stale-source
refusal run by default (`jit_cert_cache_identity_aarch64` and the in-crate
`exhaustive_stale_source_and_raw_none_never_reuse_a_source_bound_verdict`)
over an exhaustively checked `zext i8 -> i32`. Relocation-name binding is
pinned only at the verifier-input digest the cache key carries: since E0.2
the raw tail call's `B` row is instruction-derived and not credit, so its
certificate is unverified and CachedVerified stores no verdict for it (no
symbol-bearing AArch64 instruction has a credit route). Five receipts planted
under the victim's exact key (none, foreign request, wrong input, wrong
architecture, non-reusable) are refused by the in-crate
`planted_receipts_under_the_victim_key_are_never_served`. They still need the
discovered AY/Clean authority for outer-cache identity and fail without it.
The formal-frame `JIT_SOURCE_NATIVE` campaigns stay opt-in. On the Mac
development host (2026-09-29, with an overlay AY/Clean pair that discharges
the frame query) they authenticated their tools and then refused the constant
function `answer` on its `MOVZ`, which E0.2 had left without a credit route.
The 2026-10-03 constant owner changes that route, but these opt-in campaigns
have not been requalified here; their earlier failure remains historical
(record).

## trust-ir coverage

The canonical machine-IR's legacy allocators remain infallible in signature,
and most callers still use them, but they are admitted (L10-P5): a stale or
exhausted register, instruction, block, stack-slot or jump-table counter is
refused by name at the instruction-selection exit, at the pass manager's
entry and exit, at each pass's first allocation and at the codegen phase
boundaries, and the allocators saturate instead of wrapping. This is a
refusal boundary, not a repair or a transaction: a refused function is not
emitted, and a refusal at a phase boundary does not roll back that phase.
Within one pass, an ID written by hand after the pass's first allocation and
then issued again by the same pass is not detected, and a pass that numbered
IDs by hand and then raised the counter past them itself would hide a counter
left stale before it (SROA did; it now allocates its planned range first).
That new IDs come only from the allocators is checked by tests on generated
and corpus functions, including far and near-miss stale counters before each
allocating pass, not proven for every pass. Provenance maps passed beside a function are not admitted, and
memory exhaustion is not handled. The x86-64 path is not admitted at all: its
passes run on `X86ISelFunction` (the x86 pass manager reports
`id_admission: Ok` unconditionally), and several of them still number
registers by hand from `next_vreg`. Required stack-guard
admission rejects invalid reservations before frame edits; this does not make
the entire frame-lowering pass transactional.

The accepted trust-ir surface is incomplete. Important gaps include:

- complete aggregate, record, enum/union, vector, sequence, closure, and
  reference-counted-value semantics;
- full constant, global, relocation-bearing initializer, TLS, and zero-fill
  handling;
- complete calls, indirect calls, casts, pointer provenance, atomics, memory
  ordering, volatile access, allocation/deallocation, and lifetime operations;
- complete dialect, parser/binary, proof metadata, source provenance, and
  interpreter parity; and
- uniform ABI/layout handling for every accepted type at every function
  boundary.

`Inst::MakeAggregate` lowers for struct, tuple, record, array and supported
native enum values. Construction fills fresh storage at authoritative offsets;
inactive fields and padding are not manufactured. Direct-tag enums use their
checked discriminant/descriptor image; single-variant untagged enums use their
checked payload layout. Niche-tagged variants store their reserved lane, while
a runtime untagged constructor requires independently derived typed payload
validity disjoint from that range. Unconstrained integer/raw-pointer niche
payloads remain refused. Variant-dependent niche offsets require an exact
untagged payload carrier, full field-range validation, and unambiguous typed
projections; new floating/vector carrier classes remain unqualified. The
[actual Result regression](crates/trust-cg-codegen/tests/result_aggregate_native.rs)
runs complete source-derived pointer/error and nested enum/str payloads,
overlapping stores, signed tags and typed Bool niches at O0/O3 on Darwin ARM64.
These are implementation tests, not Rust ABI, SourceNoUB or kernel proofs.
`CastOp::Transmute` lowers as an equal-size reinterpretation only where
trust-ir's own layout evidence answers `SameSize`: a same-width scalar pair in
registers, every other shape through a store/load slot. It stays refused by
name for unequal sizes, bool/char/reference/`Rc`/function-pointer/fat-pointer/
enum/record/closure/refinement/handle leaves, a source with padding bytes, and
a struct whose emitted layout differs from its declared one. Both lowerings
are testing evidence only: native O0-O3 runs on aarch64-apple-darwin
([construct sweep](crates/trust-cg-codegen/tests/e2e_aarch64_construct_sweep_casts.rs))
against the pinned reference interpreter and C models. That interpreter
executes the `Transmute` spelling only over integer/pointer scalars, so the
other shapes are checked against its `Bitcast` or store/load twin. trust-ir's
lowering-target subset still excludes `MakeAggregate` and non-scalar
`Transmute`, a `MakeAggregate` module has no tMBC wire image (it is never
cached, and Core admission refuses it), and no per-construct proof obligation
exists for either. Without that image `CompileService` refuses every
`MakeAggregate` module by name (`compile.identity_input`), for object and
executable-memory artifacts alike, so that lowering is reachable only through
the direct `Compiler` entry points. Both lowerings live in the shared
adapter, so they also compile for x86-64 and Linux AArch64, where no native
test has run them.

The Rust bridge's native lowering repairs (scalar unions, thin-pointer loops,
trait-object pointers and upcasts, slice-tail structs, TypeId constants,
ControlFlow residuals, closure wrappers, uninhabited arguments, try_fold
returns, zero-sized Drop, trait-object memory leaves, tuple/cleanup flags,
wide-pointer newtype reads, f16 pointees, wide scalar-pair arguments, 128-bit
atomic loads, carrying multiply-add, reference-to-wide-pointer returns and
formatter reference cells) are each recorded, with the full-`core` diagnostic
root count of its run, in their own `reports/perf/2026-09-2*` report. The
[maximal-suffix record](reports/perf/2026-09-27-maximal-suffix/README.md) is
the first frozen Linux AArch64 core diagnostic object build that exits 0 with
no failing roots; it is an object build, not a sysroot rebuild. Later records
still report failing roots in the optimized-core and std censuses
([core panic](reports/perf/2026-09-28-core-panic/README.md),
[projected aggregate borrows](reports/perf/2026-09-29-projected-aggregate-borrows/README.md)),
and CG-built core does not yet link every consumer
([core link](reports/perf/2026-09-28-core-link/README.md)). The proof-required
ABI test still fails TCG-PROOF-465 on uncovered AArch64 instructions. These
repairs are native diagnostics: their runs disable proof certificates and
frontend verification, and they grant no instruction proof or completion
credit; a certificates-on census, instruction proofs, the sysroot rebuild and
every product completion gate remain open. Pointers to struct chains ending in
a trait object are carried only for unpacked chains
([trait-object tails](reports/perf/2026-09-27-dyn-tail/README.md)); packed
chains, extra dereferences inside a projection, aggregate prefix loads and
stores, projected unsize destinations and dynamic-tail drop or cleanup stay
outside that lowering. On Linux AArch64, direct aggregate-returning calls with
live cleanup end in an `Invoke`
([residual conversions](reports/perf/2026-09-28-residual-conversion/README.md)).
The Linux aggregate bridge target requires three formerly refused shapes as
native positives against the LLVM twin at O0–O3: the trait-object leaf
cleanup control (`Holder::wrap`, whose closure returns a trait object while a
guard is live; once a `TCG-EH-CALL-EDGE` refusal), stores through a
transparent wide-slice newtype pointee, and 128-bit atomic stores and
fetch-adds, whose exclusive-pair loops are also inspected structurally. Shapes
the maintained bridge tests assert stay refused are 128-bit atomic
compare-exchanges, scalar f16 addition and load-return values, and zero-sized
Drop locals aligned beyond the frame's 16 bytes; a reference-to-wide-pointer
return that borrows a discarded call temporary also stays refused.

The Linux AArch64 rustc-private bridge now admits
[direct C variadic calls](reports/perf/2026-09-29-direct-c-varargs/README.md)
with promoted 32/64-bit integers, `f64` and thin raw pointers. It queries
rustc's call `FnAbi` for the actual anonymous types and preserves the fixed
extern declaration. The final merged LLVM/CG O0–O3 matrix passes 950,288
checks and 1,024 caught panics, including register/stack overflow, libc calls,
C-unwind cleanup and pointer mutation. Strict bridge checks pass; machine
proof admission still refuses with `TCG-PROOF-465`. Complete paired O2 std
censuses fall from 216 to 200 failed roots, removing 16 and adding none.
The subsequent [thin-reference extension](reports/perf/2026-09-29-variadic-references/README.md)
admits anonymous thin references with real referent storage and refuses
unresolved snapshot bindings. The combined matrix passes 1,982,480 checks and
2,048 caught panics, including pointer identity, shared `UnsafeCell` mutation
and writes observed by `Drop` during C-unwind cleanup. The paired O2 census
falls from 200 to 196 failed roots, removing those four reference failures
without adding or changing any remaining diagnostic. Wide references,
aggregate values, 128-bit values and nonempty indirect variadic calls remain
outside this path. Since 2026-10-15 (decision record LD-29) each such call is
judged by the whole-signature placement check, the declaration's fixed values
and the anonymous tail together against the call-site `FnAbi` (that whole-call
judgment is the only one such a declaration gets); before, that check skipped
C-variadic signatures, and an over-aligned scalar newtype as a FIXED argument
was a silent wrong value (it is now refused by name; see "Over-aligned C-ABI
ARGUMENTS on AArch64 ELF"). A call through a C-variadic `fn` pointer that
passes no anonymous argument is not this path: it is an ordinary `fn`-pointer
call whose pointer signature the same check judges; one that passes an
anonymous argument is refused by its argument count.

The [thin-reference call repair](reports/perf/2026-09-29-reference-call-storage/README.md)
extends stable referent storage to ordinary C/Rust and indirect call arguments.
It fixes the measured repeated-reference pointer-identity miscompile and adds
cell stores for discriminants, shared reborrows and exact-layout wrapper fields.
The combined LLVM/CG O0–O3 matrix passes 5,783,568 checks and 2,048 caught panics;
both O0/O2 CG-core/alloc mixed runtimes pass their native consumers. Strict bridge
checks pass, while machine-proof admission still refuses. Complete O2 std
censuses increase from 196 to 207 failed roots: two disappear, twelve newly
refuse unresolved reference storage, and one exposes an unsupported projected
zero-sized payload borrow in `ControlFlow<()>::eq`. That dated census also
identified shared trait-object coercions copying referents and changing pointer
identity. The source-audit follow-up now preserves known canonical cells/slots
and refuses unresolved shared coercions with `[TCG-DYN-REF-IDENTITY]`; equal SSA
values cannot justify inventing a new referent address. The subsequent
unsize-triggered pre-pass allocates canonical scalar/thin-pointer cells using
the existing layout and admission predicates, and borrowed aggregate fields
receive stable parent storage on both primary targets. Unsupported pointee
and alias shapes still refuse. These changes do not remeasure this std census.
Full CG std, self-hosting and performance superiority remain unfinished.

On Linux AArch64, selected call-exposed destructor-bearing owners whose complete
runtime image is a canonical pointer now use the existing checked scalar
frame home. Borrows observe that owner's actual address; reads, moves and
drop lowering use the same home. The
[Rc/Box call-reference regression](crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg/tests/owned_closure_drop_differential.rs)
requires eight native LLVM matches at O0–O3, with certificates off. Unresolved
referents retain `[TCG-REF-ARG-STORAGE]`, including the existing integer-drop
storage control. This bounded qualification does not establish other target
lanes or general layout, reference/provenance and FnAbi completeness.

**A celled field reference through an entry reference (x86-64, 2026-09-30).**
The unsize pre-pass cells the field reference derived `Debug` passes as
`&&self.last_field`, so `_n = &(*self).k` becomes a store through a deref
place. That store admitted a field address only for a primitive leaf or a
pointee `memory_aggregate_ref_pointee` routes, so on x86-64 macOS a pointer,
newtype or tuple field of a flat struct refused with `Place deref memory store
from Rvalue::Ref (projected source's base is not a reference to a
memory-eligible aggregate)` — `<core::ffi::va_list::VaListInner as
Debug>::fmt`, the one lowering root of the Darwin `core` O0 census on `main`
`73e5a69f5` — and a nested-struct field refused with `Ty::Adt multi-field
struct`. On x86-64 the store now holds `arg + rustc layout offset` when the
base is a thin `&T`/`&mut T` entry argument the body never rebinds and the
projection is a `Field` chain over a struct or tuple, and the address-only
store of a memory-eligible pointee's field is admitted on macOS as on Linux.
`m148_x86_entry_ref_field_addr_xback` checks pointer, newtype-field, tuple and
nested-struct fields, a write through a `&mut` field reference observed by the
caller, and the real derived and hand-written `Debug` output, in all four rlib
x bin cells at O0-O3 (`tests/tools/m145_xback.py --test`). Still refused: the
same store through a LOCAL reference (a call result, a reborrow) or through an
argument the body rebinds, and the new admission on AArch64, which no host here
executes. Opt out with `no-x86-entry-ref-field-addr` (and
`no-x86-thin-ref-aggregate-addr` for the address-only arm).

The Linux AArch64 [slice-tail from-end indexing repair](reports/perf/2026-09-29-slice-tail-from-end/README.md)
uses the pointer's length metadata when optimized MIR folds a slice borrow
into `(*r).tail[-k]`. The existing tail-place check binds that length to the
indexed slice and its rustc field offset. Native LLVM/CG O0–O3 comparisons
pass 391,424 new checks for reads, writes and returned addresses, including
nested sized prefixes and multi-element patterns. Further projection into
an indexed aggregate remains refused; the generic walker still refuses
from-end indices without their runtime length. Strict bridge coverage passes,
while machine-proof admission still reports `TCG-PROOF-465`. The complete
paired O2 std census falls from 219 to 216 failed roots: the three path roots
are removed, with no added roots or changed remaining diagnostics.
The [subsequent main alignment](reports/perf/2026-09-29-slice-tail-main-alignment/README.md)
repeats the native checks after the TrustIR and x86 verifier merges. It records
three reproduced pre-existing proof-test failures and one checker-identity
qualification refusal, alongside the passing Linux AArch64 checks.
The [final CSE/peephole reconciliation](reports/perf/2026-09-29-slice-tail-sync/README.md)
records the later x86 fixes, their focused checks and a fresh indexing run.

**Constant-index slice and array places** (2026-10-03, every target). A raw
borrow of a constant slice index, `&raw (*s)[k of n]` or `&raw (*s)[-k of n]`
(GVN's fold of a known index: `<[T]>::swap(0, i)` in core's `heapsort`,
`get_unchecked(1)` in `find_existing_run`; a slice-pattern binding cast to a
pointer), is the element address `data + k*stride`, from the end
`data + (len - k)*stride`, as the `&` borrow already was; `sort_unstable` at
O2/O3 and the corpus guest `p13_sort_std` compile and agree with LLVM. A
from-end index into a memory-backed slice is resolved against the slice's
runtime length when a whole aggregate element is copied out, its
discriminant read or a field of it borrowed, and `[.., last]` over
`&[&dyn Trait]` no longer reads element 0 at O1-O3 (it compiled and printed
the wrong element before). A whole aggregate element of a local array at a
GVN-folded constant index, an array's `[_, mid @ .., _]` sub-array in the
shapes the test covers, and a whole scalarized aggregate stored into a slice
element are lowered. Still refused by name (its review, 2026-10-04): an
array sub-array bound from a reference (`let [_, mid @ .., _] = a` with
`a: &[P; 5]` at O2/O3; `let [x, mid @ .., z] = &local_arr` at O1-O3,
"indexed memory place projection Subslice ... not supported"); a nested
constant index under a from-end one (`if let [.., [a, _, z]] = s
{ swap(a, z) }` on `&mut [[u16; 3]]` at O2/O3, "unsupported &raw shape");
and a from-end aggregate whose memory field projection is a constant index
(`[.., Some(x)]` over `&[Option<NonZeroU32>]` at O1-O3, `[.., l]` over
`&[Vec<i64>]` at O2/O3).
`crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg/tests/slice_constant_index_aarch64.rs` runs
108 guest x level cells over `i64`, `u8`, `(u32, u32)` and a struct against
LLVM, proofs off: 76 agree and 32 are refused by name. Still refused:
`<[T]>::sort`/`sort_unstable` over a non-integer element at O0/O1 and
`sort_by_key` over one at O2/O3 (at O0/O1 the guest's `sort` call is refused
first; the interception models integer elements only, while std's own
`sort_unstable` over a tuple or struct compiles and agrees at O2/O3), the
stable sort's `driftsort_main` at O2/O3 (`Vec::as_uninit_slice_mut`),
`select_nth_unstable` (core's `min_index` fold), and a field of a from-end
element reached through a slice-tail DST reference (`(*h).tail[-1].f`), whose
walk is not given the length.
FIXED 2026-10-08, two wrong orders in the slice-sort interception (measured
on trust-cg main `c279e5d5a` against LLVM): `__trustcg_vec_sort_*` compared
zero-extended elements with a signed `Sgt`, which for a 64-bit unsigned
element put every `u64`/`usize` value at or above 2^63 first (O0/O1, the
levels the interception runs at for these programs); and `sort_unstable_by_key`
was routed to the stable insertion sort used for `sort_by_key`, while std's
unstable sort may leave equal keys in another order (wrong at every level for
a `Vec<u64>`, at O0/O1 for a `Vec<u32>`). The helper now compares with the
element's signedness (`Ugt` for unsigned), and `sort_unstable_by_key` takes the
ordinary call path, so std's own body sorts it (it compiles and agrees at
O0-O3 for the `Vec<u64>` case; other shapes refuse by name at O2/O3, as they
did before). `sort_by_key` and plain `sort`/`sort_unstable` over integers
(equal elements are indistinguishable) stay intercepted. The 2026-10-09
integration keeps `sort_by_cached_key` on std's ordinary body as well;
the replacement cached insertion-sort model is removed, not qualified as
a performance improvement.
`crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg/tests/slice_sort_order_aarch64.rs`: 16 cells,
10 match LLVM, 6 refused by name, none wrong; each of its programs depends on
one of the two fixes, and the test fails with either one reverted.
FIXED 2026-10-08, a compile that never finished: `address_identity_referents`
(the ADDR-IDENTITY analysis behind `[TCG-ADDR-IDENTITY]`) propagates the places
each reference can address to a fixpoint, and a reborrow appends its steps to
its source's path. A loop that reborrows a slice by a sub-slice of itself
(`p = rest` under `[first, rest @ ..] = p`) appended them once per pass, so a
single such loop over a local array never finished compiling at any opt level
(trust-cg main `c5919a122`; LLVM compiles it in 0.6 s). Derived paths are now
capped at 24 elements; a longer one becomes one saturated place distinct from
every real one, and its base is reported as needing real storage, so the cap
can only add storage, never remove it.
`crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg/tests/subslice_loop_compile_bound_aarch64.rs`:
four loop shapes (one loop, four loops, a swapped pair, nested rows) x O0-O3,
every cell compiles within 120 s and matches LLVM.
REMOVED 2026-10-08, the `[TCG-FMT-LEN]` refusal: every integer `format!`
placeholder whose value derived from a length (`println!("{}", v.len())`,
`String::len`, `&str` lengths, length arithmetic) refused, at -O0 and often at
-O3. It was added for a `str::len` value the format emitter read from an
unwritten slot; that cause was fixed at its source two days later and never
re-measured. Removing it exposed one live miscompile, the
`ChunksExact`/`RChunksExact` cursor layout (fixed under OD-169). Measured on a
246-program corpus x O0-O3 x panic abort/unwind (1968 cells) against LLVM,
main `65e816a73` vs this change: 495 match on both, 643 refused before and
match now, 830 refused on both, none wrong and none worse. `black_box` of a
`Vec` is no longer claimed by the Vec interceptor; BTreeMap and HashMap keep
the same claim (refused by name).

The Linux AArch64 [dynamic Fn argument repair](reports/perf/2026-09-29-fat-fn-arguments/README.md)
spreads length-metadata references and raw pointers through the virtual method's
checked `FnAbi` scalar-pair plan. It covers strings, slices, `CStr`, slice-tail
DST references and borrowed `Box<dyn Fn/FnMut>` calls, including a pointer/length
pair split between x7 and the stack. The new LLVM/CG O0–O3 matrix passes 67,696
checks and 9,216 caught panics. Concrete closure vtable/export ABI restrictions,
other aggregate tuple elements, indirect-return refusals and Box cleanup-edge
restrictions remain. Strict bridge coverage passes; machine proof admission
still reports `TCG-PROOF-465`. Full std and compiler completion remain open.

The Rust bridge's [const-evaluated allocation images](reports/perf/2026-09-20-frontend-global-images/README.md)
now use canonical byte arrays or packed byte/relocation structs with exact size
and source alignment. Fresh unwind globals validate, and native static-data
checks cover packed pointers, function pointers, self-cycles and mutable cells.
The [immutable-reference repair](reports/perf/2026-09-20-frontend-const-references/README.md)
uses canonical SymbolAddr constants after reconciling aliases and checking exact
emitted storage identity. All 38 fresh modules validate. Conflicting views,
interior/mutable references and unrepresentable images stay outside this repair.
Declared tuple global images now honor canonical offsets. A module carrying
v42 declared tuple layouts compiles natively only when every row EQUALS the
declaration-order layout the byte path emits (offsets, size, align; WS7.7);
a row that differs, such as rustc's reordered `(u16, u64, u8)`, is refused as
`DeclaredTupleLayoutDisagrees`, never substituted, and honouring reordered
tuples remains open. The wasm lane still admits only the flat
pointer-transport profile. These repairs establish neither reference validity
nor complete global/TLS support.
The [direct global-address leaf repair](reports/perf/2026-09-20-global-address-leaves/README.md)
now compiles nine aligned/literal/scalar/array address-return functions at O0/O1
with backend checks enabled. Native value/alignment/identity, ABI and exact ELF
CFI checks pass. Unwinding retains its frame-proof gaps.

First-class closures (`L05-P4`) lower only in the shape trust-ir G18-2
states: a `Constant::Closure` at `Ty::Closure` is the struct of its captures
in capture order with no code lane, and `Inst::CallIndirect` over a closure
callee is the direct call to the closure's static code identity with the
captures spread as leading arguments. That identity is read off the defining
literal through `Copy`/`InsertField` only; a closure that reaches an
application dynamically — a function or block parameter, a `Select`, a
projection out of an enclosing aggregate, a `Call` result or memory — is
refused by name because the value carries no runtime code pointer, and an
apparent or physical signature or calling-convention mismatch is refused
rather than reconciled. Closure, `FnDef` and `SymbolAddr` constants nested as
aggregate fields materialize; a `PhantomData` constant at `()` (trust-ir's one
spelling of `()`'s value, now that typed admission refuses `{ }` there) lowers
as the zero-sized value the empty aggregate did, and is refused at any other
type or as a field of a function-body aggregate constant (a `[(); N]` splat
and a global initializer's `()` field lower it to zero bytes), as
`Sequence`/`Set`/`Record` constants at
scalar-typed fields stay refused. The AOT
local-binding census counts a closure application to a bodied `Internal` or
`Private` body as a direct edge, so it meets the same Darwin AOT refusal as a
direct call. trust-ir's own codegen-intent validator still refuses every
closure application (no closure layout table exists at the pin), so this is
trust-cg's reading of the ratified spread ABI executed natively on Darwin
against the reference interpreter and a C model — not a trust-ir-certified
layout, and no proof obligation binds the spread call edge.

Sequences and boxed sets (`L05-P8`) lower through one backend-defined image
([`sequence_layout`](crates/trust-cg-lower/src/sequence_layout.rs)): trust-ir
states the length-prefixed packed form but no layout, so the `u64` header, the
element slots and the result-buffer ABI are trust-cg's own, not a
trust-ir-certified layout and not interoperable with another backend's
sequences. What executes natively on aarch64-apple-darwin and
aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu at O0-O3, against the trust-ir reference
interpreter and a C model: `Constant::Sequence` and
`Constant::Set` images of every admitted element type, collections as
parameters, block parameters, `Copy`/`Select` operands, call arguments
(including to C) and results, and `SeqMapAddK`/`SeqMapNot`/`SeqMap` as counted
loops, in straight-line code, loops (including a loop that keeps the previous
iteration's image live) and recursion, with a fresh cell per `SeqMap` element;
each run-time length witness is shown to trap on a C callee that breaks it
(`e2e_aarch64_sequences.rs`). What stays refused by name (`[TCG-SEQ]`):
`ExtractElement`/`InsertElement` over any sequence or set, including a
constant this backend materialized, because trust-ir's codegen gate names the
element op `UnlowerableForCodegen` (must-refuse row `sequence_element_op`);
every load, store, alloca, GEP, cast or arithmetic that spells a collection,
since trust-ir gives it no byte layout; a collection nested in another type;
`SetRepr::Bitset` (no universe is stated); a `Constant::Set` two of whose
elements store the same image (after narrowing to the slot width and rounding
to its precision, so `Int(-1)` and `Int(255)` repeat in an `I8` set);
elements other than `Bool`, 8- to 64-bit integers, `F32` and `F64`;
a collection result beside other results, from a variadic, indirect or
invoked callee, from a declaration or a body another object may replace
(`Weak`/`LinkOnce`, a definition preemptible under a shared-object relocation
model, or a weak definition dyld may coalesce, ODR or not), or whose length
is not one static count or one sequence parameter's count on every path; a
collection crossing a definition or call edge of any calling convention but
C; and every target but AArch64. A `WeakOdr`/`LinkOnceOdr` callee in an ELF
executable (`static`, `pie`), or a hidden one under `pic`, keeps its length:
its ODR promise lets the static link replace its body only with an equivalent
one. On AArch64 Linux GNU, `static`-model callers of a default-visibility one,
linked into an executable by the host `cc`, execute at O0-O3 with the object's
own weak definition and with an equivalent strong C definition that the link
keeps instead. A replacement that breaks that promise meets only the caller's
post-call header check below.
A C caller must size the result buffer from the published length; the callee
checks the length it returns but cannot check the buffer's capacity, and a
trust-cg caller's check of the returned header runs after the callee wrote, so
it detects but cannot prevent an overrun by a callee that broke its length. A
loop that produces a sequence per iteration allocates a fresh stack image per
iteration, released only at function return. The compile service's
exported-ABI classifier still refuses a collection at an exported boundary,
and modules carrying `SeqMap*` stay out of batch merges. This is execution
evidence, not a proof: no proof obligation binds the image, the loop
expansion or the result-buffer edge.

The Rust bridge now makes thin reference/raw-pointer address casts explicit
and routes pointer/integer casts through TrustIR's bare `Ptr` carrier. The
[retained cast regressions](reports/perf/2026-09-20-frontend-pointer-casts/README.md)
cover actual O0/O1 frontend output and twelve scalar native executions.
This supplies no pointer provenance, lifetime or dereference authority.
Integer-to-reference reconstruction remains refused. Complete aggregate-reference
semantics and pointer-validity/native composition remain open; pointee layouts
are not inferred from structural tuple equality.

`Inst::Dealloc` is refused on every public lowering entry, in every body
(licensed, claim-less or `Ungated`, and a body this backend skips rather than
lowers, such as an `AvailableExternally` definition), with `[TCG-DEALLOC]`
quoting trust-ir's own `UnlowerableForCodegen` finding: the entries that run
the codegen prerequisites consume it from `validate_module_for_codegen_with`,
and the validated strict entry, which reuses a complete `validate_module`
report instead, reads it from trust-ir's lowerability layer
(`codegen_lowerability_errors`). The instruction arm refuses too, as a
backstop no public entry reaches. It names only a pointer: neither the
allocator that owns the region nor the layout being released. trust-ir refuses
every `Dealloc` for codegen and says a backend must not recover either from
dataflow (G18-1, re-decided 2026-09-27, trust-ir `7b0947ee`; must-refuse row
`refuse/dealloc_instruction`), and this backend conforms: the lowering that
recovered both from same-function `HeapAlloc` sites (2887cbf01) is retired.
A release is spelled the way its runtime pins it: `Release` for a
reference-counted cell, or a call to the runtime's deallocation entry point
(`__rust_dealloc(ptr, size, align)`, `free(ptr)`) paired with its allocation
call, which is what the rustc bridge and Clean already emit. trust-ir states no
allocator layout for `HeapAlloc`; this backend sizes one by its natural-C LIR
type times the count, so a `HeapAlloc` result released by a hand-sized
`__rust_dealloc` call is sound only under that backend convention (the
allocator-balance controls pin it for `u64`, `u32` and `[u64; 3]` at align 64).
`SwiftHeap` and `CleanHeap` allocation stays refused: no Swift runtime is
modelled, and Clean cells are released by `Release` reaching zero.
Allocator-balance execution evidence with call-spelled releases exists at
O0-O3 on aarch64-apple-darwin; the ELF twin's object-level check runs on this
host, and its native run (Linux AArch64 only) predates the call spelling
([retained floor run](reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-integrated-gates-3/README.md),
which released through `Dealloc`).

x86-64 vector compares follow trust-ir's per-cell rule (`docs/dialects.md`,
trust-ir `7b0947ee`): every x86-64 module entry asks trust-ir's one reader,
`chc_x86_vector_icmp_cell_status`, and refuses an integer vector `ICmp` on a
cell the `chc_x86` manifest publishes as fail-closed
(`[TCG-X86-VECTOR-ICMP]`, `VectorCompareCellFailClosed`). At the pinned
trust-ir no covered cell is fail-closed: the four unsigned `<16 x i8>`
compares, the last ones, were published available at trust-ir `72dee4b6`, so
an x86-64 module entry admits all forty cells. The refusal therefore has no
real subject at this pin: its arm is tested over a synthetic reader that
answers a fail-closed cell, and module entry's call with trust-ir's reader is
pinned by a token scan (trust-cg-lower
`src/adapter_x86_vector_icmp_gate_tests.rs`; test rung, and the scan does not
show that every x86-64 entry reaches the call). trust-ir records the rule as
the `none` corpus row `refuse/vector_icmp_fail_closed_cell_x86`, and a cell
that turns fail-closed again (a changed query not yet re-certified) arrives
there with its status row and a module row. On x86-64 the unsigned compares
lower through a sign-bit-bias composition (SSE's `pcmpgt*` is signed;
`<2 x i64>` uses the SSE2 dword-halves sequence). An x86 ISel unit test
executes the `<16 x i8>` and `<8 x i16>` sequences on its own model of their
SSE2 opcodes (every `u8` pair, a boundary set of `u16` pairs), which checks
the bias and the operand order on any host; the two-address rewrite after
ISel and real x86 execution are not covered there, and the x86 JIT execution
tests are `cfg(x86_64)`. The function-level and LIR-direct entries
(`translate_function`, `compile_lir_*`) bypass the module-entry gate.
AArch64 has no bias composition: its ISel lowers the same compares to NEON
`CMHI`/`CMHS` directly, and it admits all forty cells. The available cells
rest on two named grounds: `eq`/`sgt` on the instruction model alone (their
registered obligation is degenerate by construction and certifies nothing),
every other available cell — the sixteen unsigned and the sixteen
signed-composite cells — on a certificate whose exact query digest
`trust-cg-verify/tests/x86_icmp_manifest_cells.rs` pins and which
`scripts/check_x86_icmp_certificates.py`, a leg of `scripts/soundness_check.sh`,
re-runs under trust-ir's rule as code (`CHC_X86_ICMP_CERTIFICATE_RULE`, read
through the compiled dependency): it builds the rule's AY (which must be the
pinned one) and the rule's Clean by revision, and requires `unsat` with
`unproved_steps=0`, no `hole` or `lia_generic` step, and Clean's `cert
verify-external` exiting 0 with the proof fully verified, per cell. That is a
checked SMT proof for each composition obligation, checked by the Carcara
Alethe checker inside Clean (unverified software with a documented record of
false accepts), not a Clean-kernel certificate and not a Lean theorem. It is
re-run only where the leg runs (nothing runs `soundness_check.sh` per landing
today), and it does not bind the obligation to the bytes ISel emits per
compile. Each cell's spec side is trust-ir's own bit-vector statement of the
compare (`trust_ir::chc_x86_vector_icmp_spec`, printed node for node by
`trust_ir_bv::SmtAlgebra`), held structurally by the manifest test; its tie
to trust-ir's `ICmp` semantics is trust-ir's tests, not a proof. Each cell's
machine side applies exactly the instruction models trust-ir publishes for it
(`native_instructions`, less the bias materialization, which stays outside
the certificate), and those models never route through the statement (a
token scan); the models themselves remain trusted. The
compiler's own admitted AY (the toolchain's 0.26.0, `075a482ae`) answers a bare
`unsat` on all forty queries but `unknown` under `--strict-proofs` on all 32
composite ones (measured 2026-09-29), so a compile cannot re-derive these
certificates. The unsigned certificates are on the per-lane spelling of the
sign-bit bias, the one the lowering materializes; from 2026-09-27 until the
pin move that adopted the rule as code they were on a two-64-bit-halves
respelling that worked around a tree-sized node cap in AY `f28345ff`'s
proof-producing checker, which AY has since fixed at the root.
A cell's feature guard is held at instruction
selection (`pcmpeqq` needs SSE4.1, `pcmpgtq` SSE4.2; the unsigned
`<16 x i8>` cells are baseline SSE2). `<8 x i8>` `eq`/`ne` on x86-64 is
lowered with no descriptor and no registered x86 obligation: an ungoverned
gap, not a grant.

Aggregate passing follows trust-ir `docs/SPEC_RATIFICATIONS.md` §17: under
`StructPassingPolicy::Unclassified` every native entry refuses a by-value
aggregate slot as trust-ir's ONE predicate (`Module::is_by_value_aggregate_slot`)
defines it — refined aggregates, vectors and closures included
(`TargetStructPassingUnclassified`); `AlwaysMemory` is refused outright (this
backend consumes no pre-lowered `byval` spelling) and a recorded
`ParamAttrs.pass` fact is refused as unconsumed surface. Under `NativeC` this
backend classifies by its own C register ABI. The rustc bridge, which stamps
`NativeC`, checks its placements against rustc's `FnAbi` for returns and for
arguments (`[TCG-RET-ABI]`, `[TCG-ARG-ABI]`); rustc's `FnAbi` source is a
required parameter of every such gate and of the call-argument builder. A
memory-placed Rust-ABI argument (rustc's `Indirect { on_stack: false }`) is
PRE-LOWERED on x86-64 and AArch64 (not Windows) — the indirect argument lane,
see "Cross-backend `Memory`-argument ABI" below — as an ordinary `Ptr`
parameter, which is not a by-value aggregate slot, and the gate compares that
pointer. Every other target is refused before any lane is placed
(`[TCG-AGGREGATE-ABI-SCOPE]`). One table decides every placement mode
(`abi_reg_lanes::arg_memory_placement_verdict`): a caller-made copy with no
lane, a `byval` copy off x86-64 System V and an ignored argument are refused by
name, and x86-64 System V `byval` (C-ABI only) is admitted as a MODE. That
per-argument table decides each argument's mode; WHERE every argument lands is
decided per SIGNATURE: the bridge runs rustc's backend value list (a `Pair`'s
two scalars, a narrow `Cast`'s one integer, an `Indirect` pointer, a `byval`
image of the value's size and alignment) and its own declared value list
through trust-cg's own classifier for the target (AArch64
`classify_params_with` with the target's variant; x86-64
`x86_sysv_param_locations`, the function both x86 selector sides call) and
refuses `[TCG-ARG-ABI]`, by name, any argument byte whose register byte or
stack byte differs — register numbering, exhaustion and stack offsets
included (`check_signature_placement`, for every declaration: bodies, callees,
`fn` pointers, the virtual lane and the `Fn`-trait dispatch spread). An
argument it cannot judge is refused, never passed, and there is no interim:
an `extern "rust-call"` function item or shim is declared with its argument
tuple's ELEMENTS, as rustc's `FnAbi` lists them (`rust_call_spread`), and is
compared like any other declaration. What
a pass establishes, and what it rests on: the declaration places every byte
where trust-cg's classifier places rustc's values — which is where LLVM places
them only if that classifier places rustc's value alphabet as LLVM does and
`rustc_backend_values` models `rustc_codegen_llvm`'s lowering of each
`PassMode`. Both premises are shared by the two sides of the comparison, so
their evidence is the cross-backend family matrix
(`tests/signature_placement_families_xback.rs`, aarch64 natively and x86-64
under Rosetta), TEST rung — the check turns "the matrix passed for these rows"
into "every declaration is compared"; it does not make the classifier right.
See "Register exhaustion" under Rust integration.

`Inst::Retain`, `Inst::Release` and `Inst::IsUnique` lower to calls of
`clean_inc`, `clean_dec` and `clean_is_exclusive` only when the module
declares exactly that Clean triple as bodyless externals; a missing, partial,
mis-typed or locally defined triple fails closed. Their native execution
evidence is Linux AArch64 only, at O0-O3, on `CMalloc`/`RustHeap` cells
against a C counting runtime that stands in for the Clean runtime. trust-ir
defines the three ops only on a `SwiftHeap`/`CleanHeap` cell (Lean's
`requireArcRef`, and the reference interpreter since trust-ir `25624afd`,
which this backend pins: it refuses the three on any other allocation as
undefined behaviour, "not a reference-counted cell", and a host-neutral row
checks that it refuses every row of the corpus as compiled), and this
backend refuses those cells, so the program that run executes is undefined
in trust-ir: it tests
the lowering against the driver's side-table model of the triple, not the
pinned runtime, and is no evidence that the program is defined. Its results
are compared with the trust-ir reference interpreter's on a twin of the
corpus whose cells are all `CleanHeap`; `arc_dealloc_at_one`, whose twin
frees a `CleanHeap` cell with `Dealloc`, is refused there as undefined and is
checked only against its closed form
([retained run](reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-arc-ops/README.md); it predates the
2026-09-27 change that frees the `arc_dealloc_at_one` cells by a call to
`__rust_dealloc` / `free` instead of `Inst::Dealloc`, and the twin, and has
not been re-run on a Linux host since). Correctness of the
runtime calls rests on the runtime that is linked, not on a proof: the
adapter emits no obligation for them and the bounded fsym preflight
classifies ARC ops as unsupported. `Ty::Rc` has no modelled ABI and stays
refused, as do `SwiftHeap`/`CleanHeap` cells and cross-function frees.

Borrows, binding frames and `Undef` (`L05-P9`) lower through one named
legalization stage, `borrow-frame-undef-legalization`
([`borrow_frame_undef.rs`](crates/trust-cg-lower/src/borrow_frame_undef.rs)).
It decides each function before any of its instructions is lowered. It runs
on every adapter entry, the strict one included, because it rewrites no
module. It records what was lowered in `ProofContext::borrow_frame_undef`,
which the retained strict-LIR identity hashes. That receipt grants no
authority, and no pass optimizes on it. Refusals carry `[TCG-BFU]`.

- `Borrow`/`BorrowMut` lower to a copy of the operand pointer, which is what
  trust-ir's interpreter returns, and `EndBorrow` lowers to nothing. Each
  borrow's root and kind are recorded. The adapter's validation tolerance
  does not refuse trust-ir's borrow-STRUCTURE findings, so the stage
  re-checks them. It refuses a `BorrowMut` of a `Ref`/`PtrConst` value or of
  a value that may be a shared `Borrow`'s result, an `EndBorrow` of anything
  but a borrow result, and a borrow of anything but a thin or fat pointer.
  A borrow of the statically null pointer (`NullPtr` or a zero pointer
  constant, through `Copy` and `PtrToPtr`) is also refused, because trust-ir
  makes it undefined behaviour. A pointer that is null only at run time is a
  copy like any other.
  Borrow LIVENESS (one `EndBorrow` per path, no two live unique borrows, no
  use after `EndBorrow`) stays the producer's obligation, as it is in
  trust-ir. The backend neither checks it nor derives an aliasing or
  validity fact from a borrow.
- Each `OpenFrame` gets one zero-filled stack slot, laid out from its slots'
  LIR carriers. `BindSlot` stores in place, `LoadSlot` loads, and
  `CloseFrame` emits nothing. In trust-ir `BindSlot` is functional: an older
  handle keeps its old slots. In-place storage matches that only while no
  superseded handle is live, so the stage checks this by SSA liveness over
  the frame handles, within each block and across every block edge, and
  refuses the function otherwise. The check is a static analysis exercised
  by tests, not a proof. It also refuses by name:
  - a handle used by anything other than `BindSlot`, `LoadSlot`,
    `CloseFrame` or a `Br`/`CondBr`/`Switch` argument (a call, return, store,
    copy, select, borrow or `Invoke` argument, for example);
  - a block parameter that merges a handle with a non-handle, or handles
    from two `OpenFrame`s;
  - a handle that reaches an entry-block parameter along a back edge (on
    function entry that parameter holds the caller's argument);
  - a slot type outside the scalar carriers (integers, pointer-width
    integers, `Bool`, `F32`/`F64` and thin pointers; `Char`, `F16`,
    fat-pointer, vector, aggregate, handle and refined slots are refused);
  - a slot index or type that disagrees with the frame definition;
  - a frame that no `CloseFrame` ends.
- The NoUndef model: an admitted scalar `Undef` is the all-zero bit pattern
  of its carrier (`0`, `false`, a null pointer or `+0.0`), and the unbound
  slots of a fresh frame read the same zeros. In trust-ir `Undef` is poison.
  Moving it around is defined, but inspecting it is undefined behaviour.
  The stage traces every poison value through `Copy`, `Select` arms, block
  arguments and frame slots. Poison values are each `Undef` and each
  `LoadSlot` of a slot that some path leaves unbound or binds to poison. If
  one reaches any other use, the function is refused. Other uses include
  arithmetic, a comparison, a cast, a branch, switch or select condition,
  `Assume`/`Assert`, a division, a call argument or return, a dereference,
  or a volatile or atomic store. An `Undef` consumed by arithmetic that the
  program then masks is therefore refused, not compiled; the reference
  interpreter faults at that arithmetic. One case is not traced: poison
  written to memory by a plain `Store`, loaded again and then inspected.
  That program has undefined behaviour in trust-ir and reads the zero the
  backend stored. This refines undefined behaviour; it does not agree with a
  defined result. Aggregate and vector `Undef` stay refused, because the
  pinned interpreter models scalar poison only. So do `Char`, `F16`,
  refined, fat-pointer and handle `Undef`, any `Undef` that carries a proof
  annotation, and a `FreshSymbolicHavoc`-marked `Undef`. That marker is a
  nondeterministic-choice marker outside the lowering-target subset
  (must-refuse row `undef_fresh_havoc_feeds_assume`, pinned by reason in
  `must_refuse_corpus`).

Execution evidence is on aarch64-apple-darwin only.
[`e2e_aarch64_borrows_frames`](crates/trust-cg-codegen/tests/e2e_aarch64_borrows_frames.rs)
compiles its corpus at O0–O3 and runs each of its ten functions on ten
inputs, thin and fat-slice-pointer borrows included. Every native value must
