No AArch64 function with a frame promotes today, so no certificate carries
the sentence end to end yet. The x86-64 certificates (ELF and Mach-O) do not
carry it at all, although their objects can contain frame CFI.

AArch64 ELF object emission takes an explicit relocation model
(`CompilerConfig::relocation_model`, `PipelineConfig::relocation_model`,
`trust-cg --relocation-model static|pie|pic`), recorded in the compile policy's
artifact projection and the artifact-cache identity. `static` and `pie`
currently select the same code: definitions are addressed PC-relatively,
imports through the GOT, and thread-locals use local-exec (definitions) or
initial-exec (imports). A `static`/`pie` object that defines a thread-local
therefore cannot go into a shared object. GNU ld 2.42 links it anyway, and
on the Linux host that library read and bumped the executable's own
thread-local instead of its own, so `link_driver::run_link` (the CLI's link
step) refuses the input by name before a `--shared` link runs, and removes and
refuses the output of any other link with such an input unless the linker
wrote an executable or a relocatable object (see the link diagnostics
paragraph below). `pic` loads the address of every default-visibility,
non-local definition from the GOT, keeps calls to them as `CALL26` relocations
for the linker's PLT, never inlines a preemptible function, and reaches every
thread-local through a TLS descriptor (TLSDESC; local-dynamic reuses
general-dynamic). The descriptors of a strong hidden thread-local definition
name an object-local anchor at the definition, as GCC's section anchor does,
so no linker lists it in a shared object's `.dynsym`; named by its global
hidden symbol, gold lists it there as `TLS LOCAL HIDDEN` (not exported). gold
still does so for a hidden thread-local that some object references by that
symbol: a weak definition (which a strong one elsewhere may replace, so it is
never anchored), a declaration, or a GCC object's `extern` one. Hidden,
protected and Internal/Private definitions are not
preemptible. Under `pic` the adapter addresses hidden, protected and
Internal/Private data and functions PC-relatively in every address form
(`GlobalAddr`, the importer's global-address stub, `FnDef`, a capture-free
closure and a function-body `SymbolAddr`, with or without an offset), and
calls to them bind at link time without a PLT entry. For Internal/Private
functions this holds on AArch64 ELF and, under the `static` model (the only
one Mach-O implements), on AArch64 Mach-O (see the function-binding
paragraphs below): every other object path still refuses a direct call to one
(`AotDirectModuleFunctionBindingUnsupported`) and a materialized address of
one (`AotStaticFunctionIdentityBindingUnsupported`). Under `pic` a strong or ODR
hidden or protected function may be inlined and grant purity. A
`Weak`/`LinkOnce` one may not, since another object may replace it at static
link. `RelocationModel::symbol_address_is_got_indirect` decides the address
form of definitions and declarations for the adapter and the emitters'
relocation-model check, and preemption for the module inliner and structural
purity (through its definition case, `definition_is_preemptible`). Every
declaration, hidden and protected ones included, is addressed through the
GOT under every model. An absent weak reference must read 0, which no
PC-relative form yields in a PIE or a shared library. A hidden or protected
declaration's definition in the same output may be a GNU IFUNC, and GNU ld
2.42 (PIE, static PIE, shared object) and gold (PIE, shared object) resolve
a PC-relative reference to one to its PLT stub while GOT slots and data
words hold the resolved function. Calls to a hidden or protected
declaration bind without a PLT entry. A hidden or protected DATA declaration
(a data import) is addressed through the GOT for the same reason: its name
may be a GNU IFUNC function defined in the same output, and a PC-relative
form then reads the IFUNC's PLT stub with GNU ld (PIE, static PIE, shared
object) and gold (PIE, shared object), as GCC 13.3's `extern` hidden array
form does. The emitters refuse a PC-relative page reference to a weak
undefined symbol, or to a declared function or data import with a stated
visibility, under every model; a default-visibility declared function's
PC-relative address is still admitted under `static` and `pie`, as before. `definition_is_link_replaceable`
decides static-link replacement for the module inliner (AArch64, x86-64 and
RISC-V objects, whose writers bind `Weak`/`LinkOnce` definitions weak; the
x86-64 COFF emitter refuses them) and structural purity (every target). Protected data is PC-relative as in LLVM,
not GOT-addressed as in GCC 13. On the Linux host GNU ld 2.42, gold and
LLD 22 all refuse the copy relocation an executable would need to move it,
and GNU ld resolves a protected symbol's GOT slot with `R_AARCH64_RELATIVE`
anyway. LLD's `--ignore-data-address-equality` turns its refusal into a
warning: it makes the copy, and a `--no-pie` program that sets the variable
read back 97 where one variable gives 99 (the second verifier of the tenth
closure audit's repair, 2026-09-26). The driver refuses that option on
Linux (`[TCG-LINK-COPY-RELOCATION]`, below), so through `run_link` the
three linkers do refuse the copy. An executable linked against an older default-visibility build still copies the word at
load time: glibc 2.39 only warns, and the library then reads its own copy
whichever form it uses. A protected function definition's address is
PC-relative too, and a protected declaration's comes from the GOT. GNU ld
and LLD refuse the canonical PLT entry a non-PIE executable taking it
needs (LLD's `--ignore-function-address-equality` turns that refusal off,
and the executable's and the library's addresses of the function then
differ; the driver refuses it with the data option). gold links such an
executable without a canonical address (its `.dynsym` value is 0) for any function a shared library defines, default
ones included, so the executable's and the library's addresses differ
whatever form either object uses, as they do for GCC-built objects. With
gold, an absent weak hidden function reference in a PIE or a shared library
also reads the load base instead of 0 (gold exports it to `.dynsym`, and
glibc resolves a hidden symbol to its own image), for GCC's GOT form as for
this backend's. gold 2.42 also links into a shared object a
position-dependent reference (`R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21` with
`R_AARCH64_LDST32_ABS_LO12_NC`, from a non-PIC object) to a
default-visibility variable the object defines, binding it locally without
a diagnostic, where GNU ld and LLD refuse it ("recompile with -fPIC"). A
`--no-pie` executable that copies the variable then writes its copy while
the library's code reads its own (measured 132 where one variable gives
99). Since 2026-10-24 (L02-P2 closure audit) `link_driver::run_link`
refuses that link on every linker, by name and before the linker runs
(`[TCG-LINK-PREEMPTIBLE-DIRECT]`, `link_driver::direct_address_refusals`):
a direct-address relocation (the `ADRP`/`ADR`/`ADD`/`LDST` lo12, `MOVW`,
literal, 16/32-bit data, GOT-relative and conditional-branch kinds, and the
local-dynamic TLS kinds) in an allocated section of a positional AArch64 ELF
input, against a symbol that input binds non-local with default visibility
and no relocatable input gives a hidden, internal or protected visibility.
The conditional branches (`R_AARCH64_CONDBR19` for `CBZ`/`CBNZ`/`B.cond`,
`R_AARCH64_TSTBR14` for `TBZ`/`TBNZ`) and the local-dynamic TLS kinds
(`R_AARCH64_TLSLD_*`) have been refused since 2026-11-05 (the r1105
verifier, OD-SHARED-PREEMPTIBLE-BRANCH-TLSLD-20261105). Until then the
driver installed such a library on every linker. GNU ld 2.42 and gold 2.42
resolve a `CBZ` or `TBZ` to a default-visibility function the same
`-shared` link defines straight to that definition, with no PLT entry. They
also resolve a `DTPREL` offset of a default-visibility thread-local into
the library's own TLS block. Both export the name `GLOBAL DEFAULT`, so an
interposing `-rdynamic` executable's definition was ignored (7 where 55 was
expected). LLD 22.1.6 routes the branches through the PLT and refuses the
`DTPREL` kinds. Not refused, because every linker on the host honours the
loader's binding for them or refuses the link itself: `ABS64`, `CALL26`,
`JUMP26` and `PLT32` (GNU ld and gold 2.42 refuse `PLT32`, LLD routes it
through the PLT), and the GOT-slot, descriptor, initial-exec and
general-dynamic TLS forms. Local-exec TLS has its own refusal.
An input that reaches the link another way (a `-Wl` operand, a `-l`
library, an archive member, a linker script's `INPUT()`) is read from the
linker's input trace, and an image that is not a confirmed executable is
refused and removed. The refusal is deliberately conservative: a link
option that makes such a symbol non-preemptible (`-Bsymbolic`, a version
script that localizes it, `--exclude-libs`, `--dynamic-list`) does not lift
it. The linker's own `_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_`, `_DYNAMIC`, `__ehdr_start` and
`__start_<sec>`/`__stop_<sec>` are exempt (measured bound inside the output
by all three linkers when no link option or linker script names them), as
is a name another input hides or protects, but neither exemption is taken
from the name or the inputs alone (OD-SHARED-EXEMPT-NAME-REBINDING-20261024).
A `-Wl` option that can define, re-bind or redirect the name voids it before
the link: a `--defsym` of a linker-defined name (gold 2.42 then exports
`__start_<sec>`, `__stop_<sec>` and `__ehdr_start` `GLOBAL DEFAULT`, and
until the round-3 verifier the driver installed such a library, whose code
ignored an interposing executable's definition; a name another input hides
stays hidden, and exempt, under a `--defsym` of it), a `--wrap` of either
kind of name (the reference then binds to `__wrap_<name>`), a
`start-stop-visibility` other than `hidden`, `internal` or `protected`
(GNU ld and gold export the start and stop symbols `DEFAULT`), and a linker
script option, `--just-symbols` or any other piece whose bindings the driver
does not read, which voids every exemption. After the link a use still
exempt is refused when the image's dynamic symbol table exports its name
with default visibility (a linker script read as an input can assign it), or
when that table cannot be read. It
reads the symbol a relocation names, so an object that addresses a
default-visibility definition through a section or other local symbol is
not seen. GCC 13.3's `-fPIE` code addresses its own `int g` as `.data + 0`,
and so does its `-fno-pic -O1` code (`R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21` against
`.data + 0`, the r1105 verifier). GNU ld, gold and LLD all link either into
a shared object with `g` exported `GLOBAL DEFAULT` and bound locally, and
`trust-cg --shared` installed the `-fno-pic` one passed as a `-Wl` operand
(the route measured). An `-rdynamic` executable's `g` is then ignored by
the library's code.
trust-cg's own objects name the definition's symbol. The CLI's `--shared` without `--relocation-model` compiles AArch64 Linux
modules `pic` (OD-SHARED-PIC-DEFAULT-20261024), whose code addresses such a
variable through the GOT and whose module inliner keeps every
default-visibility definition preemptible. An explicit `static` or `pie`
there is kept, and the direct-address refusal alone did not cover it: those
models treat the module's own definitions as non-preemptible, so at O1-O3
the inliner splices a default-visibility function into its in-module
callers and leaves no relocation to refuse. GNU ld, gold and LLD all
installed such a library, and an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer of the inlined
function was ignored by the library's own callers (the round-2 verifier's
`callpre`, 10 where 80 is expected; in its random differentials 9 of 304
`static` libraries and 12 of 292 `pie` ones differed from a GCC `-fPIC`
twin under `LD_PRELOAD`). Since 2026-10-24
(OD-SHARED-NON-PIC-DEFINITION-20261024) the CLI states the model of the
objects it compiled (`LinkRequest::compiled_relocation_model`), and
`run_link` refuses a Linux shared-object link of `static` or `pie` objects
that define any symbol with default visibility no positional input hides or
protects, at every optimization level and on every linker
(`[TCG-LINK-PREEMPTIBLE-DEFINITION]`, `link_driver::non_pic_definition_refusals`;
before the linker, and after it for an image that is not a confirmed
executable); a module whose every definition is local, hidden or protected
still links. The same refusal covers the `static` objects of an x86-64 or
RISC-V Linux `--shared` link (the only model those targets implement). It
reads only the objects whose model the request states: an object linked in
from elsewhere (a `-Wl` operand, a library, a `run_link` caller that states
no model) is not examined for it. `link_driver::run_link` links with the C driver's default linker,
GNU ld on the Linux host. Default-visibility `Weak`/`LinkOnce` definitions and
their ODR forms are preemptible like `External` ones (the ODR forms may still
be inlined), and `ExternalWeak` references are GOT-indirect under every model.
The `Pipeline` emitters' `pic` check reads the per-function symbol bindings, so
a local, hidden or protected function binding may be addressed PC-relatively
in a `Pipeline` object (off AArch64 ELF the `Compiler::compile` refusals above
still apply to Internal/Private functions). The TLSDESC resolver call is
modeled with the conservative AAPCS64 clobber set, not the ABI's stronger
register-preservation guarantee. No obligation models the `R_AARCH64_TLSDESC_*`
relocations or the linker's relaxation of the four slots: proof-required
promotion rejects objects containing them. `pie`/`pic` are refused on Mach-O,
COFF, non-AArch64 ELF and the JIT; the rustc bridge forwards rustc's
`-C relocation-model` (`static`, `pic`, `pie`, and the target-default PIC)
on AArch64 Linux and compiles every other target with `static`. On AArch64
Linux ELF and on Mach-O the bridge carries rustc's function linkage and
visibility onto every mono-item function (CGU-private `Internal` copies
included, `src/function_linkage.rs`), and since 2026-10-24 onto the functions
it synthesizes: the allocator shim's `__rust_*` wrappers and marker and the C
`main` take the session's default visibility (`-Zdefault-visibility`) and the
shim's `__rdl_*` callees are hidden declarations (default on Mach-O, whose
undefined symbols carry no visibility), as in rustc's LLVM backend (ruling
OD-BRIDGE-SYNTHESIZED-VISIBILITY-20261024; L02-P1). x86-64 Linux ELF carries
them too since OD-X86-BRIDGE-ELF-PRIVATE-ROUTE-20261106 — the hidden
`__rdl_*` declaration is exactly the fact that route needed. On COFF, which
spells no function visibility, the bridge still refuses those requests by name
(OD-BRIDGE-UNSPELLED-BINDING-20261024, below). Object and LLD
link/relaxation tests (`rust-lld`, else an `ld.lld`; `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD`, which
the Linux floor sets for this target since the L02-P6 fifth closure audit,
makes a missing LLD a failure) run on every host. The native controls run only on
Linux AArch64 hosts: the `dlopen` and multi-thread control of
`e2e_aarch64_elf_relocation_model` links with GNU ld only, and the hidden
and protected visibility controls of `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` link with
GNU ld, gold and LLD at O0-O3: executable interposition and `LD_PRELOAD` of
strong, weak and COMDAT (`linkonce_odr`) functions, local binding of strong
functions and data, and the `.dynsym`, `LD_PRELOAD` and outsider-link
controls of strong data definitions in every implicit section (`.data`,
`.bss`, `.rodata`, `.data.rel.ro`) and of weak and COMDAT data and
strong, weak and COMDAT thread-local definitions. Since the fourth closure
audit the visibility cross-product table also puts every admitted
definition and declaration, from `Compiler::compile` and the three
`Pipeline` module emitters, into one such library (`.dynsym` and
`LD_PRELOAD` only).

With `-g` (`emit_debug`), AArch64 ELF and Mach-O objects carry the same
DWARF 4 `.debug_abbrev`, `.debug_info`, `.debug_str` and `.debug_line`
sections, plus `.debug_loc` when a variable uses a location list. ELF
relocates code addresses with `R_AARCH64_ABS64` and section offsets with
`R_AARCH64_ABS32`. Single-function compiles describe parameters,
provenance-derived register, spill-slot and constant locals, and a line
program. Whole-module objects from
`Pipeline::compile_module_emission_with_debug_provenance` describe the same
parameters and locals for each function. The caller passes each function's
register-debug provenance, retained in `PreparationMetrics` by a `-g`
preparation. The ranges are counted over the instruction list the module
encoder emitted and moved to the function's text offset. A function passed
without provenance keeps its provenance-backed locals' DIEs with empty
location lists, as a single-function compile does. The other whole-module
entry points, including the `Compiler` and CLI path and the parallel module
emitter, describe subprograms and line rows only, with no parameters or
variables. Emission refuses line rows, scopes or location ranges outside
their function. For a module function past text offset 0 that refuses a
range left function-relative only when it starts below the function (as
every entry-range parameter location does); an unshifted range that lands
inside the function passes emission and is caught only by the tests'
location checker and gdb. A register location starts after its defining instruction.
Frame-base locations cover only code where X29 is the frame pointer. From
O1, a stack-slot local is still described in its frame slot over that whole
range, even where the optimizer keeps the value in registers, so the slot
can be stale. In the debugger fixture, gdb reads `acc` as 0 at O1–O3 where
the source value is 10. The debugger tests therefore check only its name
there. SROA keeps such a slot allocated after promoting its accesses (it
retires to zero bytes only a promoted slot no debug variable names), and its
2026-09-30 admissions of argument-register loads and formal live-in reads do
not apply to a slot a debug variable names; describing a promoted local by a
register location instead is open. There is no
`DW_AT_linkage_name`, prologue-end or epilogue-begin marker, lexical scope
from any producer, or type beyond the v1 base, pointer, struct and enum
set. The rustc bridge requests line-table debug information only, on
aarch64-apple-darwin with proof certificates off (L06-P7; see Rust
integration). A whole-module compile unit lists every source file its
functions come from and switches the line program to each function's own
file; a function a producer named (`Function::display_path`) is described by
that name rather than its object symbol. The certified
relocation inventory refuses any object with DWARF sections (fail-closed).
ELF DWARF describes one `.text` section, so `-g` together with function
sections or COMDAT function text (bodies in their own `.text.<symbol>`
sections) is refused (fail-closed).
`aarch64_elf_dwarf` checks objects at O0–O3 with `llvm-dwarfdump --verify`.
It checks line rows and location ranges against `llvm-objdump`
disassembly. That covers single-function objects and whole-module objects
with each function at text offset 0 or past another, from the provenance
entry and from the lines-only `compile_module_emission` entry (no parameter
or variable DIE), plus a structural check of Mach-O module objects from the
provenance entry. A module's line program is one sequence: in a leaf-first
module the leaf's last row also covers the fixture's prologue until the
fixture's first row, so gdb reports the fixture's entry at the leaf's
source line; the checks test only where rows start. On macOS, lldb
statically resolves the ELF object's lines and variables. These are
structural checks, not a proof that a location holds the source value.
`e2e_aarch64_elf_debugger_linux` drives gdb or lldb on Linux over a
single-function object. It first passed on a Linux AArch64 host on
2026-09-20
([record](reports/perf/2026-09-20-linux-cfi-debugger-closure/README.md)).
It also drives gdb over a whole-module object with the fixture past a leaf
at O0–O3. There gdb reads the parameter at the fixture's entry; at the
body-line stop the constant local, and the spilled probe (its value where
gdb's static ranges cover the stop, unavailable where they do not); and the
register-held probe at the start of its first range only. Other addresses a
range claims are not probed
([record](reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-module-dwarf-variables/README.md)).
No debugger reads Mach-O module objects in these tests.

Every AArch64 `.eh_frame`, every x86-64 ELF `.eh_frame` (both the
backtrace-only zR lane and the zPLR EH lane) and every Mach-O DWARF-fallback
`__eh_frame`, on both architectures, passes the independent
`verify_eh_frame_roundtrip` decode check before emission. Callee-saved D8–D15 saves use `DW_CFA_offset_extended`. The
CFI is synchronous only: no epilogue rows are emitted, so from an
epilogue's X29 reload through its return the rows do not describe the
frame. Asynchronous unwinding from those PCs, for example by signal
handlers or profilers, is unsupported. `aarch64_elf_cfi_differential`
compares `llvm-dwarfdump --eh-frame` rows with the disassembled prologue
and the pipeline's `FrameLayout` at O0–O3. It covers GPR and FPR saves,
spills, and unrolled and looped stack probes, and measures the epilogue
windows. Its corpus has no stack-protected frame; AArch64 Linux ELF canary
frames are not compared.

Every AArch64 ELF object carries an empty `.note.GNU-stack`, and CLI links
for Linux targets pass `-Wl,-z,noexecstack`. A `-Wl` group that asks for an
executable stack (`-z,execstack` or `-zexecstack`, also after
`-z,noexecstack`) is refused before any process runs, for every link on
every target ("an executable stack is refused: every Linux link requests -z
noexecstack"; run for AArch64 and x86-64 Linux and AArch64 Darwin), and
gold's one-dash group `-szexecstack` is refused as
`[TCG-LINK-OPTION-GROUP]`. These refusals read only the `-Wl` groups the
driver is given: a C driver (`cc`) that appends `-z execstack` itself still
gets an executable stack installed (verifier note, 2026-10-15). trust-cg
emits no BTI landing
pads and no PAC instructions, so it emits no `.note.gnu.property`
(`GNU_PROPERTY_AARCH64_FEATURE_1_AND`) note, and the link driver refuses the
`-Wl` requests `-z force-bti`, `-z pac-plt` and `-z bti-report[=<mode>]` with
`[TCG-LINK-BTI-PAC]` on every target. `-z force-bti` marks the output BTI
under GNU ld and lld; `-z pac-plt` makes lld mark it PAC and GNU ld add
authenticating PLT stubs; `-z bti-report` marks nothing and is refused as
part of a BTI link configuration. CG code therefore runs without BTI or PAC
protection. A link outside the driver can still force BTI: on the Linux
AArch64 host GNU ld 2.42 marks the output BTI-compatible and only warns about
each unmarked input, which for an ordinary link includes the host's
`Scrt1.o`, `crti.o` and `crtn.o` as well as the CG object. An ordinary
executable forced that way dies with SIGILL before `main` prints, at
`_start` in the unmarked `Scrt1.o`. Only a startfile-free harness, in which
the CG object is the one unmarked input, reaches the indirect call into CG
code, and it dies with SIGILL at the CG function's first instruction. The glibc 2.41 dlopen refusal of
executable-stack objects is checked only on glibc 2.41 or later; that host
has glibc 2.39. Writable
all-zero definitions without pointer slots use SHT_NOBITS `.bss`, and
all-zero TLS templates without pointer slots use `.tbss`. A zero-initialized
COMDAT definition (`LinkOnce`, `LinkOnceOdr` or `WeakOdr`) of either kind is
an SHT_NOBITS `.bss.<sym>` or `.tbss.<sym>` member of its own `GRP_COMDAT`
group. Immutable zero constants stay in
`.rodata`, and Mach-O still stores zero definitions in `__data`. The Linux
`PT_GNU_STACK`, dlopen and zero-fill execution controls are in the Linux
regression floor; the other checks are object-level tests. The link-once
control links two objects that define the same zero data and thread-local
with GNU ld 2.42 on the Linux AArch64 host. It is execution evidence for that
linker and the glibc TLS runtime, not a linker proof; lld and other ELF
linkers have no native run.

AArch64 ELF objects bind each function definition from its trust-ir linkage:
`Internal`/`Private` as `STB_LOCAL`, `Weak`/`LinkOnce` and their ODR forms as
`STB_WEAK`, and `External` as `STB_GLOBAL`. AArch64 Mach-O objects do the
same with `N_EXT` cleared for `Internal`/`Private` and `N_EXT | N_WEAK_DEF`
for the weak and link-once forms. On AArch64 ELF, `Compiler::compile` also
carries trust-ir v45 function visibility: `Hidden`/`Protected` on a global or
weak definition become `STV_HIDDEN`/`STV_PROTECTED`, and on a declaration
(a bodyless `External` or `ExternalWeak` function, or an
`AvailableExternally` one) they become `STV_HIDDEN`/`STV_PROTECTED` on its
undefined `STB_GLOBAL` (`STB_WEAK`) symbol. For a strong declaration, GNU
ld 2.42, gold and LLD 22 then refuse a link whose output does not define
it, even when a shared library does. A weak (`ExternalWeak`) hidden or
protected declaration is different. GNU ld and LLD link it and its address
reads 0, both when nothing defines it and when only a shared library does.
gold links the absent case (the hidden one with the load-base defect above)
and refuses the shared-library case (`hidden|protected symbol 'x' is not
defined locally`). Data declarations (data imports) follow the same rules on
AArch64 ELF: a hidden or protected import's undefined symbol carries its
visibility (`STT_TLS` for a thread-local import), a strong one does not link
into a `-z defs` shared library that finds its definition only in another
shared library (with any of the three linkers), a weak one reads 0 when
absent (gold's hidden load-base defect included), and GNU ld, gold and LLD
refuse the copy relocation a non-PIE executable would need for a library's
protected word. gold has a protected twin of that defect. It keeps an absent
weak protected data declaration in a shared library's `.dynsym` as `WEAK
PROTECTED UND`, with a GOT slot against it. The library then reads 0 until
some image defines the name at run time. Once one does (an `LD_PRELOAD`
library), the library reads its own load base instead. GNU ld and LLD read 0
in both runs, and GCC 13.3's `extern` weak protected form behaves the same with
all three linkers (reproduced 2026-09-26, L02-P6 fourth closure audit).
`merge_modules` gives a merged function or global the most
constraining visibility any input states, so a hidden or protected data import
or function declaration restricts the definition another input supplies,
whatever the definition's own visibility (a hidden import of a protected
definition is hidden). The same holds when no input defines the name (the
merged declaration's or import's undefined symbol carries it) and when every
input defines it identically (a read-only weak or COMDAT word the merge
deduplicates). `merge_modules` refuses an `ExternalWeak` or
`AvailableExternally` function or global in any input. Visibility on an `Internal`/`Private` function
is refused by name (`[TCG-FUNCTION-VISIBILITY]`). Mach-O, x86-64, RISC-V,
the JIT and Wasm refuse non-default function visibility, on definitions and
declarations alike, with two exceptions: `Compiler::compile` for AArch64 and
x86-64 Mach-O admits `Hidden` on an `External` definition and writes it as a
private extern (`N_EXT | N_PEXT`; the rustc bridge's CGU-private functions),
and for x86-64 ELF admits `Hidden` and `Protected` on a definition and on a
codegen declaration (rulings OD-X86-ELF-DEFINITION-VISIBILITY-20261027 and
OD-X86-BRIDGE-ELF-PRIVATE-ROUTE-20261106, below).
Every other hidden Mach-O function comes from the `Pipeline` binding API (as
`N_PEXT`), and the Mach-O emitter refuses a visible undefined reference.
x86-64 (Mach-O, ELF and COFF) and RISC-V objects bind every
`Internal`/`Private` function definition local (a non-external Mach-O symbol,
`STB_LOCAL`, `IMAGE_SYM_CLASS_STATIC`), re-read from the object after
emission (since 2026-10-24, L02-P1; before, they were global, and another
object's undefined reference or weak definition bound to the module-local
body at link time; the x86-64 emitters take the binding from one carrier,
the compiler's `X86FunctionSymbolFacts`, since ruling
OD-X86-BINDING-ONE-CARRIER-20261105). On x86-64 Mach-O and COFF and on
RISC-V `Compiler::compile` refuses every reference to one by name: a
direct call, a `FnDef` or capture-free closure address, and a `SymbolAddr`
naming it in a body or a global initializer
(`AotDirectModuleFunctionBindingUnsupported`,
`AotStaticFunctionIdentityBindingUnsupported`). x86-64 ELF admits those
references and reads them back (ruling OD-X86-ELF-LOCAL-BINDING-20261027,
below); a `SymbolAddr` naming a module-local function is relocated there
against its local symbol. A reference that names
another symbol binds to the symbol its own name spells: the x86-64 Mach-O
emitter keys its symbols by nlist name only, so a declaration, address or
import spelled `_x` beside a definition of `x` is the undefined `__x`.
Until the L02-P1 round-2 repair (2026-10-24) it also looked references up
under their bare spelling, and each such reference reached the
module-local `x` (a call, a code or data address, a data import, a call to
the External `_md_g` reaching the internal `md_g`, the backend's
`__udivti3` call beside an internal `___udivti3`, and the `__eh_frame`
personality beside an internal `_rust_eh_personality`). A definition or
reference whose nlist name is one of the emitter's own LSDA labels
(`_GCC_except_table_<fn>`) is refused by name
(`[TCG-MACHO-SYMBOL-COLLISION]`). A module-local function named exactly
like a runtime symbol the backend calls by name (`__udivti3`, measured on
all six object targets) stays refused by name before lowering
(`ModuleLocalFunctionShadowsRuntimeSymbol`); it was the bare-spelling
lookup that let `___udivti3` capture that call on x86-64 Mach-O. Their weak and link-once
definitions (ODR forms included) are weak on x86-64 ELF and Mach-O and on
RISC-V, where the module's own calls to one are relocated so the linker's
choice of definition reaches them; the COFF emitter writes no COMDAT section
or weak external and refuses one by name (`UnsupportedLinkage`, after
trust-ir to LIR lowering and before instruction selection). Every other
x86-64 and RISC-V definition is global (x86-64 ELF writes a hidden or
protected definition's `STV_*` since ruling
OD-X86-ELF-DEFINITION-VISIBILITY-20261027; COFF refuses a hidden one by
name, and so does RISC-V, through the adapter's default object symbol
policy). Because dyld coalesces a
default-visibility weak definition with the first definition of its name in
load order, the AArch64
Mach-O AOT path addresses non-hidden weak and link-once data and function
definitions through the GOT (as clang does) and leaves calls to them as
`BRANCH26` relocations that ld64 routes through a stub. On AArch64 ELF,
`Compiler::compile` admits direct calls to and every address form of an
`Internal`/`Private` function (`FnDef`, capture-free closure, body and
initializer `SymbolAddr`), under every relocation model and with function or
explicit sections. `Compiler::object_binds_module_local_functions` is the
one predicate for this, and a static-call candidate through such an address
stays an indirect call. The emitters bind every reference by NAME, so the
path also refuses what name binding would get wrong, and so does every other
object path and the JIT, because every object writer and the JIT resolve a
name the backend references on its own through the module's own symbols
first. `trust_cg_lower::backend_symbol_shadow` is the one finder. It runs
before lowering, whether or not the module makes the reference, at every
public entry that reads a trust-ir module: `Compiler::compile` on every
target, `Compiler::compile_module_to_jit`, and every public
`trust_cg_lower` translation entry, which refuses with
`AdapterError::BackendSymbolShadowed`: the compatibility
`translate_module*` entries, the strict entries (`translate_module_strict_*`
on a module, `translate_validated_module_strict_*` on a validation report)
and the per-function `translate_function*` entries. That covers a
`Pipeline::prepare_function*` and `Pipeline::compile_module*` caller whose
LIR comes from any of them. A Linux row takes the verifier's `fmod` and
`__divti3` modules through all four routes, and links and runs, with a C
driver, any object a route lets through (every route refuses them). The
entries below trust-ir take functions
without linkage and have no module for the finder to read: `Pipeline` on LIR
a caller builds itself, and `JitCompiler::compile_raw` on MachIR, which
resolves a named call to a function of its input slice first. There each
supplied function is the image's definition of its name, so one named like a
listed symbol receives the backend's call. One translation entry skips the
finder: `translate_validated_module_strict_for_core_qualification`, which
takes a `CoreQualificationFollows` token. The token's one constructor,
`CoreQualificationFollows::caller_runs_core_qualification`, is `unsafe`. Its
Safety section requires that no code from the translation be emitted or run
before Core's qualification and address-free compilation checks accept it.
Outside Core admission a caller can construct the token only by writing
`unsafe`; code inside `core_admission.rs` can hand the construction to
other code in the crate, for example through a macro it exports, without
the caller writing `unsafe`. Within this checkout the one production
construction is a private helper in Core admission (`core_admission.rs`). The strict adapter's wrapper takes the
token from its caller rather than building it. A drift row pins, per file,
every mention of the token, its constructor, the entry and those two
helpers in every Rust source of the checkout (`crates/`, `fuzz/`, the bridge
workspace, benchmarks and reports, tests included; hidden directories and
Cargo target directories are skipped). A forgery that names none of them is
not seen: for example a macro exported from `core_admission.rs` that wraps
the construction, or code spliced in with `include!` from a file that is not
a `.rs` source. Core
refuses the backend's calls itself, at two points. Proof-grade qualification refuses
a retained LIR call without a source call origin
(`LirCallSourceOriginMismatch`), which stops the calls the adapter makes
(`frem`'s `fmod` beside a module-local `fmod`). Address-free compilation
refuses a machine call made below LIR, which has no retained LIR call
occurrence (`FixupOccurrenceMismatch`): the i128 division helpers, an
aggregate copy's `memcpy` and the stack protector's `__stack_chk_fail`, with
or without a same-named Internal body, at O0, O2 and O3. `core_jit_planning`
pins both. Core therefore never binds a backend call to a module body, and
it still admits an exactly called Internal body named `memcpy`. Core's
`InterposableModuleFixup` refusal is not part of this: no module reaches it.
After the occurrence checks, a by-name fixup belongs to a retained call bound
to a declared import whose symbol is the call's name, and trust-ir validation
refuses a module that also defines that name (`DuplicateFunctionSymbol`). It
would fire only if the encoder's fixup kind disagreed with the call's
`EXACT_MODULE_CALL` flag. The finder reports a module-local
(`Internal`/`Private`) function named like any of the 29 names of
`trust_cg_lower::RuntimeSymbol` (`ModuleLocalFunctionShadowsRuntimeSymbol`);
module-local data named like any of them or like the EH personality the
module's function names select; and any other data definition (External,
weak, link-once, ODR; an initializer-less or `available_externally` global
is an import, not a definition) named like a listed ROUTINE or like either EH
personality (`DataShadowsBackendSymbol`). An External FUNCTION of such a name is the
program's own routine, which the linker would pick for every object anyway,
and compiles. The 29 names are the one list the adapter, the AArch64 and
x86-64 instruction selectors, AArch64 frame lowering and the `trust-cg-opt`
machine passes draw the names they emit or read the meaning of from:
`memcpy`, `memmove`, `memset`, `fmod`, `fmodf`, `__fixsfti`, `__fixdfti`,
`__fixunssfti`, `__fixunsdfti`, `__floattisf`, `__floattidf`,
`__floatuntisf`, `__floatuntidf`, `__divti3`, `__udivti3`, `__modti3`,
`__umodti3`, `_Unwind_Resume`, `__stack_chk_fail`, `__stack_chk_guard`,
`malloc`, `free`, `__rust_alloc`, `__rust_dealloc`, `clean_inc`, `clean_dec`,
`clean_is_exclusive`, `__sincos_stret` (the Darwin sin/cos merge emits it)
and `calloc` (the vectorizer reads it: two distinct results of a call
named exactly `calloc`, not flagged `EXACT_MODULE_CALL`, stand in for a
`NoAlias` fact; a module-local `calloc` is refused, and an External one is
the program's own allocator, taken to keep C library semantics as a hosted C
compiler does; the rewrite also needs `InBounds` proof facts, which are
cleared without validator replay authority, so it has no production effect
today). `__stack_chk_guard` is data (the
canary), so an External data definition of it, a freestanding runtime's own
canary, compiles. At the base these modules compiled on every path that
lowered them, and they compiled to wrong code: a module-local `fmod`
received `frem`'s call in the Linux AArch64 JIT (`my_rem(5,3)` returned 42
at O0 and O2), in AArch64 Mach-O objects (`bl _fmod` against the local
`_fmod` at O0, the local body inlined at O2) and in AArch64 ELF objects; a
local `__sincos_stret` function or datum received the Darwin sin/cos merge's
call; x86-64 Mach-O branched into local data named `fmod`, `__divti3`,
`memcpy`, `memset` or `malloc`; x86-64 and RISC-V bind a module-local
function global, so it received the call and was exported. A module-local
function or datum with any other name (`printf`, `puts`, `sqrt`, `log`, ...)
compiles. The list's drift rows are source scans of `trust-cg-lower` (every
file), of AArch64 frame lowering in `trust-cg-codegen` (`frame.rs` and every
file under `frame/`) and of `trust-cg-opt` (every file). They share one
test-only scanner (`trust-cg-lower/src/source_scan.rs`). It walks the
crate's module tree from `lib.rs`, following `mod` declarations, `#[path]`
attributes and declarations inside inline modules. A file is test code only
when every declaration reaching it passes `#[cfg(test)]`, so a file declared
both ways is scanned, and a source file the walk does not reach fails the
row. A small lexer drops comments, keeps string and char literals as single
tokens and reads raw identifiers (`r#Symbol` as `Symbol`), and each item,
statement, field or arm carrying `#[cfg(test)]` is removed by its own
braces, `;` or `,`. All three rows fail on a listed name spelled as a string
literal, with or without the Mach-O underscore (in `trust-cg-lower` outside
the list's own file), and on a symbol operand built from a literal. The
`trust-cg-lower` and `trust-cg-opt` rows also fail on a symbol variant
imported by `use` (a glob, a list or the variant itself), after which a bare
`Symbol(..)` would not be counted, and on any change in any file's pinned
count of symbol-operand uses (in `trust-cg-lower` only the two selectors
have any, so a use in any other file fails).
That count takes every `Symbol` or `ExactModuleSymbol` path segment after
`::`, whatever names the enum (`MachOperand`, `X86ISelOperand`, a type
alias, `Self`, `<MachOperand>`, including inside a `macro_rules!` body), and
every `.as_symbol` and `.as_exact_module_symbol` accessor; each
`trust-cg-opt` file's uses are classified in the test. The `trust-cg-lower`
row also fails on a string-literal callee passed to a selector call helper
and on a by-name call the adapter builds outside the one runtime-call
helper and the source direct-call lowering. A self-test plants each shape
(including a match-arm read, the verifier's plants after an out-of-line test
module, the type-alias, `Self`, qualified-path, raw-identifier, macro-body
and `ExactModuleSymbol` forms, and a file declared both as production and as
test code) and requires detection. A non-test `include!` spelled as such
(any path) fails the scan rows, because the scanner does not read the
included text; a renamed import of it (`use std::include as x; x!(..)`) or
one passed to a macro as an identifier is not seen. The rows are source
scans, not a proof that no code path references a runtime routine by name.
A name assembled by `concat!` or formatting (for example compared through
`Debug` output), a symbol operand built inside a macro from a `$` fragment,
a further invocation of a macro whose body already holds a counted use, a
name read through a helper defined in another crate, or an unlisted name
routed through an existing site by a variable, would pass them. The sin/cos merge also reads `sin` and `cos` by
name; those are not on the list, because the pass runs only for Darwin and
skips calls flagged `EXACT_MODULE_CALL` (the JIT's exact module calls).
Darwin objects used to refuse every direct call to a module-local function;
since they bind module-local functions (below), an Apple AArch64 compile
refuses a module-local `sin` or `cos` that a body references
(`ModuleLocalFunctionShadowsRuntimeSymbol`,
`refuse_darwin_sincos_merge_shadow`, reading the pass's own
`SINCOS_MERGE_CALLEES`). Measured before that refusal: a module whose
Internal `sin` and `cos` add 1.0 and 2.0 printed `1.3570081004945758`
(libm's `sin(0.5) + cos(0.5)`) at O2 and O3 instead of `4`. An unreferenced
module-local `sin` or `cos` still compiles on Darwin, and a referenced one
compiles for ELF, where the pass is inert. Behind the finder,
on AArch64 ELF, the object read-back below refuses a branch into data and a
personality slot holding a data address. The x86-64 JIT shares the JIT
refusal; it was not executed on this Linux AArch64 host, and neither were
the Mach-O and x86-64 objects, whose refusals are compile-level rows. A
source call to a function that is not a module-local definition and is
named `memcpy`, `memmove` or `memset`, declared with C's prototype and
convention (`void *(void *, const void *, size_t)`, `void *(void *, int,
size_t)`; LD-100), or that is an `llvm.memcpy`/
`llvm.memmove`/`llvm.memset` intrinsic declared at LLVM's type, is given the
routine's semantics (`classify_adapter_direct_call`), and the AArch64
selector expands a constant-length `memcpy` or zero `memset` of up to 32
bytes inline. A program's own External `memcpy` body with C's prototype
therefore does not run for such a call. That matches a hosted C compiler
treating these as builtins (clang and GCC by default), not GCC's
`-ffreestanding`/`-fno-builtin`. Declared otherwise, the plain name is an
ordinary call of the function (until 2026-10-23 the name alone decided, and
`memcpy` declared `i64 (i64, i64, i64)` copied from address 4 to address 3);
an intrinsic name at another type is refused by name. The LLVM importer
gives the gate only the prototype the module's own header states: an
unprototyped `(...)`, unmodeled or missing header of the three names, and a
Mach-O `\01_` label naming one, are refused by name (rule 8 of the ruling;
signed from a call, such a header read as C's prototype). A function named
like any routine the backend calls on its own (`RuntimeSymbol`: `memcpy`,
`fmod`, the i128 helpers, the allocators, ...), declared with a hidden
return buffer (`sret`) and called directly, is refused by name by AArch64
instruction selection (rule 11, 2026-10-24): the selector keys that fact by
the symbol's name, and until then its own `memcpy`, `memmove` or `memset`
call for an intrinsic in the same function passed the destination in `x8`
(the import crashed where llc's build copies). A personality the
module defines module-locally is reached through an
object-local `DW.ref.<personality>` slot, as GCC does for a `static`
personality, not through the shared weak slot an external personality
uses. A module that defines a non-local data global named like either
personality's slot (`DW.ref.__gxx_personality_v0`,
`DW.ref.rust_eh_personality`) is refused by name before lowering, on every
target (`DataShadowsBackendSymbol`): every unwind table's slot of that name,
its own object's included, would resolve to it. Before that refusal, on
the Linux host, a module with exception-handling frames and such a global
went wrong with every linker. GNU ld 2.42 and gold gave the frames the
module's word as the personality pointer, and a throw through them died
with `SIGBUS`, in a PIE and in a shared library. LLD 22 resolved the
module's own word to the slot instead (the module read the personality's
address, not its initializer; its throws were caught), and refused a PIE in
which a g++ object's slot group came first ("relocation refers to a symbol
in a discarded section: DW.ref.__gxx_personality_v0"). A module-local global
of that name is a separate `STB_LOCAL` symbol
beside the slot and still compiles, as does any other `DW.ref.` name. The
compiler then reads the emitted object back
(`AotModuleLocalFunctionBindingViolated`, a cached object included). It
refuses any symbol spelling a module-local function's exact name (a name
containing `@` included) other than its defined `STB_LOCAL` `STT_FUNC`
symbol, a spelling `name@...` of such a function's name unless the module
itself names a function or global exactly so, whatever its binding (a
reference to a versioned symbol elsewhere such as `helper@VERS_1`, or an
Internal global `helper@x`, beside a local `helper`), and a non-local symbol
overlapping the definition. It also
refuses a relocation reaching the definition's start through a non-local
symbol, a data slot holding its address that is labelled by a non-local
symbol the module did not declare, and a text reference to a module-local
function no function body of the module references. That last rule is per
function: it is silent when any body references the function, so it cannot
tell a backend call by the same name from the module's own call, and it
cannot see a runtime call the inliner has already replaced by the local
body; the name refusals come first for that reason. The check reads names,
addresses and bindings: a reference into the middle of a function, or
through another object, is out of its reach. A second read-back check
(`AotCodeReferenceReachesData`) refuses a `CALL26`/`JUMP26` whose symbol is
defined in a non-executable section and a relocated word in a slot labelled
`DW.ref.*` whose symbol is defined in a non-executable section: a runtime
call or a personality bound to data. It is the backstop behind the data
refusal, runs on AArch64 ELF and Mach-O objects (on Mach-O: an
`ARM64_RELOC_BRANCH26`, or a personality reference in `__eh_frame` or
`__compact_unwind`, whose symbol is defined outside every instruction
section), and leaves undefined, absolute and common targets to the linker. The Linux controls link two objects, each with its own
Internal or Private `helper`, with a third object that defines a global
`helper`, through GNU ld, gold and LLD: each object reaches its own helper,
and an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer reaches none of them inside shared objects.
Two objects that each define a module-local `rust_eh_personality` unwind
their own frames with their own personality, in either link order. This is
execution evidence, not a linker or loader proof.

AArch64 Mach-O objects bind module-local functions too (2026-09-30). The
Mach-O module emitter already cleared `N_EXT` on an Internal/Private
function and resolved every fixup through the same name-to-symbol map; the
compiler now admits direct calls to and every address form of such a
function for Apple AArch64 triples and reads the emitted object back with an
independent Mach-O reader (`check_aarch64_macho_module_local_function_binding`,
`AotModuleLocalFunctionBindingViolated`, a cached object included). For each
module-local `f` it refuses any symbol spelled `_f` other than its one
`N_SECT` definition in an instruction section with `N_EXT` and `N_PEXT`
clear (debugger `N_STAB` entries aside; Mach-O has no symbol versioning), an
external symbol inside the definition (up to the next symbol naming a module
function), an external relocation reaching the definition's start through an
external symbol (the addend from an `ARM64_RELOC_ADDEND` prefix or an
`ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED` in-place word), a section-relative relocation outside
the `S_ATTR_DEBUG` sections (not modelled), a data word holding the address
in an atom whose symbol (the nearest at or below it, as
`MH_SUBSECTIONS_VIA_SYMBOLS` splits atoms) is external and not one of the
module's globals, and a text reference no body makes. A non-external symbol
is invisible to the static linker outside its object and to dyld, so no other
object or image can supply the definition. The ELF-only object facts (weak
undefined references, function visibility and sections) stay refused on
Mach-O by the adapter, through a separate predicate
(`aot_object_admits_elf_symbol_facts`). The macOS AArch64 controls
(`tests/aarch64_macho_module_local_binding.rs`) link two objects, each with
its own Internal or Private `helper`, with a third object defining a global
`helper`, through `cc` (ld64) and `run_link`, at O0-O3 sequential and
parallel: each object reaches its own helper through direct calls, local
and global function pointers and address takings, `nm` reads two
non-external helpers and one external, `objdump` shows each module's direct
call branching to its own, and the clang twin with `static` functions agrees.
Each module linked into its own `-interposable` dylib resists a
`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` interposer whose `__DATA,__interpose` tuple replaces
`helper`, while the same run's executable-defined `helper` and an External
near-twin's direct call are interposed (`DYLD_FORCE_FLAT_NAMESPACE` alone
interposed nothing on this host's dyld). Execution evidence for ld64 and dyld
on that host, not a linker or loader proof. Proof certificates make no
binding claim on either format: a call row is `covered_elsewhere` and the
relocation inventory names kinds, not targets. The Darwin linked-image
replay (`record_darwin_linked_image`) resolves a non-external definition
inside its own object; it records an image with one module-local `helper`
beside an external one, and it refuses (removing the output) an image in
which two objects' local helpers share a name, because it places atoms by
the image's symbol table, which names `_helper` twice as a local. That
replay residual is fail-closed: it does not certify the image.

x86-64 ELF objects bind module-local functions too (2026-10-27, ruling
OD-X86-ELF-LOCAL-BINDING-20261027). The x86-64 ELF module emitter now binds a
bodied `Internal`/`Private` function definition `STB_LOCAL` in the symbol
table's local partition, so every `R_X86_64_PLT32` call and `R_X86_64_64`
address slot in the object reaches that object's own body and the name never
enters a linked image's export surface; the compiler admits direct calls to
and the address of such a function for x86-64 ELF triples
(`aot_object_binds_module_local_functions`) and reads the emitted object back
with the arch-neutral ELF reader the AArch64 path uses
(`check_elf_module_local_function_binding`, a cached object included), plus
the code-reference backstop parameterized by this target's branch relocation
(`R_X86_64_PLT32`; `R_X86_64_PC32` is excluded because the same emitter
writes it for RIP-relative data). The same emitter now writes `STV_HIDDEN`
and `STV_PROTECTED` on a function DEFINITION, which the adapter admits for
this path alone (`ObjectSymbolPolicy::X86_64_ELF_MODULE`, ruling
OD-X86-ELF-DEFINITION-VISIBILITY-20261027). The ELF module emitter additionally writes
undefined-function weakness and visibility and declared-only weak or non-default
symbols through one helper (OD-X86-ELF-UNDEFINED-REFERENCE-20261106). Its GOT-based
undefined-reference model refuses a direct PLT32 call to a weak undefined
callee. The adapter admits the VISIBILITY of those facts for this target
(`FunctionSymbolFactPolicy::AdmitElfSymbolVisibility`, ruling
OD-X86-BRIDGE-ELF-PRIVATE-ROUTE-20261106), on a definition and on a codegen
declaration alike, so a declaration stating one reaches emission. That facet
exists instead of `AdmitElfSymbolFacts` precisely because the wider variant
also bundles a function SECTION, which this emitter cannot spell. A WEAK
undefined reference stays refused on its own facet
(`WeakUndefinedReferencePolicy::Refuse`), so the emitter's weak-undefined
facts stay unreachable from an admitted module and its call-loop GOT backstop
is a fail-closed second barrier rather than the gate. Data-import weakness and
visibility and explicit function sections remain refused. The x86-64 Mach-O and COFF writers and RISC-V
bind an unreferenced module-local definition local as well (the L02-P1
repair above, merged on 2026-11-05, ruling
OD-X86-BINDING-ONE-CARRIER-20261105: the Mach-O and COFF emitters read the
same facts, and only the raw-bytes form refuses a module-local fact); a
module whose bodies reference such a definition is refused on those paths
by the identity census, since no reference is read back there. As first
landed on 2026-10-27 this passage said those writers still bound it global;
that held only until the merge. The Linux x86-64
controls (`tests/x86_64_elf_symbol_binding.rs`) read symbols and relocations
back with an ELF64 parser written in the test, and on an x86-64 Linux GNU
host link two objects that each define their own Internal `helper` beside a C
object defining a global `helper`: at O0-O3 each reaches its own body through
the direct call and through a data slot, a gcc twin with `static` helpers
prints the same text, and in a `cc -shared` link neither local `helper`
reaches `.dynsym` while an `External` near-twin's does. Execution evidence
for that host's `cc`, GNU ld and glibc loader, not a linker or loader proof.
Neither of those emitter rulings touches the rustc bridge; the bridge's own
refusal (OD-BRIDGE-UNSPELLED-BINDING-20261024) covered this target until
OD-X86-BRIDGE-ELF-PRIVATE-ROUTE-20261106 moved x86-64 Linux onto the ELF
private-symbol route, which is where it is lifted for this triple.

Every AArch64 ELF and Mach-O object `Compiler::compile` returns (a cached one
included) is also read back for SYMBOL DISCIPLINE
(`check_aarch64_object_symbol_discipline`,
`AotObjectSymbolDisciplineViolated`), so a consumer can partition its text
into the module's functions by symbol alone, a function's extent being
`[its symbol, the next symbol or the section end)`. Each emitted function
must have exactly one symbol, defined in an instruction section, with the
binding its trust-ir linkage and visibility dictate, read from the source
module rather than the writer's plan: this is the post-emission re-read of
hidden `External` definitions (Mach-O `N_EXT | N_PEXT`, ELF `STV_HIDDEN`) as
well as of default, weak (`N_WEAK_DEF` / `STB_WEAK`) and local ones. No other
symbol may be defined in an instruction section (a label, a mapping symbol,
data, an alias), no two symbols may share an address, each instruction
section must start at a symbol, and an ELF `st_size` must be nonzero and end
at or before the next symbol with only `NOP` words after it. A fresh object
is also held to the layout its emitter reports when every function shares one
section: each symbol at its body's start and only `NOP` words outside the
bodies. The module emitters emit no range-extension veneer (an out-of-range
branch is refused) and encode a dense switch's jump table inside its
function's body; bytes outside every body (a veneer, literal pool or stub)
are refused rather than attributed. The check says nothing about whether a
byte inside a body is reachable code or data (an in-body jump table is data,
and the case arms reached only through it are code no straight-line walk
reaches), which a consumer decoding the extent must still decide. The determinism row
(`tests/object_symbol_discipline.rs`, `module_object_is_deterministic`)
compiles one module with fresh compilers on three threads, for both formats,
O0 and O2, sequential and parallel, and finds every object byte-identical;
that is a same-host, same-build observation, not a reproducible-build claim
across hosts or toolchains.

`Compiler::preflight` is the per-function refusal census of
`Compiler::compile`: in `compile`'s order it reports every function the codegen
license refuses, every body whose module-local references the object path
cannot bind (off AArch64 objects; an identity in a global initializer is
attributed to the function it names) or that is named like a backend symbol,
and every body the adapter refuses
(`trust_cg_lower::census_module_translation_with_access_model_and_license`,
the compile's own adapter configuration), instead of the first refusal alone.
It is diagnostic only. Bodies share module-wide adapter facts, so a row after
the first is the verdict reached with the earlier refused bodies' partial
facts in place. It does not report a refusal of the module or configuration
as a whole (dialect legalization, prerequisite validation and the other
module-level adapter gates end the stages that need them), the second and
later backend-symbol shadows, or any refusal after the adapter (OPT-4,
instruction selection, register allocation, emission, the post-emission
checks): an empty census does not mean `compile` succeeds.

Every other AOT target except x86-64 ELF (ruling
OD-X86-ELF-LOCAL-BINDING-20261027) still refuses direct calls to and
`FnDef`/closure address-takes of `Internal`/`Private` functions. Since the
2026-10-24 L02-P1 closure audit the source census behind those refusals
also counts a `SymbolAddr` (in a body or a global initializer) that names
such a function by string, so x86-64 Mach-O and COFF and RISC-V refuse that
reference by name too; until then it was not refused there, and an x86-64
object relocated an initializer slot against the function's then-global
symbol while the RISC-V object path dropped the slot. A module-local
personality on x86-64 Mach-O is refused by name; on x86-64 ELF it takes the
object-local `DW.ref` slot (OD-X86-ELF-LOCAL-BINDING-20261027).
`module_merge::merge_modules`
resolves every input's names in one namespace, where separate compilation
keeps a module-local definition out of every other object's reach. It
therefore renames a bodied `Internal`/`Private` function that another input
names (as a function, a declaration, a global or a `SymbolAddr`) to
`<name>.merge.<input>` before merging, together with every reference in its
own input (calls, invokes, `FnDef` and closure constants, and its own
`SymbolAddr` constants in bodies, `Switch` cases and global initializers).
The other inputs' declarations and `SymbolAddr` constants keep naming the
external definition, as under separate compilation; an independent walk and
an exact inverse check each renaming. The renamed function's local symbol
carries the new name. The merge refuses what it cannot rename apart: a
module-local EH personality another input names, and a `SymbolAddr` naming
another input's module-local global from an input with no global of that
name (data merges by name). Lowering selects a module-default personality
by name; a function stamped `Producer::TRust` takes `rust_eh_personality`
whatever the default, and keeps it in every module, so a merge cannot change
it. When a module has exception-handling structure the AArch64 ELF unwind
emitter gives EVERY function of it an FDE under the one module personality
(a module whose functions select two is refused there by name), a function
without landing pads getting a filler LSDA (one call-site entry over the
whole function, no landing pad, no action). The merge therefore refuses
inputs with exception-handling structure that select a different default
personality on their own than the merged module does, an input whose typed
catch has no `__trust_cg_eh_type_table` of its own beside an input that
declares one (its catch type indices would bind to that input's typeinfo
symbols, while compiled separately it is refused; two differing tables are
refused as differing globals), and, when some input
defines the selected personality module-locally, any other input with a
bodied function, exception-handling structure or not: compiled separately
its frames never run that routine, merged they would (the verifier's
counting personality ran twice instead of once). That refusal is
conservative: it also refuses an input made only of leaf functions, which
can never be on the stack an exception unwinds (the verifier's `b_leaf`
input). Admitting those would need a proof that the backend inserts no call
into them, so it stays a known false refusal. An input without
exception-handling structure beside an EXTERNAL merged personality still
merges. Its frames, which compiled separately carry no personality, then
run that personality with the filler LSDA, once for every unwinding phase
that walks such a frame: one extra call per frame when nothing catches the
exception (only the search phase runs), two when a handler further up
catches it (search and cleanup phases; the verifier's C++ catch counted
`calls 2` separately and `calls 4` merged, at O0 and O2 under all three
linkers). In either phase a real personality finds no landing pad and
continues unwinding, so the extra calls are accepted; they are visible only
to a personality with side effects.
So the merge now accepts inputs that each define a function of one name
when at least one of them is module-local, which the base refused as
duplicate definitions, and refuses the module-local personality and
module-local data shapes above and the personality disagreements, which the
base merged. An external
personality's `DW.ref.<personality>` slot is emitted as GCC emits it: a
`WEAK HIDDEN` symbol alone in a `GRP_COMDAT` group it signs. A `pic` EH
module therefore links into a shared object with GNU ld 2.42, gold and LLD
22, the slot is never exported, and every object's slot, CG or GCC, coalesces
to one cell. Before the L02-P6 residual repair the slot was weak and
default-visible: GNU ld and LLD refused the `.eh_frame` `R_AARCH64_PREL32`
naming it in a shared object ("may bind externally"), and gold exported it.
A module-local personality keeps an object-local slot outside any group. Bodyless `ExternalWeak`
functions and initializer-less, non-TLS `ExternalWeak` globals become
`STB_WEAK` undefined references on AArch64 ELF only; they are addressed through
the GOT. Other object paths, JIT and Wasm still refuse `ExternalWeak` (ld64 on
macOS 26.6 also rejects an undefined weak reference outright). A
proof-emitting compile refuses a direct call to a weak undefined function,
because the linker resolves that branch outside the modeled `CALL26`/`JUMP26`
formula. Non-ODR weak definitions are neither inlined nor used for purity
inference on AArch64 ELF or Mach-O. The Linux
link-and-run controls for these bindings run in the Linux regression floor.
The v45 hidden/protected shared-object and `LD_PRELOAD` interposition rows are
in the same floor target, `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding`. Every hidden and
protected visibility row there runs a GNU ld, a gold and an LLD leg; the v45
text-module row and the Pipeline-level executable-interposition row linked
with GNU ld alone until the L02-P6 second closure-audit repair
(2026-09-24). Six native rows still link with GNU ld only: default-visibility
weak and Internal functions, `ExternalWeak` references, a separately
compiled declaration, the public translation routes, and the `run_link`
(the CLI's link step) shared-library `LD_PRELOAD` row for Internal and
Private helpers. The retained floor runs of integrated gates 20, 25, 28 and
31 passed the target 20/20, 41/41, 48/48 and 59/59 with no `SKIP` line (gate
31 at `fdaa93f6e`). They predate that repair's gold and LLD legs and its
eight weak/COMDAT data and thread-local and Pipeline-route TLS anchor rows.
Those rows ran in the retained floor runs of integrated gates 32, 33 and 34
(`records/run-i44`, `run-i45`, `run-i46`: 67/67, each with 28 LLD-leg
lines). The three strong-data rows of the L02-P6 third closure-audit repair
(2026-09-26: hidden, protected and default strong definitions in `.data`,
`.bss`, `.rodata` and `.data.rel.ro`, through `Compiler::compile`, both
`Pipeline` emitters and a `pic` library linked by all three linkers) ran in
gate 35's `records/run-i48` (70/70 at `824d77e4f`, 36 LLD-leg lines) and
gate 35b's `records/link-i49` (70/70). The seven visibility-table rows of
the fourth closure-audit repair (below) ran in gate 36's retained floor run
(`records/run-i50`: 77/77 at `01b84f0c8`, each table pass line naming GNU
ld, gold and LLD). The four rows of the fifth closure-audit repair (below)
ran in gate 40's retained floor run (`run-i57`: 81/81 at `e3508e8d4`, no
`SKIP` line) and in the sixth closure audit's runs at `23ee1104a` (81/81).
The sixth repair's repeated-declaration row and its extension of the native
declaration-library row (below) ran in that repair's own runs (82/82, debug
and the floor's `--release` build) and in the seventh closure audit's three
runs at `fdcd95468` (83/83, the table having gained a row since; no `SKIP`
line, every table pass line naming GNU ld, gold and LLD). The floor pins
its minimum (83), that of
`e2e_aarch64_elf_relocation_model` (21; run with
`TCG_REQUIRE_LLD=1` since the fifth repair, so its three LLD link legs fail
rather than print `SKIP` without an LLD) and, since the third repair, that of
`v41_abi_residue_objects` (18). All of them are execution evidence for GNU
ld, gold, LLD and the glibc loader on that host, not a linker or loader
proof.
Since the L02-P6 fourth closure audit (2026-09-26) the target also generates
the whole visibility cross-product
(`tests/aarch64_elf_symbol_binding/visibility_table.rs`), instead of pinning
the classes each audit found. It covers {definition, declaration} x eight
linkages (the five definition linkages, `internal`, `external_weak`,
`available_externally`) x {default, hidden, protected} x {function, mutable,
read-only, pointer-bearing read-only, zero-fill and thread-local (`.tdata`,
`.tbss`) data} x {implicit section, explicit name, explicit `.text`}: 1,008
cases. It admits 337 of them and refuses 574. For every refused case the
row runs `Compiler::compile` under `static` and `pic` and asserts the
diagnostic that names the refusal. For the 45 bodyless functions with a
definition linkage that diagnostic is `[TCG-DECLARATION-LINKAGE]` (since
`907e8f9d6`), and the row also asserts trust-ir's validator's `EmptyFunction`
message. Each of the 97
the text form cannot state as its own row has a witness. Every admitted case is checked through
`Compiler::compile` (sequential and parallel, O0-O3) and the `Pipeline`
unwind, layout-less and relocation-free emitters, under `static`, `pie` and
`pic`, with and without function sections. The checks cover binding, type,
visibility, section and flags, COMDAT group, GOT or PC-relative address,
TLS access and the `.Ltls` anchor. The emitters' relocation-model
backstop is checked for every PC-relative address the shared predicate
forbids or allows, and structural purity (the pure callees of the public
module translation) against the same replacement predicates. The native row links every route's `pic` object into one
library with GNU ld, gold and LLD at O0-O3 and checks `.dynsym` and
`LD_PRELOAD` interposition for every admitted case. `static` and `pie` are
covered at object level only. The table does not reach the
single-function emitter route, which takes no visibility input and spells
every symbol `STV_DEFAULT`. It does not reach the rustc bridge, whose
function linkage and visibility are pinned by its own native rows
(`function_linkage` and `synthesized_visibility` in the required
`aarch64_c_fnabi_aggregate_linux` target, L02-P1), or the other object
formats, whose refusals other rows pin. A bodyless `weak`, `linkonce`, `linkonce_odr`, `weak_odr` or
`internal` function is refused by trust-ir's validator (`EmptyFunction`) and,
since `907e8f9d6`, by `Compiler::compile` as `[TCG-DECLARATION-LINKAGE]`,
naming the function and its linkage (before, the adapter failed on an
unnamed `unknown block reference`). An
initializer-less `weak`, `linkonce` or ODR global is a strong data import:
its undefined symbol keeps its visibility but is `STB_GLOBAL`.
Since the L02-P6 fifth closure audit (2026-09-26) the target also checks
two shapes the table does not generate. The first is a merge in which no
input defines a name (two declarations of a function, two imports of a
word) or every input defines it identically (read-only `linkonce_odr`,
`weak`, `linkonce` and `weak_odr` words). It runs for every ordered pair of
visibilities at object level under `static`, `pie` and `pic` at O0-O3. For
the (default, default) pair and each ordered pair of distinct visibilities it
also runs in a `pic` shared library linked merged and separately, beside a C
definition, by GNU ld, gold and LLD, for `.dynsym` and `LD_PRELOAD`. The
second is the function-body `SymbolAddr` of a data definition and the
importer's global-address stub, at offsets 0 and 8, checked against
`GlobalAddr` the same way for strong, read-only, `weak` and `linkonce_odr`
words of each visibility. In the linked library no dynamic relocation or GOT
slot may name a hidden or protected word. The audit's seven surviving
mutants (the merge's declaration-only visibility and identical-input
deduplication, and the stub and data-`SymbolAddr` address forms) and seven
new ones at neighbouring sites were applied one at a time. Each is killed by
this target; the address-form row lists the edits. Under the audit's two
address-form mutants (S01, S02) the programs still print the expected
values: those mutants are caught by the object's relocations and the linked
library's GOT slots and relocations, not by execution.
Since the L02-P6 sixth closure audit (2026-10-03) the target also pins
repeated declarations of one function in one module. trust-ir's validator
reports `DuplicateFunctionSymbol` for any repeated name, and since WS7.3
every ingestion entry refuses that finding (decision LD-54): for every
ordered pair of (`external` or `external_weak`, default, hidden or protected)
declarations, identical ones included, the module reaches `Compiler::compile`
from the `.trust_ir` text parser, the bare `TRUST_IR` and `tMBC` binary
containers and JSON with both declarations intact, and is refused under
`static`, `pie` and `pic` at O0-O3 by that finding. The function catalog's
comparison (`compatible_external_declarations`) still guards the adapter's
diagnostic entries, which take a module without admission: two bodyless
declarations may share a symbol there only when both are `external` and
agree on its whole contract. Through the AArch64 ELF diagnostic entry every
decoded pair that differs, and two identical `external_weak` ones, is
refused by that comparison, and the three identical `external` pairs
translate. `merge_modules` does not reach that check: it keys functions by
name, so it folds one input's repeated `external` declarations into the most
constraining visibility in either order, as it does across inputs, and it
refuses an input with an `external_weak` function by name (decision LD-06).
Each folded module compiles from every entry under every model at O0-O3 to
one undefined `STB_GLOBAL` symbol with that visibility. The audit's mutants
K19 (visibility dropped from the comparison: hidden then protected compiled
to a `GLOBAL PROTECTED UND` that a linked library exported) and K20
(`external_weak` admitted beside `external`: a `WEAK` undefined reference
whose call died with SIGSEGV) had passed the seven floor targets the audit
ran for this row. Replayed on the 2026-10-03 repair (`d146b224f`, debug
build, `TCG_REQUIRE_LLD=1 TCG_REQUIRE_GOLD=1`; unmutated 82/82 with no
`SKIP` line), each failed the row and the catalog's unit test; LD-54 records
their replay against the row as WS7.3 leaves it. The `pic` declaration library's native
row now also links a default `available_externally` function: its call must
go through the PLT and an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer must take it. The audit's
K6 (that body spliced under `pic`) had failed one object row only; it now
also fails the native row, first at the compile result's splice disclosure.
With that row's object and link checks turned into reports in a scratch
build, its `LD_PRELOAD` run printed the template's 55 where the interposer's
555 belongs (O1, GNU ld). The audit's K5 (the sequence-result ABI ignoring
load-time preemption) passes this target and is killed by the floor target
`e2e_aarch64_sequences` (`calls_to_replaceable_sequence_returning_bodies_are_refused_by_name`).
The object rows for v45 function visibility and explicit function sections
cover both the sequential and the parallel `Compiler::compile` emission
paths, and the compiler trace shows which path produced each object.

Explicit sections (trust-ir `Global.section`) are placed only by the AArch64
emitters. On ELF a zero-fill name (`.bss*`, `.tbss*`, `.sbss*`, `.lbss*`)
is an SHT_NOBITS section (`SHF_TLS` on `.tbss*`) when its global is all
zero with no pointer slot. A nonzero initializer or a relocated pointer slot
there is refused by name (`[TCG-SECTION-NOBITS]`). GNU ld 2.42 places
`.sbss*` and `.lbss*` as orphans, and AArch64 has no large-data flag for
`.lbss`. Every other decision comes from one table,
`object_sections::ELF_NAME_RULES`: where GNU ld 2.42's default AArch64
scripts (PIE, `-no-pie`, `-shared`; `-z relro` or `-z norelro`) and LLD
22.1.6's built-in rules put each input-section name. A unit test re-derives
the GNU column from the retained `ld --verbose` script
(`crates/trust-cg-codegen/tests/fixtures/gnu-ld-2.42-aarch64linux.xdw`) and
from a retained list of the rules BFD applies by name outside the script
(`crates/trust-cg-codegen/tests/fixtures/gnu-ld-2.42-bfd-by-name.txt`). The
LLD column was probed. A name either linker places in a read-only or
`PT_GNU_RELRO` output refuses a mutable global as `[TCG-SECTION-READONLY]`:
`.rodata*`, `.rodata1`, `.data.rel.ro*`, `.bss.rel.ro*` (LLD only), `.toc`
(LLD only), and the `.init_array`/`.fini_array`/`.preinit_array` tables. A
relocated pointer in a read-only one is refused the same way. `.tcommon`,
which GNU ld folds into its `.tbss` output, refuses a non-TLS global as
`[TCG-SECTION-TLS]`. `.text*`, `.init`, `.fini`, `.stub` and `.iplt` land in
executable outputs and are `[TCG-SECTION-EXEC]`. Names a linker parses,
synthesizes, types by name, drops or discards, or that crtbegin/crtend walk,
are `[TCG-SECTION-RESERVED]` for every data global. These are the unwind and
exception families (`.eh_frame.*`, `.eh_frame_entry*`, `.sframe*`,
`.gcc_except_table.*`, `.gnu_extab*`, `.exception_ranges*`), `.igot*`,
`.relro_padding`, `COMMON`, `.rela*`, `.relr.dyn`, the stabs names and
`.stab*str`, `.line`, `.gnu_debuglink`, `.jcr` and `.tm_clone_table`, and, for a global or a
function, the four coverage-mapping names LLVM 22 makes non-allocated
metadata by name (`__llvm_covmap`, `__llvm_covfun`, `__llvm_covdata`,
`__llvm_covnames`): llc 22.1.2 emits each without flags, so it is never
loaded, where this backend loaded it (a program reading such a global
through its symbol read it with the import and read garbage or faulted with
llc; refused since the L02-P13 second closure-audit repair). Before
the 2026-09-23 repair the catch-all admitted these as writable data, and a
mutable zero global stored through `.tcommon`, `.gnu_extab`,
`.gcc_except_table.x`, `.exception_ranges`, `.sframe` or `.eh_frame.x` died
with SIGSEGV under GNU ld 2.42 (inside `PT_GNU_RELRO`), and through `.jcr`
under both linkers. Others were misplaced rather than faulting:
`.tm_clone_table` joined crtstuff's TM clone list and `COMMON` joined
`.bss`. `.eh_frame_entry` and `.stab`/`.line` failed the GNU link. ELF also
refuses legacy `.ctors`/`.dtors` and writer-owned names. A name no row
matches is an orphan under both linkers and keeps the global's own flags;
that includes the names one character past a family (`.data.rel.rox`,
`.tcommon.x`, `.jcrx`, `.eh_framex`, `.eh_frame_entq`, `.rodata1.x`,
`.stabx`). The exception is a name BFD matches by a raw prefix: it parses
every input whose name starts with `.eh_frame_entry` as compact unwind
entries and fails the link, and it types orphans named `.rela*` and
`.stab*str`. Those rows cover every spelling, so `.eh_frame_entryx`,
`.eh_frame_entry_x` and `.relax` are refused although they are one
character past a script pattern. The first version of the table matched
only `.eh_frame_entry` and `.eh_frame_entry.*` and admitted the other
spellings. An independent sweep found this, and the rule is now the
prefix. A COMDAT or retained definition's implicit `<base>.<symbol>`
section is classified by the same table. A symbol that would move it to
another row is refused by name, with the explicit rule's code. For example,
a mutable link-once or retained global named `rel.ro` gets `.data.rel.ro`
or `.bss.rel.ro`, which is `[TCG-SECTION-READONLY]`. A retained global
naming an explicit section other globals also name gets a second section of
that name, as llc's unique section, so the others stay collectable. The
explicit-section, COMDAT and retained sections are emitted in the order llc
creates them (a shared section where its first ordinary member is
declared, a COMDAT or retained definition's own section where it is
declared), because the linker concatenates same-named inputs in that order:
a constructor table's run order and a `__start_`/`__stop_` walk follow
llc's whichever kinds of member a section mixes, where llc keeps module
order. llc does not where its `GlobalMerge` pass runs: at O3, and at O1
and O2 for globals a `minsize` function uses, it first combines the
mutable members one function uses together and that bind locally
(`internal`, `private`, hidden, protected or `dso_local`, and not listed in
`@llvm.used` or `@llvm.compiler.used`) into one object, emitted after the
section's other members. The importer keeps declaration order. Measured
with llc 22.1.2 on a set of six members, two of them default external ones
(static and PIE, GNU ld, gold and LLD): the walk differed from llc's in
the 6 O3 runs and equalled it in the 18 at O0-O2; with a `minsize` walker
it differed at O1-O3 (18 of 24 runs); under llc's
`-aarch64-enable-global-merge=false` all 48 runs equalled it. The
verifier's fuzz of mixed member kinds found the same: 2,779 of 2,800 walks
equal, and the 21 that differed were O3 walks of sets with unlisted
`internal` members. An `unnamed_addr` constant that LLVM makes mergeable
is refused by name in an explicit section (see the importer paragraph):
llc writes it in a section of its own flags and entry size, apart from the
section's other members, so it is walked elsewhere. A first version of this
repair emitted every retained global's own section after the shared ones
and ran a used `.init_array` entry after an unlisted one declared later
(24 of 24 runs reversed against llc); until the repair's verifier round
every COMDAT member's section still came after all the others (since
before the repair), so a COMDAT member declared before ordinary members of
a named section was walked last and its `.init_array` entry ran last (24
of 24 walks and 36 of 36 constructor runs differed from llc's, GNU ld,
gold and LLD, O0-O3). The implicit sections (`.data`, `.bss`, `.rodata`,
`.data.rel.ro`, `.tdata`, `.tbss`) still come before every placed one, so
an explicit section named like one of them is a second input section of
