that name after it, where llc puts both kinds of member in one section in
module order. That moves addresses inside one output section only; no
constructor table or `__start_`/`__stop_` walk (none of these names is a C
identifier) reads that order. A sweep
of every name LLVM 22 classifies by name, and of the names this table
classifies, compiled a writable, a constant and two all-zero globals and a
function in each with llc 22.1.2 and with the importer: apart from the
refusals, two classes still differ from llc in flags only. An immutable
global in a `.data*`, `.data1` or `.data.rel.ro*` section is
`SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE` where llc keeps the global's own read-only flags; both
linkers merge either into the same writable (or `PT_GNU_RELRO`) output. An
all-zero global in `.lbss*` is SHT_NOBITS and writable where llc writes
PROGBITS with the global's own flags (LLVM 22 does not classify `.lbss` by
name); a nonzero one there is refused (`[TCG-SECTION-NOBITS]`) where llc
places it. None of the sweep's constants was `unnamed_addr`: one that LLVM
makes mergeable gets `SHF_MERGE` and an entry size from llc and neither
from the import, which therefore refuses it by name in an explicit section
since the L02-P13 second closure-audit repair's second verifier round (the
importer paragraph has the measurements). The sweep's globals hold no pointer; the verifier round of the
L02-P13 second closure-audit repair measured two more differences of that
kind, in flags and header fields only: a constant holding a relocated
pointer in an explicit section (a `tcgcp` set, an `.init_array` entry) is
`SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE` under every relocation model, where llc's `static`
model keeps it read-only (`A`; its `pic` model also writes `WA`), and an
`.init_array` section carries `sh_entsize` 8 where llc writes 0. The
constructor and walk runs above equal llc's under every linker; a `-no-pie`
link of a `static` object gives such a named set a writable output section
(`WA` under GNU ld, gold and LLD) where llc's is read-only (`A`), which
only a store through a pointer to a constant (undefined behavior) can
observe. The table is evidence about
these two linker versions and their default scripts, not a linker proof. A
custom `-T` script, `-z separate-code`, LLD's `-z pack-relative-relocs`
(a synthetic `.relr.dyn`), other linkers (gold, mold) and other BFD versions
may place names differently. Mach-O refuses segments other than
`__DATA`, `__DATA_CONST` and `__TEXT`, `__mod_term_func` and special sections,
and a mutable global in `__DATA,__const` (read-only after fixups).
Explicit function sections (trust-ir v45 `Function.section`) are placed by the
AArch64 ELF module emitters only. Each named function lands in an
`SHF_ALLOC|SHF_EXECINSTR` section of that name with its relocations and FDE:
functions naming one section share it, a COMDAT function gets its own grouped
section of that name, and `.text` names the shared default section, which
`-ffunction-sections` does not split. The accepted names are an allowlist:
a `.text`-prefixed name or a name without a leading `.`, which GNU ld 2.42's
default script and lld fold into `.text` or place as executable orphans.
Refused by name: data-class names (`.data*`, `.rodata*`, `.rodata1`,
`.bss*`, `.tdata*`, `.tcommon`, constructor tables, `.ctors`/`.dtors`,
`.jcr`, `.tm_clone_table`), the unwind and debug families (`.eh_frame*`,
`.gcc_except_table*`, `.gnu_extab*`, `.exception_ranges*`, `.sframe*`,
`.stab*`), every other dot-prefixed name, `.init`/`.fini`, writer- or
linker-owned names, a name a data global in the object also uses, a COMDAT
function naming `.text`, a section on a declaration, malformed names (on
every lane), and `COMMON`, the one undotted name both linkers fold into
`.bss` (`[TCG-SECTION-DATA]`). Mach-O,
x86-64, RISC-V, the JIT and Wasm refuse every function section, `-g` refuses
the split text, and a function's `retained` flag is still refused.
AArch64 Mach-O places relocated immutable globals (vtables, function-pointer
tables) in `__DATA,__const`; ld64 and the standalone linker map it into the
`SG_READ_ONLY` `__DATA_CONST` segment, so a store to one faults once dyld has
applied its fixups (the Mach-O counterpart of `.data.rel.ro` under
`PT_GNU_RELRO`). Mutable relocated globals stay in `__DATA,__data`.
AArch64 Mach-O also relocates the pointer slots inside a thread-local's
`__DATA,__thread_data` initial-value template (`__thread void *p = &x;`, a
per-thread function or interior pointer): ld64 and the standalone linker
rebase the template and every thread starts from the fixed-up pointers.
AArch64 ELF relocates the same templates in `.rela.tdata` (see the ELF
paragraph above); x86-64 Mach-O still refuses a relocated TLS template by
name, and x86-64 ELF refuses every thread-local definition.
A function-body `Constant::SymbolAddr` with a non-zero addend lowers on every
target as the bare symbol reference plus an explicit add, never as an
addend-carrying relocation. One naming a thread-local the module declares is
refused by name in the trust-ir adapter (`[TCG-TLS-SYMBOL-ADDR]`) instead of
being lowered to a plain `ADRP`/`ADD` (ELF) or page (Mach-O) reference to
the TLS symbol, which a linker may accept (GNU ld 2.42 only warns) with an
address that is no thread's copy; `GlobalAddr` is the TLS access path. The
refusal is tested on AArch64 triples only, and a lower-IR `GlobalRef` or
`ExternRef` handed to the `Pipeline` API that names a thread-local object
global is still not refused.
The rustc bridge places `#[link_section]` statics on AArch64 Mach-O and ELF
(a function's or a thread-local's section is refused by name), and the JIT
refuses every explicit section. Function sections and COMDAT groups are AArch64 ELF
only. AArch64 Mach-O has no section groups: a COMDAT function must be bound
weak and is emitted as an `N_WEAK_DEF` atom (every object sets
`MH_SUBSECTIONS_VIA_SYMBOLS`); x86-64 ELF emits `Weak`, `LinkOnce`, `WeakOdr`
and `LinkOnceOdr` functions and globals as `STB_WEAK` definitions in its shared
`.text` and data sections, with no groups. On AArch64 ELF only the ODR function
linkages (`LinkOnceOdr`, `WeakOdr`) become COMDAT (`STB_WEAK` in their own
grouped `.text.<symbol>`); `Weak` and `LinkOnce` functions are plain
`STB_WEAK` definitions in `.text`, and because another object may replace them
at link time the compiler keeps their bodies out of the module inliner and the
structural purity inference (as it does for every preemptible definition under
`pic`). An all-zero COMDAT data definition without a pointer slot uses an
SHT_NOBITS group member (`.bss.<sym>`, or `.tbss.<sym>` for a thread-local);
immutable non-TLS zero data stays in PROGBITS `.rodata.<sym>`. The
Linux execution controls for constructors, per-function `--gc-sections` and
cross-object COMDAT deduplication, including zero link-once data and
thread-locals, run in the Linux regression floor. The
`--gc-sections` row over named function sections is registered in the same
floor target and ran in its qualifying run, but no full floor run has
included it yet. All are execution evidence for GNU ld and glibc on that
host.

Strict byte/halfword register-offset admission and independent word checking
do not establish source-bound memory proofs. Scalar full unrolling folds
only the admitted full64 RO index modes/arithmetic domain and preserves both
the index coefficient and invariant scale. Low32 packed extensions and
unsupported typed expressions conservatively retain RO accesses; this is not
a promise that every valid address expression is fully unrolled. The separate
RI whole-address affine path remains outside that repair's qualification.

The standalone Mach-O linker (`link`, `link_with_dylibs`) loads
`GOT_LOAD_PAGE21/PAGEOFF12` and `POINTER_TO_GOT` targets from
`__DATA_CONST,__got` slots and `TLVP_LOAD_PAGE21/PAGEOFF12` targets from
`__DATA_CONST,__thread_ptrs` slots, keeping every `LDR` (no relaxation). dyld
binds imports, including `__tlv_bootstrap` for `__DATA,__thread_vars`
descriptors, and rebases image definitions and 64-bit data pointers through
chained fixups. It refuses by name pc-relative `ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED` (the
platform linker rejects it too), 32-bit or `__TEXT` absolute image pointers,
PC-relative or difference references to dylib imports, non-TLV references to
thread-locals, malformed TLV descriptors, TLS templates aligned above 16 bytes,
and section types that need initializer, interposing or indirect-pointer
processing. It does not load `S_ATTR_DEBUG` input, so its images carry no unwind
or debug tables. Input `__DATA,__const` and `__DATA_CONST` data land in
`__DATA_CONST,__const` (read-only after fixups); thread-local or zero-fill
storage there is refused. `link_dylib` emits an `MH_DYLIB` that exports its
external, non-private definitions (TLV descriptors as per-thread exports) and
binds its own references to strong definitions directly. Its
default-visibility weak definitions are exported `[weak-def]`, and every
stubbed call, GOT slot and data pointer naming one binds through dyld's
weak-definition lookup (`MH_WEAK_DEFINES | MH_BINDS_TO_WEAK`); a direct page
reference to one is refused (`DirectWeakDefinitionReference`), and weak
thread-local exports stay refused. An executable exports nothing, so its own
weak definitions are resolved statically and take no part in dyld
coalescing. The linker implements no interposable internal binding, flat
namespace, re-exports or symbol table. On macOS AArch64,
`e2e_macho_standalone_got_tlv` runs a GOT stack guard, a two-thread TLS global
and a libSystem data import at O0–O3 next to ld64-linked twins, serves a CG
dylib to an ld64-linked program next to an ld64-built twin dylib and to a
standalone-linked program that imports its functions, data and thread-local,
and checks the images with `dyld_info`. `e2e_aarch64_macho_dylib` links CG
objects with exported, hidden and weak functions and data into dylibs with
ld64 and `link_dylib` and, on macOS AArch64, checks `dlsym` visibility, dyld
weak coalescing with (and without) an executable's weak definitions under the
two-level namespace and ld64 `-flat_namespace`, flat import rebinding,
`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`/`__interpose` interposition of the dylib's exports and
imports (not its direct internal calls), store faults on the relocated
vtable after dyld binding, and ld64 `-dead_strip` keeping only a retained
(`N_NO_DEAD_STRIP`) definition. These are execution checks of those programs, not
linker proofs. The stack-guard admission regression still uses the platform C
linker as an independent object consumer.

Code signing on Apple Silicon: the standalone linker writes an ad-hoc,
linker-signed SHA-256 CodeDirectory over 4 KiB pages (identifier `trust-cg`)
into every executable and dylib and re-reads each image with the independent
verifier `macho::codesign::verify_ad_hoc_signature` before returning it
(`LinkerError::CodeSignatureSelfCheck`/`CodeSignatureContract`). It never
requests the hardened runtime and embeds no entitlements or requirements; a
program that needs either must be re-signed with `codesign`. It writes no
`codeLimit64`, so an image over 4 GiB is refused (`LayoutOverflow`). After a
successful arm64 Darwin link through the system driver, `link_driver::run_link`
checks ld64's signature with the same verifier and removes an unsigned or
invalidly signed output (`error[link:code-signature]`, for example after
`-Wl,-no_adhoc_codesign`); x86_64 Darwin outputs are not checked. The verifier
checks byte-level consistency only: it refuses certificate (CMS) signatures,
non-SHA-256 hashes, scatter, encryption, linkage hashes, bundle-bound
`Info.plist`/resources and fat files by name, and accepts an executable-segment
limit anywhere inside `__TEXT` because the Xcode 27 ld64 records the `__text`
size where `codesign` records the `__TEXT` size. It admits only 4 KiB and
16 KiB code pages and requires the 32-bit `codeLimit` (and any nonzero
`codeLimit64`) to equal the signature offset, so images whose signed prefix
exceeds 4 GiB are refused. `codesign --verify --strict` accepts `--pagesize`
0 and 8192 signatures and a zero `codeLimit` beside a correct `codeLimit64`,
but the macOS 26.6 arm64 kernel kills those images, so the verifier refuses
them. The kernel's signing policy (hardened runtime, library validation,
launch constraints, notarization) is trusted base. `macho_code_signature_native` checks that `codesign --verify
--strict` accepts standalone images, that the kernel runs them and `dlopen`
loads the dylib, and that a changed code byte, a broken SuperBlob and an
unsigned ld64 output are refused by the verifier and `codesign` and killed with
SIGKILL, and that the kernel-killed page sizes and code limit above are refused
by the verifier, on macOS 26.6 only.

Linked-image evidence (`L02-P5`): `macho::linked_image::record_linked_image`
(and `trust-cg --linked-image-evidence` / `link_driver::record_darwin_linked_image`,
which write `<output>.linked-image.json` and remove the output on refusal)
binds an arm64 Mach-O executable or dylib to its input objects by replaying
the objects' relocations against the image, with its own image and object
readers. What it binds: every non-relocation byte of every placed atom; each
`ARM64_RELOC_*` site outside the linker-consumed `__LD,__compact_unwind`
against the resolution the image's fixups (chained
`DYLD_CHAINED_PTR_64`/`_64_OFFSET`, or `LC_DYLD_INFO` rebase, bind, lazy-bind
and weak-bind opcodes), `__stubs` entries, GOT/TLV slots, ld64's `LDR`->`ADD`
relaxations or the linker's static resolution gives; that every fixup inside
object content is at a pointer relocation and every other fixup lies in the
linker's GOT, lazy or TLV pointer slots; that every nonzero byte of a
file-backed section the linker does not synthesize lies in a placed object
atom (so code or data from a link input the request does not name, such as
a `-Wl` object or an archive member, is refused); bind ordinals against
supplied export lists, the objects' weak-import intent, that no name the
objects define is bound to another image, and that every dependent dylib
but libSystem is named by a bind; that a coalescable weak definition (one
the image exports `[weak-def]`) is reached only through dyld's weak lookup;
that `__DATA,__const`/`__DATA_CONST` content lies in `SG_READ_ONLY`
`__DATA_CONST`, code in an executable segment and mutable data in a writable
one; the entry point, header flags, symbol table and exports trie against the
placed definitions (address, kind, weakness; nothing an object defines
hidden or local is exported, and a dylib exports every default-visibility
definition); and the image's SHA-256, UUID, `LC_BUILD_VERSION` tools and
verified ad-hoc signature (cdhash). Every link through the driver removes a
record an earlier link left next to its output, so a record never sits next
to an image it does not describe. What it does not bind: dyld's run-time
choices beyond those fixup semantics (load order, which image a weak lookup
or an interposition selects, whether a named dylib loads), what a dylib
exports at run time (only the supplied list: an image's exports trie, a TAPI
v4 stub such as the SDK's `libSystem.B.tbd`, or a declared set; the CLI
supplies libSystem and `-l` libraries it finds), the linker's own code in
the sections it synthesizes other than the `__stubs` entries and slots a
replayed relocation reaches (stub helpers, `__unwind_info`), all-zero or
zero-fill content outside the object atoms (alignment padding, ld64's
`__dyld_private`, or a zero-initialized variable of an unnamed input),
`__eh_frame` and the relocations of sections the linker consumes
(`__LD,__compact_unwind` is counted, not replayed), and signing policy. The
placement a linker claims is accepted only as far as those checks confirm
it. Objects with `__eh_frame`, literal sections, section-relative
(`r_extern = 0`) relocations or linker optimization hints, flat-namespace
images, images with load-time initializer or interposing sections, arm64e
and universal files, classic image relocations and threaded binds are
refused by name (`[TCG-IMAGE-UNSUPPORTED]`, `[TCG-IMAGE-PARSE]`), each kind
with a control in the tests below (an `S_MOD_INIT_FUNC_POINTERS` section
stands for the load-time sections). Two ld64 links ld64 accepts without a diagnostic
are refused: `-no_data_const` (relocated constants left in writable
`__DATA`, `[TCG-IMAGE-CONST-WRITABLE]`) and a direct page reference to a weak
definition a dylib exports for coalescing (`[TCG-IMAGE-WEAK-DIRECT]`).
`macho_linked_image_evidence` and the CLI's `linked_image_evidence` run the
positive records (ld64 with chained fixups and `LC_DYLD_INFO`, the standalone
linker, executables that exit 42 and dylibs serving a CG program) and the
corruption controls (a patched branch target or opcode; a changed page,
page-offset or GOT-load register; a moved GOT slot, TLV template offset,
data pointer, `SUBTRACTOR` difference, export address or entry point; a
wrong import ordinal; a flipped weak-import bit; a cleared `SG_READ_ONLY`
or `MH_PIE`; an unwritable `__DATA`; a patched instruction; a wrong
placement claim; an object missing a pointer relocation or defining an
exported name hidden or local; a missing or unnamed input object; an unused
`-needed-l` dylib) on macOS 26.6 with ld-27037.1; the standalone rows are
host-neutral. This is independent replay evidence on the image bytes, not a
proof, and it is not composed with the object-level proof inventory.

Stack canaries are admitted for Apple Mach-O and AArch64 Linux ELF with a
global `__stack_chk_guard` (glibc, musl), read through the GOT. Android's
thread-pointer guard, the BSDs, illumos/Solaris and bare-metal triples are
refused by name. The Linux native canary, static, `-nostdlib`, `-z text`,
shared-object and relocation-range controls in `e2e_aarch64_link_runtime` ran
on the Linux AArch64 host (21/21 in
`reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-tls-model-link-controls`; 28/28 with the
per-kind relocation-limit controls below in
`reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-reloc-kind-limits`), as the Darwin controls
did on macOS. The Darwin run predates the seven added tests.

Relocation ranges: an object whose own text layout puts a `CALL26`/`JUMP26`
or direct `ADRP` target outside the psABI window is refused
(`RelocationWindowExceeded`); no range-extension veneer is emitted. Distances
between objects or sections are the linker's: ld64 reports `B/BL out of
range`/`ADRP out of range`, while GNU ld, lld and gold may insert veneers
for `CALL26`. On Linux the driver refuses, in every spelling it reads,
each linker option the fail-open scan below found to turn that refusal off
(`--noinhibit-exec`, GNU ld's `-w`/`--no-warnings`), and a successful link
that still reports such a value (`[TCG-LINK-RANGE-WARNING]`); a way to
silence the linker that neither rule sees would not be caught (the table
below). The Linux control (`call26_beyond_128_mib_is_reached_through_a_linker_veneer`)
places the callee 504 MiB from its trust-cg caller and requires, through
GNU ld 2.42, LLD 22.1.6 and gold 2.42, that the program returns 42 and that
no `BL` in the image branches to the callee itself. Its `JUMP26` twin
(`jump26_beyond_128_mib_is_reached_through_a_linker_veneer`) does the same
for a trust-cg tail call (`B`, `R_AARCH64_JUMP26`, which the O2 build
emits): through each linker the tail branch reaches a veneer and the
program returns 42. The link diagnostic
parser classifies gold's `relocation overflow in R_AARCH64_*`, gold's `TLS
variable referred by reloc N is too far from TP` (naming the relocation by
its number) and LLD's
`improper alignment for relocation R_AARCH64_*` (a scaled `:lo12:` target
that is not a multiple of its access size) as `relocation-out-of-range`,
naming the relocation; none of these messages names the symbol. gold's
`unexpected opcode while processing relocation` line that follows its TLS
message stays unclassified: alone it names no range failure. Inside one function the encoder
refuses by name a jump table its `ADR` cannot reach (`ADR->jump table offset
<delta> does not fit in imm21`, `-2^20 <= delta < 2^20`; tables follow the
body, so only the upper edge is reachable) and any block, instruction or
jump-table offset, or LSDA code length, beyond the u32 relocation/LSDA
domain. A real compile pins the imm21 edge (a second table reached across a
first table of about 262,000 entries: delta `2^20 - 4` admitted, `2^20`
refused). The u32 ceilings need 4 GiB of code in one function; they are
pinned at `u32::MAX`/`2^32` by unit controls that run a real compile with a
unit-test-only synthetic text prefix added inside the four checks
(`pipeline::text_offset_ceiling_tests`), not by a 4 GiB object. Every relocation kind the AArch64
ELF writer accepts has a disposition, `AArch64RelocType::relocation_limit`,
pinned by a unit test over every code the checked writer decodes
(`every_serializable_aarch64_relocation_kind_has_a_pinned_limit`). `X` is the
psABI value (the aaelf64 source read on 2026-09-23, whose change history
runs to 2026Q3); "linker" means the static linker's overflow check:

| Kind (`R_AARCH64_`) | Emitted for | Window on `X` | Who refuses an out-of-window value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ABS64` | data pointer slots, DWARF code addresses | none (64-bit field) | nothing to refuse |
| `ABS32` | DWARF32 section offsets (`-g`) | `-2^31 <= S + A < 2^32` | trust-cg for an addend above `2^32 - 1` (`[TCG-RELOC-WINDOW-ABS32]`), otherwise the linker; GNU ld 2.42 also refuses negative values |
| `PREL32` | `.eh_frame` pointers | `-2^31 <= X < 2^31` (the signed bound of aaelf64 2026Q2; earlier releases allowed `X < 2^32`) | the linker, then the linked image: GNU ld 2.42 refuses `X >= 2^31` itself (classified `relocation-out-of-range`); gold 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 write `2^31 <= X < 2^32`, which an `sdata4` reader takes as negative, so `link_driver::run_link` stages every Linux link and decodes its image's `.eh_frame` as an unwinder does (what section names and `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` locate, and every `.eh_frame` input the link map places, whatever its output section is called, through the driver's own map; an image whose map was not written or cannot show that is `unclassified`): an FDE whose range is outside executable memory, a personality or LSDA pointer outside allocated memory, or a `.eh_frame_hdr` table that disagrees with the FDEs, or a live FDE that a lookup by start would miss, is refused (`relocation-out-of-range`, `[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-WINDOW]`). A pointer whose 32 bits also give another file-backed address where it must lie (another range of code, another address with contents, another section start) is refused as `unclassified` (`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]`); a truncated value that lands in other code or data, and whose true target has contents, looks like that. An image the check cannot complete (an encoding or augmentation it does not read, a truncated record, an image that is not ELF) is also `unclassified`. The check reads the image, not the input relocation, so an image with 4 GiB of file-backed memory in which some pointer has such another address is refused even when its linker, GNU ld included, was given the right address |
| `CALL26`, `JUMP26` | calls, tail calls | `-2^27 <= X < 2^27` | trust-cg for a target in the object's own text, otherwise the linker, which may insert a veneer that clobbers IP0/IP1 (GNU ld 2.42, LLD 22.1.6 and gold 2.42 each veneer both kinds in the native controls); a call to an imported or preemptible function reaches a PLT entry the linker writes, whose `adrp x16` to its `R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT` slot no input relocation describes and GNU ld 2.42 does not check (see the GOT-page row: `run_link` refuses an image not shown in reach that holds such code) |
| `ADR_PREL_PG_HI21` | direct `ADRP` | page delta `-2^32 <= X < 2^32` | trust-cg for a function in the object's own text, otherwise the linker (GNU ld, gold and LLD refuse; the driver refuses `--noinhibit-exec`, which turns that refusal into a warning, and a successful link that reports such a value: see below the table) |
| `ADD_ABS_LO12_NC`, `LDST{8,16,32,64,128}_ABS_LO12_NC` | page offsets of a direct `ADRP` | none: low 12 bits; the `ADRP` carries the high part | trust-cg fuses an `LDST` form only at a guaranteed access-size alignment |
| `ADR_GOT_PAGE`, `TLSIE_ADR_GOTTPREL_PAGE21`, `TLSDESC_ADR_PAGE21` | GOT, initial-exec and TLS-descriptor `ADRP` | page delta `-2^32 <= X < 2^32` | the linker: LLD 22 refuses, but GNU ld 2.42 does not check and writes the delta truncated (as it does for the other GOT-addressing kinds an input can carry; see the table of them below), so `link_driver::run_link` stages the link, re-reads the staged image and, before it reaches the output, refuses one it cannot show keeps every executable byte within the window of every place a GOT slot can lie when a positional input or, on Linux, any AArch64 ELF relocatable object the linker's input trace names carries such a use (a `-Wl` operand, a `-l:<file>` library, a regular or thin archive member, a linker script's `INPUT()` or `GROUP()` file, or a C runtime start file): `relocation-out-of-range` (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`) for a use whose own slot, named by its dynamic relocation, no code byte reaches, otherwise `unclassified` (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`, a conservative refusal), and `[TCG-LINK-INPUT-TRACE]` when the trace does not show what was loaded. Whatever the inputs, it also refuses such an image when it holds GOT-addressing code the linker wrote itself, whose `ADRP`s GNU ld 2.42 leaves as unchecked: a PLT (`R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT`, `DT_JMPREL` or an executable `.plt`), an IPLT (`R_AARCH64_IRELATIVE` or an executable `.iplt`) or the lazy TLS descriptor trampoline (`DT_TLSDESC_PLT`): `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]` for a PLT entry's `JUMP_SLOT` slot or the trampoline's `DT_TLSDESC_GOT` word that no code byte reaches, otherwise `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`; gold 2.42 aborts on the probe's GOT placements either way. In an executable the linker may instead relax a `TLSIE_*` or `TLSDESC_*` access to its own thread-local into the local-exec pair `movz`/`movk` (`TPREL_G1`, `TPREL_G0_NC`), whose window is `0 <= TPREL(S + A) < 2^32` (the 16-byte TCB aligned up to the `PT_TLS` alignment, plus the offset in the block): GNU ld 2.42 writes a larger `TPREL` truncated without a diagnostic, gold 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 refuse it (classified), and `run_link` refuses an executable whose thread-local block reaches `2^32` above the thread pointer, its end included (a zero-size thread-local there has that `TPREL`; `unclassified`, `[TCG-LINK-TLS-TPREL-UNPROVEN]`) |
| `LD64_GOT_LO12_NC`, `TLSIE_LD64_GOTTPREL_LO12_NC`, `TLSDESC_LD64_LO12`, `TLSDESC_ADD_LO12` | GOT slot page offsets | none: low 12 bits of the slot the paired `ADRP` checks; slots must be 8-byte aligned | the linker lays out aligned slots |
| `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12` | local-exec TLS | `0 <= TPREL(S + A) < 2^24` | trust-cg when the 16-byte TCB plus the thread-local's offset in its object's TLS section plus the addend already reaches `2^24` (`[TCG-RELOC-WINDOW-TLSLE]`), otherwise the linker (GNU ld 2.42, gold and LLD 22 refuse `2^24`; not suppressible through the driver, below the table) |
| `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_LO12_NC` | local-exec TLS | none: low 12 bits of the `HI12` value | nothing to refuse |
| `TLSDESC_CALL`, `NONE` | descriptor-call marker; `NONE` never | no value | nothing to refuse |
| `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_LO12` | never emitted | `0 <= X < 2^12` | not applicable |

"The linker" in this table is the linker's own refusal. The driver keeps
every option it knows to switch that refusal off out of the link, but it
does not re-derive these kinds' windows from the image, so the refusal is
only as complete as that list.

*Correction (2026-09-26, the tenth closure audit):* `-Wl,--noinhibit-exec`
makes GNU ld 2.42, gold 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 write the output and exit 0
after an error, and `run_link` treated exit 0 as success. With a 16 MiB C
`.tdata` before trust-cg's local-exec thread-local, all three installed
`add x0, x0, #0x0, lsl #12` for a `TPREL` of `0x1000010`, and the program
wrote the C thread-local instead of its own (exit 1; SIGSEGV when
`--static`); a `-nostdlib` link whose trust-cg `ADRP` reached a word 8 GiB
away installed `adrp x0, 0` through GNU ld and gold (SIGSEGV). Every
spelling a linker reads is now refused before any process runs
(`[TCG-LINK-NOINHIBIT-EXEC]`): each spelling the measured option table
lists for any of the three linkers, GNU ld's `noinhibit_exec` alias (which
`--help` does not print and the table therefore did not list; `strings
ld.bfd` shows it, and `-Wl,--noinhibit_exec` links), and any prefix of
either name from three letters. A second defense covers a way to make the
linker finish such a link that still reports the value: a successful link
whose standard error reports a relocation value outside its window (GNU
ld's `relocation truncated to fit`, gold's `relocation overflow in` and
`TLS variable ... too far from TP`, LLD's `out of range` and `improper
alignment`, classified as `relocation-out-of-range` or
`tls-model-mismatch`) is refused as `[TCG-LINK-RANGE-WARNING]`, with the
linker's lines, and nothing is written. A `cc` that adds
`-Wl,--noinhibit-exec` behind the driver's back shows it in `link_options`
`linux_got_page::a_link_the_linker_would_refuse_is_never_made_to_succeed`,
through all three linkers; the 16-byte-pad twin links and runs through the
same `cc`.

*Correction (2026-09-26, the verifier of that repair):* the second defense
is not independent of the linker. GNU ld 2.42's `-w` (`--no-warnings`)
suppresses every message, errors included, and an error then no longer
fails the link: `-Wl,-w` installed trust-cg's truncated
`TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12` (the program printed `w=49` instead of 84, also
`--pie` and `--no-pie`) and its `adrp x1, 0` (SIGSEGV), with nothing on
standard error for `[TCG-LINK-RANGE-WARNING]` to read. `--no-warnings` and
its one-dash and prefix spellings (to `--no-warni`) are refused as
`[TCG-LINK-NO-WARNINGS]`, and so is `-w`; LLD reads `-w` as suppressing
warnings only and gold rejects it, so it is refused whatever the linker.
GNU ld and gold also read a one-dash piece that is not one of their long
options as a group of short options (`-ws`, `-sw` and `-wx` are `-w` with
another option to GNU ld; gold links `-sofoo` into `foo`, outside the
stage, and `-szexecstack` with an executable stack), so every such group
is refused (`[TCG-LINK-OPTION-GROUP]`, below). A scan of every flag of the
three measured tables (and each value of `--unresolved-symbols` and of the
`-z` keywords that suppress errors) against five links each linker refuses
(a far `ADRP`, a `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12` past `2^24`, a misaligned
`LDST64_ABS_LO12_NC`, and undefined references in a static and a dynamic
program) found the options that make one succeed: `--noinhibit-exec` (all
three), `-w` and `--no-warnings` and their groups (GNU ld), the
undefined-reference options below, the relocatable-output options `-r`,
`-i`, `-Ur` and `--relocatable` (which leave every relocation to a later
link; with the C runtime the link fails), gold's one-dash groups that
begin with `-r` (the same), and GNU ld's `--unique`, whose far link
succeeded because `--section-start=.far` no longer named the unique output
section, which it placed within the window (the image is correct). The
driver refuses every one of these in each spelling it reads but the
relocatable-output options. A way to make a linker finish a link with an
out-of-window value that is neither among these nor leaves a message would
not be seen; the kinds GNU ld truncates without any option are the
GOT-addressing ones below, which the image check reads.

Options that let an undefined reference of the linked objects link are
refused as `[TCG-LINK-UNRESOLVED-SYMBOLS]`: `--warn-unresolved-symbols`
(all three linkers), gold's `--weak-unresolved-symbols`,
`--unresolved-symbols=ignore-all` and `=ignore-in-object-files` (and the
option without its value in the same group; each linker accepts exactly
the four values), and `-z undefs` in an executable's link (GNU ld, LLD;
gold rejects it). The reference then resolves to 0. A shared object's
link allows undefined references already (they stay dynamic imports; a
hidden one is still refused), and there GNU ld 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 wrote
the same bytes with and without `-z undefs` (after `-z defs` too, for PIC
and non-PIC inputs), so since the eleventh closure audit `--shared` links
admit it (`link_options`
`linux_got_page::ordinary_links_the_eleventh_audit_found_refused_are_installed`
compares the bytes). `--unresolved-symbols=report-all` and
`=ignore-in-shared-libs` are admitted: the latter, like
`--allow-shlib-undefined`, lets the undefined symbols of the shared
libraries the link reads through, which the dynamic loader resolves or
refuses to run the program over.

A second scan (2026-09-26, after the second verifier of the repair) ran
every flag of the three measured tables, every `-z` keyword each linker's
`--help` names and the four `--unresolved-symbols` values (10,980 links)
against links whose refusal or value trust-cg's code relies on: a copy
relocation of a library's protected variable and a protected function's
canonical PLT entry in a `--no-pie` program, a local-exec access to a
library's thread-local (each refused by the linkers that refuse it
without options), a copy-relocated default variable (99), a default
function's address equality and an undefined weak reference (0). It
reported 440 pairs whose link succeeded where the plain link was refused
or whose program returned another value; through the driver every one is
refused but `-z nodefaultlib` (GNU ld, gold), whose programs are
installed and fail to load their C library (exit 127, a loud failure).
The refusals the scan added, each in every spelling the driver reads:
gold's `-z nocopyreloc`, which resolves a `--no-pie` program's
position-dependent reference to a library's variable to 0 without a
diagnostic (the program dies with SIGSEGV; GNU ld and LLD refuse the link
and are a no-op in a PIE), refused by name for every linker
(`[TCG-LINK-COPY-RELOCATION]`); LLD's `--ignore-data-address-equality`
and `--ignore-function-address-equality` (the same code; above); LLD's
`--unique`, which puts `crti.o`'s and `crtn.o`'s `.init` and `.fini`
pieces in separate output sections so the program runs into the
prologue's end (SIGILL), and a `--start-lib` that no later `--end-lib`
closes, with which LLD reads the C driver's own start files, which follow
the `-Wl` groups, as lazy objects and drops `crtn.o` (SIGILL), both
refused as `[TCG-LINK-C-RUNTIME-LAYOUT]` (a closed `--start-lib` is
admitted and runs; `--unique` is refused whatever the linker, although
GNU ld reads it for orphan sections only and links a correct image, and
gold rejects it); and the entry-point rule below, which refuses the
verifier's `-export-dyn` and the scan's 35 one-dash spellings that gold
or LLD read as `-e<symbol>` (`-error-limit`, `-execute-only`,
`-enable-linker-version`, ...) when nothing defines the symbol.
`link_options` `linux_got_page::options_that_let_a_relied_on_refusal_or_the_entry_go_are_refused`
measures each outside the driver and through it. A way to turn off a
refusal these links do not exercise would not be seen.

One-dash groups of short options are refused as `[TCG-LINK-OPTION-GROUP]`.
The driver's checks read a piece by its first letter (`-o<file>`,
`-z<keyword>`, `-T<script>`), and a group hides the options after the
first: gold 2.42 reads a one-dash piece that is not one of its one-dash
long options letter by letter, each letter that takes no argument (`E G M
N S V X d g i n p q r s t v x`) followed by another option, so `-sofoo` is
`-s -o foo`, `-son` is `-s -o n`, `-no-dynamic-linker` is `-n -o
-dynamic-linker` and `-debug-names` sets the entry point `bug-names`. GNU
ld 2.42 does the same with a piece that is no long option of its own nor a
prefix of exactly one (`-sw` is `-s -w`), with a deprecation warning, and
fails a group that holds an option taking an argument ("unable to
disambiguate"); LLD reads no group. So a one-dash piece of two or more
characters that begins with one of `E G M N S V X d g i n p q r s t v w x`
is refused unless its name (before any `=`) is one of the 217 one-dash
long options gold links exactly as their two-dash spellings (or rejects as
unknown), measured on the host for every name of the three tables that
begins with such a letter; GNU ld reads each of those it knows as its long
option and fails the others. `link_options`
`linux_got_page::short_option_groups_are_refused_and_one_dash_long_options_are_read_as_such`
measures the rule: no other letter starts a group in either linker, and
every one-dash name the three linkers' `--help` list that the driver
admits links through gold as its two-dash spelling. The cost: GNU ld's
one-dash abbreviations of long options that begin with those letters
(`-no-as-need`), GNU ld's one-dash spellings gold groups
(`-no-dynamic-linker`, `-non_shared`, `-dT=<file>`) and the deprecated
groups themselves are refused; each has a two-dash spelling. The piece
`-dT` alone, which GNU ld and LLD list as their alias of
`--default-script`, is admitted since the eleventh closure audit (Fedora's
`LDFLAGS` pass its package note so): gold reads it as `-d -T`, so each
linker reads the next piece as a linker script, which the checks read it
as, and gold wrote the same bytes with `-dT <script>` as with `-T
<script>`, a common symbol included. A piece that
begins with a letter taking an argument (`-lwayland`, `-L/w/lib`,
`-export-dyn`) is one option with its argument, read by that letter as
before. gold 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 read `-export-dyn` as `-e xport-dyn`
(GNU ld reads it as `--export-dynamic`), and for an entry symbol nothing
defines they write `e_entry` 0, gold with a warning and LLD without one:
the second verifier of the repair found `--pie` and `--no-pie` programs
installed that died before any of their code ran (SIGSEGV, SIGILL). Every
executable's entry point is now read in the image
(`[TCG-LINK-ENTRY-POINT]`, below), and those links are refused. An input
path that begins with `-`, which the C driver would read as an option, is refused as
`[TCG-LINK-OPTION-INPUT]`.

The eleventh L02-P10 closure audit found that the image check compared byte
ranges while the kernel and `ld.so` map `PT_LOAD` segments by page (an
`AT()` linker script mapped another file page over trust-cg's `.data`, and
`-z max-page-size=16` and LLD's `-n` installed images that failed at load).
That rule is now a page model at every page an AArch64 kernel maps with; see
`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]` below.

The trust-cg refusals see only what one object fixes: a lower bound, or a
target in its own text. The image check in `run_link` does not find the
GOT by section name. A linker script can move the GOT's contents into an
output section of any name (`.slots : { *(.got) *(.igot) }` with `INSERT
BEFORE .got`), and a slot the linker fills itself needs no dynamic
relocation (every slot of a position-dependent executable for a symbol it
defines). Until the 2026-09-23 repair the check compared the farthest code
byte with the farthest `.got`/`.got.*` byte, which was not conservative:
with the GOT's slots moved to 8 GiB and `.got.plt` left at 2 GiB, GNU ld
2.42 wrote `adrp x1, 0` for the `ADR_GOT_PAGE` site, the check admitted the
library, and an executable using it died with SIGSEGV. The check now takes
every executable byte (an `SHF_EXECINSTR` section or a `PF_X` `PT_LOAD`
segment) as a possible GOT-page `ADRP`. It takes every place a slot can lie
as a possible target: every allocated section with file contents, every
`PT_LOAD` segment's file contents, every target of the relocation tables
the dynamic section names (`DT_RELA`, `DT_REL`, `DT_JMPREL`, `DT_RELR`) and
of the allocated relocation sections (a static `.rela.iplt`), the GOT words
`DT_PLTGOT` and `DT_TLSDESC_GOT` name, and each zero-fill section or
segment tail that holds such a target. Zero fill that holds no target does
not count, so a large `.bss` is admitted. The possible slots also include
every non-allocated section that is placed at an address or writable.
GNU ld 2.42 refuses a GOT in a `NOLOAD` section ("section has no
contents"). It accepts `INFO`, `COPY`, `DSECT` and `OVERLAY` output
sections, which are not allocated but keep the address the script gives
them. Laid over `NOLOAD` zero fill, such a section's undefined-weak slot
reads zero, its right value. On 2026-09-23 a static executable built that
way at 8 GiB was installed by the first repair and died with SIGSEGV,
while its 1 GiB twin runs. The sections an ordinary image does not load
(`.comment`, `.symtab`, `.debug_*`) are at address 0 and not writable, and
none of the 4,684 ELF executables and shared objects scanned on the Linux
host has another kind. Program headers describe only loaded memory, so an
image without a section header table (`-z nosectionheader`) is never shown
in reach and is refused as unproven. Its dynamic tables are still read
through the program headers to label an observed overflow. The check
cannot see:

- a slot the linker fills but places in allocated zero fill that no
  relocation or tag names, where it reads zero. GNU ld refuses that for
  `NOLOAD`, and LLD checks the window itself.
- a non-allocated section left at address 0 that is not writable. GNU ld
  keeps a GOT's write flag there and rejects `(INFO READONLY)`.
- a zero-fill slot filled through Android's packed `DT_ANDROID_RELA`
  relocations.
- code that is not executable where it is loaded.

Linker-written code is a route that no input relocation shows. A call to
an imported or preemptible function carries only `R_AARCH64_CALL26`, which
the linker checks, but it reaches a PLT entry whose `adrp x16` to its
`R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT` slot (and the PLT header's to `DT_PLTGOT`) GNU ld
2.42 writes without checking the page window, as it does for
`ADR_GOT_PAGE`. Until the second L02-P10 closure audit (2026-09-23) the
image check refused only for an input's GOT-page use, so `trust-cg --format=text
-shared -nostdlib --relocation-model pic -o libplt.so caller.trust_ir
-Wl,--section-start=.got.plt=0x200010000` exited 0 and installed a library
whose `.plt` held `adrp x16, 0x10000` for a slot at `0x200010018`; a
`cc -rdynamic` user that defines `tcg_desc_bump` and calls `tcg_call_desc`
died with SIGSEGV, as it did with `.got` placed at `0x200000000` too, while
the twin with `.got.plt` at `0x80010000` runs. An image not shown in reach
is now refused, whatever its inputs, when it holds a PLT, an IPLT or the
lazy TLS descriptor trampoline. A slot such code is known to address (each
PLT entry's `JUMP_SLOT` slot and the trampoline's `DT_TLSDESC_GOT` word)
that no code byte reaches is an observed overflow
(`relocation-out-of-range`, `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`); other such code
(a PLT header, an IPLT, whose `IRELATIVE` target can also be a data word)
is a conservative refusal (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`). The code is
found from the dynamic section (`DT_JMPREL`, `DT_TLSDESC_PLT`), the dynamic
and allocated relocation tables and the executable `.plt` and `.iplt`
sections. A linker script can hide a static image's IPLT: the third
L02-P10 closure audit's script merged `.iplt` into `.text` and `.rela.iplt`
into a `PROGBITS` `.rodata`, and `trust-cg --format=text --static --nostdlib
--no-pie -Wl,ifunc.o -Wl,-T,script_0x200000000.ld -o prog helper.trust_ir`
installed a program whose IPLT held `adrp x16, 0` and which died with
SIGSEGV, as did the same program linked with `-z nosectionheader` and
`.got.plt` at 8 GiB. So the image is no longer the only evidence: a defined
`STT_GNU_IFUNC` symbol in a positional or traced AArch64 ELF relocatable
input is a page-window use of its own (the linker gives every IFUNC a PLT or
IPLT entry), and an image not shown in page reach is refused naming it
(`unclassified`, `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`). Both audit programs are
now refused, GNU ld's own die with SIGSEGV, and their 2 GiB twins with
section headers link and return 42; with `-z nosectionheader` the 2 GiB
twin is refused too (no image without a section header table is shown in
reach). This is refusal, not location: the driver does not find a hidden
IPLT in the image, because nothing in an image without section headers or
symbols marks it. Not seen: linker-written code for an IFUNC that no
examined input defines (only a link outside the driver, or one whose
inputs are not AArch64 ELF relocatable objects, can have one); an image
that cannot be read as ELF, which is refused only when an input carries a
GOT-addressing use; and other linker-written stubs (range-extension and
erratum veneers, which GNU ld builds with `ADRP` only for a target in
range).

The check models every aaelf64 relocation that addresses a GOT slot from
the place it patches, each with its own window, and reads every positional
and traced AArch64 ELF relocatable input for it
(`link_driver::AARCH64_GOT_ADDRESSING_RELOCATIONS`, pinned against a
transcript of the aaelf64 source read on 2026-09-23 by the unit test
`got_addressing_kinds_match_the_psabi_tables`). The GNU ld 2.42 column is
what that linker did on the Linux host with the GOT placed out of the
window (`-shared -nostdlib`, `.got` at 8 GiB for the page and data kinds,
16 MiB for the others; objects from GNU as 2.42, or with the type patched
where GNU as has no syntax):

| Kind (`R_AARCH64_`) | Access | Window on `X` | GNU ld 2.42 out of window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ADR_GOT_PAGE`, `TLSIE_ADR_GOTTPREL_PAGE21`, `TLSDESC_ADR_PAGE21`, `TLSGD_ADR_PAGE21` | `ADRP` | page delta `-2^32 <= X < 2^32` | links, delta truncated |
| `TLSLD_ADR_PAGE21` | `ADRP` | page delta `-2^32 <= X < 2^32` | refuses ("relocation truncated to fit") |
| `TLSIE_LD_GOTTPREL_PREL19`, `TLSDESC_LD_PREL19` | load-literal `LDR` | `-2^20 <= X < 2^20` | links, offset truncated |
| `GOT_LD_PREL19` | load-literal `LDR` | `-2^20 <= X < 2^20` | refuses |
| `TLSLD_LD_PREL19` | load-literal `LDR` | `-2^20 <= X < 2^20` | does not recognize the type |
| `TLSGD_ADR_PREL21`, `TLSDESC_ADR_PREL21` | `ADR` | `-2^20 <= X < 2^20` | links, offset truncated |
| `TLSLD_ADR_PREL21` | `ADR` | `-2^20 <= X < 2^20` | refuses |
| `GOTPCREL32` | 32-bit data word | `-2^31 <= X < 2^31` | does not recognize the type |
| `AUTH_ADR_GOT_PAGE`, `AUTH_TLSDESC_ADR_PAGE21`, `AUTH_GOT_LD_PREL19`, `AUTH_GOT_ADR_PREL_LO21` (PAuth ABI) | `ADRP`, `LDR`, `ADR` | as the non-PAuth form | does not recognize the type |

Every row is checked the same way, whatever one linker does with it. An
access sits in executable memory (a data word anywhere), and the image does
not record which instruction addresses which slot, so a narrow-window use
is in reach only when every place a slot can lie is within 1 MiB of every
code byte. A tiny-model library larger than 1 MiB is therefore refused
conservatively even when GNU ld wrote it correctly. The closure audit's
tiny-model reproducer (`ldr x0, :gottprel:ievar` followed by 1.5 MiB of
text, `trust-cg -shared -nostdlib --relocation-model pic
-Wl,tie_0x180000.o -o lib.so b1_scalars.tmbc`) and its general-dynamic
reproducer (`adrp x0, :tlsgd:gdvar` with `-Wl,--section-start=.got=0x200000000`)
were installed before this check modeled their kinds; their users died
with SIGSEGV and read module 0. Both are now refused, as are the `ADR` and
descriptor load-literal routes with `.got` at 16 MiB, and each 64 KiB or
2 GiB twin links and runs. An image whose code and possible slots are more
than 1 MiB apart (any library or executable that large) is not shown in
reach for the narrow kinds, so its linker input trace is read, and a trace
that does not show what was loaded (`-Wl,--verbose`, `-Wl,-M`) now refuses
it with `[TCG-LINK-INPUT-TRACE]`.

The `LDR` GOT-base forms (`LD64_GOTPAGE_LO15`, GCC's small-PIC `-fpic` GOT
load, `G(GDAT(S)) - Page(GOT)`; `LD64_GOTOFF_LO15`, `G(GDAT(S)) - GOT`;
and their PAuth forms; all `0 <= X < 2^15`) are checked too. *Correction
(2026-09-23):* these forms were first exempted on the ground that the
linker places both the slot and the base and rejects an out-of-range
value. That holds for GNU ld and gold 2.42, which refuse
`LD64_GOTPAGE_LO15` out of range, but not for LLD 22, which writes it
truncated to 15 bits. With 6,000 GOT slots, `trust-cg -shared -nostdlib
--relocation-model pic -Wl,gb.o -o libgb.so b1_scalars.tmbc` linked through
LLD was installed: `dv_last`'s slot lay `X = 48528` above the page of
`_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_`, LLD wrote `X & 0x7ff8`, and the user printed
`f_gb=1904` instead of 4242; a default PIE linked through LLD was installed
and wrong too. LLD does the same for a GOT reference to an IFUNC in a
static program, whose slot it puts in `.got.plt` 64 KiB from `.got`. Each
linker measures these forms from `_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_`, which is not
always the start of `.got` (GNU ld's PIE and gold's large GOT keep slots
below it), so the check reads the base from the image's symbol table and
requires every place a slot can lie (the whole section holding the base,
each `GLOB_DAT`, `AUTH_GLOB_DAT` and `IRELATIVE` target, and the
`IRELATIVE` entries between `__rela_iplt_start` and `__rela_iplt_end`) to
be at or above the base (or its page) and less than 32 KiB above it. A use
whose own `GLOB_DAT` slot is outside that window is an observed overflow
(`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`); any other use of an image not shown is
refused conservatively (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`), including every
image whose base cannot be located: a stripped image, one without a
section header table, and an LLD image whose code never names
`_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_`. The conservative refusal also rejects a library
GNU ld wrote correctly with a GOT larger than 32 KiB. Such an image, and
any image without the symbol, now has its linker input trace read, so a
trace that does not show what was loaded refuses it. Not seen: an IFUNC
slot whose `IRELATIVE` relocation a linker script hid from the section
headers and from `__rela_iplt_start`/`__rela_iplt_end` (so no start-up
code applies it), and a `_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_` that an input or a linker
script defined away from the base the linker measures from.

*Correction (2026-09-26, the tenth closure audit):* that rule refused
every GCC small-PIC (`-fpic`) object in a stripped link, through all three
linkers and in every output kind (the image has no symbol table to locate
the base in), and every `-fpic` object in an LLD `--static` link (static
glibc's IPLT slots, `IRELATIVE` targets in `.got.plt`, lie 74 KiB above
the base page), although the programs ran. GNU ld 2.42 and gold 2.42
refuse a GOT-base value out of its window themselves (measured again with
4,400 slots: GNU ld's `relocation truncated to fit` for both kinds,
gold's `relocation overflow in` for `GOTPAGE_LO15` and an internal error
for `GOTOFF_LO15`, in dynamic, `--static` and `--no-pie` links; LLD 22.1.6
wrote `GOTPAGE_LO15` truncated and every program died with SIGSEGV, and
rejects `GOTOFF_LO15`), so for a linker whose `--version` names it exactly
as the option table was measured the GOT-base windows are now the linker's,
as a direct `ADRP`'s are, and the options found to switch that refusal
off are refused (above). For LLD the image is still checked, with two
refinements. A stripped LLD image's base is LLD's synthetic GOT as the
driver's map places it (`<internal>:(.got)`): LLD measures the form from
the page of that section (`RE_AARCH64_GOT_PAGE`) and defines
`_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_` at its start on AArch64; the map's address equals
the unstripped twin's symbol in dynamic, PIE, `--no-pie` and `--static`
links. And an `IRELATIVE` target is a possible slot only of a use against
a symbol the image defines as an IFUNC (`STT_GNU_IFUNC`): LLD points a
GOT-base form against a non-preemptible IFUNC at its IPLT slot in
`.got.plt` and keeps the symbol's type, and when the IFUNC's address is
also taken directly it gives the symbol `STT_FUNC` and puts the GOT slot,
holding the IPLT entry's address, in `.got` (both read on the host). A
use against a symbol the image's symbol table defines, none of its
definitions an IFUNC, and that its object does not bind locally, is
checked against the section holding the base and the `GLOB_DAT` targets
alone. The audit's links now install and run: every stripped `-fpic`
link through GNU ld and gold, LLD's stripped dynamic, PIE and `--no-pie`
links, LLD's unstripped `--static` link (its uses name
`__stack_chk_guard`), C++ `-fpic` programs and libraries stripped with
`-s`. Still refused (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`, conservative): LLD's
stripped `--static` `-fpic` link (no symbol table to show that a symbol is
no IFUNC; its synthetic GOT is placed, but the IPLT slots are 74 KiB
above), an LLD image whose GOT itself spans more than 32 KiB, a use of an
object's local symbol, and a use against an IFUNC whose IPLT slot is out
of the window. The last is a real overflow: a static program that loads
an IFUNC's address through its `-fpic` GOT slot, linked by LLD outside
the driver, reads the wrong slot and dies with SIGSEGV
(`linux_got_page::small_pic_objects_link_where_their_got_window_is_shown`
refuses it and runs its canonical twin).

The other aaelf64 GOT relocations need no image check. The `MOVW` GOT-base
forms (`MOVW_GOTOFF_*`, `TLSGD_MOVW_*`, `TLSLD_MOVW_*`,
`TLSIE_MOVW_GOTTPREL_*`, `TLSDESC_OFF_*` and their PAuth forms) measure a
slot from the GOT base as well, but no linker on the host writes one out of
its window (the 2026-09-23 probe of all three linkers): GNU ld 2.42 refuses
`MOVW_GOTOFF_G1` (against an IFUNC whose slot is in `.got.plt` 8 GiB away)
and `TLSDESC_OFF_G1` (`.got.plt` 8 GiB from `.got`) out of range, keeps the
`TLSGD_MOVW_G1` and `TLSIE_MOVW_GOTTPREL_G1` slots in `.got` next to the
base, where their +-4 GiB window cannot be exceeded, and does not recognize
the other checked forms (every `MOVW_GOTOFF_*` but `_G0_NC` and `_G1`,
`TLSLD_MOVW_*`, the PAuth forms); gold 2.42 stops with an internal error
or does not recognize every one; LLD 22 recognizes none; and the `_NC` and
`G3` forms carry no psABI check. The low-12-bit forms (`LD64_GOT_LO12_NC`,
`TLSGD_ADD_LO12_NC`, `TLSLD_ADD_LO12_NC`, `TLSIE_LD64_GOTTPREL_LO12_NC`,
`TLSDESC_LD64_LO12`, `TLSDESC_ADD_LO12` and their PAuth forms) carry no
check and pair with a checked row; `TLSDESC_LDR`, `TLSDESC_ADD`,
`TLSDESC_CALL` and `AUTH_TLSDESC_CALL` mark instructions without a value.
Only AArch64 ELF relocatable inputs are read. On Linux those include the
objects LLD 22.1.6 compiles from LLVM bitcode, which the driver keeps and
reads. An image whose compiled objects are not read is refused whenever
these checks need them (`[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]`, the 2026-10-15
correction below). A link made outside the driver is not examined.

An image whose possible sites and slots span more than a use's window is
refused. A use whose own slot a dynamic relocation names
(`R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT`, `R_AARCH64_TLS_DTPMOD64`, `R_AARCH64_TLS_TPREL64` or
`R_AARCH64_TLSDESC` against the use's non-local symbol), and whose slot no
possible site reaches within the use's window, is an observed overflow
(`relocation-out-of-range`, `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`). Every other use is a conservative refusal
(`unclassified`, `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`), whose text says that no
overflow was observed. The conservative refusal also rejects libraries that
GNU ld and LLD link correctly, such as one with an executable section 8 GiB
from a GOT that its own code reaches. A link with such an input is staged
like a local-exec link (below): the linker writes into a driver-owned
directory, a refused image is removed with it, and the requested output is
neither read nor removed. A staged image that cannot be read as an ELF
image, or whose dynamic section names a relocation table the image does not
hold, is refused as `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNCHECKED]` (`unclassified`), not
as an observed overflow. The check covers only links through `run_link` (the
CLI's link step) and only AArch64 ELF relocatable inputs: the positional
inputs and, on Linux, every one the linker's input trace names, including
archive members and the C driver's own start files, and the objects LLD
compiles from LLVM bitcode (unread ones refuse the image,
`[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]`), but not shared
libraries (which apply no relocation to the link) or links made outside the
driver. On a non-Linux ELF target (an explicit `*-unknown-none` or other
triple whose operating system is not Linux) the link is not traced, and only
positional inputs are read. The native
controls in `e2e_aarch64_link_runtime` place sections with
`--section-start` or a linker script, not with 4 GiB images. Since the
eighth closure audit the direct `ADRP`, `ABS32` and `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12`
controls run through the link driver with GNU ld 2.42, LLD 22.1.6 and gold
2.42. Each far layout that moves the trust-cg access out of its window
requires the linker's own refusal, a `relocation-out-of-range` diagnostic
of the kind that names the trust-cg access (its target symbol, its
function or its object), or the driver's refusal by name, and nothing
installed. A diagnostic of the kind at another place (the C runtime's own
page references) does not count. The driver keeps a classified diagnostic
without a target once per kind, relocation and place: gold names no
target symbol, and its lines at different places were collapsed into one
before the ninth closure audit, so each of gold's lines now prints its own
`error[link:relocation-out-of-range]` line. The function a gold or LLD
line names the place in is kept as the diagnostic's `function`, apart
from its subject (the target), so the printed `error[link:..]` line is
unchanged and a failure in `g` never hides a later one that references
`g`.
- **`ADR_PREL_PG_HI21`.** The word lies in its own read-only
  `.tcg_far_data` 8 GiB above `.text` (pinned at 8 MiB). All three linkers
  refuse it at `far_word.o`'s `tcg_read_far`: GNU ld and LLD name the
  target `tcg_far_word`, and gold and LLD the function `tcg_read_far`. LLD and gold also
  refuse the C runtime's page references there, each kept as its own
  diagnostic. Placing `.data` instead made LLD lay `.text` out after it (no
  distance) and gold stop with an internal error. The 1 GiB twin runs
  through each.
- **`ABS32`.** With `--section-start=.debug_str=0x100000000` GNU ld
  refuses the offsets. LLD and gold keep a non-allocated `.debug_str` at
  address 0 whatever `--section-start` asks, so that placement does not
  move it: their images, `.debug_str` at 0, are installed and run, and
  that control shows nothing about their window. A second control uses a
  complete linker script that puts the `.debug_str` input into an
  allocated `.rodata` at 4 GiB (a static `-nostdlib` program): all three
  linkers refuse it (GNU ld `relocation truncated to fit` against
  `.debug_str`, LLD `out of range`, gold `relocation overflow in
  R_AARCH64_ABS32`, each at `debug_probe.o`), and its twin, `.rodata` after
  `.eh_frame`, runs through each. A debug section kept non-allocated cannot
  move past 4 GiB through LLD or gold.
- **`TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12`.** All three refuse the thread-local behind a
  16 MiB pad (gold names only the function `tcg_le_edge_bump`); the edge and the
  other order run.

These, with the `ABS32` script control, not the one-time probe below, are
now the per-kind evidence for gold and LLD. A GOT placed 8 GiB from a `pic` shared object's
code, or 64 KiB past the window's upper edge, is refused by the driver as
an overflow after GNU ld links it, and a file already at the output keeps
its bytes, while the 2 GiB twin links and runs. So are the GOT's slots moved
to 8 GiB by an `INSERT` script, with and without a section header table,
and a position-dependent executable's linker-filled slot moved the same way
(refused as unproven); GNU ld links both into programs that do not pass
without the driver. The same script with the slots at 1 GiB links and runs.
An executable section 8 GiB from the code, with no GOT reference, is refused
as unproven, although the library GNU ld writes without the driver loads
and runs. A static executable whose script moves its GOT into an `INFO`,
`COPY`, `DSECT` or `OVERLAY` section at 8 GiB is refused as unproven, and
GNU ld's unchecked executables die with SIGSEGV. Its 1 GiB twins link and
run. With `-z nosectionheader`, both placements are refused. These rows ran
32/32, with nine source mutants killed, in
`reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-got-page-region` (`records/repair/`). GNU ld 2.42, gold 2.42
and LLD 22.1.6 were probed with assembler
inputs (`reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-reloc-kind-limits`): at both edges
of the `ABS32`, `PREL32` and `ADR_PREL_PG_HI21` windows, and at the upper
edge of the `TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12` window (`2^24 - 1` and `2^24`). That
probe placed the GOT-page kinds' GOT (`ADR_GOT_PAGE`,
`TLSIE_ADR_GOTTPREL_PAGE21`, `TLSDESC_ADR_PAGE21`) only at 2 GiB and at
8 GiB, not at either `+-4 GiB` edge, and gold gave no evidence for them (it
aborts with an internal error on both placements); only the driver control
above goes 64 KiB past the upper edge, with GNU ld. This is linker and
execution evidence, not proof.

Until the 2026-09-23 closure audit at `5ddb13664`, nothing refused a
`PREL32` `.eh_frame` pointer between `2^31` and `2^32` when the link used
gold or LLD, which still apply the earlier bound: `trust-cg -o btfar
b1_scalars.tmbc -Wl,bt.o
-Wl,--section-start=.eh_frame=0x10000000,--section-start=.eh_frame_hdr=0x0fff0000,--section-start=.text=0xd0000000`
with a `cc` that links through LLD or gold first on `PATH` installed a
program whose FDEs begin at `0xffffffffd0000000..` and whose `backtrace()`
found one frame (six in its near twin). Every Linux link is now staged (a
plain `-nostdlib` executable link too, without the input trace), and its
image's `.eh_frame` is decoded as an unwinder reads it
(`link_driver::eh_frame_check`). With a section header table, every
allocated `.eh_frame` section and the section the `.eh_frame_hdr`
`eh_frame_ptr` names are read whole, CIE by CIE and FDE by FDE. Without
one, the `.eh_frame` that `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` locates is read: the FDEs its
table names, or every record to the terminator. Each FDE's `pc_begin` is
decoded with its CIE's `R` encoding (a PC-relative value of every fixed and
LEB128 format, or an absolute one in an `ET_EXEC` image), and
`pc_begin..pc_begin + pc_range` must lie in one executable span
(`SHF_EXECINSTR` sections and `PF_X` `PT_LOAD` segments); an FDE whose
`pc_begin` value is zero was removed by the linker and is skipped, as
unwinders skip it. The `P` personality and `L` LSDA pointers must resolve
into allocated memory (the whole 8-byte slot when indirect). Every
`.eh_frame_hdr` table entry must name an FDE and locate its `pc_begin`, the
entries must be sorted, and with a section header table every live FDE of
the indexed `.eh_frame` must have one; a truncated table fails the same
way. A failure is `relocation-out-of-range` with
`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-WINDOW]`, one line for the FDEs, one for the personality
and LSDA pointers and one for the table. `DW_EH_PE_datarel` (whose base
unwinders disagree on in `.eh_frame`), `textrel`, `funcrel`, `aligned` and
indirect `pc_begin`s, an augmentation letter other than `R`, `P`, `L`, `S`,
`B` and `G`, a CIE version other than 1, 3 and 4, a 64-bit length, a
truncated record, an absolute pointer in a position-independent image, a
dynamic relocation into `.eh_frame` or `.eh_frame_hdr` and an image that is
not ELF are `unclassified` with `[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]`. No refusal
touches the requested output. On the Linux host the audit's placement is
refused through LLD and gold (GNU ld refuses it itself), the same objects
linked by LLD or gold outside the driver backtrace one frame, and the edge
twin (`.text` at `0x8ffe0000`, every FDE 128 KiB inside the window) and the
near twin link through all three linkers and backtrace through a trust-cg
frame into `main`. For trust-cg's own `zPLR` output (a catch-all landing
pad under `__gxx_personality_v0`) with `.gcc_except_table` at `0xd0000000`,
GNU ld refuses the personality and LSDA `PREL32` fields itself, LLD and gold
write them and their programs die with SIGSEGV at the throw, and `run_link`
refuses those images; the default placement catches through all three. The
decoder agreed with GNU readelf 2.42 on every FDE of
410 sampled host images (1,279,346 FDEs), and all 5,770 of the host's ELF
executables and shared objects that are not separate debug files pass the
check (the 273 debug files, whose sections have no contents, are unproven).
Section names and `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` are not all: the check also decodes
every `.eh_frame` input the link map places, whatever its output section
is called (see "Where the `.eh_frame` input lies" below). It does not see
frames a program registers itself at run time (`__register_frame`) from
memory no `.eh_frame` input fills. Without `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME`
(`-Wl,--no-eh-frame-hdr`, or a linker script that discards
`.eh_frame_hdr` or merges `.eh_frame` into another output section, after
which GNU ld 2.42 writes no `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` either: its verifier's
dynamic C++ program with `.eh_frame` merged into `.rodata` aborts at its
throw, through the CLI of `0996df987` as well) no unwinder on the host
finds the FDEs of a dynamic image (an executable, PIE or shared object)
unless code registers them: `backtrace()` then stops at its first frame and a C++ throw
terminates, identically through GNU ld, gold and LLD. But any code can
register them: a constructor that calls `__register_frame_info` on the
image's `.eh_frame` input, in the image, in a library it links, in a
library reached only as another library's `DT_NEEDED`, or through
`dlsym`. The ninth closure audit's LLD programs did each, and backtraced
through the registered frames. So a dynamic image's `.eh_frame` input
is decoded wherever the driver's own link map places it, like a static
one's, and an image whose map was not written, cannot be read, or shows
that input where it cannot be read whole is refused whatever its kind and
inputs (see "Where the `.eh_frame` input lies" below). A
static executable registers its frames itself: GNU ld's and LLD's do so
through `crtbeginT.o`, and libgcc's registered search finds them without
`PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` (a `backtrace()` of 6 frames and a caught throw on the
host), while gold 2.42's register nothing. So does any image linked with
`crtbeginT.o`: a `--static` link given `-Wl,-Bdynamic` is an `ET_EXEC`
with a `PT_INTERP` whose own copy of libgcc's unwinder (from
`libgcc_eh.a`) searches the registered frames first. It reads neither the
LSDA's tables nor the slot an indirect personality pointer names, nor
`.debug_frame`, and it does not check Darwin's `__eh_frame` or links for
another operating system. In particular the type-table (TType) entries
another compiler writes in an LSDA in `.gcc_except_table` (g++'s
`R_AARCH64_PREL32` references to the `DW.ref._ZTI*` slots of its typed
catches) are not read: the ninth closure audit linked a g++ `catch(int)`
object through LLD 22.1.6 with a linker script that moved those slots 3
GiB above `.gcc_except_table`, and the CLI installed a static and a PIE
program whose TType entry was truncated and which died with SIGSEGV at its
throw (GNU ld refuses that layout itself; the 2 GiB twin catches).
trust-cg's own LSDAs carry no relocation (a typed catch is refused, and a
catch-all is a null entry), so the boundary is foreign LSDA contents in a
driver-linked image. Staging makes every Linux link refuse `-o
/dev/null` and need a writable output directory.

Those checks alone left a gap, found by the 2026-09-24 closure audit at
`43de0bebe`: a value that LLD or gold writes
truncated can land in other code or data, and passed. With a 256 KiB
`tcg_pad` at `0x10000000`, `.eh_frame` at `0x90000000` and trust-cg's
`.text` moved by a linker script to `0x110010000`, both installed a
`-nostdlib` program whose three FDEs describe `tcg_pad`, and with trust-cg's
`zPLR` object's `.gcc_except_table` moved alone 2^32 above the image's first
load segment, LLD installed a C++ program whose LSDA pointer names that
segment and which dies at its throw. Now a 4-byte (2-byte) `pc_begin`,
personality or LSDA pointer that resolves where it must lie is also refused
when its bits give another file-backed address, a multiple of 2^32 (2^16)
away, that lies there too: another range of code (`SHF_EXECINSTR` contents
or `PF_X` file bytes) for a `pc_begin`, another address with contents (the
whole slot when indirect) for a personality or LSDA pointer, and for the
`eh_frame_ptr` another start of an allocated section with contents (or an
address with contents without section headers). Zero fill (`.bss`, a
segment's memory past its file bytes) is no such address: an LSDA, a
personality slot or function, and code all have contents. Such a pointer is
`unclassified` with `[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]`, one line with the count
and the first pointer's field, value and both addresses: the image cannot
show which of the two its linker was given. An image with 4 GiB of
file-backed memory in which some pointer has such another address is
refused even when its linker, GNU ld included, was given the right address.

A truncated FDE has a second way to do harm, found by the fix's
independent verifier. An empty function (GCC emits a zero-range FDE for
`__builtin_unreachable()`) has no code for another address to lie in. When
LLD writes its `pc_begin` truncated into another function, the table's
entry for it hides that function's FDE, and a throw through the function
terminates. libgcc looks an FDE up by its start. It takes the entry with
the greatest start at or below the pc, and the last one among entries that
begin together, and looks no further. LLVM libunwind falls back to a linear
scan of `.eh_frame` when the entry it finds does not cover the pc, so only
overlapping ranges mislead it.

A live FDE is refused (`relocation-out-of-range`,
`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-WINDOW]`, one line naming the hidden FDE and the one
the lookup takes) in two cases:
- another FDE begins inside its range;
- the last table entry for its start names a narrower FDE.

In a program that registers its frames, libgcc first searches the FDEs it
registered. That search returns any FDE that covers the pc, never a
zero-range one, and libgcc falls back to the table only when it misses. A
static executable registers them (`crtbeginT.o`), and any other program
can (the driver does not read whether it does). Two rules follow:
- in a static executable a hidden FDE is refused as `unclassified`
  (`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]`), because the registered search may still
  find it; in any other image it stays `relocation-out-of-range`, since the
  table's lookup misses it;
- a narrower FDE with a range that begins together with a wider one is
  `unclassified` whatever the table names, in every image, because a
  registered search may take it. The fourth verifier's LLD static program
  with such an FDE terminates in 19 of 41 layouts. Until the second repair
  after the ninth closure audit's verifier this held only in images whose
  inputs were read to register frames; the same program linked
  dynamically by LLD, which catches (its table decides when nothing
  registers), is now refused too, a conservative refusal.

When no table entry locates a tie's start, the order of FDEs the image does
not fix decides the tie, and it too is `unclassified`. These are not
refused: two zero-range FDEs at one address, adjacent FDEs, and a
zero-range FDE whose start's last table entry names the wider FDE (static
or not). A static executable that registers nothing (gold's `crtbeginT.o`,
or a `-nostdlib` link without it) is still labelled `unclassified` where the
table alone decides.

Without section headers, the records from `eh_frame_ptr` are read even
when there is a table, so an FDE the table drops is still seen: the second
verifier linked a library with `-z nosectionheader` to bypass the rule.
Without a table, libgcc reads records until a zero length, so the walk
must reach a terminator; otherwise the image is unproven. The fourth
verifier had GNU ld, which writes no table when it cannot parse an input
`.eh_frame`, install a library with a 64-bit record after which libgcc
read on and aborted.

With a table, the walk may also end at the first record that is not
`.eh_frame`'s:
- one that runs past the file bytes of the `PT_LOAD` holding it, or into a
  following `.eh_frame_hdr`;
- one with a 64-bit length;
- an FDE whose CIE pointer names no CIE the walk read.

GNU ld writes no terminator for a `-nostdlib` link, and its default script
puts `.gcc_except_table` or `.sframe` right after `.eh_frame` in the same
segment. The third verifier found those bytes refused as records; with a
table they now end the walk. A table entry that names an FDE at or past
where such a walk ended leaves the image unproven. LLD writes a
terminator, and it is the linker whose table drops FDEs. gold cannot link
without section headers.

A static Linux link now passes `--eh-frame-hdr`, which the C driver passes
for every other link. gold 2.42 resolves `crtbeginT.o`'s
`__EH_FRAME_BEGIN__` to 0 and registers no unwind information, with or
without the flag, so without it every throw of its static C++ programs
aborts. The flag makes the table reachable, and they catch. A
`-Wl,--no-eh-frame-hdr` given after it brings gold's abort back; since the
v4 verifier's repair such an image is refused, since `crtbeginT.o`
references a registration function and gold's map does not show where it
registers (see "Where the `.eh_frame` input lies" below). LLD
writes a zero-filled `.eh_frame_hdr` section and no
`PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` when a linker script discards `.eh_frame`. A zero-filled
`.eh_frame_hdr` that no `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` locates is ignored.

Where the `.eh_frame` input lies (the eighth closure audit, 2026-09-24).
The check used to read `.eh_frame` by section name or through
`PT_GNU_EH_FRAME`, but libgcc reads a static executable's frames where
`crtbeginT.o` registers them, whatever the output section is called.
`trust-cg --static --no-pie -o c_far b1_scalars.tmbc -Wl,bt2.o -Wl,-T,renb.ld
-Wl,--no-eh-frame-hdr
-Wl,--section-start=.ehx=0x10000000,--section-start=.text=0xd0000000`, with
`renb.ld` renaming the output `.eh_frame` to `.ehx` and LLD's `cc` first on
`PATH`, installed a program whose 916 FDEs were all truncated and which
aborted in `_Unwind_Backtrace`. Every staged Linux link now asks the linker
for its map (`-Xlinker -Map=<stage>/link.map`, after every argument of the
request since the second repair after the ninth audit's verifier;
`tcg-link.map` for an output named `link.map`), and every `.eh_frame` input
piece the map places is decoded too:
- **Formats.** GNU ld 2.42 lists input sections after `Linker script and
  memory map` (discarded input comes before it) up to a `--cref` table,
  gold 2.42 after `Memory map` (its merged data as ` ** eh_frame`), and
  LLD 22 in a `VMA LMA Size Align Out In Symbol` table. LLD prints each
  piece of its synthetic `.eh_frame` at its output section's address plus
  the piece's offset in the synthetic section, which is where it lies only
  when that section begins its output section. A `.rodata` merging
  `.eh_frame` after other input put the synthetic section at the end while
  the map printed its pieces at the start, so an output section holding
  pieces and anything else at the input indent (other input, a data
  command, or a symbol assignment inside the section, such as
  `.ehx : { tcg_ehx_start = .; KEEP(*(.eh_frame)) }`) does not show where
  they lie. Such an output section is read as unplaced, by its name,
  address and size.
- **Runs.** Adjacent pieces form a run, read record by record like a
  section. A run the `.eh_frame` sections already read hold is skipped,
  and an FDE two walks read counts once. A run no `PT_LOAD` maps is not
  loaded and is not read. A run that the file bytes of no one `PT_LOAD`
  hold, or whose last record runs past it, is unproven.
- **The driver's own map, always.** The driver's `-Xlinker -Map=<path>`
  goes after every argument of the request, and the linker is given no
  map path of the user's: the value of every map file option a `-Wl`
  group holds (`-Map`, `--Map`, with `=<file>` or the file as the next
  piece, in the same group or the next, and GNU ld's `-Ma`, `--Ma`,
  `-M=<file>`, `--M=<file>` and `--M <file>`) is replaced by the driver's
  path (an absolute UTF-8 path without `%` or `,`: the stage's, else one in
  a fresh private directory in the first of `TMPDIR` and `/tmp` whose path
  is one). When there is none, a link whose groups hold a map file option
  is refused before the linker runs (`[TCG-LINK-MAP-UNSTAGED]`), since the
  linker would write that map at the user's path, the output's own file
  included, whatever the checks then decide; a link whose groups hold none
  asks for no map. Before the v5 verifier's repair the groups were given
  unchanged there: with `TMPDIR` and the output's directory each holding
  `,`, GNU ld, gold and LLD wrote `-Wl,-Map=prog` over `prog`, the output
  of a refused link. The map the group asks for is written by the driver from its
  own after the link (a failed one too), where the linker that wrote it,
  read from the map's header, would have written it: GNU ld the last map
  option's file (a later `-M` sends the map to standard output alone), LLD
  the last file option's unless any option sends the map to standard
  output, and gold the last file option's whatever follows it (it also
  prints the map for `-M`); GNU ld's first `%` replaced by the output path
  the user named (`.map` added when the `%` ends the value),
  `<directory>/<output name>.map` for a directory, nothing for an empty
  value or a path that is neither a directory nor a regular file
  (`/dev/null`), and a warning when it cannot be opened (GNU ld 2.42 links
  on); the literal path for gold and LLD, and a failed link
  (`LinkError::LinkMap`, nothing installed) when it cannot be written. A
  path that names an existing file that is neither a regular file nor a
  directory (a pipe, as `/dev/stdout` and `/dev/fd/1` do when standard
  output is one, a device, a socket) is written as given, following its
  links, without creating or truncating anything, and only when what was
  opened is neither; before the v5 verifier's repair `-Map=/dev/stdout`
  into a pipe failed gold's and LLD's links (its link names
  `pipe:[<inode>]`, no path). A
  map is never written to the file the output path names: each path's
  symbolic links are followed (`readlink`, a dangling link included, at
  most 40) and its directory resolved, and paths that end at the same file
  (or, when neither exists, at the same path) are one; such a map is not
  written, with a warning. Any other map is written to the file its path's
  links end at, created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` or truncated with
  `O_NOFOLLOW`, so a link the driver did not resolve is not followed. The
  driver's warnings and the linker's are printed for a refused link and
  every other outcome too. A `-Wl` group whose last map option is a bare
  `-M`, `--print-map`, `-print-map` or `-Map=-`, or another piece beginning
  `-M` (read as `-M` and more options), or a dangling `-Map`, keeps the
  driver's option before the group, so GNU ld and LLD write no map file
  (gold writes the driver's too), and LLD sends the map to standard output
  for `-M` wherever it stands. A `-Wl` group that ends in an option taking
  a separate operand takes the driver's option as that operand, and no map
  is written. Before the second repair after the ninth audit's verifier
  the driver's option came first, a group's map replaced it, and the
