  driver read the user's. Before the v4 verifier's repair a group's map
  path reached the linker: gold wrote `-Wl,-Map=prog,-M` (and
  `--print-map`, `-print-map`, `-Mx`) itself over the output of a refused
  or failed link, and a map path that named the output through a dangling
  link (`maplink -> prog`), as `./prog`, or as the target of an output
  that is a link, created the output's file with the map.
- **The dependency file, likewise.** The linker is given the driver's path
  (beside its map) for the value of every piece a measured table reads as
  `--dependency-file` (`=<file>` or the next piece; GNU ld's prefixes, gold's
  one-dash spelling), and, after the checked image is installed, the driver
  writes the file where the last such option asks (each linker writes that
  one), its first target naming the output instead of the staged image,
  never over the output's own file (with a warning) and as a map is
  written; a refused or failed link writes none, and a link without a map
  path of the driver's is refused before the linker runs
  (`[TCG-LINK-DEPFILE-UNSTAGED]`). Until the eleventh closure audit's
  repair the linkers wrote the user's path themselves: its target named the
  driver's deleted staging directory
  (`./.tcg-link-<pid>-<n>-<hash>/prog:`), and `-Wl,--dependency-file=prog
  -o prog` left a refused link's output holding the dependency file.
- **Whether an image registers is not read.** Until that repair the driver
  read it (objects, shared objects' imports, the image's own imports,
  `--defsym` aliases, and every linker script the link's options lead to,
  found as it took the linkers to find them) and let an image whose inputs
  were read to register nothing go without a map. The round-2 verifier
  found eight LLD routes past that reading, each with
  `-Wl,-Map=/dev/null`: a `.deplibs` library, a script's `INPUT` in the
  script's own directory, `-sysroot=`, a joined `-L=<dir>` and a relative
  `=dA` under a sysroot, `# /*` and `/*` in a quoted name hiding an
  `INCLUDE`, and `-T =<file>`. Each installed a program with every FDE
  truncated that registered them and aborted. Modelling each linker's
  script search is an unbounded surface, so the reading is removed, and
  the driver's own map decides for every image.
- **Refusals.** Each is `unclassified` (`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]`),
  naming the reason:
  - **A map that does not place the input, whatever the inputs.** The link
    wrote a map and it cannot be read (in no format the check reads, past
    a bound, or it cannot be opened), or LLD's map shows `.eh_frame`
    pieces in an output section it cannot place them in, and that output
    section is not read whole by other means (a section named `.eh_frame`,
    or the `.eh_frame` `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` locates, read to its terminator).
    Since the ninth closure audit this holds whatever the inputs: before
    it, an image whose inputs registered nothing was installed, and
    through LLD two `--no-pie` programs with the in-section assignment
    above (`.ehx` at 256 MiB, `.text` at `0xd0000000`,
    `-Wl,--no-eh-frame-hdr`) were installed with 13 FDEs truncated,
    trust-cg's among them, and backtraced 1 frame: their frames were
    registered at run time by `libregd.so`, reached only as the input
    `libneed.so`'s `DT_NEEDED`, and by `libregx.so` through `dlsym`. The
    same layout near is refused too (a conservative refusal); with the
    start named outside the section the map places the pieces, and the
    near program runs. An output section no `PT_LOAD` maps is not read.
  - **No map, whatever the image.** The link wrote no map where the
    driver asked: a linker that ignores `-Map`, `-Wl,-M` or `-Wl,-Map=-`
    through GNU ld or LLD (standard output), or a `-Wl` group that consumes
    the driver's option. Every such image is refused, whatever its kind and
    inputs. `-Wl,-M` also makes the input trace unreadable, so through GNU
    ld and LLD a traced link with it is refused by the trace check too
    (gold writes the driver's map file too, and its links are installed).

  A readable map's input is decoded in every image. A map is read to at
  most 1 GiB, 16 MiB a line and 4,194,304 pieces. The driver's map is a
  fixed short name in the stage, so neither a `%` in the output's name
  (which GNU ld 2.42 replaces in a `-Map` path) nor a name of 252 to 255
  bytes (with `.map` added past the file-name limit) keeps it from being
  written: before the ninth closure audit either made every `--static`
  link refused. When the output's directory holds `%` or `,` (or is not
  UTF-8), the map goes into a fresh private directory of `TMPDIR`, or of
  `/tmp` when `TMPDIR` cannot hold it either, removed with the stage; with
  neither, a link with a `-Wl` map file option is refused before the
  linker runs, and any other asks for no map. LLD
  22.1.6 itself cannot write an output whose name is longer than 244 bytes
  or whose directory holds `%` (it writes through a temporary file named
  `<output>.tmp` with seven random characters, replacing each `%` of that
  path), inside or outside the driver.

The verifier of `84ceb2eb7` found the first cut keyed on `PT_INTERP`: with
`-Wl,-Bdynamic` a `--static` link still loads `crtbeginT.o`, and through
LLD `.eh_frame` merged into `.rodata` at `0x10000000` (route A) or renamed
with `-Wl,-Map=/dev/null` (route B), with `.text` at `0xd0000000`, was
installed with every registered FDE truncated and aborted in
`_Unwind_Backtrace`. Route A is refused as unproven (LLD's map cannot place
its pieces), and route B, with or without `-Wl,-Map=/dev/null`, as
`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-WINDOW]`. Near twins (LLD's renamed layout with and
without `-Map=/dev/null`, GNU ld renamed and merged, one with
`-Wl,--M=<file>` and one with `-Map=/dev/null`, and gold) run and unwind
through a trust-cg frame into `main`; LLD's merged near layout is refused
as unproven. Later verifiers found shared objects, GCC `-flto` objects and
shared objects' imports read wrongly or not at all by the registration
reading, and the round-2 verifier of the ninth audit's repair eight script
routes (above); each such program is now checked through the driver's own
map, and the `--as-needed` false refusal of a library that imports a
registration function without being loaded is gone. With the map read,
the `.eh_frame` input is decoded, or the image refused, whoever registers
it.

On the host the audit's layout through LLD is refused as
`[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-WINDOW]` with and without `-s`, with a user's `-Map`
(written from the driver's map), and with `.eh_frame_hdr` discarded by the script instead
of `--no-eh-frame-hdr`, while LLD's program outside the driver dies with a
signal in its backtrace. GNU ld refuses the
layout itself. The renamed, stripped, `.eh_frame_hdr`-discarded and (GNU
ld) `.rodata`-merged near twins backtrace through a trust-cg frame into
`main` through GNU ld and LLD, as do gold's static programs with and
without a user map. LLD's
merged layout and `-Wl,-M` are refused as unproven by name. The map costs
a static C++ link about 8-12 ms on the host (GNU ld 0.080 to 0.088 s, LLD
0.037 to 0.049 s, gold 0.051 to 0.059 s). Not seen: a `-nostdlib` static
link that adds `crtbeginT.o` but not `crtend.o` leaves no terminator, and
libgcc's registered search then reads past the `.eh_frame` input; the check
reads the input, not what follows it. The check reads a placed run past
zero words (padding), while libgcc's walk of registered frames stops at
the first, and GNU ld keeps the zero padding between the `.eh_frame` inputs
of an output section not named `.eh_frame`.

A static executable with a live FDE, outside the C start files (`crt1.o`
and the like, whose `_start` frames lie before the registered ones), that
has no `.eh_frame_hdr` table entry (which libgcc falls back to through
`dl_iterate_phdr`; static glibc answers it: a static program whose FDEs lie
before the registered ones backtraces 7 frames with the table and 1
without) is found only through the frames the program registers. For such
an image the registrants are read by behaviour: every loaded AArch64 ELF
relocatable input (a positional object, and each object and archive member
the linker's input trace names) whose symbol table has an undefined
reference to `__register_frame_info`, `__register_frame_info_bases`,
`__register_frame`, `__register_frame_table`, `__register_frame_info_table`
or `__register_frame_info_table_bases` (versioned, or `__real_` for
`--wrap`). Every registrant must be the C driver's own `crtbeginT.o` (the
file `cc -print-file-name=crtbeginT.o` names, compared by device and inode,
under the name `crtbeginT.o`), whose `frame_dummy` passes
`__EH_FRAME_BEGIN__`, a symbol at offset 0 of its `.eh_frame` input; the map
must show where that lies; the link's inputs must all be shown (a trace
problem is not); and nothing may take the place of the C runtime's own
code, by the one rule the frame registration, the static-PIE relocator and
the IFUNC applier below share (since the v6 verifier's repair). A name is
the C runtime's when its start-up or unwinding code is reached through it
(the registration functions, libgcc's FDE lookup `_Unwind_Find_FDE`,
`__libc_start_main`, `_dl_relocate_static_pie`, and the linker-defined
`__rela_iplt_start`, `__rela_iplt_end`, `_DYNAMIC`, `__ehdr_start` and init
and fini array bounds), or when it is reserved (begins with `_`) and one of
the C runtime's own linked inputs references it. No `-Wl` piece may be a
linker script, multiple definitions or `--just-symbols` (`-T`, `--script`,
`-dT`, `--default-script`, `-c`, `--mri-script`, `-z muldefs`,
`--allow-multiple-definition`, `--just-symbols`, `-R`, read conservatively
in every GNU ld spelling: `-T`, `--T`, `-dT` and one-dash `-c` and `-R`
prefixes, prefixes of 2 or 4 letters of the long names, of 7 of
`allow-multiple-definition` and of 1 of `just-symbols`, and `-z muldefs` or
`-zmuldefs`); no `--defsym` may define such a name or name one in its
expression, and no `--wrap` may wrap one (an inert `--defsym` or `--wrap`
is read and allowed; one whose value is not read is not); no linker input
(a `-Wl` operand or input object) may be a linker script, and no `-l`
library may be one in any directory the linker may search (the `-L`
directories, `-L=` ones under each `--sysroot` and as spelled, the C
driver's `-print-search-dirs`, the linkers' defaults (GNU ld 2.42's
`SEARCH_DIR`s) and those defaults under each `--sysroot`), looked up as
`lib<name>.a` and, wherever a dynamic lookup is in effect for it (a link
that is not static, or after `-Bdynamic`, `-dy` or `-call_shared` in any
GNU ld spelling until `-Bstatic` or `--pop-state` undoes it), as
`lib<name>.so` too, except the C driver's own scripts (glibc's `libm.a` is
`GROUP ( libm-2.39.a libmvec.a )`, and `libc.so`, `libm.so` and GCC's
`libgcc_s.so` are scripts). The C driver's own libraries (`-lgcc`,
`-lgcc_eh` or `-lgcc_s`, and `-lc`, named after every piece unless
`--nostdlib`) are looked up the same way in the directories the request
and its `-Wl` pieces name, which the linker searches before the driver's
own; so a typed `-L d5` whose `d5/libc.a` is a script is refused, even one
that only forwards to glibc's (`INPUT ( .../libc.a )`), since the check does
not read scripts. The lookup reads every piece in each way one of the
linkers reads it (one-dash `-library` as GNU ld's `-l ibrary` and as the
library option), and reads the piece after any other option as a piece
too. A `-Wl` piece is an option's value, not an input, only when every one
of GNU ld 2.42, gold 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 that accepts the spelling was
measured to take it as the value: `scripts/generate_linker_options.py`
links each of 4,733 candidate spellings (every name the three `--help`
outputs list, with one dash and two, and every prefix of a GNU ld long
name; `--help` is only the candidate list) followed by a script input
through each linker, and records `Next` only on positive evidence (the
link succeeded without reading the script, or the spelling alone is
reported to want a value), `NotNext` when the linker read the script, a
spelling the linker rejects as unrecognized, unknown or ambiguous as not
accepted, and any other outcome as unsettled (GNU ld 908 `Next`, 2,555
`NotNext`, 405 unsettled; gold 161, 1,531, 208; LLD 133, 574, 126). A
script-like file after an option the linkers read differently, whose
reading is unsettled, or that no linker accepts is refused as not
classified. The table records each linker's `--version`; where it reads a
script-like file as an option's value (the only reading that lets a piece
through), the driver asks the link's linker for its version (`<driver>
-Wl,--version`) and refuses the link, saying so, unless it is one of the
three the table was measured on. `scripts/tests/test_generate_linker_options.py`
runs `--check` (versions and `--help` hashes) and `--check --sweep` (a new
measurement of every spelling, about 7 s) wherever the three linkers are
installed, and fails with "regenerate" on drift. Before the v8 verifier's
repair the table was parsed from `--help` on two or more spaces, so a flag
whose description is one space from its name
(`--no-copy-dt-needed-entries`, `--dynamic-list-cpp-typeinfo`, and in LLD
`--lto-pgo-warn-mismatch`, `--no-warn-ifunc-textrel`,
`--use-android-relr-tags`) read as taking a value, and gold's `--static
-Wl,ifs_main.o,--no-copy-dt-needed-entries,redir.ld` was installed and dies
with SIGSEGV; and the lookup read no sysroot and not the C driver's own
libraries, so gold's `-Wl,--sysroot=DIR,-lredir9` and `-L d5` were
installed too. Before the v7 verifier's repair a short hand list decided,
and static links with LLD's `--symbol-ordering-file order.txt`, gold's
`--section-ordering-file`, `--export-dynamic-symbol-list`, one-dash
`-version-script` and `-dynamic-list`, or `--error-handling-script` were
refused (the `=` spellings installed); and a static link looked a library
up as `.a` alone, so gold's `--static -Wl,-Bdynamic,-Ld1,-lredir2,-Bstatic`,
whose `libredir2.so` is `__libc_start_main = main;` (gold's trace and map
show no script), was installed and dies with SIGSEGV. And no
loaded input may define such a name (a global or weak definition) unless it
is a member of the C driver's own `libc.a`, `libgcc_eh.a` or `libgcc.a` or
one of its start files (`cc -print-file-name`, compared by device and
inode; on the host only `libgcc_eh.a`'s `unwind-dw2-fde-dip.o` defines the
registration functions), since such a definition takes the place of the C
runtime's (the linker then loads no member for the name, or keeps the
first under `-z muldefs`). That includes a definition of one of the
compiler support routines the C driver's own `libgcc.a` defines (its
archive symbol table is read) that the C runtime's code calls, which is
named as such in the refusal: libgcc's outline-atomics helpers, through
two of which (`__aarch64_cas8_acq_rel`, `__aarch64_swp8_acq_rel`)
libgcc_eh's `__register_frame_info` takes its lock during a static
program's start-up (measured under gdb; glibc's `malloc` and `atexit` call
`__aarch64_cas4_acq` there too), and its 128-bit float routines
(`__addtf3`, `__multf3`, ...), which glibc's `printf` calls. A Rust
staticlib's `compiler_builtins` defines both kinds (a Rust 1.97.1
staticlib defines 26 helpers and 18 such routines that the host's `libc.a`,
`libgcc_eh.a` or `libgcc.a` reference) and compiler-rt's builtins do too, so every static link with
such an input is refused (the eleventh closure audit's finding; the same
links outside the driver run, and dynamic links with the staticlib are
installed and run). The eleventh audit's repair measured whether an
identical definition could be admitted: the staticlib's helpers are
libgcc's instructions without the leading `bti c`, but its 128-bit float
routines are Rust code, and the driver does not read what any definition
does, so the class stays a conservative refusal (`link_options`
`linux_got_page::ordinary_links_the_eleventh_audit_found_refused_are_installed`
refuses an object defining the two helpers through the three linkers and
runs it outside the driver); LLD's map may print no script command (an assignment or a
data command, which only a script gives LLD), GNU ld's map may `LOAD`
no file that is neither ELF nor an archive (a script read as an input),
and gold, whose trace and map name no script, may have opened no such
file: a gold link (its `--version` or its map says so) runs once more with
`-Wl,--debug=files` into the stage, and every `Attempt to open <file>
succeeded` of that record is checked like GNU ld's trace; a record that
cannot be made or names no file refuses the link (a gold link that reaches
these checks costs a second link, about 20 ms for a small static program);
and libgcc's walk from the start (to the first zero length) must reach
every such FDE. Otherwise the image is `[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]`,
naming the reason; a link in which no input references a registration
function registers nothing and is not refused on these grounds (libgcc
then finds such an FDE by no route, as in any program without a table).
Where `__EH_FRAME_BEGIN__` lies, derived from the linkers and confirmed in
gdb (`x0` at `__register_frame_info`) for the standard order of the start
files, `crtbeginT.o` first, `bt.o` before `crtbeginT.o`, `crt1.o` before
it, with `--gc-sections` and (LLD) `--icf=all`, and the C driver's own
order:
- GNU ld 2.42: the address of `crtbeginT.o`'s `.eh_frame` input section,
  which is what `frame_dummy` passes although GNU ld's `.symtab` value of
  `__EH_FRAME_BEGIN__` differs when it edits `.eh_frame`.
- LLD 22.1.6: LLD writes each CIE it keeps followed by the FDEs that name
  it (`EhFrameSection::finalizeContents`), keeps one of equal CIEs (with
  the same personality), and resolves a symbol at offset 0 of an input
  through `EhInputSection::getParentOffset`: to the address of the input's
  own CIE when LLD kept it (the map lists `crtbeginT.o:(.eh_frame+0x0)`),
  else to the start of its synthetic `.eh_frame` section, the address of
  the one output section that holds its pieces and nothing else. An output
  section holding the pieces and anything else (an assignment, a data
  command, `. += <n>`, other input) does not show that start, and neither
  do pieces in more than one output section.
- gold 2.42: `crtbeginT.o`'s `frame_dummy` passes 0 and registers nothing,
  and its map names no piece of `crtbeginT.o`; a static gold image with such
  an FDE is refused (the map does not show where it registers).
Before the round-3 verifier the driver took LLD's output section start, and
a `--static --nostdlib` link whose trust-cg objects came first (so
trust-cg's CIE, then `crtbeginT.o`'s own) was installed with its backtrace
cut to 2 frames; the round-3 repair took the CIE `crtbeginT.o`'s first
listed piece named, which the v4 verifier showed wrong for LLD (in the
standard order `crtbeginT.o`'s CIE merges into `crt1.o`'s, it registers from
the synthetic start, and the image, refused, backtraces 7 frames). The v4
verifier also found images installed whose registrant was not shown: a
copy of `crtbeginT.o` under another name or repacked with `ld -r`, through
GNU ld and LLD (the driver recognised `crtbeginT.o` by file name), and
through LLD a `SECTIONS { .eh_frame : { __eh_start = .; KEEP(*(.eh_frame))
} } INSERT AFTER .rodata;` or `. += 0x38;` script (the output section was
unplaced and recorded no start, which the walk took as nothing to check);
each backtraced 2 frames. Each is refused now; a script's table twin is
installed where the linker writes a complete table and the section named
`.eh_frame` begins with a record (not GNU ld's renamed or merged
`.eh_frame`, which has no table, and not a script that puts other bytes at
the start of `.eh_frame`, such as LLD's `. += 0x38` or a `LONG` there,
which the check reads from that start and refuses, as before). Through GNU ld a
foreign input whose `.eh_frame` is 4 bytes short of a multiple of 8, ahead
of an 8-byte-aligned one in a renamed `.ehx`, stopped the walk after 9 of
916 FDEs, and the program aborted in `_Unwind_Backtrace`; that layout needs
a script and is refused as such. The v5 verifier's `override.o`, which
defines `__register_frame_info`, `__register_frame_info_bases` and
`__deregister_frame_info` as no-ops, linked `--static` with
`-Wl,--no-eh-frame-hdr,-z,muldefs`, was installed through GNU ld and LLD
(the check read only references), and its program registers nothing and
does not backtrace; it is refused now in every multiple-definition
spelling, and so is an input that defines the functions and
`_Unwind_Find_FDE` without `-z muldefs`. Its table twin installed and
backtraced; since the v6 verifier's repair `-z muldefs` also leaves glibc's
start-up code unknown, and every static glibc link with it, or with a
linker script, is refused as `[TCG-LINK-IRELATIVE-UNAPPLIED]` whatever its
table (below). A static link without a table given an inert `--defsym`,
refused before, is checked and installs. Not read: what a registrant's
call registers at run time, whether `frame_dummy` runs (a program whose
entry skips glibc's start-up code registers nothing), and a lookup or
unwinder of the program's own when there is a table (the check reads the
table and libgcc's lookup, not the program's). The round-2
verifier's dynamic GNU ld layouts, registered from `tcg_ehx_start` at the
start of `.ehx`, stop at the padding after `crt1.o`'s input (4 records) and
abort, inside and outside the driver alike, with no truncated pointer; the
registrant check reads static executables only.

A staged Linux image that names a program interpreter (`PT_INTERP`) and has
no dynamic section (`PT_DYNAMIC`) is refused as `unclassified`
(`[TCG-LINK-INTERP-NO-DYNAMIC]`). The kernel runs the interpreter, glibc's
`ld.so`, which reads the program's dynamic section as it starts: on the
host glibc 2.39 faults in `audit_list_add_dynamic_tag` before any of the
program's code runs. LLD 22.1.6 writes such an image for a dynamic
`-nostdlib --no-pie` link that needs no shared library (the ninth closure
audit found `trust-cg --no-pie --nostdlib` installing one that died with
SIGSEGV); GNU ld 2.42 and gold 2.42 write no `PT_INTERP` for that link and
their programs run, as do LLD's `--pie` and `--static` twins. The
converse is refused too (`[TCG-LINK-DYNAMIC-NO-INTERP]`): an `ET_EXEC`
without an interpreter whose dynamic section names shared libraries
(`DT_NEEDED`) or gives a relocation table a non-zero size (`DT_PLTRELSZ`,
`DT_RELASZ`, `DT_RELSZ`, `DT_RELRSZ`). The kernel starts it without the
loader, nothing loads its libraries, binds their symbols or applies its
relocations, and it faults. LLD 22.1.6 writes one for `--static` given
`-Wl,-Bstatic,-lgcc_eh,-Bdynamic` (libc then linked dynamically) without
`-Wl,--dynamic-linker` (the ninth audit's verifier: installed, SIGSEGV),
and for `--static` given `-Wl,-Bdynamic,--as-needed,-lm,--no-as-needed,-Bstatic`
when `libm` is unused: no `DT_NEEDED`, but a `DT_DEBUG` and relocations
(its round-2 verifier: installed, SIGSEGV). GNU ld 2.42 names its default
`/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1` for the first, and the program runs; for the
second its image is static. `--no-pie -Wl,--no-dynamic-linker` gives GNU
ld and LLD such an image too; it runs only when started through the loader
(`/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 ./prog`), and is refused. A default or
`--pie` link with `-Wl,--no-dynamic-linker` gives them a PIE (`ET_DYN` with
`DF_1_PIE`) that needs `libc.so.6`, names no interpreter and faults (the
round-3 verifier); it is refused too. A PIE without an interpreter that
needs no library but holds dynamic relocations (a non-zero size tag, or an
allocated `SHT_RELA`, `SHT_REL` or `SHT_RELR` section that is not empty)
runs only when something linked into it applies them: the v4 verifier's
`--pie --nostdlib -Wl,start.o,--no-dynamic-linker`, whose own `_start` calls
through a function pointer in `.data` (one `R_AARCH64_RELATIVE`), was
installed and died with SIGSEGV. Such a PIE is refused unless the loaded
inputs (as the registrants above are read) show glibc's relocator, by
identity, and nothing that can take the place of the C runtime's code (the
rule above; also a script GNU ld's trace names, and an LLD script command
or a script GNU ld's map loads): exactly one input defines
`_dl_relocate_static_pie`, it is a
member of the C driver's own `libc.a` (`cc -print-file-name=libc.a`, by
device and inode), it references `_DYNAMIC` (it reads the image's dynamic
section) and another input references it (glibc's `__libc_start_main`
calls it); and exactly one input defines `_start`, the C driver's own
`rcrt1.o` or `grcrt1.o` (by device and inode), whose `_start` calls
`__libc_start_main`. glibc's static PIE (`rcrt1.o`, `libc.a`'s
`dl-reloc-static-pie.o`, `--pie --nostdlib -Wl,--no-dynamic-linker,...`)
passes and runs through GNU ld and LLD; one linked with `crt1.o`, whose
`_dl_relocate_static_pie` is a 16-byte stub, is refused (it dies with
SIGSEGV). Before the v5 verifier's repair the relocator was taken by
name: its `norel.o`, which defines `_dl_relocate_static_pie`, reads
`_DYNAMIC` and relocates nothing, called from `start2.o`'s own `_start`,
passed (GNU ld's program dies with SIGSEGV); it, and glibc's relocator
called from a `_start` of the program's own, are refused now; so is the
v6 verifier's glibc static PIE given `--defsym=_dl_relocate_static_pie=0`,
installed before (a core dump). The image must also start at that start
file's `_start` (read since the tenth closure audit, below). Not read:
that the relocator runs before a relocated word is read. On the host the three linkers write no
`PT_DYNAMIC` for a `--static` link (with or without `--export-dynamic` or
`--eh-frame-hdr`): static glibc applies its `IRELATIVE` relocations itself
(`apply_irel`, from `__rela_iplt_start` to `__rela_iplt_end`), and no tag
names them. A static executable (an `ET_EXEC` without `PT_INTERP`) that
holds IFUNC relocations is refused as `unclassified`
(`[TCG-LINK-IRELATIVE-UNAPPLIED]`) unless the loaded inputs show glibc's
applier, by identity: a member of the C driver's own `libc.a` that
references `__rela_iplt_start` (`libc-start.o`), with `_start` from the C
driver's own `crt1.o` or `gcrt1.o`, and nothing that can take the place of
the C runtime's code (as for the relocator); and, where the image has a
symbol table that defines both, `__rela_iplt_start` and `__rela_iplt_end`
must be exactly the one relocation section that holds its IFUNC
relocations, holding nothing else (a result, whatever moved them: the v6
verifier's `--defsym=__rela_iplt_start=0` program, installed before, dies
with SIGSEGV, and a `__libc_start_main` of the program's own under
`-z muldefs` hangs; both are refused now). The image shows them by an
`R_AARCH64_IRELATIVE` in an allocated relocation section (for a
`--static --nostdlib` program GNU ld 2.42 and gold 2.42 write it in
`.rela.plt`, LLD 22 in `.rela.dyn`) or a dynamic table, or by bytes between
`__rela_iplt_start` and `__rela_iplt_end`; an image without section headers
or without a symbol table, which cannot show them all, is read through its
inputs (any that defines an `STT_GNU_IFUNC`), and so is one that shows none
where something can take the place of the C runtime's code (a script can
drop them). The v5 verifier's
`--static --nostdlib -Wl,ifs.o`, whose own `_start` calls an IFUNC, was
installed through the three linkers (and `--no-pie --nostdlib` through GNU
ld and gold): nothing applies the relocation, GNU ld's program hangs, and
gold's and LLD's die with SIGSEGV. Each is refused now, as is the program
linked with `libc.a` whose `_start` is its own; every glibc static link,
whose `libc.a` has IFUNCs, installs as before. A program whose own
`_start` applies its IFUNC relocations (the GOT-page tests' IPLT probes,
which return 42 outside the driver and installed before) is refused too,
a conservative refusal: the check does not read what an applier's code
does. Every static glibc link with a linker script or `-z muldefs` is
refused so too, whatever its table (a conservative refusal: its table
twins ran). *Correction (2026-09-26, the tenth closure audit):* until
then every `-Wl` piece that begins with `-T` or, with one dash, `-c` was
taken to name a script, so static glibc links with GNU ld's address
options (`-Ttext-segment=`, `-Tbss=`, `-Tdata=`, `-Ttext=`, joined or
separate) and one-dash `-check-sections` and
`-compress-debug-sections=<type>` were refused though their images ran.
Such a piece is now read by the measured option table of the link's
linker (by its exact `--version`): it is taken to name no script when that
linker's table lists its spelling (the name before any `=<value>`) only
under names that read no script and only as a settled reading. A spelling
the table does not list, or lists as unsettled, can be a script option's
short form with its file glued (`-T<file>`, GNU ld's `-c<file>`): gold's
and LLD's `-Tbs=` and `-Ttext-seg=` are `-T` with a script named
`bs=...`, and stay unread (those linkers fail such a link unless the file
exists), as does every such piece for a linker the table was not measured
on. Each of the audit's links now installs and runs through each linker
that accepts the option (`link_options`
`linux_got_page::static_links_with_address_options_are_installed`); a real
`-T` script is still refused. The entry point is read since the same
audit: a static executable's IFUNC applier, and a static PIE's relocator
(above), are glibc's only when the image starts at the C driver's start
file's `_start`, which calls `__libc_start_main`. The check places that
`_start` through the driver's link map (the start file's input section
that holds it, from the start file's own symbol table, plus the symbol's
offset), not the image's symbol table, so a stripped image is read the same
way and another symbol named `_start` does not decide it, and requires the
image's `e_entry` to be that address. `--static -Wl,main_ifunc.o,myentry.o,-e,_mystart`,
whose `_mystart` calls a `main` that calls `memcpy` through its IFUNC,
was installed through GNU ld (the program hung), LLD and gold (SIGSEGV);
it, `--entry=`, a `--defsym` of `_start` and a script's `ENTRY`, stripped
or not, are refused, naming the entry point and the start file's `_start`,
and a glibc static PIE started at `_mystart` (SIGSEGV outside the driver)
is refused as `[TCG-LINK-DYNAMIC-NO-INTERP]` the same way. The
registration rule does not read the entry point: an entry that skips
glibc's start-up code registers nothing, and the frames then found are
the ones the table gives, as in an image without a registrant; a
registrant other than the C driver's own `crtbeginT.o` is refused anyway.
Every executable's entry point is read as well (the second verifier of
the repair, 2026-09-26): an `ET_EXEC` or PIE whose `e_entry` is 0, or,
when it has an executable `PT_LOAD` segment, lies in no such segment's
file contents, is refused as `[TCG-LINK-ENTRY-POINT]`
(`entry_point_problem`), static or dynamic. gold 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6
write 0 for an entry symbol nothing defines (`-e nosuch`, and the
one-dash spellings they read as `-e<symbol>`, above); GNU ld 2.42 starts
such a program at `.text` with a warning, which this rule does not see. A
dynamic executable whose entry is a defined symbol of the user's (`-e
main`) is admitted: its start is the user's control flow, as below.
A dynamic executable's C-runtime rebinding is not checked (the applier,
relocator and registrant rules read static images only):
`-Wl,--defsym=__libc_start_main=main` installs through the three linkers
and the program aborts (exit 134) in `_start` after `main` returns. There
`ld.so` applies the relocations and IFUNCs and the unwinder reads the
table, so it is control flow of the user's, not a relocation window or an
unwind table.
Not read: IFUNC relocations a
linker script moved into a section of another type in an image whose
symbol table does not define `__rela_iplt_start`; a script the linker
reaches another way than those read (the image's bracket still shows a
moved `__rela_iplt_start`); and a non-reserved name the C runtime calls
(`memcpy`, `exit`, `malloc`) the program defines, which takes the place of
the C library's by design (in a static PIE the relocator then calls it). An `ET_EXEC` whose dynamic
section needs no library and gives no relocation table a
size, and a PIE without relocations, are not refused on these grounds. A
shared object (`ET_DYN` without `DF_1_PIE`) is not read for a loader: the
kernel does start one that is run as a program, and the v4 verifier's
`--shared -Wl,cmain.o,-e,main` images (with or without
`--no-dynamic-linker`), which name no interpreter, start and fault through
GNU ld and LLD; the driver links a `--shared` output as a library for the
dynamic loader to load, and does not check that it can also run as a
program. An image of a link the request asks to be
static (`--static`; the CLI has no static-PIE mode) that names an
interpreter or needs a shared library anyway is refused as
`[TCG-LINK-STATIC-DYNAMIC]`: a `-Wl,-Bdynamic` linked a library dynamically
into static glibc's start-up code. The refusal names the `-Wl` options in
effect, read as GNU ld reads an abbreviation (`-Bdyn`, `--Bdynami`,
`-call_sh`, `-dy`): a `-Bdynamic` a library follows before the next
`-Bstatic` (`-dn`, `-non_shared`, `-Bst`, ...) or the last such switch
(the C driver's own libraries follow every group), and the last program
interpreter no later `--no-dynamic-linker` drops; `-pie` is refused before
linking. GNU ld's image of `--static
-Wl,-Bdynamic,--as-needed,-lm,...` for a program that calls `libm` names
its interpreter, needs `libm.so.6` and faults (SIGSEGV); GNU ld's and every
linker's `--dynamic-linker` image of `--static -Wl,-Bdynamic`, which run,
are refused too, by design. gold 2.42 names its own
default interpreter, `/lib/ld.so.1`, which the host lacks: such a
`--static` image is refused as above (before, it was installed and did not
start, `No such file or directory`), and the driver does not check that
the interpreter a dynamic image names exists. These are load failures,
not relocation windows; only links through `run_link` are checked.

Relocations in a format glibc's AArch64 port does not apply are refused as
`[TCG-LINK-RELOCATION-FORMAT]` (the tenth closure audit, 2026-09-26).
glibc 2.39's AArch64 dynamic loader and start-up code apply `Elf64_Rela`
entries and `DT_RELR` packed relative relocations only
(`ELF_MACHINE_NO_REL`); LLD 22.1.6 writes other formats on request, and the
driver installed each: `--static -Wl,-z,rel` put the `R_AARCH64_IRELATIVE`
relocations in an `SHT_REL` `.rel.dyn` and left `__rela_iplt_start`
undefined (SIGSEGV in `__libc_early_init`); a static PIE with `-z rel`
(SIGSEGV) and a PIE with `--pack-dyn-relocs=android` (`DT_ANDROID_RELA`,
`call_init` jumps to 0) were never relocated; a PIE with `-z rel` (an
`ld.so` assertion on `DT_PLTREL`) or `--pack-dyn-relocs=relr` (`DT_RELR
without GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR dependency`) did not load (exit 127). `-z rel`
is refused by name (GNU ld 2.42 ignores it, gold 2.42 rejects it), and an
image is refused when it has an allocated `SHT_REL`, `SHT_ANDROID_REL`,
`SHT_ANDROID_RELA` or `SHT_ANDROID_RELR` section that is not empty, a
nonzero `DT_RELSZ` (or a `DT_REL` without its size), a `DT_PLTREL` other
than `DT_RELA`, any Android packed-relocation tag, or `DT_RELR` in an image
`ld.so` loads (one naming an interpreter, or a shared object) that has
version needs (`DT_VERNEED`), a `DT_NEEDED` entry that begins with
`libc.so.`, and no `DT_VERNEED` version named `GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR` (or whose
version entries or needed names cannot be read). GNU ld's
and LLD's `-z pack-relative-relocs` add that dependency and their PIEs
run; a static PIE's own relocator applies `DT_RELR` (LLD's
`--pack-dyn-relocs=relr` static PIE runs) and is not refused for it.
*Correction (2026-09-26, the verifier of that repair):* the rule first
required the dependency of every image `ld.so` loads, and refused an LLD
shared object with `DT_RELR` that imports nothing (no `DT_NEEDED`, no
`DT_VERNEED`), which `dlopen`s and runs. glibc 2.39's
`_dl_check_map_versions` checks the dependency only for an image with
version needs; measured on the host, an object with `DT_RELR` and no
`DT_VERNEED` loads (with no `DT_NEEDED`, or needing `libm.so.6` without a
versioned symbol), one whose `DT_VERNEED` names only `libm.so.6` versions
loads too, and one whose `DT_VERNEED` names a `libc.so.6` version is
refused. The rule then required the dependency of every image with
`DT_VERNEED`. *Correction (2026-09-26, the second verifier):* glibc's
condition also names the C library. Measured with LLD shared objects that
have `DT_RELR` and no dependency: version needs naming only `libm.so.6`,
or only a library of the user's (`libv.so`), load when no `DT_NEEDED`
entry names `libc.so.6`, and are refused (`DT_RELR without
GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR dependency`) when one does, whatever library the
version needs name; an entry `libc.so.7` (a link to the C library) is
refused too, while `./libc.so.6` and `x/libc.so` load, so glibc compares
the start of the `DT_NEEDED` string as written with `libc.so.`. The rule
now requires the dependency only of an image with version needs and a
`DT_NEEDED` string that begins with `libc.so.` (`needs_libc`; an
unreadable string table or name counts as one, conservatively), and the
`libm.so.6`- and `libv.so`-only objects that the rule refused before are
admitted (`link_options`
`linux_got_page::relr_shared_objects_are_refused_only_when_glibc_refuses_them`
installs the `libv.so` case and runs it with `dlopen`, and refuses it with
`libc.so.6` added). An image without section headers or a dynamic section
shows neither; the pre-link `-z rel` refusal covers that route
(`-z nosectionheader` with `-z rel`).

An image whose loaded memory is not what its sections hold is refused as
`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]` (the same audit, and the eleventh). `-Wl,--no-check-sections` let
GNU ld 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 place a C section `.ovl` 16 bytes into
trust-cg's `.data` (gold 2.42 fails such a link): GNU ld printed nothing,
its program read 0 for the trust-cg global whose bytes in the file held
42, and LLD's read the C value there. The driver's checks read a section's
bytes at its file offset, so they had not checked what the program runs.
The option is refused by name in every spelling a linker reads
(`[TCG-LINK-NO-CHECK-SECTIONS]`), and, independently, an executable or
shared object is refused when two allocated sections of nonzero size
overlap (a `.tbss`, thread-local zero fill that occupies no memory of its
own, aside), or when an allocated section with file contents lies in part
in a segment's memory but not in the file part of one segment that maps
its file offset to its address. A section no segment loads any byte of was
not read by this rule, on the claim that reading it faults; the claim was
false, and such a section is refused now (the twelfth-round correction
below).

*Correction (2026-09-26, the eleventh closure audit):* those byte-range
rules did not describe the loaded memory. The kernel (for an executable, a
PIE, a static PIE) and glibc's `ld.so` (for a shared object) map each
`PT_LOAD` in whole pages, in program-header order, so a later segment's
mapping replaces an earlier one's bytes and permissions in the whole page
they share. A linker script with `AT()` load addresses made GNU ld 2.42
and LLD 22.1.6 write a `PT_LOAD` for a C section at 0x500800 after one for
a 0x10700-byte `.pad`, and the loader mapped the page of trust-cg's
`.data` and `.bss` (0x500000) from a file page inside `.pad`: the driver
installed programs (no-PIE, PIE, static `-nostdlib`) and a shared library
whose trust-cg globals read 0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a, although the file held 42
and 0 there. The rule is now a page model (`page_mapping_disagreement`),
in pages of `P` bytes: the largest of the host's page (`AT_PAGESZ`, 4 KiB
here) and every `PT_LOAD`'s `p_align`, rounded up to a power of two and at
most the machine's largest page, 64 KiB on AArch64 (whose kernels are
built with 4, 16 or 64 KiB pages; GNU ld, gold and LLD give AArch64
segments `p_align` 0x10000). That repair modelled `P` alone, on the claim
that a layout that holds at `P` holds at every smaller page; the claim was
false, and the model now also runs at each smaller page (the twelfth-round
correction below). It refuses an executable or shared object in which:
- a `PT_LOAD` has more file bytes than memory (the host kernel does not
  start such a program);
- an `ET_DYN` image's (a shared object's, a PIE's, a static PIE's)
  `PT_LOAD`s are not in ascending `p_vaddr` order in its program headers:
  `ld.so` reserves an object's memory from its first `PT_LOAD`'s page to
  its last one's end, and an out-of-order segment of LLD's shared object of
  the audit's script was mapped outside that reservation. An `ET_EXEC`'s
  segments are each mapped at their own address with nothing reserved, and
  LLD writes them out of order for a `--section-start` below another
  section (such programs run), so an `ET_EXEC`'s may be out of order when
  no two share a page; an `ET_EXEC`'s empty `PT_LOAD` (`p_memsz` 0), for
  which the kernel maps nothing, is left out (glibc refuses a shared
  object's empty one that is off its page, and a last one at address 0
  ends the reservation: "failed to map segment");
- two `PT_LOAD`s overlap in memory;
- a `PT_LOAD`'s `p_vaddr - p_offset` is not a multiple of `P` (`-z
  max-page-size=16` through each linker; each such program died with
  SIGSEGV as it started);
- two `PT_LOAD`s share a page and map it from different file pages
  (different `p_vaddr - p_offset`), or the later one's permissions lack one
  of the earlier one's (LLD's `-n`: an executable and a writable segment in
  one page, and the program died with SIGSEGV at its entry point), or the
  later mapping does not read zero where the earlier one's zero fill lies,
  or the later one holds no file bytes, which the kernel maps as a zero
  page over the earlier one's file bytes (a data word read 0 on the host),
  and those are not zero;
- a segment that is not writable has its zero fill begin in a page of its
  file contents over file bytes that are not zero: the kernel maps that
  page from the file and does not clear it (a read-only `NOBITS` section
  after file bytes read the `.symtab` bytes that follow them, through GNU
  ld and LLD; glibc's `ld.so` clears it, so for a shared object this is
  conservative).
The audit's next-page twin (`.ovl` at 0x501000) ran on this 4 KiB-page
host, but it shares the 64 KiB page its `p_align` allows and is out of
order, and it is refused; the next-64 KiB-page twin is installed and runs
in every form (`link_options`
`linux_got_page::pages_the_loaders_map_from_other_file_bytes_are_never_installed`,
which also runs the refused images outside the driver). Conservative
consequences: an image linked with `-z max-page-size=4096` that holds a
64 KiB-aligned variable is modelled with 64 KiB pages (GNU ld and LLD give
that segment `p_align` 0x10000) and refused, although it runs with 4 KiB
pages (gold keeps its segments apart and it is installed); and an image
laid out for pages smaller than the host's, or run on a host with larger
pages than the one that linked it with smaller `p_align`, is judged at the
page the rule chose. The model is the measured behaviour of the host's
kernel 6.17 and glibc 2.39; other loaders were not measured. An image
without a section header table is read by its segments alone. Host survey
(2026-09-26, the page model run over every regular ELF executable and
shared object under `/usr/lib`, `/usr/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/usr/libexec`,
`/usr/local`, `/opt` and the toolchain directories, at the host's page and
at 64 KiB): of 6,779 images it refuses 273, exactly the separate
debug-information files under `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id` (their allocated
sections are `NOBITS`, so a read-only segment holds 0x20c file bytes of a
0xf4ac-byte memory image; such a file is never loaded), and none of the
other 6,506.

*Correction (2026-09-27, the verifier of the eleventh repair at
`61627b7a6`):* that promise had four holes. Each was measured on the host,
each is refused now with the output's bytes left as they were, and each
refused layout is also linked and run outside the driver (`link_options`
`linux_got_page::pages_at_every_size_unloaded_sections_and_relro_stores_are_never_installed`):
- **Smaller pages.** A layout that holds at `P` need not hold at a smaller
  page. Take trust-cg's `.data` and `.bss` at 0x500000, a C `.zz` without
  file bytes at 0x500800 and a `.dd` at 0x502000, all from one file page:
  `.dd` is the last mapping of the 64 KiB page, and `.zz` the last mapping
  of the 4 KiB page, which the kernel maps as a zero page. LLD 22.1.6 wrote
  such no-PIE, PIE and static programs (`INSERT` and full scripts), the
  driver installed them, and on this 4 KiB host `tcg_val` read 0 where the
  file held 42. A read-only `.rr` at 0x500800 with `.dd` at 0x502000 made
  the 4 KiB page of `.data` read-only, and GNU ld 2.42's and LLD's
  programs died with SIGSEGV on their first store. The page model now runs
  at `P` and then at each smaller page a kernel of the machine uses: 16 and
  4 KiB on AArch64, whose kernels use 4, 16 or 64 KiB pages (8 and 32 KiB
  are not modelled), 4 KiB on x86-64, and every power of two down to 4 KiB
  for any other machine. Both layouts are refused at 4 KiB. LLD's twin,
  with `.zz` in the next 64 KiB page, is installed and runs.
- **Sections outside every segment.** An allocated section of nonzero size
  (a `.tbss` aside) must lie in the memory of one `PT_LOAD` (an image with
  no `PT_LOAD` maps nothing: `ld.so` refuses it, and such a program starts
  in unmapped memory). A `PHDRS` script's `:NONE` put trust-cg's `.data`
  after `.bss`, in the data segment's page but outside its memory. GNU
  ld's and LLD's static programs read `tcg_val` as 0, and the user of
  LLD's shared object read the bytes of `.comment` there.
- **Zero fill that reads file bytes.** A `NOBITS` section must read zero:
  where it lies in a segment's file part, the file's bytes there must be
  zero (in the zero fill the page model shows it). LLD gave an unsegmented
  `.data` the file offset under trust-cg's `.bss`, which lay between two
  sections of the data segment, and `tcg_z` read 42.
- **Write-protected data** (`[TCG-LINK-WRITE-PROTECTED]`). The page model
  read only `PT_LOAD` permissions. An `INSERT BEFORE .init_array` script
  put trust-cg's `.data` inside GNU ld's `PT_GNU_RELRO`, which `ld.so` and
  glibc's static start-up make read-only after relocation: PIE, no-PIE and
  static programs died with SIGSEGV on the first store, and so did the
  user of such a shared object. A `PHDRS` script's `FLAGS(4)` gave `.data`
  a read-only segment, and LLD's static program died the same way. An
  input section of the link's own objects, as the
  driver's map places it, is refused when it may hold mutable data and
  lies in a segment without `PF_W`, or meets the pages `_dl_protect_relro`
  protects: `PT_GNU_RELRO`'s start and end rounded down to the page, at any
  modelled page. Such a section is allocated, writable and not
  thread-local, and its name is not one where only immutable data goes
  (`.data.rel.ro`, `.bss.rel.ro`, `.init_array`, `.fini_array`,
  `.preinit_array`, `.toc`). The `PT_GNU_RELRO` part applies only where
  something applies that segment: a shared object, a program with
  `PT_INTERP`, a static program whose symbol table defines
  `__libc_start_main`, or one without a symbol table that is not
  `--nostdlib`. GNU ld gives a `--nostdlib` static program a
  `PT_GNU_RELRO` over its `.data`; nothing applies it, the program runs,
  and it is installed. GNU ld's map names the link's first input as the
  file of the `.dynamic`, `.got` and other sections the linker makes; a
  name the object holds no section of is not trust-cg's.

Bounds of the correction: a section trust-cg makes writable only because
it holds relocated immutable data under a name of the user's counts as
mutable (conservative); an own object that cannot be read counts all its
sections as mutable (conservative); and a stripped `--nostdlib` static
program that links glibc's start-up through its own `-Wl` inputs is judged
to apply no `PT_GNU_RELRO`, so trust-cg's `.data` placed there by a script
would be installed and its first store would fault (a residual, loud).
The host survey, re-run with the corrected rule, gives the same counts:
of 6,779 images it refuses the 273 debug-information files and none of the
other 6,506, at the host's page and at 64 KiB. Run over the same images as
a proxy, with each image's `.data` and `.bss` sections taken as trust-cg's,
the write-protection rule flags 24 of the 6,744 that have them. All 24 are
the klibc programs under `/usr/lib/klibc/bin`: their interpreter is
klibc's library, not `ld.so`, they have no dynamic section, and GNU ld gave
them its `PT_GNU_RELRO` over `.data`. The driver refuses such an image
anyway (`[TCG-LINK-INTERP-NO-DYNAMIC]`). The rule flags none of the other
6,720. The eleventh repair's verifier's ordinary-link sweep (1,026 links
through GNU ld, LLD and gold), its probes of skeptic 2's rows and its
330-link layout matrix give the same verdict for every link.

*Correction (2026-10-03, the twelfth closure audit at `23ee1104a`):* three
more classes were installed and are refused now, each with the output's
bytes left as they were and each refused layout also linked and run outside
the driver (`link_options` `linux_got_page::tls_templates_that_do_not_hold_trust_cgs_thread_locals_are_never_installed`,
`segments_without_the_permissions_trust_cgs_sections_need_are_never_installed`
and `llvm_bitcode_inputs_are_read_through_the_objects_lld_compiles`):
- **Thread-local template** (`[TCG-LINK-TLS-TEMPLATE]`). No rule related
  `PT_TLS`, from which glibc 2.39 initializes each thread's block (a copy of
  its first `p_filesz` bytes, read from memory at `p_vaddr`, then zeros up
  to `p_memsz`), to the thread-local sections. GNU ld 2.42 given a `PHDRS`
  script whose `PT_TLS` held `.tbss` alone (no-PIE and PIE), LLD 22.1.6
  given an `INSERT` script with `-z norelro` (a PIE, and a shared object
  whose user read 0) and LLD given `-Wl,--section-start=.tbss=0x700000`
  without any script (no-PIE and PIE) wrote images whose trust-cg
  thread-locals read 0 or other bytes (the bytes `/lib/ld-` of `.interp`)
  with exit status 1 and no crash. An executable or shared object with an
  allocated thread-local section of nonzero size is now refused unless one
  `PT_TLS` with memory holds every such section and begins at the first;
  its `p_align` is a power of two that divides its `p_vaddr` (glibc places
  a block whose start is not aligned at another offset from the thread
  pointer than the linkers compute); its file part lies in one `PT_LOAD`'s
  file part; the sections do not overlap; each with contents (`.tdata`)
  lies in the file part; the file part holds no other allocated section;
  and a zero-fill thread-local section in it lies over zero bytes
  (`tls_template_disagreement`). Through the driver's map, each of
  trust-cg's own thread-local input sections must lie in that `PT_TLS` (an
  image without section headers included); in an executable, each
  local-exec `ADD` pair of trust-cg's, and each initial-exec or descriptor
  access the linker relaxed to the `MOVZ`/`MOVK` pair, to a thread-local
  trust-cg defines must hold `TPREL = align_up(16, p_align) + (S + A -
  p_vaddr)` (variant 1: the 16-byte thread control block, then the block);
  and the symbol table must give each global thread-local trust-cg defines
  its offset from `p_vaddr`, the base each linker measures the offsets in a
  descriptor or dynamic relocation from (`own_tls_disagreement`). Not read
  (the template rules carry them): an access the linker left in its GOT or
  descriptor form, whose offset lies in a GOT slot or descriptor (GNU ld,
  gold and LLD relaxed trust-cg's descriptor accesses to a thread-local the
  executable defines into the pair, `--no-relax` included); a shared
  object's code; a local or
  stripped symbol; an access whose section the map does not place once. The
  rules are the measured behaviour of glibc 2.39 and the three linkers; other
  loaders were not measured.
- **Read and execute permission** (`[TCG-LINK-SEGMENT-PERMISSIONS]`). Only
  `PF_W` was checked for trust-cg's sections. A `PHDRS` script that gave
  trust-cg's `.rodata` a `PT_LOAD` without permissions (`FLAGS(0)`) through
  GNU ld, LLD and gold, and one that gave its `.text` a read-only segment
  through GNU ld and gold (LLD's twin was refused only by the `.eh_frame`
  check), installed static programs that died with SIGSEGV on their first
  load or instruction. An input section of trust-cg's that the map places is
  now refused when the `PT_LOAD` holding it lacks `PF_R` and the section is
  allocated (a zero-fill thread-local one, which occupies no memory of its
  own, aside), or lacks `PF_X` and the section is code (`SHF_EXECINSTR`).
  The rule shares its predicate (`own_section_lacking`) with the `PF_W` part
  of `[TCG-LINK-WRITE-PROTECTED]`, and the page model shows no later mapping
  takes a permission from a segment's pages. trust-cg's code reads its own
  `.text` (its switch jump tables lie there, read with `adr` and `ldrsw`), so
  an execute-only segment is refused too, whether or not the hardware would
  let such code run. gold 2.42's map prints the last code input section of
  an output section (trust-cg's `.text` in an ordinary link, the one owning
  its stub table) at `0xffffffffffffffff`; such an input is placed by the
  symbols the map lists under it (their addresses less their values in the
  object, which must agree), else taken as its whole output section for the
  segment rules, and refused when the map shows neither.
- **LLVM bitcode** (skeptic 2). The driver read no LLVM bitcode input: a
  static LLD image whose bitcode archive member defined libgcc's
  outline-atomics helpers (`__aarch64_cas8_acq_rel`, which a static
  program's frame registration calls through libgcc_eh) was installed and
  hung in `__register_frame_info`, while its ELF twin was refused
  (`[TCG-LINK-IRELATIVE-UNAPPLIED]`); and every static LLD link with a direct
  bitcode input (full or ThinLTO) was refused on the untrue reason that the
  linker reads it as a linker script. Bitcode (raw `BC` `0xC0DE`, and the
  wrapper `0x0B17C0DE`) is now recognized in direct inputs and archive
  members and is never read as a script. A traced link whose trace names a
  bitcode input runs again through LLD 22.1.6 with `--lto-obj-path` after
  every argument of the request, which keeps each object LLD compiles, and
  that link is the one checked and installed (the option makes LLD emit and
  link its regular LTO object even when it is empty, so a ThinLTO-only image
  differs from the first link's by that object). The objects' symbols,
  local-exec and GOT-addressing uses join the loaded inputs', so the C
  runtime stand-in rule reads them like an ELF input's: the audit's
  outline-atomics member is refused by name, and the audit's static
  bitcode links (full, ThinLTO, an archive) are installed and run.
  Objects that were not shown (an object LLD wrote empty because it took it
  from its ThinLTO cache, a link naming its own `obj-path`, and bitcode
  another linker reads) were refused by name only through the stand-in
  rule of a static program. GNU ld 2.42 and gold 2.42 fail such a link on
  the host, which has no LLVM plugin; a plugin was not measured. That left
  a dynamic image's checks without those objects' uses, and the 2026-10-15
  correction below closes it. Such a link is linked twice, so a `-Wl` option
  that writes a file of its own writes it again.

*Correction (2026-10-03, the first verifier of that repair at `be368f243`):*
two of those rules had a hole, and the repair of them found a third class.
All three are closed now (the same `link_options` tests
`tls_templates_that_do_not_hold_trust_cgs_thread_locals_are_never_installed`
and `segments_without_the_permissions_trust_cgs_sections_need_are_never_installed`,
plus link-driver unit rows):
- The thread-local section rules read the section header table, and an image
  without one was not checked against them. GNU ld 2.42 given `-z
  nosectionheader` and a `PHDRS` script that put `.tbss` before `.tdata`
  wrote a `--nostdlib` PIE whose two sections shared their bytes, so
  trust-cg's zero-fill thread-local read 42. A twin whose `PT_TLS` began at
  `.data` had a C reader of trust-cg's thread-local read `.data`'s bytes.
  The driver installed both. An image without a section header table that
  has a `PT_TLS` with memory is now refused, because where its thread-local
  sections lie is not shown. LLD 22.1.6 also accepts `-z nosectionheader`.
  The rule refuses the linkers' own layouts written that way too; that
  refusal is conservative.
- The loaded-bytes section rules (`[TCG-LINK-LOADED-BYTES]`) also read the
  section headers, and they read the output section's type. With `-z
  nosectionheader`, GNU ld and LLD placed trust-cg's `.data` in no segment
  under a `PHDRS` script's `:NONE`, and the driver installed static programs
  whose trust-cg global read 0. A script that marked trust-cg's `.rodata`
  `(NOLOAD)` made GNU ld and LLD write a zero-fill output section there.
  The image rule admits zero fill, so the driver installed programs whose
  trust-cg constant read 0; gold 2.42 loaded the bytes. Each of trust-cg's
  own allocated input sections is now held to the section rules where the
  map places them, with or without section headers
  (`own_loaded_disagreement`). It must lie in the memory of a `PT_LOAD`. A
  section with contents in its object must lie in that segment's file part.
  The part of a zero-fill section inside the file part must lie over zero
  bytes. A zero-fill thread-local section, which occupies no memory, is not
  read. GNU ld's and LLD's links are refused now, and gold's `(NOLOAD)` link
  is installed and runs. In an image without section headers, the sections
  of the other inputs are still read through the segments alone (the page
  model).
- The read rule did not see trust-cg's `.eh_frame` through LLD 22.1.6 or gold
  2.42. LLD's map prints `.eh_frame` input as pieces, and gold's prints its
  merged `** eh_frame` data with no file. A dynamic no-PIE `PHDRS` script that
  gave `.eh_frame` a `PT_LOAD` without permissions was refused through GNU ld
  but installed through LLD and gold. Those programs died with SIGSEGV in
  `_Unwind_Find_FDE` at their first `backtrace`. An own object's LLD pieces
  are now own input sections. Where their output section also holds other
  input, the map does not show where they lie, and the whole output section
  is taken instead. gold's merged data is taken as holding each own object's
  allocated `.eh_frame` that its map does not list as an input; the map does
  not say which merged span holds which input, so this is conservative. All
  three links are refused now, and their `FLAGS(4)` twins are installed and
  run.

*Correction (2026-10-15, the thirteenth closure audit at `baf1a4dee`):*
the local-exec and GOT-addressing checks read the uses of the objects LLD
compiles from LLVM bitcode only when the driver could read all of them.
When it could not, it skipped them silently, and their absence counted
only against a static program's C runtime. Two kinds of dynamic link were
installed without those uses:
- a ThinLTO link with `--thinlto-cache-dir`, where LLD writes 0 bytes for
  each object it takes from the cache, and the driver's own first link
  fills the cache;
- a link with the user's own `--lto-obj-path`, where LLD writes the objects
  there.

The audit's shared object and PIE, whose bitcode's `f_gb` loads 6,000 GOT
slots through `R_AARCH64_LD64_GOTPAGE_LO15`, read 2,349 and 2,073 wrong
slots. LLVM's fat LTO objects under `--fat-lto-objects` are the same class
(found in the repair): LLD links what it compiles from an object's
`.llvm.lto` bitcode in place of the object's own code, which is what the
driver read.

Now:
- The link the driver checks and installs puts its own `--lto-obj-path`
  and an empty `--thinlto-cache-dir=` after every option of the user's.
  LLD 22.1.6 reads the last of each, so it writes every object it compiles
  into the stage, in full, after each spelling of either option it accepts.
  The user's `obj-path` still receives the first link's objects, and the
  first link still uses and fills the user's cache. The installed image is
  the second link's, compiled without the cache.
- When the last of `--fat-lto-objects` and `--no-fat-lto-objects` in the
  `-Wl` groups is the first, each loaded AArch64 ELF relocatable object
  holding a `.llvm.lto` section counts as a bitcode input, and the link runs
  again to keep what LLD compiled. A `--no-fat-lto-objects` that could be
  the value of the option before it does not count. The object's own code
  is still read too (conservative).
- A loaded ELF relocatable object that is not AArch64 LP64 (another class,
  byte order or machine) counts as a bitcode input whatever the `-Wl` groups
  say: LLD 22.1.6 links one only through the bitcode of its `.llvm.lto`
  section, under `--fat-lto-objects`, and rejects it otherwise.
- The `-Wl` groups do not show an option the C driver adds itself. LLD's
  map of the link decides the rest: LLD names each object it compiles after
  the output (`<output>.lto.o`, `<output>.lto.<input>.o`), and its input
  trace names none of them. When the first link's map places input sections
  of a file the trace does not name, the link runs again to keep what LLD
  compiled, and the second link reads whatever LLD wrote there. (False for
  an input named like one of those objects; the fourteenth closure audit's
  correction below replaces the map's names with what LLD wrote.)
- The compiled code is refused as unread when one of these holds:
  - a counted bitcode input's objects are not read: another linker's, an
    LLD whose `--version` is not the measured one, or anything LLD did not
    write to the stage in full;
  - the checked link's map places input sections of more files the trace
    does not name than the driver read compiled objects (a C driver that
    also gives a later `--lto-obj-path`, for example);
  - that map is not read while a loaded AArch64 object holds a `.llvm.lto`
    section and no compiled object was read (replaced by the fourteenth
    closure audit's correction below: such an object needs what LLD wrote
    read in full, whatever the map shows).

  Every check that must read each loaded input's uses then refuses the
  image by name: `[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]` (`unclassified`, a
  conservative refusal). That covers the local-exec check of every shared
  object and the GOT-addressing checks of any image not shown in reach, in
  every link mode. The IFUNC applier rule no longer takes unread objects
  to define no IFUNC. An executable whose GOT is shown in reach needs no
  such read and is installed, whatever its compiled code.

The audit's ThinLTO-cache, user-`obj-path` and fat-LTO reproducers (shared
and PIE) are refused for the use in the object LLD compiled
(`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`, `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`), and LLD
outside the driver writes them wrong. Ordinary full and ThinLTO links are
installed and run: with a cache (static, PIE, shared object), with a user
`obj-path` (static, no-PIE) and with fat LTO objects (static, PIE)
(`link_options`
`linux_got_page::got_base_code_lld_compiles_from_bitcode_is_read_on_every_lto_route`
and `llvm_bitcode_inputs_are_read_through_the_objects_lld_compiles`).

Not measured: an LLVM plugin for gold or GNU ld (the host has none).

LLD's distributed ThinLTO (`--thinlto-distributor`) was measured with one
local distributor, which compiles each job with `llc`:
- LLD writes the distributed object (`lto.o1`) to the driver's path, so it
  is read.
- The audit's GOT-base ThinLTO module, linked through it as a shared object
  without a cache and with a cold and a warm one, is refused for each of its
  6,000 GOT uses in that object.
- An ordinary ThinLTO module is installed as a PIE and as a static program,
  and both run.

Other distributors were not measured. Their objects are read when LLD writes
them to the driver's path. Otherwise they are refused by name in two cases:
the driver's path holds no complete object of LLD's for a counted input, or
the checked link's map shows more compiled files than objects read.
Decisions LD-58, LD-60 and LD-64.

*Correction (2026-10-15, the third verification of that repair at
`05097cc57`):* the repair still installed two routes unread. In both, LLD
linked code it compiled from a fat object's `.llvm.lto` bitcode, and the
driver read the object's own code.
- A fat container whose ELF class, byte order or machine is not AArch64
  LP64: x86-64, i686, big-endian AArch64, and AArch64 with `e_machine`
  patched to x86-64. These were tried as files, in an archive, and found
  with `-l`. Only AArch64 LP64 objects were counted.
  - The GOT-base PIEs read 2,073 wrong slots and the shared objects read
    2,349.
  - A static program whose container held the outline-atomics bitcode was
    installed, and was still running when killed after 10 s.
- A C driver that adds `--fat-lto-objects` itself. The decision read only
  the `-Wl` groups, so the AArch64 fat PIE read 2,073 wrong slots.

The rules above close both. Through the repaired driver:
- Each foreign container is refused with exactly its AArch64 control's
  diagnostics: 6,000 `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]` for a PIE, and 3,651
  `UNPROVEN` with 2,349 `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]` for a shared object.
  The foreign static program is refused.
- The C driver's PIE is refused for the 6,000 uses in the object LLD
  compiled.
- With a later `--lto-obj-path` or an unmeasured LLD as well, the PIE is
  refused as `[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]`.

Ordinary fat objects through that C driver, and in a foreign container, are
installed and run. Decision LD-64.

*Correction (2026-10-15, the fourteenth closure audit at `8cc4ab677`):*
LLD's map decided by file name, and a user chooses the names of the inputs.
LLD 22.1.6 names the object it compiles from a fat object's ThinLTO bitcode
`<input directory>/<output>.lto.<stem>.o`, and
`<output>.lto.<archive>(<member> at <offset>).o` for an archive member.
Neither name depends on the driver's stage, so a user can predict it. When
the link also loaded an input of that name, the map placed the compiled
object under a name the trace names. No second link ran and nothing was
read. Through a C driver that adds `--fat-lto-objects` itself, the driver
installed:
- a PIE that printed `f_gb=1904` (correct: 4242), because its truncated
  `R_AARCH64_LD64_GOTPAGE_LO15` load read another slot;
- a shared object whose user printed the same;
- a static program carrying the outline-atomics bitcode, which hung until
  it was killed after 10 s.

The repair found two more of the same: the archive member's decoy, and the
file's decoy through an LLD whose `--version` the driver did not measure.
Each installed a PIE that printed `f_gb=1904`.

Now:
- The link runs again to keep what LLD compiled whenever a loaded input
  holds bitcode, judged by its bytes and never by its name. That covers
  raw bitcode, an ELF relocatable object of another kind, and an AArch64
  one with a `.llvm.lto` section, as a file or as a stored or thin archive
  member. An AArch64 object the reader cannot read counts too.
- Once such an AArch64 object is loaded, what LLD wrote where the driver
  had it keep its objects must be read in full, whatever the map names.
  Given `--lto-obj-path`, LLD 22.1.6 wrote an empty `lto.o` and nothing else
  for every measured link that compiled no bitcode. Those were a PIE and a
  static program without bitcode, and a ThinLTO fat object without
  `--fat-lto-objects` (PIE, shared object, static program) or with
  `--fat-lto-objects --no-fat-lto-objects`. Every measured link that
  compiled bitcode left a non-empty `lto.o`: full LTO, ThinLTO, and the fat
  object under the option. So an empty `lto.o` alone is read as "LLD
  compiled nothing", and the object's own code, which the driver read, is
  what was linked. (Incomplete: under `--lto-partitions=<N>` LLD writes
  `<N>` empty files when it compiles nothing; see the fifteenth closure
  audit's correction below.)
- Anything else that is not read in full refuses every check that needs
  the compiled code as `[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]`. That covers nothing
  written, an empty object beside others (beside a non-empty one since the
  fifteenth closure audit's correction below), and a linker other than the
  measured LLD.
- A map in GNU ld 2.42's or gold 2.42's format shows a link LLD did not
  make. Both linkers reject `--fat-lto-objects` and linked the object's own
  code; an LLVM plugin for them was not measured.
- A counted bitcode input whose link left only an empty `lto.o` stays
  refused (conservative).
- The map's names can still add a link and a refusal (more untraced files
  than objects read). They no longer withhold either.

Through the repaired driver, each decoy link is refused with the tag of its
control without the decoy. Only addresses the decoy's bytes move differ, and
the unmeasured LLD's reason:
- the PIE and the archive member's PIE as `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]`,
  and the shared object as `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-WINDOW]`, each for the use in
  `lto.o1`, the object LLD compiled from the fat object's `.llvm.lto`;
- the static program as `[TCG-LINK-IRELATIVE-UNAPPLIED]`, naming the
  helpers `lto.o1` defines (its text is the control's);
- the unmeasured LLD's PIE as `[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]`. The control
  names the map's untraced file, and the decoy link names the unread
  objects.

One new conservative refusal: through an unmeasured LLD, a link that loads
an AArch64 fat object is refused as unread wherever a check needs the
compiled code, even without `--fat-lto-objects`. Such a link runs the
object's own code (at `8cc4ab677` it was installed and printed
`f_gb=4242`), but the driver cannot read what that LLD compiled. Every
LLD 22.1.6 link that loads a fat object is now linked twice, as bitcode
links are. (There was a second, unstated one, lifted by the fifteenth
closure audit's correction below: an LLD 22.1.6 link that loaded a fat
object without the option and passed `--lto-partitions=2` or more.)

Installed and run with a decoy in the link:
- an ordinary ThinLTO fat object through the C driver, static and PIE (the
  bitcode's code);
- the GOT-base fat object through LLD without the option (a PIE), through
  GNU ld (a PIE and a shared object) and through gold (a shared object),
  each running the object's own `f_gb`.

These are `link_options`
`linux_got_page::compiled_code_lld_wrote_is_read_whatever_the_inputs_are_named`.
Decision LD-69.

*Correction (2026-10-15, the fifteenth closure audit at `b3070867f`):* LLD
22.1.6 writes one file per LTO task where `--lto-obj-path` says: `lto.o`,
then `lto.o1`, `lto.o2`, ..., one per regular LTO partition
(`--lto-partitions=<N>`, 1 by default) and then one per ThinLTO module.
When it compiles nothing, each is empty. The fourteenth audit's repair read
only an empty `lto.o` alone as "LLD compiled nothing". So an LLD link that
loaded a fat object without `--fat-lto-objects` and passed
`--lto-partitions=2` or more (in any spelling, or added by the C driver) was
refused as `[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]` wherever a check needed the
compiled code. The reason it gave blamed a ThinLTO cache the driver had
disabled. That refused a shared object, a static program, a static PIE and
the GOT-base PIE, each of which `8cc4ab677` installed and each of which ran
the object's own code.

Measured, with `--lto-obj-path` and an empty `--thinlto-cache-dir=`:
- 240 links that compiled no bitcode wrote exactly `<N>` 0-byte files,
  `lto.o` to `lto.o<N-1>`, and each executable ran the object's own code.
  They had no bitcode input, or a ThinLTO or full LTO fat object without the
  option, as a PIE, no-PIE, static, static-PIE or shared object, under
  `--lto-partitions=1` to `4` in each spelling LLD accepts:
  `--lto-partitions=`, `--plugin-opt=lto-partitions=`,
  `-plugin-opt=lto-partitions=` and the separate `-plugin-opt
  lto-partitions=`. LLD rejects the separate `--lto-partitions <N>`.
- 108 more such links under 18 other LTO options, with 1 and 3
  partitions, also wrote only 0-byte files. 72 ran the object's own code
  (`--save-temps`, `--thinlto-jobs=`, `--lto-O0`, `--lto-CGO1`,
  `--fat-lto-objects --no-fat-lto-objects`, and seven others). 36 linked no
  image (`--lto-emit-asm`, `-plugin-opt=emit-asm`, `-plugin-opt=emit-llvm`,
  `--lto-emit-llvm`, `--thinlto-index-only`, `--thinlto-single-module=`).
  4 more, with a later `--thinlto-cache-dir=`, cold and warm, did the same
  and ran the object's own code.
- 60 links that compiled bitcode left every file non-empty. They were full
  LTO, ThinLTO, and a ThinLTO and a full LTO fat object under the option,
  under 1 to 4 partitions, with the options before or after the driver's,
  as a PIE, static program or shared object. An empty partition's object
  is 560 bytes.
- Two kinds of measured link that compiled bitcode left an empty file:
  - `-plugin-opt=emit-llvm` left every file empty and wrote LLVM bitcode
    where the linked image belongs. Every Linux link's `.eh_frame` check
    refuses that output as `[TCG-LINK-EH-FRAME-UNPROVEN]` ("the image cannot
    be read as an ELF image").
  - A later `--thinlto-cache-dir=`, cold or warm, left the module's file
    empty beside non-empty partition objects.

Now:
- Only empty files, one per task with none left out, read as "LLD compiled
  nothing", under any number of partitions.
- These stay refused as unread:
  - an empty file beside a non-empty one. Where that is the reason given,
    it now says LLD does this for a task whose object it takes from
    elsewhere (its ThinLTO cache), rather than asserting a cache;
  - a counted bitcode input whose link left only empty files;
  - a non-empty file that is not an AArch64 relocatable object.
- New: a task's file left out (`lto.o1` with no `lto.o`, or `lto.o2` with
  no `lto.o1`) is refused, empty or not. LLD wrote no such set in any
  measured link.

Through the repaired driver:
- The audit's shared object and static program (`--lto-partitions=2`) are
  installed and print `v=OK`, as at `8cc4ab677` and outside the driver.
- The GOT-base PIE (partitions 2, 3 and 4 in three spellings, and through a
  C driver that adds `--lto-partitions=3`) and its shared object are
  installed and print `f_gb=4242`.
- In skeptic 2's sweep harness (185 LLD links each), the 20 links
  `b3070867f` refused this way are installed and print `v=OK`. Every other
  row is unchanged.
- What LLD compiles under partitions is still read. Through a C driver that
  adds `--fat-lto-objects --lto-partitions=3`, the GOT-base PIE is refused
  as `[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNPROVEN]` for the use in `lto.o3`, and an ordinary
  fat object is installed and runs its bitcode's code (PIE and static).
- With a later cache as well, the PIE is refused as unread.

A second low finding of the same audit is fixed too. When a link loaded a
counted bitcode input and an uncounted fat object (a C driver added the
option), a refusal named each compiled object after the counted input
alone. In the audit's link, `lto.o2` was in fact compiled from the fat
object's `.llvm.lto` (outside the driver it defines the fat object's
`f_gb`). Each object read is now named after both possible sources ("the
LLVM bitcode input `<counted>` or the LLVM bitcode input `<fat object>`'s
`.llvm.lto` section"), since LLD's task order does not show which input a
task compiled. The verdict is unchanged.

These are `link_options`
`linux_got_page::lld_links_that_compile_nothing_are_installed_under_lto_partitions`
and the unit row `compiled_nothing_is_only_empty_files_one_per_task`.
Decision LD-69 (correction).

Two refusals of the thread-local rules are conservative, and their reasons
now say so. In the first, `PT_TLS` begins with bytes that are not thread-local,
before its first thread-local section. GNU ld measures thread-local offsets
from that first section, so its programs read other bytes. LLD and gold measure
from `p_vaddr`, so their hand-written `PHDRS` layouts with `.data` inside
`PT_TLS` ran correctly outside the driver; the check refuses either. In the
second, the file part of `PT_TLS` reaches past the file part of its `PT_LOAD`.
That is refused because the template's bytes are not shown to be in memory
there, even where a page mapping happens to hold them.

Linker diagnostics printed to standard output are outside this row, but
one: GNU ld 2.42 prints `<ld>: <input>: note: the message above does not
take linker garbage collection into account` on standard output after a
warning it gives with `--gc-sections` (a static glibc program's use of an
NSS function such as `getpwuid`), and the trace reader skips that line
(the eleventh closure audit found such static links refused; they are
installed and run now). A passthrough that prints to standard output (LLD 22.1.6's
`--print-gc-sections`, `-y` and `--trace-symbol`, GNU ld 2.42's and LLD's
`--print-memory-usage`, GNU ld's `--verbose` and `-M`) leaves the input
trace unreadable, and every such link that needs its trace is refused as
`[TCG-LINK-INPUT-TRACE]` (a conservative refusal; the tenth closure
audit's false-refusal lens judged it out of scope).

Host survey, 2026-09-24: 6,368 ELF executables and shared objects, holding
5,091,400 FDEs.
- **Aliasing.** No image has a pointer with a second address.
- **Hidden FDEs.** 14 images have a hidden FDE: the Qt6 libraries bundled
  with NVIDIA Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute, linked by LLD 17. LLD's
  table keeps one entry per start (the first in `.eh_frame` order), and
  here it names a zero-range FDE ahead of the function's real one.
  - In `libQt6Core.so.6`, the zero-range FDE is the empty
    `QProcess::setupChildProcess`'s, and it hides `QProcess::readData`.
    That is a leaf, so no throw passes through it, though a backtrace
    loses it.
  - In `libQt6Qml.so.6`, 14 zero-range FDEs hide the 0x73c-byte
    `QV4::Compiler::Codegen::visit(QQmlJS::AST::ExportDeclaration *)`, a
    function a throw can pass through.
  - libgcc finds no unwind information for them, and the check would refuse
    such an image if trust-cg linked it.
A staged image of at most 1 GiB is read back whole. Until the 2026-09-24
closure audit, a larger one was too: `trust-cg --static --nostdlib --no-pie
-Wl,start.o -Wl,--section-start=.far=0x2000000000 -o far b1_scalars.tmbc`
through LLD wrote a 128 GiB sparse image (LLD extends the first `PT_LOAD`
from the ELF header to `.far`), and reading it back killed the CLI for
memory (exit 137) and left its `.tcg-link-*` staging directory. A larger
image is now read back as the ranges its checks read, at their file offsets
(`link_driver::read_large_image`): the checks run on what was read, each
range a check asked for that was not read is read for the next run, and a
run that asks for nothing more saw what it would have seen in the whole
file. To find every table in one run, a missed read finds zeros while the
image is being read back (never in the run that is kept), and a scan past
what was read is read ahead. The audit's link completes with a peak RSS of
38 MB, LLD's included, and its program exits 42 (`link_options`, with
`-Wl,--build-id=none`: LLD's own build-id hash reads the whole image). An
