image is refused as `unclassified` with `[TCG-LINK-IMAGE-UNCHECKED]`, before
what its checks still need is read and naming the cause (and the bytes
read from the file in all, including those read ahead and dropped), when
the ranges its checks read without zeros, and those they still ask for,
come to more than 1 GiB, or when they
still ask for ranges after 64 runs (a chain of reads that each depends on
the last, such as an `.eh_frame` without section headers whose CIEs lie in
thousands of pages, can take that many); the requested output is not
touched. Whatever an image's size, each of the two layout checks (the
GOT-addressing and the `.eh_frame` one) holds at most 4,194,304 of each of
section headers, dynamic relocation targets (every table it reads
together), dynamic-section entries, `.eh_frame` records, `.eh_frame_hdr`
entries and GOT-base symbol addresses; takes at most 16,777,216 steps
through relocation entries (those that name no target, such as
`R_AARCH64_NONE`, included), symbol tables, `.eh_frame` records and
terminators, the search for another address an `.eh_frame` pointer's
bits give, and the zero bytes scanned for LLD's `.eh_frame_hdr`
placeholder; and copies at most 64 MiB of section names and 64 MiB of
dynamic-symbol names. A relocation table that the dynamic section and a
section header, or two headers, name alike
(type, offset, size, entry size) is read once; overlapping tables are
each read, within those steps. An image with more than one `PT_DYNAMIC`
is not read: linkers write one, and glibc and musl apply the last while
Android's linker applies the first. An image that needs more makes that
check unreadable or unproven, by name, and is refused: an unreadable GOT
layout whatever the inputs (`[TCG-LINK-GOT-PAGE-UNCHECKED]`: GOT-addressing
code the linker wrote itself cannot be ruled out in it), an unproven
`.eh_frame` on Linux. Of the host's 6,626 images, the one with the most
dynamic relocation targets (an Electron executable, 595,711) names about 7
times fewer. A PLT, IPLT or TLS descriptor trampoline with more
than eight slots out of reach names eight and counts the rest. Some
costs stay proportional to a product a hostile image can make large:
comparing each dynamic relocation target with each allocated `SHT_NOBITS`
section and `PT_LOAD` tail, each input use with each target, and each
linker-written slot with each executable region. Four others are
bounded: a symbol's name is compared only at the length of the names
looked for (and a function name for a diagnostic is read to at most 4 KiB),
so a string table without NULs no longer costs each symbol its whole
length; FDEs that begin together find the table's last entry for their
start in a map built once; the `.eh_frame` pointer search takes no
step when the pointer and the memory it is searched in lie within one
window of its field (every 4-byte pointer of the host's 6,626 images, whose
allocated memory spans at most 685 MiB), and otherwise the fewer of
one step per span and one per candidate address, within those steps; and
the zeros of `.eh_frame_hdr` sections that no `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` locates,
scanned for LLD's zero-filled placeholder, are counted on their own, at
most 16,777,216 of them before a non-zero byte, so headers that name the
same zeros again cost no more. A staging directory
is removed when a check's panic unwinds through `run_link`; a process that aborts or is
killed leaves it. The arm64 Darwin code-signature check still reads its
output whole.

On ELF, a zero-offset load/store
of a non-weak data symbol this object defines at an alignment covering the
access size is fused into `ADRP; LDR/STR #:lo12:`
(`R_AARCH64_LDST*_ABS_LO12_NC`); other accesses keep `ADRP+ADD`, and sites
whose page register is still needed stay unfused. A 16-byte-aligned
`v4i32` global is read and written through the fused Q-register form
(`LDST128`), and the Linux AArch64 host ran it. The five LDST value
obligations are in the strict corpus with a named formal floor
(`aarch64_elf_ldst_lo12_rows_are_formally_verified`). On the macOS host used
for this change, AY refuted all five negative controls but returned UNKNOWN
(incomplete proof certificate) for the five positives, as it does there for
the pre-existing AArch64 ELF relocation and TLS rows. No formal proof of the
LDST rows is recorded yet, and their unit checks are evaluation-based; the
production ELF relocation registry nevertheless cites that lane for them, as
it does for the other ELF rows.

The runtime-dependency manifest classifies undefined symbols by an exact name
table; unknown names are `external`, and the table does not establish that a
given C library, libgcc or unwinder exports a symbol. The CLI's link-failure
classifier recognizes GNU ld, lld and ld64 message texts; other wording is
reported as `unclassified`. Its two TLS kinds match only messages captured on
the Linux host: `tls-model-mismatch` for a local-exec relocation
(`R_AARCH64_TLSLE_*`) that lld refuses in a `-shared` link or GNU ld refuses
against an undefined symbol, and, in an executable, one that meets a
thread-local a shared library defines (GNU ld's `relocation truncated to fit:
R_AARCH64_TLSLE_* against symbol ... defined in <section> section in
<library>` when the library's file name ends in `.so` or `.so.<digits>`, and
lld's `relocation R_AARCH64_TLSLE_* cannot be used against symbol ...;
recompile with -fPIC`); and `tls-symbol-type-mismatch` for GNU ld's four
TLS/non-TLS definition/reference clash messages. The same GNU ld truncation
against a library not named that way, or against a thread-local an object
defines, stays `relocation-out-of-range`. lld's own clash message is
not matched: the host's LLD 22.1.6 crashed on a TLS definition paired with a
non-TLS reference and linked the reverse pairing without a diagnostic.
Through `run_link` that pairing (an initial-exec reference to `t` in one
object, a non-TLS `int t` in another) is installed and the program dies
with SIGSEGV (the second verifier of the tenth closure audit's repair,
2026-09-26): a residual, since neither the diagnostic parser nor the image
checks read the symbol types of the inputs.
x86-64 and RISC-V TPREL relocations are not matched. Before a shared-object
link, `link_driver::run_link` also reads each input that parses as an
AArch64 ELF64 relocatable object and refuses any local-exec TLS relocation
in it (`error[link:tls-model-mismatch]`, `[TCG-LINK-TLS-MODEL]`). On Linux,
`parse_wl_group` refuses every `-Wl` spelling that GNU ld 2.42 reads as a
driver-owned option. That covers one or two dashes, every prefix of the long
name, `=<value>`, the joined short forms `-o<file>`, `-h<name>` and
`-R<dir>`, and a bare `-G`. Prefixes that 2.42 reads as another option or
rejects as ambiguous (`--ou`, `--no`, `-st`) are refused too. So are the
single-dash spellings of unrelated options that begin with `o` or `h`
(`-orphan-handling`); their two-dash spellings are accepted. `-hash-style`
spelled out, which GNU ld 2.42, gold 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 all read as
`--hash-style` (the same bytes; the eleventh closure audit found it
refused), is admitted since that audit; its prefixes (`-hash-st=`, which
LLD reads as `-h ash-st=`) and `-hash-size` (which LLD reads as `-h`) are
still refused.
`-G <number>` is refused although it only sets the small-data size
(`--gpsize=<number>` is accepted). The model follows GNU ld 2.42's reading,
checked against the host's ld. It relies on 2.42 rejecting a grouped short
option that takes a value (`-sofoo`: `unable to disambiguate`). An older GNU
ld that accepted such grouping is not modelled. The first read-back read the
requested output path itself. That let `-Wl,--outp=<file>` or `-Wl,-o<file>`
put the library elsewhere, and it could read and delete a file that
`-Wl,--version` never wrote. Now every other link with such an input writes
to a fresh driver-owned directory next to the output. The staged image is
read back and moved onto the output only when it is `ET_EXEC`, `ET_DYN` with
`DF_1_PIE`, or `ET_REL`. Otherwise it is removed with the directory and
refused (`LinkError::OutputRefused`). A successful link that wrote no staged
image is refused (`LinkError::OutputMissing`, `[TCG-LINK-NO-OUTPUT]`). No
refusal reads or removes a file already at the output path. An `ET_DYN`
output of a linker that does not set `DF_1_PIE` on a position-independent
executable would be refused too. These are checks on the objects, on the
linker's input trace and on the staged file's header, not on the link. The
positional inputs (the AArch64 ELF64 relocatable objects `run_link` receives
as its inputs) are scanned before the link. An object can also reach the
linker as a `-Wl` operand (`-Wl,le.o`, also inside `--start-group`), as a
`-l:<file>` library, as a member of a regular or thin archive (taken by
reference or with `--whole-archive`), through a linker script's `INPUT()` or
`GROUP()`, or from the C driver itself. On Linux, every link that is not a
plain executable link (a `-nostdlib` executable request with no `-l`
library, no `-Wl` group and only positional AArch64 ELF relocatable inputs
that carry no local-exec and no GOT-page relocation) is therefore staged
and run with the linker's input trace (`-Wl,--trace,--trace`, passed before
every other argument). GNU ld 2.42 then prints each file it opens and each
member it takes from a regular archive as `(archive)member` (a thin archive's
member as its own path); LLD 22 prints each loaded object as a path or
`archive(member)`; gold 2.42, whose `--trace` prints the same form, names a
thin archive's member by the path it opened (`dup/libthin.a(dup/sub/one.o)`
for the recorded `sub/one.o`), which is read as the member whose file it is
(until the eleventh closure audit every gold link that read the trace of
such a member was refused). The forms were checked on the Linux host. When the staged
image is not `ET_EXEC`, `ET_DYN` with `DF_1_PIE`, or `ET_REL`, every AArch64
ELF relocatable object the trace names is read (archive members from the
archive, every copy of a repeated member name), and a local-exec relocation
in any of them refuses the image with `[TCG-LINK-TLS-MODEL]`, naming the
loaded input (`le/libtcgarc.a(tcgtls.o)`). Each of those routes had exited 0
through `trust-cg --shared` with GNU ld 2.42 (its user exited 236); `link_options`
`linux_tls::local_exec_objects_on_every_link_route_are_refused_by_name` now
refuses all eight, leaves no output and keeps a file already at the output
path, and its `pic` twins link and return 42. A trace that does not show what
was loaded is refused with `[TCG-LINK-INPUT-TRACE]` (kind `unclassified`): a
line that names no readable file or member (a passthrough that prints to
standard output, such as `-Wl,--verbose` or `-Wl,-M`, or a file deleted after
the link), a positional object missing from the
trace, or an AArch64 relocatable object the reader cannot parse (a
positional one included). The objects LLD 22.1.6 compiles from LLVM bitcode,
which the trace does not name, are read with the traced ones, and such an
image whose compiled objects are not read is refused with
`[TCG-LINK-LTO-OBJECTS-UNREAD]` (the 2026-10-15 correction under
`[TCG-LINK-WRITE-PROTECTED]`). The reader reads ELF extended section numbering
(`e_shnum` 0, `e_shstrndx` `SHN_XINDEX`, a symbol's section in
`SHT_SYMTAB_SHNDX`), which an assembler writes for 65,280 sections or more
(a plain `g++ -c` of a 6,000-class translation unit wrote 120,027): until
the eleventh closure audit every such input was unreadable and refused
wherever it was read. A `--shared` link with such a passthrough is
therefore refused rather than examined. Both scans read `SHT_REL` as well as
`SHT_RELA` sections: the AArch64 psABI uses `SHT_RELA` only, but GNU ld 2.42
linked a local-exec pair moved into an `SHT_REL` section into a `-shared`
library outside the driver, applying it. GCC's LTO plugin deletes the
objects it compiles for the link (`/tmp/cc<random>.ltrans0.ltrans.o`),
which GNU ld's trace names: until the tenth closure audit (2026-09-26)
every `-flto` object (slim or fat, C or C++) was refused as
`[TCG-LINK-INPUT-TRACE]` in GNU ld's default PIE link and in every GNU ld
and gold static link, although the programs ran. A traced GNU ld or gold
link (by the linker's exact `--version`) whose trace names such an object
that is gone is now linked again, with `TMPDIR` set to a fresh directory in
the stage and `-Wl,-plugin-opt=-save-temps` (the plugin then keeps the
objects), and that link, whose trace names readable objects, is the one
checked and installed; gold's record of opened files is made the same way.
The objects are removed with the stage. Every one of the audit's LTO links
now installs and runs, with output paths holding spaces, commas and `%`
(`link_options` `linux_got_page::lto_objects_link_through_gnu_ld_and_gold`).
Such a link is linked twice, so a `-Wl` option that writes a file of its
own writes it again. A positional input that holds GCC LTO IR (a
`.gnu.lto_` section) makes a link traced too: the plugin loads the objects
it compiles, so the link loads more than its positional inputs. LLD reads
no GCC LTO IR. A shared-library input is not
scanned: the linker binds against its dynamic symbols and applies none of
its relocations; a local-exec reference
from an executable to a shared library's thread-local is the linker's own
refusal, classified as `tls-model-mismatch`. A traced link that writes nothing
at the staged path (`-Wl,--version`) succeeds unless a positional input needs
the read-back or the trace names a local-exec or GOT-addressing input. Staging
makes every Linux link (since the `.eh_frame` check, a plain executable link
too) refuse `-o /dev/null` and need a writable output directory (see the
staging consequences below).

Still unexamined by the trace: a plain executable link, which loads only its positional
inputs (unless a C driver that ignores `-nostdlib` adds others); a file
replaced between the link and the read of the trace's files; code a linker
plugin generates without a traced file (LLD's in-memory LTO); a file a
linker writes at a path other than the staged one; and links made outside
the driver (for example `cc -shared` on a `trust-cg -c` object). The GOT-page
window check (see the relocation limits above) reads the same trace: until
the 2026-09-23 L02-P10 residuals it read only positional inputs, and the
closure audit installed a library with a truncated `ADRP` from
`-Wl,<got_page.o>`, `-l :got_page.o` and a `--whole-archive` member. The
image is checked first, and the trace is read only when the image is not
shown in reach for some GOT-addressing window, so a link whose code and
possible slots lie within 1 MiB reads no input after the link. A link
with the C runtime is now traced as well, because the host's start files
carry GOT-page `ADRP`s (`Scrt1.o`'s `R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE` against
`main`, `crti.o`'s and `crtbeginS.o`'s): GNU ld links an executable whose
`.got` is placed 8 GiB from its code (with `.data` kept near) and it dies
with SIGSEGV, which the driver now refuses by name. This is execution and
object evidence on one host's GNU ld 2.42 and LLD 22, not a proof about
every linker's trace.

GNU ld treats `-Bstatic`, `-dn`, `-non_shared` and `-static` as one option.
`-Wl,-static` is refused as the spelling of the typed `--static`. The other
three are accepted deliberately: they are the positional library-search
switch used as `-Wl,-Bstatic ... -Wl,-Bdynamic`, and they do not select the
output kind.

No forwarded value may begin with `@`: the output path, an input path, a
`-L` directory, a `-l` name, the soname or a run-time search path. The C
compiler driver, collect2 and GNU ld expand an argument `@<file>` into the
file's contents, which no trust-cg check sees. `--rpath @resp` with `resp`
holding `/x --shared -o libevil.so` made GNU ld write a local-exec library
at `libevil.so`. So each such value is refused before anything runs
(`[TCG-LINK-RESPONSE-FILE]`); a path can be spelled `./@...`. On Darwin, a
run-time search path or install name that begins with a dyld path token
(`@loader_path`, `@executable_path`, `@rpath`) is accepted. Whether ld64
expands those as response files has not been checked, because there is no
Darwin host.

On Linux, `run_link` stages every link, so that every image's `.eh_frame`
is checked (see the relocation limits above), and traces every link except
a plain executable link (a `-nostdlib` executable request with no `-l`
library, no `-Wl` group and only positional inputs the AArch64 ELF reader
reads) whose positional inputs carry no local-exec relocation and no
GOT-addressing use (a GOT-addressing relocation or an `STT_GNU_IFUNC`
definition; see the relocation limits above). The traced links are every
`--shared` link, every link with the C runtime (so every default `trust-cg
-o <program>` link), every link with `-l` or `-Wl`, every link with a
positional input the reader cannot read, and every link with a local-exec
or GOT-addressing input. The unreadable-input group includes every
non-AArch64 Linux link (x86-64, RISC-V), plain executables included: such a
link is staged and traced, but no local-exec relocation is read from its
inputs. Until the `.eh_frame` check, a plain `-nostdlib` executable link
wrote its output directly. On Darwin only a link with a local-exec or
GOT-addressing input is staged. Only the remaining links (a Darwin link
without such inputs, and a link for another operating system) write the
output directly. The
consequences below apply to every staged link. A staged link does not move
its image onto an existing output that is neither a regular file nor a
symbolic link (a device, FIFO, socket or directory); it is refused
(`LinkError::OutputStaging`), so every staged link to `/dev/null` fails, and
a staged link needs a writable directory next to its output. (The CLI never reaches the
link for an existing FIFO output: its output-alias check opens the FIFO
first and blocks, whatever the link's inputs.) The arm64 Darwin
code-signature check still reads, and on refusal removes, the output path
itself. A staged link that is killed (for example
by SIGTERM) after the linker wrote its image can leave the
`.tcg-link-<pid>-...` directory, mode 0700, beside the output, holding an
unchecked image. Nothing installs that image, but nothing removes it either.
A staged link replaces a symlink at the output path with the image; it does
not write through the link. The host's GNU ld 2.42 and LLD 22.1.6 do the
same on an unstaged link, but a linker that wrote through the symlink would
have written its target.

AArch64 frame lowering probes the stack like LLVM's `probe-stack=inline-asm`:
static local areas move SP at most 4096 bytes between `str xzr, [sp]` probes
(a counted loop from five steps, 20 KiB, up), a residual above 1 KiB or before
a runtime allocation is probed, and runtime-sized allocations probe every
4096-byte step and their final SP. This defends guard regions of at least
4 KiB only if callers leave at most 1 KiB untouched above SP, as trust-cg
callers and callers built with LLVM inline probing (rustc's AArch64 default)
do; code built without stack-clash protection gives no such bound.
Deallocation is unprobed, and the invariant is tested (decode
emulation, Darwin guard-page and JIT execution), not proved. A static probe
loop needs the frame pointer, so an SP-based layout that would need one is
refused; shrink-wrapping and the O2/O3 fall-through layout pass (which refuses
conditional back edges) decline functions containing one. The Linux guard-page
control is registered but has not run on a Linux host; x86-64 and RISC-V
frames remain unprobed.

U10 prologue stack-limit checks
(design) are AArch64-only and opt-in
through reserved trust-ir function tags; x86-64, RISC-V and wasm32 refuse a
tagged module with `[TCG-STACK-LIMIT-REQUEST]` instead of dropping the
request. On AArch64 a request is refused (`[TCG-A64-STACK-LIMIT]`) on every
proof-required or verifying route (`StackLimitNotProofQualified`: the check's
instructions have no LIR source, so v1 credits nothing), with a runtime-sized
allocation, a hidden `sret` parameter, a convention other than C, Fast, Cold or
Rust, a limit parameter that does not arrive whole in one of X0-X7, and when a
check branch would need relaxation (text beyond the ±1 MiB `B.cond` range):
the net accepts only the exact `B.LO`. Shrink-wrapping is declined for a
requesting function. The `[TCG-A64-STACK-LIMIT]` net and its certificate are
per-compile structural validation over the final stream, never Exhaustive or
Formal credit; the check's 64-bit lemma is solver-backed only when the formal
proof lane's AY/Clean gate discharges it, and is otherwise tested (exhaustive
at 8 bits, sampled at 64). The module reserve bound R that every compile
reports is computed under assumptions no compiler can check: the declared
external allowance (default 0) for any call that leaves the module (runtime
imports, libc, the TLS resolver), Darwin's 128-byte red zone below a leaf's
SP, and signal handlers running on the thread stack; an indirect call counts
every emitted function, a superset of its possible targets. The `Pointee`
limit is loaded before any authentication the body performs, so the host must
keep `[x<k>+off]` readable on every entry, including thunk, indirect and host
entries. A consumer must read the per-function acknowledgment and treat a
tagged function without one as unchecked: a backend from before U10 drops the
unknown tag as a non-fatal proof diagnostic. Unlike this request, the LLVM
importer's stack-protector tags are not refused off AArch64: the x86-64 and
RISC-V pipelines compile such a function without a canary.

The final AArch64 stream passes a frame dataflow net (`[TCG-A64-SPILL-SLOT]`,
Enforce by default) that models framed functions, calls, probe loops and
landing pads, and checks spill store/reload pairing, reads of call-clobbered
registers and of caller callee-saved values, and the restoration of SP,
X19-X28, X29, D8-D15, the return address and uncorrupted return lanes at every
exit. A return lane is judged "clobbered in the epilogue" only when computed
after the teardown began in the exit block itself; code in a return block
shared with a frameless path (shrink-wrapping) is frameless by design. It is a
validation net over the emitted stream, not a proof of frame lowering, and
rests on stated assumptions: spill and callee-save cells are
never written through escaped pointers; a call writes only its outgoing
stack-argument bytes; spill traffic is identified by the
`SPILL_SLOT_ACCESS` flag that spill materialization stamps (unflagged loads
are not initialization-checked, since locals may be read partially
initialized). The final stream does not carry callee result arity, so X0-X7
and V0-V7 count as defined by every call: a return lane overwritten by an
intervening call's result register is not detected. A 128-bit (Q-view) read
of V8-V15 after a call that did not redefine it is rejected
(`call-clobbered-upper-half-read`). Any write, including a lane insert, counts
as defining the upper half. A swapped reload is detected only when its consumer
reads a register the call clobbered; two reloads exchanging destinations that
both hold defined values need the allocator's value identities. For the same
reason the stream carries no spill-slot identity: a reload must read exactly
the bytes one spill store wrote, so an offset shifted onto unwritten or
non-spill bytes, into a spill cell or across two cells is rejected, but a
reload shifted by whole slots onto another spill cell that same-width spill
stores wrote on every path is not (a unit test pins this gap). Flagged spill
accesses through an unresolved base (SP after a runtime allocation) and
oversize states decline with a counted reason. Spill materialization flags
only single-register `LDR`/`STR` accesses and never forms a pair spill. The
encoders refuse a flagged pair (`[TCG-A64-PAIR-SPILL]`) or other shape
(`[TCG-A64-SPILL-SHAPE]`) before the net would decline it. Any hand-built
stream passed to the public encoders must be ABI-valid (restore callee-saved
registers and the link register it clobbers).

Post-allocation value flow (`L10-P1`,
[`post_ra_value_flow`](crates/trust-cg-verify/src/post_ra_value_flow.rs),
`[TCG-A64-POST-RA-VALUE-FLOW]`) compares the function entering register
allocation with the final resolved stream: every effect (load, store, call,
atomic, barrier, trap carrier, return, tail call) in the same order on equal
values, every branch decided the same way, through spill materialization,
coalescing, rematerialization, the call-argument fixup, reload CSE, late
post-index formation, branch forwarding, copy lowering, frame lowering
(frame-index elimination, prologue/epilogue, shrink-wrapping, stack probes,
the stack protector, the ELF TLSDESC expansion and lo12 fusion), guard
expansion, branch layout, relaxation, loop-head padding and branch
resolution. It infers where each value lives (a register, a spill cell,
rematerialized, a pointer advanced in step with an induction variable) by
matching per-edge values at joins instead of reading the allocation map,
follows calls under AAPCS64/DarwinPCS (results in X0-X7/V0-V7,
X8-X18/X30/V16-V31/NZCV and the V8-V15 upper halves unknown, each register
its own unknown, a narrow argument judged at the width it was written, SP an
argument of every call so a callee finds its stack-passed arguments where
they were stored, every frame cell below the call's SP dropped), follows
exceptional edges to landing pads, refuses any write of X18, and checks that
every exit restores SP, X19-X29, the return address and the D8-D15 halves
(before frame lowering every exit reads SP as an argument). It is not on by
default: on the compile corpus under the dedicated scope it costs +5.4% to
+6.1% (AOT lanes) and +8.1% to +9.4% (JIT lanes) instructions retired over
the same scope without it, +20% to +23% on the ay kernels and up to 1.34x on
one small fixture (2026-10-13 with the review fixes: +5.7% to +5.8% AOT,
+8.3% to +8.9% JIT, at most 1.31x), so the default tier records the stages
as an uncovered run (its default-tier cost is within noise, and +5.8% on the
rustc bridge's proof-grade lane, which runs it), and it runs under the dedicated and all-passes scopes,
which every proof-grade publication (the rustc bridge's default route
included) and certified pass-execution pipeline enforce: a stage it does not
validate refuses the compile as `PassValidationFailed` naming
`post-ra-value-flow` (`TRUST_CG_POST_RA_VALUE_FLOW_STAGES=split` compares at
the allocation and frame boundaries separately to localize a failure). It is
translation validation under its model, not a proof of any pass: equal
normalized terms are its only acceptance; it interprets moves, constants,
zero extensions, add/subtract of an immediate, 64-bit register
add/subtract/shift-left as wrapping affine forms of at most eight atoms
(past that an add stays uninterpreted) and known-zero high bits,
compares a plain access at its effective address whatever its spelling
(immediate, pre/post-index, register offset with no extend or an LSL, the
`[Xn, #:lo12:sym]` form of the lo12 fusion), judges an expanded TLSDESC
sequence as the `TlsDescCall` it replaced (the resolver slot is assumed
constant once filled), and treats every other operation as uninterpreted;
program memory is not tracked (value flow through it is compared only as
matched loads and stores); FP operations are pure (FPCR/FPSR are not
threaded); every frame-storage access after frame lowering (spill,
callee-save, canary, probe and any other access frame lowering inserted) is
checked to lie below the CFA, off every program stack slot the function
names and off the outgoing stack-argument area, except a stack probe of the
current SP (`STR XZR, [SP]`, or a summarized probe loop), which may touch a
program slot or the outgoing area only where it writes wholly below every
byte an earlier write on any path may have touched (a write at a known CFA
offset touches that offset; a write the model cannot place, through an
unknown pointer, a call or another opaque effect, is assumed to reach no
lower than the 128-byte red zone below the SP it runs at, i.e. no pointer
into the stack below SP outlives its allocation); that a callee
writes nothing of its caller's spill or save cells is assumed (AAPCS64
stack discipline: it writes below the SP it is entered with, its incoming
argument area, which holds no storage, and memory passed to it); the
frame layout's slot offsets are taken as the specification of where each
slot lives, after checking that the slots the function names and every slot
register allocation created lie inside the slot area and do not overlap; the
stack-protector guard is
assumed constant; it shares the allocator's operand-role and the optimizer's
memory-effect tables. An induction relation is inferred only between one
implementation location and one specification location (`base + k·leaf` with
a constant `k` and a base valid at the join). It refuses by name, as
unmodeled, an LL/SC atomic expansion, a dynamic stack allocation, a
stack-limit check, a loop of inserted blocks other than a static probe loop,
an operand past a plain access's address and any other operand shape outside
its model. Where it runs, the frame net's whole-slot and swapped-reload gaps
above are closed: a reload is accepted only when the cell it reads holds the
value the specification uses there, so a reload from another spill slot
holding another value is refused (the default tier does not run it, so
there the gaps stand). An incomplete model is fail-closed: a correct compile
it cannot show equal is refused on a proof-grade route, never accepted.
`Pipeline::encode_and_emit` receives an already allocated function, so it
has no pre-allocation function to compare with and runs no comparison.
Evidence (2026-10-12, Apple M4 Max, `origin/main` `1359b3bca` merged): it
validated every one of the 13,702 AArch64 function compiles of the compile
corpus at both split stages and under the composed comparison, with no
emitted-byte change (the corpus identity check against `origin/main` passed
for all 534 entry and lane pairs in the default and the dedicated tier). Run
over the whole Darwin floor under the dedicated scope, it first left 11,119
of 207,616 comparisons unproved; the classes were model gaps, closed or
named since: the lo12 fusion (940, which also showed that a symbol offset
operand had been read as `#0`, a soundness gap: two accesses of different
symbols at one base compared equal), the TLSDESC expansion (2,646), late
post-index formation (52), a resolved self-loop behind an empty block (1),
and the named LL/SC (6,566) and dynamic-allocation (910) refusals; four were
the four functions existing tests deliberately corrupt (a canary
overwritten), correctly refused. A second run with those fixes validated
200,134 of 207,643; the rest were the named LL/SC (6,566) and
dynamic-allocation (910) refusals, the four corrupted canaries, a TLSDESC
call compiled for Mach-O (which the backend refuses) refuted as a write of
X18, and 28 comparisons of generated loop kernels (a post-indexed pointer
reaching the latch through a join inside the loop, a branch to an empty
anchor), fixed since: those kernels now validate all 843 of their
comparisons. The final run, on the head with `origin/main` `7c60cee46`
merged, validated 203,072 of 210,553 comparisons; every other one is a named
LL/SC (6,566) or dynamic-allocation (910) refusal, one of the four corrupted
canaries, or the Mach-O TLSDESC call. No miscompile was found.
`e2e_aarch64_post_ra_value_flow` validates ten native kernels (calls in
loops, 40-value pressure, a jump table, stack-passed arguments, FP calls, a
local array, a 32 KiB probed frame, a protected array, a 32-bit array sum
late post-index formation strength-reduces, the pressure loop beside a live
stack array) whose 40 builds match a C reference, its fifteen
corruption-control tests refuse planted corruptions of their real stage
inputs (five of them in the composed comparison the pipeline runs as well as
the split stage), and three wiring tests pin the refusal by name of an
unmodeled function under a refusing policy, its unproved record under the
diagnostic one and the default tier's uncovered record. Review of the first
version found four acceptances, now refused with tests: SP moved between a
call's stack-argument stores and the call (natively, the callee read its
stack arguments 16 bytes low, or ran on a misaligned SP), a spill slot moved
consistently by eight onto a live program stack slot (natively, wrong
results for every even input), a compare of two caller-saved registers after
a call decided "equal" (all clobbered registers shared one unknown), and a
spill cell below SP surviving a call. With those fixes the compile corpus
still validates all 13,702 compiles at both split stages and composed
(2026-10-13, Identity PASS on all 534 pairs against the same binary with the
comparison off, dedicated and default tier), and the whole Darwin floor under
the dedicated scope validated 203,106 of 210,589 comparisons: the rest are
the named LL/SC (6,566) and dynamic-allocation (912) refusals, the Mach-O
TLSDESC call refuted as a write of X18, and the four functions a test
deliberately corrupts (a program store over the canary slot), now refused by
the private-storage check. This is a bounded differential and corpus result,
not coverage of every function the backend accepts.

Q-register (128-bit) spills use 16-byte, 16-byte-aligned slots and flagged
single `STR`/`LDR Q` accesses. On the Apple M4 Max host,
`e2e_aarch64_vector_spills` ran four programs at O0-O3 against C models. They
keep 40 vectors live, 28 vectors and 28 scalars live, 12 vectors live across
a call, and 56 vectors live in a dynamic frame, where far FP-relative Q slots
are legalized through X16. The frame net models every stream and checks every
Q reload. The file's corruption controls reject by name a deleted Q spill
store, a Q reload shifted by half a slot, onto the frame record or below the
frame, a Q reload into the wrong register, and a Q value kept in V8 across
the call. A Q reload moved by one whole slot onto another Q cell passes the
net, as the gap above states; on the leaf program, native execution against
the C model catches it. This is native differential and structural evidence,
not a proof of register allocation or spill placement. The Linux GNU arm of
the file has not run.

The allocation validator compares the allocator's physical-register
reservations with an independently recomputed AArch64 physical liveness; the
interference check itself still consumes the allocator's reservation map. The
AArch64 tied/implicit-operand audit behind the parked slot-liveness model is
not complete, and composed native O0-O3 controls combining spills,
callee-saved GPR/FPR pairs, multi-result calls and indirect callbacks under
pressure are not in the Linux or Darwin floors.

Switch and indirect-call lowering have native controls at O0-O3 on the Linux
floor (L04-P11): a 64-function selector-width and strategy matrix against a
C `switch` oracle, with each function's jump-table, binary-search or linear
strategy read back from its code words, and function-pointer tables,
switch/call interplay, stack and mixed-class arguments and values live
across calls into callees that overwrite X1-X17, V0-V7 and V16-V31 (not
X18 or the caller-saved upper halves of V8-V15). The
two new tests have not run on a Darwin host. Their proof side is thin: the
jump-table obligations cover only the ADR base and the scaled `LDRSW`
address. The table entry contents and the `ADD`/`BR` target binding have no
instruction obligations (BR is covered-elsewhere), and while the bounds
check's `CMP` and `B.HI` bind `cmp` and `condbr` obligations, nothing links
the compared bound to the table's size, so a wrong entry or bound is caught
only by the final
layout cross-check against the recorded CFG, by `switch_proofs`' model of
representative tables and by execution.

Native AArch64 link-and-run controls share one host helper,
`crates/trust-cg-codegen/tests/common/native_host.rs`, across AArch64 macOS
(Mach-O) and AArch64 Linux GNU (ELF); `scripts/native_test_host_matrix.py`
prints each target's static host support. The Linux arms added on 2026-09-18
for formerly macOS-only families (atomics, EH, coroutine, i128, FP,
vector/NEON, relocation and miscompile pins) have not yet executed on a
Linux host, and neither has the i128/u128 switch and checked-multiply
boundary control (`e2e_aarch64_i128_switch`) added on 2026-09-21. The four
f16 arms (`e2e_aarch64_f16_scalar`, `e2e_aarch64_f16_fcvt`,
`e2e_aarch64_f16_to_i128`, `e2e_aarch64_i128_to_f16`) did execute on the
Linux floor host on 2026-09-23, and `e2e_aarch64_f16_abi_linux` executes
scalar `f16` and one- to four-member `f16` HFA arguments and returns, in
registers and on the stack, in both directions against GCC's `_Float16` at
O0-O3 with bit-exact NaN payloads, plus decoded H-register and stack
placement against an independent AAPCS64 model. Its native rows are Linux
GNU only: DarwinPCS packs HFA members on the stack at their natural size
(LLVM puts the `f16` after a stack HFA3 at offset 6, and the `f32` after an
`f32` HFA3 at offset 12), while the Darwin classifier rounds every stack HFA
to 8 bytes, so a Darwin call that passes an `f16` or `f32` HFA whose size is
not a multiple of 8 on the stack, followed by another stack argument,
disagrees with clang. That Darwin divergence is unrepaired and has no native
Darwin control. `scripts/check_darwin_aarch64.py` requires the macOS arms with
per-target minimum passes; only four Linux-only targets (the AAPCS64 variadic
and aligned-aggregate stack corpora, ELF linking and host-derived target
authority) are reported compiled out on Darwin.
LSE, FP16 and DotProd families execute on Linux GNU only through an explicit
ISA profile — the pipeline's, or the production compiler's recorded
`CompilerConfig::aarch64_isa_profile` (CLI `--aarch64-isa-features`): generic
Linux AOT without one still refuses LSE and FP16 data processing by name and
emits no UDOT. `f16` transport (H-register loads and stores, full-register
copies, `FCVT` to and from `f32`/`f64`, and the `f16`/HFA calling convention)
is base AArch64 and compiles without the profile.
Nothing checks that the CPU which runs an explicit-profile object implements
the named features. The native stack-canary control in `stack_guard_admission`, the
in-crate Mach-O linker, Swift and Apple variadic ABIs stay macOS-only (Linux
ELF canaries are covered by `e2e_aarch64_link_runtime`); ELF linking/TLS
initial-exec and the generic AAPCS64 variadic, stack-slot and narrow-argument
fixtures stay Linux-only.

AArch64 Mach-O AOT exception metadata covers catch-all, cleanup and typed
catches. trust-ir's `Inst::LandingPad` carries catch type indices only, so
the compiler binds index `k` to entry `k` of the module's reserved
`__trust_cg_eh_type_table` global (an immutable array of zero-addend
`SymbolAddr` typeinfo symbols, or its trust-ir v50 `splat` when every entry
names one typeinfo, which stays one symbol and a length); a typed catch
without that binding, an index the table does not bind, or a malformed table
is refused by name (`[TCG-EH-TTYPE]`). A catch-all's slot `N + 1` must be an
`i32` action filter, so a function that catches all beside a typed catch
against a table of `2^31 - 1` or more entries is refused by name; its LSDA
image is `4 (N + 1)` bytes of type table (the unreferenced slots are one
zero run, not per-slot records). LSDA type tables use identity slots (slot `k` is catch
type index `k`), and each bound slot is an `ARM64_RELOC_POINTER_TO_GOT`
entry that ld64 and the standalone linker bind through the GOT. Typed
catches are bound only under `__gxx_personality_v0`, whose selector is the
matched catch type index; a catch-all match delivers `N + 1` for the
module's `N`-entry table in a function that catches a typed exception and
`1` in one that does not. `N` is fixed by the trust-ir input at lowering,
so it does not change with the pads the optimizer prunes or with the
optimization level. `rust_eh_personality` ignores the type table (it enters
a pad for any positive first action and delivers selector `0`), so a typed
catch in a function that unwinds under it, through `Producer::TRust` or a
module that declares that routine, is refused by name (`[TCG-EH-TTYPE]`).
A module may mix `__gxx_personality_v0` and
`rust_eh_personality` (a function stamped `Producer::TRust` takes the Rust
personality; every other function takes the module default): each
compact-unwind entry binds its own routine and the DWARF fallback emits one
zPLR CIE per personality. The compiler's reserved `RUST_EH_EMPTY_FILTER`
clause represents an empty exception filter under `rust_eh_personality`:
it stops phase-one search at a non-unwinding boundary and is skipped during
forced unwinding. It must be the sole clause of a non-cleanup pad; the
adapter and emitter validate that restriction. Its LSDA action -1 binds to
an explicit empty list, independently checked by the ELF relocation reader.
General exception-specification lists and unbound negative actions remain
refused by name (`[TCG-EH-FILTER]`); the AArch64 ELF emitter refuses typed catches
and mixed personalities by name (no `.gcc_except_table` typeinfo slot, one
shared CIE); mixed-personality DWARF-fallback frames unwind natively on
this host through their own CIEs (execution evidence at O0-O3, not a proof
of the CFI or LSDA); and the standalone linker loads no
`__LD,__compact_unwind`, so no CG landing pad is reachable through a
standalone-linked image at run time.

`e2e_aarch64_eh_raii_darwin` runs a mixed-codegen exception/RAII matrix on
the Darwin host (ledger `X-DARWIN-P7`). C++ throws, handlers and destructors,
and Rust panics and drops, cross CG frames built from trust-ir
invoke/landing-pad/resume. Each frame comes as a compact-unwind twin and a
runtime-sized twin, which trust-cg's conservative compact-unwind policy
sends to the DWARF fallback. The CG pads run cleanups, catch-all and typed
handlers and rethrows. A touch family repeats the Linux 768-case campaign's
frame on its 64 inputs (64-bit edges included) and three throw stages. It
stores to an imported memory word, and a direct and an indirect
(function-pointer slot) provider call may throw, with all three memory words
checked. The C++ object runs linked into executables and into a CG dylib that
imports its helpers and typeinfo from a separate C++ dylib. Each case must
equal a C++-only or Rust-only reference build of the same matrix (632 chain
cases, 1,152 touch cases and 184 Rust cases per build) and the test's models.
That is 15,008 cases AOT at O0–O3 (with the linked `__unwind_info` read back)
and 7,232 through the unchecked JIT at O0–O3. Mutated-frame negative controls
change exactly the cases they reach. Limits:

- The JIT refuses the four typed chains by name, so 160 cases per level run
  AOT only.
- trust-ir has no indirect invoke, so no CG landing pad covers an indirect
  call site.
- The rustc bridge is not exercised.
- A new exception thrown out of a cleanup while another is in flight is not
  exercised; C++ reaches that state only through `std::terminate`.
- This is execution evidence, not a proof of the tables, the personality
  routines or the unwinder.

AArch64 AOT exception handling on Linux GNU emits a `zPLR` CIE whose
personality is read through a weak `DW.ref.<personality>` slot, an LSDA per
EH function and a no-handler filler LSDA per plain function of an EH module.
`e2e_aarch64_eh_linux` links such objects with libstdc++/libgcc_s, and with
Rust std through a Rust harness built by the installed Trust package's
`trustc` (unverified lane), then
runs catch-all, cleanup-then-resume, nested and unwind-through shapes at
O0–O3 against an exact stage, payload and destructor model. GNU readelf,
llvm-dwarfdump and llvm-objdump read the tables back, and a dropped or
retargeted LSDA row for an invoke makes the run terminate or take the normal
path. An invoke that follows another call of its trust-ir block moves into a
block of its own, where the earlier call keeps a no-handler row: an exception
from it passes the frame's pad at O0–O3, and moving or copying the landing
pad onto its row is caught by the native mutants. Limits: catch-all and
cleanup pads only (typed catches, filters and mixed personalities are
refused), one personality per module, and a protected block that holds a
second call which only instruction selection introduces is still refused by
name ("exactly one is required by block-granular metadata"): i128
`udiv`/`sdiv`/`urem`/`srem` (`__udivti3`, `__divti3`, `__umodti3`,
`__modti3`) and an uninlined `Memcpy`/`Memmove`/`Memset` (an aggregate
copy). Calls the adapter emits split (trust-ir calls, `frem`, i128 <->
f32/f64 casts, heap allocation and free, ARC operations). On x86-64,
`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` refuses every EH module by name, so the split is
unreachable there; `x86_64-apple-darwin` compiles and reads back the split
shape at O0–O3 (verifier evidence) but has not run it. The rustc bridge's Linux twin,
`unwind_cleanup_linux`, runs a real Rust panic through bridge-lowered frames
whose cleanup pads free `Box`es and run user `Drop`s, at O0–O3, compiled
without proof certificates; that original fixture keeps its LLVM catcher.
The separate GNU/Linux AArch64 qualification
now lowers the actual core `catch_unwind` intrinsic with typed callbacks,
its bool result and real exception-pointer transfer. Its 24 scalar, four
foreign-exception and 24 helper-identity comparisons all execute both LLVM
and CG guests. Other bridge targets remain refused; indirect `TypeId`
caller-buffer returns still refuse with `TCG-SRET-ABI`. These are native
execution and tool-readback results, with certificates off; TB-12 and the
LSDA/personality proof boundary remain open.

The AArch64 in-memory JIT publishes functions carrying invoke/landing-pad
metadata, and the plain frames of a `panic_unwind` module, with in-memory
unwind tables: an FDE per function, each EH function's LSDA (plain frames of
an EH module get a no-handler filler LSDA) and a personality indirection slot
appended after the code. Every pointer field is bound through the explicit
relocation list in `ExecutableBuffer::unwind_tables()`. Before mapping, the
unrelocated section round-trips through the ENC-EHDC decoder and an
independent decoder re-reads the relocated pointers, each LSDA's call-site
coverage and each frame-pointer prologue's words, then runs each FDE's CFA
program and requires its final rules to match the saves and frame-pointer
placement decoded from those prologue words alone. Frames that save D8-D15
are refused (`JitUnwindFrameShapeUnsupported`) as a policy, not a decoder
limit: the shared CFI generator (`DwarfFde::from_layout`) describes them
with `DW_CFA_offset_extended` (DWARF 72-79) and the independent decoder
agrees with the prologue, but no native control has yet restored an
FP/SIMD callee-saved pair across a JIT landing pad. After
the read-execute seal the tables are registered (`__register_frame` per FDE
with Darwin libunwind, once per section with Linux libgcc), every FDE is read
back with `_Unwind_Find_FDE`, and deregistration precedes the unmap under the
RefCounted and ProcessLifetime teardown policies. Limits: one personality
per module and catch-all and cleanup pads only (typed catches and mixed
personalities, which Mach-O AOT emission supports, are refused here by name:
`JitUnwindTypedCatchUnsupported`, `JitUnwindMultiplePersonalities`;
exception-specification filters have no trust-ir surface), and only the
unchecked JIT.
AlwaysVerify, CachedVerified, `emit_proofs` and relocation-replay requests
refuse EH and panic-unwind publication by name
(`JitUnwindProofEvidenceUnavailable`), because the tables and their
registration carry no proof obligation. Profile hooks and the raw
`JitCompiler::compile_raw` API also refuse EH. Serialized republication
(`publish_serialized_buffer_for_target`) carries code bytes only, and the
jit-matrix TCJ1 cache refuses buffers with unwind tables. The native controls
in `jit_exception_handling` run on Darwin and, as a required Linux floor
target, on the Linux host (11/11 in
`reports/perf/2026-09-23-linux-eh-landing-pads`). On Darwin,
`e2e_aarch64_eh_raii_darwin` also publishes the untyped chains of its
exception/RAII matrix (cleanup, catch-all, rethrow and nested frames, fixed
and runtime-sized), its touch family (an imported memory word bound through
a GOT slot and two data-image pointer slots, one of them the function pointer
an indirect call throws through) and a Rust-personality module. It runs
6,496 C++ and 736 Rust cases through them at O0–O3 against the reference
builds.

The Apple Silicon JIT maps every publication with `MAP_JIT`. A process signed
with the hardened runtime (`codesign --options runtime`) receives that mapping
only when its signature carries `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit`
(`jit::ALLOW_JIT_ENTITLEMENT`) set to true; embedders that ship a hardened JIT
host must sign it with that entitlement. Without it the kernel refuses the
`mmap` (`EINVAL` on macOS 26.6) and the JIT returns
`JitError::MapJitRefused` with the process's `csops` code-signing flags and a
message naming the entitlement; it does not fall back to non-`MAP_JIT` memory.
`jit_map_jit_entitlement` re-signs copies of its own test binary and observes
the typed refusal (process exit 0) without the entitlement or with it false,
and successful publication and execution with it and without the hardened
runtime. The classification treats `EINVAL`/`EPERM` from a nonzero-length
`MAP_JIT` request as the policy refusal because the JIT's other `mmap`
arguments are fixed; entitlements themselves are not read back at run time.
Only this host and macOS release were measured.

JIT publication is write-xor-execute. `ExecutableBuffer::request_page_protection`
grants only read+execute and refuses writable requests with typed errors. The
AArch64 cache-maintenance walk uses CTR_EL0's minimum line sizes on Linux.
Darwin traps EL0 CTR_EL0 reads, so there it uses the recorded 16-byte
architectural minimum (`jit_cache_line_geometry`). The republication rows of
`jit_icache_coherence` still pass with instruction-cache invalidation removed,
on Apple M4 and on the Linux AArch64 host, because each republication gets
fresh pages. On Linux the same target has two in-place rows. They rewrite a
test-owned page through `jit::flush_instruction_cache`, which is the
publisher's walk. Both fail in every retained run when the `ic ivau` walk is
removed or its stride is doubled. They cannot detect a missing `dc cvau` walk
on that host, whose CTR_EL0.IDC is 1, and they are positive-only on a host
whose CTR_EL0.DIC is 1. A kernel that reports DIC 0 on coherent hardware, or
maintains pages on every execute-permission change, makes them fail their
non-vacuity check. These rows pin what the walk does, not that publication
calls it: removing the publisher's call to the walk (in
`MappedRegion::seal_rx_and_verify`) passes every execution row on Linux,
because the kernel maintains the fresh pages publication maps. A host-neutral
structural row detects that removal instead. It reads the per-thread walk
record (`jit::instruction_cache_walks_on_current_thread`) around each
publication and requires a completed walk that starts at the image and
covers it. The record shows the call, not its cache effect or its order
relative to the read-execute seal. On Darwin only the same-page library
control detects the removal of the invalidation walk itself, and no Darwin
run of these targets is retained.
Buffers enforce `RefCounted` or `ProcessLifetime` teardown. Under
`RefCounted`, a mapping with in-flight `JitExecutionLease`s is retired and
unmapped when the last lease is released. Raw pointers taken without a lease
remain the caller's lifetime responsibility. Installed payload bindings (v6)
and executable manifests (v3) bind page-protection and allocation state and a
page-protection witness. Lookup rejects a payload republished under different
protections. On Linux the witness is the kernel's permission string for the
whole allocation, read through `/proc/self/maps` right after the read-execute
seal and paired with the permissions the recorded protection implies
(`r-xp`). Three installed routes observe the kernel again before touching the
bytes: `get_contract_symbol_bound`,
`native_install_gate_packet(_for_surface)` and `into_installed_artifact`.
They refuse by name a writable-and-executable observation
(`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-WX]`), any other difference from the recorded
permissions (`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-MISMATCH]`), a range the kernel does not
cover (`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-UNCOVERED]`), and an unreadable or malformed
answer (`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-UNREADABLE]`). Other lookups are not
re-checked: `InstalledArtifact::entrypoint`, `entrypoint_ptr` and
`ensure_published_entrypoint_ptr` (and the Petri handoff through
`entrypoint_ptr`), raw `ExecutableBuffer` lookups, and raw pointers. A
Linux host without `/proc` therefore cannot install compile-service
executables; raw `ExecutableBuffer` publication still succeeds and records
the failed observation. No observation shows the whole process at one
instant. The `PROCMAP_QUERY` ioctl (Linux 6.11 and later, used first) returns
one self-consistent VMA per call, so a range inside one VMA, as a published
allocation is, is one kernel answer; a range spanning several VMAs is several
successive answers. The text fallback is assembled chunk by chunk with the mm
lock dropped between chunks, so while other threads change mappings one read
can list a VMA twice, list rows out of order, or combine states that never
held together. The reader retries the whole file up to 16 times when rows at
or after the range overlap or go backwards or the range is not covered,
tolerates disorder wholly below the range, and refuses by name after the last
attempt; malformed rows are refused at once. An accepted text read shows
ordered rows covering the range, each true at some moment during the read.
A `jit_wx_refusal` churn row (eight threads mapping, protecting, unmapping
and allocating) found no spurious refusal on the Linux AArch64 host with
either reader; that is execution evidence on one kernel, not a bound on the
retry's failure rate. A protection changed and restored between two observations, or changed after
one, is not detected. The witness covers the code allocation, not the
separate read-write data image. macOS and Windows bind an explicit
recorded-only source, so their lookup still compares only the publisher's
recorded state; a binding whose source differs from its target's is refused
(`[TCG-JIT-PAGE-WITNESS-SOURCE]`). Thread and
execution-lease context is not bound. Only AArch64 Linux has run the kernel
witness; the x86-64 Linux and Darwin arms are compiled from the same source
but have not run. The W^X, coherence, cross-thread and teardown floor targets
passed on the Linux AArch64 host in the 2026-09-23 floor run.

The in-memory AArch64 JIT places a module's data globals in a JIT-owned
read-write data image mapped beside the code (never `MAP_JIT`, never
executable). `GlobalAddr` bodies address it through the same `ADRP`/`ADD`
pair the object path relocates, patched at the final addresses; imports,
dyld-coalescable definitions and address-taken externals load from JIT GOT
slots appended after the veneers; pointer slots inside the image are
relocated; and the image manifest (placements, initial bytes, relocation
list, imports) is bound into each function's certificate-cache identity, the
buffer's live replay identity and its replay metadata. This is unchecked
execution evidence: no obligation models the data image, so a verifying or
proof-required JIT request refuses every data or GOT site by name. Immutable
globals share the writable mapping (there is no read-only JIT placement), a
body naming a thread-local, an explicit-section global or a weak import is
refused, the image is bounded to 1 GiB, and a data mapping the kernel places
outside `ADRP` reach of the code fails closed rather than being patched.
The image rows run natively on macOS (`e2e_aarch64_globals_darwin`) and on
Linux GNU (`e2e_aarch64_globals_linux`); the out-of-reach refusal is a unit
test, not forced in either native run.

Ordinary AArch64 compilation uses canonical shift-zero MOVZ/MOVN seeds plus
MOVK halfword repairs for wide constants. Registry form checks cover the
MOVN forms' whole 16-bit immediate domain; MOVK splice forms are sampled
evaluator evidence, and the W-form obligation uses the 32-bit view. These
checks grant no per-instruction credit. The source-bound constant owner
above independently replays a single MOVZ/MOVN against its actual Iconst,
but refuses multiword expansions, including their initial seed. MOVK
sequences still need a source-bound sequence theorem.

Register copies (MOV, the typed post-allocation copies `MOVWrr`/`MOVXrr`,
scalar FMOV between FP registers or between W/X and S/D registers, and the
`ORR Vd.16B, Vn.16B, Vn.16B` copy of an H, S, D or Q value), SMULL,
bitfield-insert BFM, scalar RBIT, `ADD #imm12, LSL #12` and `MRS TPIDR_EL0`
have decoded-word obligations: an
independent Arm ARM decode of the encoder's word whose effect on the whole
destination register is compared with what the instruction names. Since E0.2
none of them is credit for an emitted instruction: the function verifier
reaches a form's registered obligation through a name query, so under the
per-instruction credit rule above the row is reported as unverified and
never discharged for the instruction, and a function containing one of these
opcodes blocks `--emit-proofs` and proof-required JIT promotion. In its
default enforce mode ENC-5 runs that check on every emitted word of these
opcodes (`TCG_DECODE_CHECK_A64=off|warn` or `TCG_NO_DECODE_CHECK=1` remove it):
exactly (bit routing) for the copies, RBIT, BFM and MRS, and for SMULL and the
shifted ADD as an instance of a form whose value obligation is sampled
evaluator evidence, not formal proof. The function verifier binds every
instance of these opcodes to its form's registered obligation, except that
since L07-P2 a GPR copy between hardware registers is judged by its
instruction-derived obligation instead (below); since L04-P11
that includes the copies, which it used to promote as covered-elsewhere
whatever their operands and whether or not ENC-5 ran, and `MOVWrr`/`MOVXrr`,
which the coverage gate had excluded as never selected although post-RA copy
lowering emits them. The zero-source copies of a zero-sized aggregate
argument (`MOVXrr Xn, XZR`) and the FEAT_FP16 `FMOV Wd, Hn`/`FMOV Hd, Wn` bind
their own forms. A copy whose operands name no form (a copy to SP or to a
zero register, an X<->H, half-precision or cross-width FMOV, an FMOV naming
the zero register, an 8B `ORR` copy) stays unverified, is refused by its
exact shape and blocks proof-required promotion; ENC-5 still decides such
words. The NEON bitwise operations (AND, ORR of two registers, EOR, BIC,
NOT) bind their lanewise obligation only in the 16B shape (Q registers, no
selector), and ENC-5 decodes that shape's word and checks its arrangement,
operation and registers. Their 8B shapes (V64 vector operations, `Q = 0`)
bind nothing, since the 16B obligation does not state the zeroed upper half;
the function verifier refuses them by shape, so an instruction of that shape
cannot be promoted (in L04-P11's review probes the V64 functions were
already refused for their `StpPreIndex`/`LdpPostIndex` frame pair, so no
whole-compile verdict changed). A form's obligation is an identity over the transcription of
its canonical captured word, which AY discharges and a certificate records:
for `MOVXrr`, `x7 == 0 | (x7 << 0)`; for the zero-source forms an input-free
constant identity; for the vector copy `v7 == v7 | v7` per 64-bit half. The
certificate holds neither the word nor its decode. Only ENC-5 checks each
instruction's own word, and no certificate records the word, the form or
ENC-5's verdict. With or without the AY solver, a bound copy is not
credited: its form obligation is not discharged for the instruction. x86-64 `MovRI` is still exempted per
instruction and its ENC-3 check is not forced on proof-grade routes; since
X-OPCODES-P13 its covered-elsewhere certificate is positive only in a compile
whose ENC-3 ran in enforce mode, and is a blocking `covered_elsewhere_withheld`
row otherwise (see "Covered-elsewhere rows that cite a decode check" below). The form obligation covers the encoding, not the lowering's choice of
registers, widths or immediates, nor whether a W-class source's upper half is
defined when an X-width copy reads it. That TPIDR_EL0 holds the thread pointer
is ELF TLS ABI trust base, and half-precision FMOV words assume FEAT_FP16. A
native differential samples the transcribed semantics on the host CPU; it is
not a proof and covers one core model per run.

Instruction-derived obligations (ledger `L07-P2`) replace the registry name
lookup for admitted shapes of 47 AArch64 opcodes: MOVZ/MovI/MOVN/MOVK, the GPR
copies (MOV, `MOVWrr`, `MOVXrr`), ADD/SUB immediate, CMP (immediate and
register), ADD/SUB with an LSL or LSR shifted register, EOR with a ROR, UMULH,
B/BL/TailCall/B.cond, and scalar general-purpose memory: LDR/STR/LDRB/STRB/
LDRH/STRH and the sign-extending LDRSB/LDRSH with an immediate offset, W/X
LDR/STR with pre-index or post-index writeback, and LDR/STR/LDRB/LDRH/STRB/
STRH/LDRSW with a register offset (UXTW, LSL, SXTW or SXTX, scaled or not)
(`aarch64_instruction_word_proofs`). A verify-side
encoder re-derives the instruction's word from its operands, an independent
decoder gives that word its Arm ARM semantics over the X registers, SP, NZCV,
the PC and the accessed bytes, and both sides must write the same locations
with equal values. In ENC-5's default enforce mode a compile fails when an
admitted instruction's emitted word differs from the re-derived word outside
its fixup holes; under `TCG_DECODE_CHECK_A64=warn|off` the two are not bound.
The obligation is never credit. It binds the word to the machine-IR operands,
not to a source instruction, so a lowering that chose the wrong constant,
register, condition or target encodes and decodes perfectly; and nothing in the
backend discharges it with an independently checked certificate. For a bound
scalar memory row, a holding obligation is the in-process refutation check of
the Formal-only bound-memory rule (`bound_memory_authority`, owner ruling
2026-09-29). That rule credits the row only through a replayed certificate of
the form theorem of the word this obligation judged, and only on a host whose
checker the manifest qualifies. FP (`H`/`S`/`D`/`Q`) scalar memory rows,
which this lane does not model, are judged instead by their word-bound
memory-effect decomposition (below), every part decided exactly in process
(L04-P1). A holding row
is reported unverified (`INSTRUCTION_DERIVED_IS_NOT_CREDIT`) and blocks
proof-required promotion; a refutation fails the row. Its decisions are
in-process: term identity or exact bit routing for most rows, sampling (100,000
samples) for compare flags and for the address of a register-offset access
whose index is scaled (a shift on the operand side, Arm's `ExtendReg` on the
word side), and complete enumeration of NZCV for branch conditions stated
differently on the two sides. Sampling alone accepted a
`CMP` whose immediate was off by one, so a search of boundary points built from
the terms' constants runs first. On the Darwin census corpus the class holds
32,685 rows (30,488 exact, 2,192 sampled, 5 exhaustive). None refutes, but
that is by construction: the function verifier decodes the word re-derived from
the operands (proof promotion runs before the object is encoded), so there a
refutation can come only from an inconsistency inside the module. The emitted
words are bound by ENC-5: with certificates off and ENC-5 enforcing, all
21 census units compile and all 21 binaries exit with their reference codes,
which is testing evidence over one corpus, not proof.
By hand, outside the backend, Trust package 9192's AY with managed Clean 8606
checked only the 14 of 21 probe obligations whose two sides are the same term;
Clean rejected AY's proofs of 6 whose sides differ (MOVN, `MOVXrr`, MOV from SP,
both compare-flag obligations, a B.cond condition) as holey, and AY answered
`unknown` on a MOVK. So no probe obligation with differing sides has a checked
certificate on this host. A stock-Rust build of trust-cg-verify admits no AY
(`[TCG-AY-IDENTITY-UNRECORDED]`). No such certificate is credited, for the
reason above. The obligation does not cover what a fixup or relocation writes
into a branch displacement, memory contents, alignment or ordering, or a
callee. Relocation-bound ADRP, `ADD :lo12:`, GOT loads and ADR, FP-register
memory, literal loads, NEON, CSEL/CSINC, TST, UXTB and UBFM, and the
unadmitted shapes of the listed opcodes (among them a writeback whose base is
its transfer register, and a W index under a 64-bit extend) still reach the
registry refusal
(census).

Word-bound memory-effect obligations (ledger `L07-P2`, `X-OPCODES-P1`,
`L04-P7`, `L04-P1`; `aarch64_memory_effect`) are a second refutation check on
every scalar LDR/STR row above (since L04-P1 also the `H`/`S`/`D`/`Q`,
sign-extending, pre/post-index writeback and register-offset forms, whose
words come from the form binder and, for `H`/`S`/`D`/`Q`, from a verify-side
scalar encoder the independent decoder inverts) and on the LDP/STP rows
(signed offset, pre- and post-index; W, X, S, D, Q). For an `H`/`S`/`D`/`Q`
scalar row it is the only in-process check, and so the Formal-only rule's
clause-2 evidence; its holding is never credit by itself. In the ordinary opcode lane,
credit for those rows comes only from the owner's Formal-only bound-memory rule (2026-09-29,
`bound_memory_authority`). The rule needs three things: the row's own
concrete-word or instruction-derived check held; a certificate of the row's
form theorem is committed; and that certificate replays under the vendored
`drat-trim`, on a host whose `drat-trim` bytes the bound-memory manifest
authorizes. The September 29 Darwin measurement used an unauthorized
`drat-trim`, so those rows and its host-qualification test
`bound_memory_set_binds_the_exact_runtime_checker_bytes` failed there. This
is dated evidence; candidate28's Linux identity control passes. The
source-bound frame-envelope branch precedes the ordinary opcode lane; its save
and restore records are decomposed too, on the source-bound route below. In
the ordinary lane the decomposition runs after the rule. It states each row as small
obligations over the word literal: fields, each lane's address, the
writeback, and each lane's bytes as little-endian positions with zero or sign
extension. No part has an array, shift, multiplication or `zero_extend`, and
ENC-5 requires the emitted word to be that literal. Every symbolic part is
decided exactly in process, as a linear address form, an exact bit routing or
(a register-offset address whose word extends and shifts the index as the
mode does) the same term once the word's fields are folded; a register-offset
address that folds to a different term refutes only at an evaluated witness.
`aarch64_scalar_memory_silicon_differential` runs every scalar form's word
(364 words, 8,976 executions) on this CPU against the parts' machine terms
(testing evidence). A refuted part fails the row, credited or
not. A credited row stays credited. An uncredited row keeps its reason and
gains `MEMORY_EFFECT_IS_NOT_CREDIT`, with how many parts have a Clean-checked
certificate. For such an unbound row a checked part is recorded, never
credited: it is not the evidence the rule admits (OD-39 in
`docs/decision-record.md`). Neither the parts nor the form theorems bind the
operands to a source instruction, so a lowering that saves the wrong register
pair or loads the wrong slot is certified exactly as well, except on the
source-bound route below. The live AY/Clean replay of the parts is off unless
the diagnostic `memory-effect-replay` knob is given. In that September 29
Darwin measurement the Trust package's AY (9192) gets a checked certificate for none of the 488 corpus
parts (each is holey or self-check-rejected), and the package's Clean is built
without `carcara-verify`. The development AY `2657db47c` with the aterm Clean
8606, or with the development Clean `ed21fee39`, checks all 488. The added
check costs 0.4% to 1.4% more instructions retired in the certificates-on
lane. Stated and not discharged here: little-endian data, no alignment fault
(the frame lowering's 16-byte SP), no concurrent writer between a pair's
lanes, and Normal memory. Not covered: register-offset, scalar pre- and
post-index, and sign-extending scalar forms; the upper 64 bits of a V register
that an S/D pair load writes; permissions; ordering; and fixups
(report).

`SUBS #imm` (ledger `L04-P1`, `aarch64_subs_imm_proofs`). The looped
stack probe's counter decrement `SUBS X16, X16, #1` (frames of five or more
4 KiB pages) is the one emitted `SubsRI`. For both widths, every location the
word re-derived from the operands writes is stated against the comparison the
operands name: the destination (a W write clears bits 63:32; register 31 is
the zero register, register 31 as source is SP) and N, Z, C and V from Arm's
`AddWithCarry(Rn, NOT(imm), 1)` with its sums one bit wider than the operands,
against the difference, its sign, its zero test, `Rn >=u imm` and the signed
overflow of subtracting a non-negative immediate. Each of the five locations
is decided exactly in process by the bit-serial automaton; ADDS, SUB, width,
`LSL #12`, off-by-one, register, borrow-carry, signed-carry, no-overflow,
minuend-sign and inverted-Z controls refute (96). ENC-5 requires the emitted
word to be the re-derived one, and `aarch64_subs_imm_silicon_differential`
reads NZCV with `MRS` after 50 words (13,000 executions) on this Apple M4.
Testing-grade evidence: the coverage gate counts the row as accepted
regression evidence and the function verifier reports a holding `SUBS #imm`
unverified. Not claimed: that the probe loop runs the intended count or
touches every guard page, or that nothing clobbers NZCV before its `B.NE`.

Trap carriers and their expansions (ledger `L04-P12`;
`aarch64_trap_expansion`). The five conditional carriers (`TrapNullIfZero`,
`TrapDivZeroIfZero`, `TrapBoundsCheckExact`, `TrapShiftRangeIfOOB`,
`TrapOverflowExact`) are no longer skipped by the function verifier. Each is
judged by an obligation stating that the words of its expansion (the compare
or flag-setting word, `MOVZ`/`MOVK` for a wide bound, `MUL`/`SMULH`/`UMULH`/`ASR`
for a 64-bit multiplication, the conditional branch that must skip exactly the
trap, and `BRK #1`) reach the `BRK` exactly when the carrier's source condition
holds: a null pointer, a zero divisor, `index >=u bound`, `amount >=u
bitwidth`, or the tagged add/sub/mul overflowing at the tagged width. Before
register allocation the obligation is over the expansion the verifier states
for the carrier (over role registers); after it, over the instructions the
expansion recorded in `MachFunction::trap_expansions`, which must still be
contiguous before their `BRK` and, for a flag-setting expansion, leave NZCV
dead; and per compile ENC-5 binds the words in the object to it (a tampered,
partial or non-contiguous expansion, or a recorded carrier outside the model,
fails the compile in `enforce` mode). The
words are decoded and given Arm ARM semantics in `trust-cg-verify`, not by the
backend's decoder, and the obligation is decided exactly in process: every
form but the 64-bit multiplications by a bit-serial automaton over every input,
those two by sound rewriting to identical terms; a refutation fails the row
with a counterexample. That is testing-grade evidence, not a certificate.
Holding decisions are memoised per process by register-renamed form, so the
per-compile cost is one decision per distinct form (about 85 M instructions
retired in a debug build on the Darwin host; a review timed about 2 ms in
release) plus about 0.47 M instructions per further expansion of a decided
form. A
holding conditional row is credited only under an enforced source-bound
replay policy, when its register-renamed obligation, replayed through the
verification request exactly as a source-bound owner is (the request's
admitted AY and explicit Clean checker, its captured policy, the source-bound
budget, the refusals under an armed tier-0 recorder or
`TCG_REFINE_SOLVER=0`, and reuse only under the request's identity), gets a
Clean-checked proof; answers are memoised per verification walk, never across
requests. Otherwise it is uncredited (`TRAP_EXPANSION_IS_NOT_CREDIT`), so a
proof-required compile with a kept guard refuses on the `BRK` row where the
tools cannot certify (before L04-P12 the `CBZ`/`CBNZ` forms were promotable on
a skipped `BRK`). On the Darwin host the development AY `2657db47c` with Clean
`ed21fee39` certifies 29 of the 31 conditional forms of the battery; the 64-bit
signed multiplication times out and the unsigned one gets a holey certificate.
The AY of Trust package 9192 (build 9624) with the managed Clean 8606
certifies none (29 holey certificates, two timeouts at a 30 s budget). The unconditional traps (`Brk` and the five
bare `Trap*` pseudos) are judged as their single `BRK #imm16` word; whether
one may stay skipped is decided by the trap-guard layer below. A carrier outside the
model (a malformed operand list, an undecodable overflow tag, a 32-bit
multiplication, an immediate bound outside `[0, i32::MAX]`, mixed index and
bound widths) is refused by name. Not established by this obligation: that
instruction selection chose the right guard, operand, bound or tag for the
source operation (the trap-guard layer binds the carrier's kind, constants
and operand widths to its stamped source guard, not its registers to source
values), the process-level effect of
`BRK` (the native target observes SIGTRAP with ESR EC `0x3C`, ISS 1 on this
host), or agreement with silicon beyond those executions
(report).

The trap-guard layer (`aarch64_trap_guard`; ledger `L04-P12`, rulings
LD-36 to LD-39 in the decision record) only
refuses or fails trap rows, never credits one. It binds each recorded
expansion's carrier to the source guard its TV-1 stamp names (kind, bound,
bit width, overflow tag, operand widths: only an `I32` in a W register and
an `I64` in an X register bind), requires the window to execute (in the
emitted layout, on a block reached along the recorded edges, not dead code),
checks with its own window model that the window traps exactly when the
carrier's condition holds and that NZCV and X16/X17 are dead after it, and
refuses every unconditional `BRK` outside an established role: the U10
stack-limit trap alone in the overflow block of a check the stack-limit net
certifies, the unreachable word after a call to `_Unwind_Resume` or
`__stack_chk_fail`, and a source `Trap` that closes the entry block. A
source `Trap` reached through branches, and an `Assert`'s trap block, are
refused, because the polarity of the branches into them is not checked here.
Per function, a recorded expansion absent from every block fails it, and,
with the replayed LIR, a source guard, `Assert` or `Trap` that no executing
trap row implementing it accounts for refuses it (a source trap a pass
removed under evidence this verifier does not check is refused too; only a
`GuardDivZero` on a constant nonzero at its width is exempt). A window that
holds, executes and binds keeps the trap-expansion verdict above. Not
established: where a holding window sits relative to the operation its
guard protects, or that its registers hold the source values
(report).

Source-bound memory rows (ledger `L07-P2`, `X-OPCODES-P1`;
`aarch64_memory_source_binding`, 2026-10-01) are a second formal credit route
for two shapes only. A frame record, the `STP X29, X30, [SP, #-16]!` save or
the `LDP X29, X30, [SP], #16` restore of a source-bound leaf frame, is bound
to the frame theorem's record: its operands must name exactly the theorem's
slot, registers, width and writeback. A scalar `LDR`/`STR{,B,H}` immediate of
a frameless straight-line leaf is bound by the memory-leaf checker
(`source_bound_memory_leaf`). That checker interprets the LIR source and the
allocated body independently as linear forms and requires both to perform the
same access trace in lock step: pointer, offset, width, zero extension, stored
value, then the returned value. Such a row is `Formal` only when its owner's
evidence holds (the replayed frame theorem, or the complete leaf check), no
part is refuted or undecided in process, and every memory-effect part's exact
query has an AY proof that the accepted Clean fully verified. The replay is
the one the frame and ALU owners take; each receipt carries the SHA-256 of the
query it judged, so a stale or foreign certificate is refused. A frame record
now needs the frame theorem and its parts. A row the Formal-only rule credits
keeps that credit; there the binding adds a claim, not a verdict. The
authority is the identity-admitted AY and the selected Clean. An overlay
toolchain qualifies because `build.rs` pins its AY digest, the build accepts
only the overlay's pinned Clean, and the compile's proof evidence names both
digests and the manifest. With Trust package 9192 no part is certified (its AY
answers holey `unsat` or `unknown`, its Clean lacks `carcara-verify`), so every
bound row stays refused, by name. With AY `2657db47c` and Clean `ed21fee39` as
an overlay, every part of the 30 bound accesses of the native leaf set (15 at
each of O0 and O3) checks, and, with the form certificates disabled so that
this route is the only one, the verifying JIT publishes and runs the eight
copy-free leaves. With the form certificates on (the default), those leaves
already publish on this host through their form theorems, bound to no
source. Not covered:
callee-saved pairs and the FP/LR pair of any larger frame (no source-bound
frame contract owns them); scalar accesses in a function with a call, branch,
frame, spill, or a register-offset, writeback or sign-extending access; and
the `--emit-proofs` sidecar of a credited leaf access, which is refused by
name (a framed function's formal sidecar carries the frame theorem and the
twelve frame-record parts, each replayed under the sidecar's admitted AY and
fully checked). The memory-leaf checker never rejects a function: a lock-step
trace cannot tell a reordering from a miscompile, so a disagreement only
withholds the binding. Whether Clean-checked parts may credit a source-bound
memory row was left open by the September 29 record, and OD-39 refuses them
for an unbound row; OD-139 (`docs/decision-record.md`, 2026-10-06) takes it:
this route admits them only with the binding, as every source-bound owner
already does
(report).
Because every framed source-bound leaf now needs its twelve frame-record parts
on every host, a proof-tool pair that discharges the frame query but not the
parts refuses every such leaf. No Linux pair has been measured on these parts,
so the Linux floor's source-bound JIT targets (`jit_fail_closed_proof_policy`,
`jit_source_bound_arithmetic`, `jit_cert_cache_identity_aarch64`) are not yet
re-run on a Linux host under this rule (custody
record).

The local-exec TLS adds (`ADD Xd, Xn, #:tprel_hi12:S, LSL #12` and
`ADD Xd, Xn, #:tprel_lo12_nc:S`) are not credited. The registered TLSLE
obligations are relocation-arithmetic identities over TP, S and A that name
no register, word or relocation site, so the coverage gate counts both as
