deferred rows and the function verifier refuses every instance, so neither
instruction can be promoted. Since L10-P6 ENC-5 decodes their words (class,
shift, registers, the zero imm12 placeholder and the recorded GlobalRef
hole); that is emission redundancy, not an obligation for the instruction. In L04-P11's
review probes the local-exec functions were already refused for their
`StpPreIndex`/`LdpPostIndex` frame pair, so no whole-compile verdict changed.
The object relocation inventory still verifies the two TLSLE relocation rows
through the ELF reparse binding, which says nothing about the instructions.

ENC-5 does not decode every emitted AArch64 word. It runs on every emitted
instruction, but an opcode it has no arm for falls to its catch-all allowlist
(`a64-slice1: format family not yet decoded`), which checks nothing about the
word. Since L10-P6 no row the coverage gate credits is in that position:
0 of the 267 credited rows (credited by the gate's inventory rule, which since
E0.2 is not instruction credit), 0 opcode-wide (an instruction with no
operands names at most a registry theorem found by name, which is refused;
before E0.2 88 were) and 0 per instruction (before L10-P6, 104 rows the
verifier binds per instruction had no arm). With no opcode-wide credit left,
0 of the opcode-wide rows rest on a degenerate X==X obligation.
12 of the 302 emitted rows have no arm. (The 302 are the gate's emittable
class; scalar ADDP is in it although no lowering selects it yet, see the NEON
paragraph.) The emitted rows without an arm are
the 12 opaque LL/SC carriers, which have no single-word encoding: `LlscRmw8`,
`LlscRmw16`, `LlscRmw32`, `LlscRmw64`,
`LlscCmpSwap8`, `LlscCmpSwap16`, `LlscCmpSwap32`, `LlscCmpSwap64`,
`LlscLoad128`, `LlscStore128`, `LlscRmw128` and `LlscCmpSwap128`. The post-RA
expansion replaces each with its exclusive loop, whose words ENC-5 decodes,
and the encoder refuses a survivor by name (before L10-P6, 167 emitted rows
had no arm, and FRINTN, a deferred value row, was one until its FP
data-processing arm landed). The five conditional trap carriers, which joined
the emitted rows in L04-P12, have an arm that refuses any word recorded for
them: only their compare/branch/`BRK` expansion is emitted, each word decoded
against its own intent and the expansion bound as a unit to the carrier's
trap condition. `coverage_gate_tests::credited_aarch64_rows_without_an_enc5_arm_are_pinned_and_disclosed`
derives these lists from the code, pins them and requires this paragraph to
name exactly those opcodes, list by list. ENC-5's own coverage is testing
evidence about the encoder, not a proof, and the x86-64 ENC-3 check likewise
allowlists families it does not decode.

ENC-5's arms also allowlist some shapes without decoding their word: besides
the catch-all, the AArch64 arms return 28 named reasons (the same test pins
them). Most name an operand of a kind the arm does not model (a non-register or
non-immediate operand) or a branch whose target is not yet resolved; one names
the SMULL, RBIT and MRS shapes outside the decoded value model (for example an
MRS key it does not model), which the function verifier refuses; one names an
FCMP of vector (Q) registers; and two name register-register
ADD/SUB/AND/ORR/EOR with an operand after the three registers, which the
encoder drops and the function verifier refuses (no emission site produces
them). The test checks that the three-register shape is decoded and the
four-operand one refused. The immediate-shift arm, which allowlisted a missing
or register shift amount, now reports a mismatch, and the encoder refuses such
an instruction. Since L10-P6 the NEON bitwise 8B shapes, the scalar
FMOV/half-precision FCVT shapes outside the decoded value model and the
half-precision FCMP (`FCMP Hn, Hm`, which an F16 `fcmp` lowers to) no longer
reach a named exit: ENC-5's FP/SIMD slice decodes them. Whether any other credited
shape can reach a named arm exit is not inventoried, but the census below
measures which do on the Darwin floor, and a proof-grade route refuses every
one.

Since L10-P6 ENC-5 decodes every scalar floating-point and Advanced SIMD form
the machine IR names in its H/S/D (or vector) register banks
(`aarch64::decode_check_fp_simd`: FP data-processing with one, two and three
sources including FCVT, FP compare of half-precision registers (the S/D
compare keeps its flag-consumer decoder), FP immediate, FP/integer conversion
and FMOV; SIMD three same, three same (extra), three different,
two-register miscellaneous, across lanes, scalar pairwise, vector by element,
copy, scalar copy, modified immediate, shift by immediate, extract and the
LD1/ST1 one-register post-index form) and the general-purpose, PC-relative,
LSE atomic, ordered load/store, barrier, BRK and NOP forms that fell to its
catch-all (`aarch64::decode_check_int`), plus the typed MOVZ, STR, BL, BLR
and Bcc aliases and LDR (literal). Of the 325 opcodes then, 127 had an arm
before and 302 after; FRINTN, the 326th (added for the rustc bridge's `frintn`
inline assembly), has one as well, and since L04-P12 so do the five exact
guard carriers (an arm that refuses their word, since only their expansion is
emitted), so 316 of the 334 opcodes the inventory now lists do
(`aarch64_enc5_floor_census` pins the list), and no emission site
produces a word for the 18 without one: the
encoder refuses the 12 opaque LL/SC carriers and `TlsDescCall` (and the five
guard carriers); lowering removes or rewrites `Phi`, `StackAlloc` and `Copy`
before encoding; and nothing in the backend emits `Retain` or `Release`. The
encoder would spell any of those last five as NOP if one reached it (a
defensive fallback), and that word falls to ENC-5's catch-all: counted on a
compatibility route, refused on a proof-grade one. Each check reads the word
by one Arm ARM encoding class, requires every bit outside the class's fields
to hold its fixed value and compares
every field with the intent, so every single-bit corruption of a matching word
is a mismatch. The exceptions are fields a relocation or the final layout owns:
a relocated word must carry its GlobalRef hole and a zero placeholder, a
jump-table ADR keeps the offset the final-layout cross-check and the switch
binding re-derive, and a branch-holed TBZ/TBNZ keeps its offset for the branch
fixup. The operand conventions they read (operand order, arrangement,
element-size and width selectors, the machine IR's scalar views of a bitwise
vector copy, and which operand selects a general-purpose width) are the
machine IR's, shared with the encoder; the field layouts are written from the
Arm ARM, not from the encoder. A W or X view names one general-purpose
register, so the integer slice takes a word's width from its width-selecting
operand (the destination of a data-processing form, Rt of an LSE atomic, Rs
of CAS, the tested register of TBZ) or from the opcode (UMULL, SMULH, UMULH,
ADR/ADRP, the GOT/TLV loads, LDRSW, LDR (literal), the typed GPR stores) and
compares every other data register by number in either view, as ENC-5's
original arms and the encoder do. Register allocation does produce such mixes:
`AND Xd, Wn, #1` for a Trunc of an I32, I16, U32 or U16 to `Bool` (a 64-bit
class) and UMULL with 64-bit source views from the masked-UMULL fusion.
Address bases must be the X or SP view, and TST's two registers one width,
because the original memory arms and the encoder respectively require it.
Scalar FP operands are held to one H/S/D width per instruction, as the
original FCMP and FCSEL arms were: the encoder reads the FP width from operand
0 and accepts 204 mixed-width shapes the census target builds (for example
`FADD Hd, Hn, Sm`), and ENC-5 reports every one as a mismatch, a hard compile
error on every route. The floor corpus below produces no mixed FP view (its
floor passes with that mismatch in force); that is measured on that corpus,
not shown for every lowering. The need was measured: the Darwin floor run with `TCG_DECODE_CHECK_CENSUS_DIR` set records
each encoded function's ENC-5 outcomes, and `scripts/enc5_floor_census.py`
reduces them into
`crates/trust-cg-codegen/tests/aarch64_enc5_floor_census/darwin_floor.tsv`.
On this host (2026-09-27; the 259 floor targets in 235 processes, of which
the six known Darwin reds and `core_jit_planning`, whose Core admission
refuses the census variable, did not pass) the floor emitted 227 opcodes in
5,012,423 checked words before L10-P6 (`darwin_floor_before_l10p6.tsv`,
source 8a772301a): 114 of those opcodes, 53 of them among the 67 scalar
FP/Advanced SIMD opcodes emitted, had undecoded words, 435,921 words in all
(113 opcodes to the catch-all, the NEON 8B EOR to a named exit), including 19
of the 297 words of proof-grade compiles. After (`darwin_floor.tsv`, source
cde4e85c7) the same 227 opcodes emit 5,012,456 words and none is undecoded.
`aarch64_enc5_floor_census` pins the emitted and
still-undecoded lists, replays every committed real sample, corrupts every bit
of each FP/SIMD and integer-slice sample, and checks 221 clang-assembled words.
It runs the live encoder over the shapes it enumerates, not over every operand
list the encoder accepts: 1,774 same-view shapes (1,584 encoded; every
arrangement, element size and lane selector, and each integer form in both
widths) and all 772 W/X view assignments over the data registers of the
integer-slice forms it lists (764 encoded, 411 of them mixing views, each with
every single-bit corruption a mismatch). It also compiles Trunc to `Bool` from
I32, I16, U32 and U16, the masked-UMULL product, the 12 F16 `fcmp`
predicates and the f32 and f64 `trust-cg-aarch64-fp` `frintn` lowerings from
TrustIR on both the compatibility and the proof-grade route, and runs the
proof-grade refusal. The census speaks for the floor corpus only: that corpus
truncates only U64 to `Bool`, emits no masked-UMULL product, no F16 compare
and no FRINTN (only the rustc bridge's inline-assembly recognizer produces
that dialect operation, and the bridge is not a floor target), so "none is
undecoded" there did not show that those lowerings decode; the TrustIR
compiles above do, for those shapes. The census
cannot see the Core compiler routes: Core admission refuses the census
variable as an unkeyed compiler control, as it refuses every `TCG_*` variable
that is not transport or keyed identity.

On proof-grade routes (proof-required and verifying compiles and JITs, and
the Core compiler) a word ENC-5 does not decode (an `Allowlisted` outcome, the
catch-all or a named arm exit) is now a refusal, tagged
`[TCG-DECODE-CHECK-UNDECODED]`, naming the instruction, its offset and the
reason; compatibility routes still count it. The Darwin floor passing with the
refusal on is the evidence that the proof-grade routes it exercises emit only
decoded words (the census records proof-grade compiles emitting ADD with a
shifted register, ADR, ADRP, BRK, LDR from the GOT and LDRSW, all decoded
since L10-P6). None of this is a proof: agreement between two independently
written artifacts is redundancy, and neither the decoder nor the census is
bound to a formal ISA model.

The AArch64 encoder does not check arity. For 117 opcodes the function verifier
binds a shape (from a fixed operand-shape pool) whose last operand, other than
`#0`, leaves the encoded word unchanged: the encoder does not read it. Some
such operands are redundant rather than ignored (a selector the register class
already implies), and for most of the rest ENC-5 does not read the operand
either, so the word still matches the other operands. It is an open gap:
nothing refuses an instruction whose extra operand was meant to change its
meaning, and a general arity check in the encoder is not done. Since L10-P6
the forms ENC-5's FP/SIMD and integer slices decode are checked at their exact
operand count, so on those opcodes an extra operand is a decode-check
mismatch; that is a per-compile guard, not an encoder arity check.
`coverage_gate_tests::credited_aarch64_shapes_with_an_ignored_trailing_operand_are_pinned_and_disclosed`
derives the list from the code, pins it and requires this paragraph to name
exactly those opcodes: `AddRI`, `SubRI`, `MulRR`, `Msub`, `Umull`, `SDiv`,
`UDiv`, `Madd`, `Smulh`, `Umulh`, `Adc`, `Sbc`, `EorRRShift`, `AddRRShift`,
`SubRRShift`, `AddRRShiftLsr`, `LdrLiteral`, `STRWui`, `STRXui`, `STRSui`,
`STRDui`, `LdrswRO`, `Adr`, `Adrp`, `AddPCRel`, `LdrGot`, `LdrTlvp`, `B`,
`BCond`, `Bcc`, `Bl`, `BL`, `TailCall`, `Sxtb`, `Sxth`, `Sxtw`, `Uxtb`, `Uxth`,
`Uxtw`, `FaddRR`, `FsubRR`, `FmulRR`, `FdivRR`, `FmaddRR`, `FnegRR`, `FabsRR`,
`FsqrtRR`, `FmaxnmRR`, `FminnmRR`, `FcvtSD`, `FcvtDS`, `Ldar`, `Ldarb`,
`Ldarh`, `Stlr`, `Stlrb`, `Stlrh`, `Cas`, `Casa`, `Casal`, `Casl`, `Ldadd`,
`Ldadda`, `Ldaddal`, `Ldaddl`, `Ldclr`, `Ldclra`, `Ldclral`, `Ldclrl`, `Ldeor`,
`Ldeora`, `Ldeoral`, `Ldeorl`, `Ldset`, `Ldseta`, `Ldsetal`, `Ldsetl`,
`NeonAddV`, `NeonSubV`, `NeonMulV`, `NeonOrrV`, `NeonCmeqV`, `NeonCmgeV`,
`NeonCmgtV`, `NeonCmhiV`, `NeonCmhsV`, `NeonFaddV`, `NeonFsubV`, `NeonFmulV`,
`NeonFdivV`, `NeonFmlaV`, `NeonFmlsV`, `NeonUcvtfV`, `NeonScvtfV`,
`NeonDupScalarD`, `NeonFmlaLaneV`, `NeonFcvtlV`, `NeonFcvtl2V`, `NeonFcmgtV`,
`NeonSmaxV`, `NeonSminV`, `NeonUmaxV`, `NeonUminV`, `NeonDupGen`,
`NeonDupElem`, `NeonInsGen`, `NeonUmovGen`, `NeonMovi`, `NeonRbitV`,
`NeonRev32V`, `NeonRev64V`, `NeonCntV`, `NeonBitV`, `NeonUdotV`, `NeonExtV`,
`NeonLd1Post`, `NeonSt1Post`. The register ALU forms with an extra operand,
ADDS and SUBS with one, NEG with one and the immediate shifts with a register
amount left the list when the function verifier began refusing those shapes and
the encoder began refusing a non-immediate shift amount (L04-P11's fourth and
fifth reviews).

Two more latent encoder shapes are open (the L04-P11 round-6 verifier; no
emission site produces either). An absent required operand is still encoded
as 0: `BCond []`/`Bcc []` encode `b.eq .` and are credited, `Adr [X0]`/`Adrp
[X0]` encode offset 0 and are credited, and absent `Ubfm`/`Sbfm`/`Bfm` imms,
`Tbz` bit, `Dsb` option (encoding SSBB) and `Mrs` register encode 0 without
credit. And out-of-range immediates are masked: the branch condition (`& 0xF`),
the barrier option and the `Mrs` system register are masked by the encoder and
by ENC-5 alike, so ENC-5 cannot tell, and the verifier's conditional-branch
binding does not read the condition at all.

CSEL, CSINC and CSNEG are credited per instruction only through their REACHING
flag producer (`aarch64_flag_consumer_proofs`). The verifier walks back inside
the block to the first NZCV writer (calls, opaque pseudos, control flow,
implicit NZCV definitions and the block start refuse) and binds the select only
when that producer is a well-formed CMP, TST or S/D FCMP whose kind, width and
the select's own operation, width and condition name one of 384 registered
obligations: the independently decoded captured select word, executed over the
producer's modeled NZCV, equals the TrustIR `select` of the producer's
comparison predicate with the CSINC `+ 1` / CSNEG negation and W zeroing. A
select after ADDS/SUBS or any other producer, after a producer in a
predecessor block, or with AL/NV, a ZR destination or a condition with no
predicate after its producer (for example MI after CMP) stays unverified and
blocks promotion. The evidence is sampled evaluation plus a deterministic
boundary battery and refuted controls, not a formal proof; the AY/Clean strict
gate on the development Mac certifies none of these rows (incomplete
certificates, and `incomplete self-check-rejected` for FCMP-fed rows), so a
proof-required build still refuses them. It is machine-level:
it does not certify that the select's arms, condition or producer operands are
the ones the SOURCE program names (a wrong choice is a correct instance of
another form), nor if-conversion CFG preservation. AL/NV complement-dependent

The four half-precision conversions (`FCVT Sd|Dd, Hn`, `FCVT Hd, Sn|Dn`) are
credited through the same lane: the Arm ARM `FPConvert` transcription of the
captured word is compared bit for bit with an independently written IEEE 754
`convertFormat` intent, exhaustively over all 65,536 binary16 inputs for the
widening forms and, for the rounded forms, on a structured battery of ties,
near-ties, overflow, underflow and NaN payloads followed by sampling — testing
evidence, not proof, and not formally discharged (the checker lacks
floating-point syntax). Both sides assume the default FPCR (round to nearest
even, no flush-to-zero, no default NaN, IEEE rather than alternative half
precision); nothing proves the FPCR value at run time, and FPSR exception
flags are outside the model. A native control compares CG-compiled
conversions with the hardware FCVT instruction on the host; its Linux arm has
not yet executed.

The `CSET` alias has a decoded-word value obligation of its own, one per
(destination width, condition) form, fourteen conditions at each of the two
widths. It is a DISCLOSED obligation with no promotion authority: nothing in the
verifier walk cites it, and a `CSET` the source-bound NZCV-consumer bindings
decline stays UNCOVERED. Its machine side is the Arm ARM effect of an independent decode of the
conditional-select word the encoder emits — a decoder that knows nothing of the
alias and reports the raw variant bits, both source registers and the raw
condition field — and its intent side takes the predicate from the per-mnemonic
condition table. The two halves are therefore computed differently, and the
alias's condition inversion, its two zero registers and its increment are all
load-bearing: an emitted CSEL, CSINV or CSNEG in its place, a source register
other than ZR, a dropped inversion, a different condition or a different
destination each refute. The only free input is the four-bit packed NZCV, so
every form is decided exhaustively over all sixteen architectural flag states;
that is a complete in-process evaluator decision, not a kernel-checked
certificate and not a silicon differential. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: which
flag producer reaches the instruction, which source operation its lowering
completes, or that the condition is the right one for that operation. Those
remain the business of the in-block NZCV-consumer binding and its
whole-sequence theorems — which is precisely why this row is NOT wired as a
fallback arm underneath them. A row that satisfies two of the three
requirements the codebase's own `CSet` refusal names, and is silent on the
third, would promote a partial claim as if it were the whole one: the only
populations it could reach are the `CSET`s whose reaching producer or whose
condition is unattested, and the checked-MUL idioms whose `NE` means "the high
half of the product is nonzero" — a fact about WHICH register the `CMP`
compares, which a decoded-word row cannot see and whose whole-chain theorem
(`CheckedUmul_I64`) is SMT capacity-bound and does not discharge.
The in-block binding is itself a citation, not credit: the whole-sequence
theorem it names is a registry row selected by name, so a `CSET` it binds is
reported as unverified like every other name-query hit (see the per-instruction
credit rule under "Correctness and proof scope"), and the binding decides only
which theorem that refusal names.
The obligation is width-INSENSITIVE by architecture — both widths write 0 or 1
with `Xd[63:32]` clear — so the width is refused structurally here and its
independent per-compile guard is ENC-5's `cset sf` field check. The row
adds no opcode-level coverage-gate credit for `CSet` (`opcode_to_proof_query`
still returns none for it): there is no opcode-WIDE evidence, because an
opcode-keyed claim would name neither a condition nor a width.

CSEL, CSINC and CSNEG have no validated per-instruction source binding and
must block proof promotion; another verified instruction cannot supply their
missing evidence through a structural exemption. The only structural
exemptions are for bodies with no value-semantics row at all (the x86-64 empty
and call-only bodies, below). The independent decoded-word
conditional-select model and native W/X controls do not restore those proofs
or establish if-conversion CFG preservation. AL/NV complement-dependent
optimizations now decline because both conditions are architecturally true;
plain conditional selects and non-inverting forms remain available.

The separate immutable source checker now covers flat integer selects whose
conditions are exact modeled integer predicates and whose two arms are affine
values. It compares the retained TrustIR, LIR and actual raw machine operands;
its final-byte route decodes CSEL/CSINC/CSINV/CSNEG and reaching CMP flags.
It admits canonical Boolean CMP-against-zero transport and preserves width,
operand order and false-arm arithmetic. Nested selects, arithmetic/comparisons
of selected values, and general CFG if-conversion remain outside that bounded
domain (the frameless whole-body owner, `source_bound_a64_body`, states them
in its own replayed theorem; see the Correctness section). The sealed Core compiler applies the final-byte check after its actual
encoder and rejects matching affine functions with pending fixups. Mismatches
after optimization, allocation or frame lowering now fail this bounded check.
In the same domain the sealed Core, the verifying JIT and `--emit-proofs`
objects also require the function's composed transition record (L09-P3; see
the Correctness section), which names every intermediate transition instead
of comparing only the two ends.
This conditional whole-stream check has no new instruction-proof,
certificate-publication or JIT-cache authority; other source domains still
require their own complete semantics and proof evidence.

The AArch64 verifier can discharge the exact sixteen-byte FP/LR envelope of a
pure affine leaf after checking its complete LIR and machine body. In addition
to single blocks, this includes acyclic chains of at most sixteen unconditional
blocks without block arguments. Resolved branch offsets and layout fallthrough
are checked independently of the source graph and cross-checked with machine
CFG metadata. A four-block source diamond with pure constant/copy/wrapping
add/subtract arms and one integer
join return is also supported. Its branch-local values are independently
renamed and checked against the actual machine predicate and both complete
execution paths. B.cond uses reaching comparison flags; CBZ/CBNZ use the
checked register value. Empty-arm elimination and layout fallthrough preserve
the same checks. Nested conditions, loops, general block arguments and effects
in either arm remain outside this frame-binding domain. Frameless bodies with
nested conditions, general block arguments and multi-block acyclic CFGs belong
to the whole-body owner `source_bound_a64_body` instead; loops and effects
stay outside both. Branch fusion clears
retired comparisons from the instruction arena after transferring provenance.
Outside the admitted raw comparison body's live return slice, the actual
reaching CMP width and CSET condition still identify an
integer-comparison theorem (the same shared producer walk, restricted to the
scalar-body instructions, also names the FCMP -> CSET obligation for an FCMP
producer, which the integer affine domain never admits). That theorem is a
registry row selected by name rather than an obligation instantiated from the
bound instruction, so the CSET is reported as unverified and the refusal names
the theorem. An unbound CSET or an FP comparison consumer was never authorized.
The raw comparison owner instead retains an instantiated source/result query
for live CMP/CSET/copy dependencies, with exact owner-selected category custody
through attachment and export. It requires independent frame and body replay.
Its October 5 Mac controls retain the installed-tool positive proof failure;
the added owner supplies no new successfully qualified comparison publication.
The same complete-body owner can bind 32/64-bit ADD/SUB register and immediate
forms (including shifted ADD immediates) and immediate LSL. Each actual typed
instruction still requires its own independently replayed arithmetic theorem.
Optimized doubling is checked against the original source; its source stamp's
coordinates and digest remain mandatory even when its opcode class changes.
Raw target-only reconstruction reports its statistical evidence, which is not
credited.
The independent final-byte interpreter also models LSL's UBFM encoding and
rejects other bitfield forms and reserved width combinations. Required Linux
tests cover four signed/unsigned types, ten arithmetic shapes, O0–O3, actual
published bytes, wrapping edge cases, and changed-source/tool/cache controls.
Arithmetic AOT sidecars retain the verifier's exact immutable obligation after
source/body, proof and provenance checks. Export validates its report metadata,
distinguishes complete queries rather than display names, and independently
replays every included theorem. All 48 ADD/SUB/doubling type/optimization cases
export and execute correctly; missing payloads and changed authority refuse.
These unsigned sidecars identify input and object bytes but do not replace the
complete source-to-byte composition or an independent consumer check.
On Linux the maintained runner also compares each certified function's words
and its FDE `pc_begin` in the `cc`-linked executable with the object. That is
the runner's own byte comparison of one function and its unwind entry, not a
certificate over the linked image, its other code or its dynamic relocations;
this runner does not check Mach-O linked images (the separate linked-image
evidence record replays a Mach-O image against its objects, without
composing that replay with these certificates).
This bounded leaf support does not establish the checker implementation's
refinement or authorize calls, general memory effects, or whole-system builds.
On Apple arm64 an ordinary compile gives a trivial leaf a zero-byte frameless
layout (Mach-O permits a red zone), which leaves the frame owner no envelope.
A proof-required or verifying compile therefore has no red zone and takes the
zero-storage leaf policy of the ELF lane (`Pipeline::run_frame_lowering`),
including its owner-applicability choice, so these leaves keep the envelope
and their frame and ADD/SUB/LSL rows bind as they do on ELF. Until 2026-09-29
the proof-required host JIT on macOS refused every such leaf on sampled or
vacuous evidence, and Mach-O objects kept statistical ADD/SUB evidence that
strict promotion refuses. Measured on macOS over `0756ded44` under default
checker discovery (which tries the owning Trust toolchain's `clean` first):
`jit_fail_closed_proof_policy` passes 7 of 9 tests (4 of 9 with the red-zone
line reverted and the tests kept), and the `jit_source_bound_arithmetic` matrix
compiles and executes 78 of 160 combinations (0 reverted). Every refusal left
in both names only a register copy or a `MOVZ`/`MOVN` constant, the rows E0.2
left without a credit route (see the source-bound envelope item above). On
2026-09-18 the managed AY 0.13.0 and the Trust bundle's AY 0.26.0 did not prove
the leaf-frame query, and the managed Clean 0.9.0 rejected the proof of the AY
revision the Linux installation used. With that AY (`2657db47c`) and Clean tree
`ed2a80d1` selected as development overrides, ELF-target frame and arithmetic
export passed on macOS
(2026-09-18 Darwin AY development build).
On 2026-09-29 the two JIT targets pin that outcome
(record):
the matrix requires exactly its 82 copy/constant refusals and executes the 78
other combinations (11,232 calls), the O0 ADD tests require the O0 refusal on
its copy alone and publish at O1, and each names the AY and Clean it
resolved when a proof is missing. Built from an overlay of pack 9192 with AY
`2657db47c` and Clean `ed21fee39` (the only admission route for a non-pack
AY), they pass 9 of 9 and 2 of 2 from an empty proof cache. With pack 9192's
own tools they still fail on the checker, not the code: its AY answers
`(:reason-unknown (incomplete self-check-rejected))` on the frame query (its
strict proof check rejects a hole-rule step), its `clean` lacks
`carcara-verify`, and managed Clean 0.9.0 rejects the overlay AY's proof at a
`poly_simp` step.
On 2026-10-03 the LIR-bound constant owner changes the same unchanged
160-row matrix on Linux AArch64 to 108 publications and 52 exact copy
refusals, with 15,552 native calls. Sixty emitted constant byte mutations
are refused by the independent source-to-final-byte check. These results
do not requalify native Darwin execution; ELF and Mach-O constant objects
are checked separately for serial/parallel equality. See the
constant-credit report.
The subsequent OD-35 C owner brings this same Linux corpus to 160 publications,
zero refusals and 23,040 native calls. It builds independent raw source and
machine return terms over ABI inputs, including W-write zero extension and
the actual allocated register routes. AY and independent Clean replay one
source/result theorem; only register copies in the return's backward slice
receive it, and export retains the exact `A64Body` query. Unused scalar
register-formal copies are removed before allocation while retaining ABI
liveness metadata. This owner admits unconditional I32/I64 chains, at most
eight register parameters, one return and 4,096 term nodes. It refuses identity
sources, uninitialized reads and unsupported operations, including MOVK,
predicates, diamonds, general memory and calls. Source/frame/control binding,
term construction and the return-slice computation remain trusted Rust
witnesses, not implementation-refinement proofs.
The production ENC-5 gate rejects all 124 emitted constant mutations, including
44 dead constants that the return-value checker correctly leaves unconstrained;
the independent source-to-final-byte checker rejects the other 80. Both checks
reject 78 live-copy route mutations. ELF and Mach-O body exports are compared
under serial and parallel compilation; Darwin native execution is unqualified
by this Linux record. See the
body-credit report.
The converse is a code-size cost. Linux has no red zone, and a trivial
ADD/SUB/LSL leaf or constant/copy return keeps the exact envelope for its frame
owner even when its coalesced body needs no stack; a proof-required or verifying
Darwin compile pays the same. The `stp x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!`, `mov x29, sp`
and `ldp x29, x30, [sp], #16` words make it three instructions longer than the
ordinary frameless Mach-O lowering or GCC 13.3 at `-O2` on Linux AArch64.
`e2e_aarch64_copy_coalesce` pins both targets' exact words.
The envelope is kept only when the owner can judge the function's LIR source.
A leaf whose source is outside its domain (a multiply by a constant, a load or
a store beside the ADD/SUB) is frameless on ELF as on Mach-O
(2026-09-25 record);
its arithmetic keeps the sampled evidence it had inside the envelope, which is
not credit, and it no longer adds unmapped STP/LDP pair opcodes.
The allocated-body interpreter tracks caller-save integer registers X0–X17
and their W aliases, interprets lowered moves at their opcode's actual width,
and checks bounded erased-copy forms without treating them as value definitions.
Other pseudo copies and unallocated operands cannot stand for emitted moves.
Platform, callee-save, frame and link registers remain outside the body domain.
It independently replays the raw arbitrary-byte-memory theorem for both saved
registers, SP writeback and memory outside the private frame. Entry requires an
aligned, non-wrapping SP and sixteen private writable bytes below it. Calls,
spills, larger frames and arbitrary paired loads/stores remain unsupported by
this rule. The Rust source-binding checker remains part of the trusted boundary.
Frame-bearing lowering sidecars independently replay every included rule;
their unsigned metadata still does not replace source correspondence or a
consumer's independent certificate check.

The frame binder separates unsupported shapes from erroneous supported
targets. Only the admitted source (a chain or pure-arithmetic diamond view inside the
affine domain) decides whether a body is judged. Once the frame and the
chain/diamond skeleton are recognized, a different returned value, an invalid
allocated body (undefined read, clobbered LR or callee-saved register, wrong
width, unencodable immediate), an FP/LR save, establish or restore at its
envelope position with another offset, register order or effect, and a direct
branch that lands off a block start, is unencodable, names an unlaid block or
contradicts the recorded CFG are typed mismatches. Enforced source checking
rejects them by name (`[TCG-SOURCE-BOUND-FRAME-MISMATCH]`) in proof-required,
sealed-Core and verifying-JIT modes; warn mode only prints a diagnostic and off
mode does not classify. Frameless leaves, callee-saved pairs, local areas,
spills and unmodeled opcodes or control stay unsupported and keep the ordinary
uncovered-envelope result, so those shapes still have no erroneous-target
classification. The classification is only as complete as the bounded
checker: a model-invalid but architecturally correct body (for example a W
write read back at X width) is also named a mismatch, although promotion had
already refused it as unbound.

AArch64 branch relaxation (`relax::relax_out_of_range_branches`, run before
branch resolution) rewrites an out-of-range conditional only into block-target
shapes the resolved-CFG reconstruction, the block-profile splice and the
dataflow nets already accept: the complemented branch to the layout
successor over a `B` to the far target, a target swap with a near trailing
`B`, or a split of a trailing run of direct branches into a new layout-next
block. It refuses (`[TCG-A64-BRANCH-RELAX]`) a far conditional followed in its
block by anything else, which includes a jump-table bounds branch followed by
its dispatch (the switch binding below would refuse that relaxed shape
anyway), `B.al`/`B.nv`, and an unconditional branch beyond +/-128 MiB (there is
no indirect-branch form). With loop-head alignment opted in (it is off by
default since 2026-09-30: bridge knob `a64-loop-head-align`, or
`TCG_LOOP_HEAD_ALIGN=1` outside the bridge), a function it relaxes may have loop
heads off their 32-byte alignment by the instructions a second, post-padding
round inserted.

Late layout passes (post-RA post-index formation, branch forwarding,
loop-head alignment, branch resolution and relaxation) still mutate the stream
after the structural validators. Every AArch64 encode, and the relaxing
`lower` path, now re-derives block starts, local branch displacements,
jump-table ADR/entries, ADR/LDR-literal targets and symbolic fixup sites from
the final layout and compares them with the encoded words
(`[TCG-A64-LAYOUT-XCHECK]`); each fixup must also name exactly the symbol, with
its exact-module binding, that its instruction names. This detects offset and
fixup drift or corruption, not semantic errors of the passes, and it cannot
tell two exchanged recorded successors apart. A relocation kind is checked
only against the word class it patches, so two kinds for the same class (for
example `Page21` and `GotLoadPage21` on one ADRP) are not distinguished. It checks code offsets only; there is still no AArch64
counterpart of the x86-64 DWARF CFI decode cross-check. Proof-grade routes
(the sealed Core, `emit_proofs` compiles, verifying JIT validation modes and
`JitConfig::verify`) force the reaching-definition, spill-slot and decode nets
to Enforce regardless of `TCG_AARCH64_POST_RA_REACHING_DEF`,
`TCG_AARCH64_POST_RA_SPILL_SLOTS`, `TCG_DECODE_CHECK` and `TCG_NO_DECODE_CHECK`,
bind every encoded edge to the recorded CFG, and refuse the ambient late-layout
controls `TCG_LOOP_HEAD_ALIGN`, `TCG_NO_LOOP_HEAD_ALIGN`, `TCG_LOOP_ALIGN_*`,
`TCG_PIL_MAX` and `TCG_NO_POST_INDEX_LATE` (`[TCG-A64-LATE-LAYOUT-POLICY]`),
whether set in the
process environment (which those passes read directly, so a thread-local
removal override cannot hide one) or as a thread override. Ordinary and
dev-only unchecked routes still honor them; they are not part of the explicit
compile policy, and their presence only makes artifact reuse ineligible.
`TRUST_CG_DISABLE_PASSES` remains governed by that general guard.

Every AArch64 encode also binds its switch dispatch to the final bytes
(`trust_cg_verify::aarch64_switch_binding`, `[TCG-A64-SWITCH-BIND]`, fail
closed on every route): jump-table entries, the `ADR`/`LDRSW`/`ADD`/`BR`
register chain, the `CMP/B.HI` bounds check and `SUB` normalization, every
`CMP` whose flags reach a `B.cond` in its block, and every fused
`CBZ/CBNZ/TBZ/TBNZ`. It binds bytes to the final machine-IR intent and the
recorded CFG, not to the source switch: which block is the source default
and which case constant routes to which source block are established at ISel
by the switch-normalization gate and by the modelled BST proof, and the
late passes keep the intent, not a copy of the source map. Two exchanged
recorded successors are not told apart; in a table with holes, whose default
block is also a table target, the bounds branch is bound only to some recorded
successor, so a default edge moved onto another table arm is not told apart
either. A bounds branch relaxed into an
inverted branch over a `B` is refused rather than modeled, the loaded
entry is bound through the table bytes rather than a memory model, and a
word outside the modeled A64 encoding classes between two dispatch
producers refuses the binding. The compared and loaded index values are
followed through 64-bit `MovR`/`MOVXrr` copies and through
`SPILL_SLOT_ACCESS`-flagged `LDR`/`LDUR` reloads of a frame-pointer-based
slot: a reload's value is the register a 64-bit store to exactly that slot
earlier in the block wrote, or, with no such store, an opaque slot value that
two reloads share only when no word between them can write the slot (a call,
pair, atomic, writeback or register-offset word, or a store through another
base or to overlapping bytes, can). An index reloaded from an `SP`-based or
unflagged slot, or across such a writer, is refused rather than modeled. The
binding is a group-level check: it binds
each compare, conditional branch and fused branch of a compare tree to its own
intent and to a recorded successor, not the tree's case-to-block membership as
a whole, which stays the ISel gate's obligation. It trusts the recorded CFG
on every route, the compatibility route included: a conditional branch to a
block the function does not record as a successor is refused, so a
hand-built machine function must record its edges. A conditional branch that
lands on the end of its own block (the next laid-out block start) is accepted
as block-internal whether or not that block is recorded. Every `BR` must end
a bound jump-table dispatch; any other indirect branch is refused. Both `lower` routes run it as
well (`LowerError::SwitchBinding`): the relaxing route after its relaxed
layout cross-check, and `lower::encode_function`, which has no layout
cross-check, after encoding. Neither appends jump tables, so a jump-table
dispatch is refused on them.

Scalar FCSEL also lacks validated per-instruction source/flag/operand binding.
The retained S/D mux model lemmas are diagnostic obligations, not permission to
credit an arbitrary FCSEL through an opcode-only theorem name. Runtime proof
promotion therefore refuses it. Exact S/D encoding/decode checks and native
bit-preservation tests do not establish that missing lowering theorem, the
FP16 instruction path, SVE state or exception/context-switch behavior.

FCMP's corrected ordered-not-equal models are independently tested against
IEEE bit predicates. Scalar comparison templates now bind raw input bits, and
their finite evaluator checks the actual stored formulas and declarations.
This is statistical model checking, not formal source-to-emitted correspondence.
Six AArch64 templates remain structural identities and still credit nothing at
runtime. A concrete S/D FCMP binds instead to its width's packed-NZCV
obligation: an integer-only transcription of the Arm FPCompare table over the
decoded FCMP word (all four flags, with C set on unordered) against the TrustIR
relations `N = olt, Z = oeq, C = uge, V = uno`, checked by the scalar-FP
evaluator's IEEE edge battery (the one widened carrier it admits is exactly a
packed 4-bit NZCV value). A concrete CSET binds to the obligation its REACHING
producer names: `Icmp_<cc>_I<w>` after CMP, `TST w<w>: <cc>` after TST, the
FCMP -> CSET obligation of the FCMP width and condition (where NE is the
UNORDERED `une`, never the ordered `one`), and the checked-overflow idioms after
X-width ADDS/SUBS or an adjacent ADCS/SBCS. A CSET without a bound producer in
its block stays unverified. These bindings are machine-level and sampled:
they do not establish source-to-emitted FCMP correspondence (operand order is
the word's, not certified against the source `fcmp`), FPSR exception flags,
FPCR dependence, FEAT_FP16 half-precision FCMP (refused), or NZCV live across
blocks. The integer producers (ADDS, SUBS, CMP, ADCS, SBCS, TST, and the ADC/SBC
carry readers) and the conditional selects are replayed against facts recorded
natively on one Apple M4 Max; that fixture is finite regression evidence for
one CPU, and Linux-host silicon has not been recorded.

The eighteen AArch64 scalar add/subtract/multiply/divide, negate, square-root
and integral-rounding templates now bind symbolic raw input bits. Their
bounded evaluator checks the stored expressions and operand wiring over IEEE
edge cases and the configured random samples. Invalid declarations, unsupported
arithmetic rounding modes and vacuous preconditions return Unknown. These
templates remain model identities and earn no source-to-emitted lowering credit.
The external proof checker still lacks floating-point syntax support; the four
division/square-root formal obligations remain refused. Other legacy FP min/max
evaluation paths are outside this repair.

Ledger `L04-P3` adds testing evidence for these forms, never credit. An
independent integer-only IEEE 754 reference (`ieee754_reference`; Arm
default-FPCR NaN, tininess and flag rules) is compared with the instruction
executed on the host CPU and with the verifier's machine-side model for each of
the 72 scalar FP conversion, rounding and arithmetic forms the backend emits
(`trust-cg-verify/tests/aarch64_fp_ieee_differential.rs`). The comparison
covers the result, the untouched registers and the FPSR flags bit for bit. The
TrustIR operations that select those forms are compared with the same
reference after compilation on the proof-grade AOT route at O0-O3, where every
FP value word is ENC-5-matched, and through the JIT at O1/O2
(`trust-cg-codegen/tests/e2e_aarch64_fp_ieee_lowering.rs`). Inputs are
exhaustive over every binary16 operand in every run. The release run recorded
under `crates/trust-cg-verify/tests/fixtures/fp_ieee_exhaustive/` (revision
`82e983a09`, one Apple M4 Max) is also exhaustive over every binary32 operand,
every 32-bit integer and every binary16 pair; the lowerings run those 2^32 sets
in full on AOT O2 and JIT O1 only, and the first 50,000 values of them on the
other four routes. It found no disagreement in about 1.3 x 10^11 instruction
and 3.3 x 10^11 lowering comparisons. Binary64 sources,
64-bit integers, binary32/binary64 pairs and every FMADD triple set are
statistical. The models carry one NaN and no flags, so a NaN result is compared
by class. Two boundaries of that single NaN are counted and pinned: a signaling
FMINNM/FMAXNM operand, where the instruction returns the quieted NaN and the
model the other operand; and zeros of opposite sign, where the instruction
orders -0 below +0 and the model returns its second operand. TrustIR's
`FMin`/`FMax` lowering quiets its operands and admits either zero, so the
compiled code agrees. Only round-to-nearest arithmetic under the process
default FPCR is exercised. The coverage gate names this evidence in the 24
scalar FP rows' notes without changing any row: FRINTN stays RED, and the
FDIV/FSQRT formal obligations stay refused. The Linux arms have not run.

### x86-64

x86-64 has active AOT and JIT paths with ELF, Mach-O, and COFF support. Coverage
is incomplete for the SysV and Win64 ABIs, aggregates, all relocation classes,
TLS, unwind/exception handling, debug info, atomics, SIMD/AVX feature policy,
and parity between object and JIT paths. Thirty-two-bit x86 targets are not
supported. The x86-64 link-and-run tests execute only where
`common::rosetta::x86_64_link_run` links and runs an x86-64 program: an
x86-64 host, Rosetta 2 on an opted-in Apple silicon host, or a cross driver
named by `TRUST_CG_X86_64_CC` (default `x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc` on non-x86 Linux)
with a binfmt_misc/qemu-user handler. The Linux AArch64 floor host has neither,
so there those tests compile and check each object's container and symbols,
and print a runtime `SKIP:` for execution.

The ten SSE lane-routing coverage credits (`Pshufd`, `Pmovmskb`, `MovdqaRR`,
the four `Punpck*`, `Ptest`, `Pblendvb`, `Packuswb`) have one part that is not
internally consistent by construction: `x86_sse_lane_gate`'s SDM-vs-silicon
differential, which compiles only for `target_arch = "x86_64"` and is the
only evidence that catches a shared misreading of the SDM. `MovdqaRR` and
`Pmovmskb`, whose machine and source sides are the same construction, rest on
it plus their wrong-model controls alone. Its recorded runs are on an Intel
i7-7920HQ (`d0aeb997`, `2fc2d576`); every host that runs the maintained gates
is now arm64 and no native x86-64 executor exists
(OD-LANDING-HARDWARE-20261008), so a current commit's record carries no run of
it: the release verdict refuses a record without the x86-64-native class
(OD-34 option A), and the landing verdict names the ten credits
`NOT ANCHORED` (OD-LANDING-X86-DEFERRAL-20261008). Built for any
other target the two silicon tests are named `#[ignore]` stubs that fail if
forced (L13-P14, 2026-10-12), so a direct or full-matrix run on an arm64 host
lists them as `NOT RUN` instead of passing without them, as it did before.
Rosetta 2 is not accepted as the anchor (OD-34): it would compare the model
with Apple's translation of the SSE instructions, not with an x86-64 CPU. The
measuring Mac (Apple M4 Max, macOS 26.6.2) has no Rosetta 2 installed, and the
Trust package's sysroot carries no `x86_64-apple-darwin` standard library
(`trustc --test --target x86_64-apple-darwin` fails with E0463).

On x86-64, per-instruction proof credit comes from two sources: an operand
reconstruction whose input space is small enough to discharge completely
(Exhaustive), and the source-bound body theorem (see
[Correctness and proof scope](#correctness-and-proof-scope)), which is the
only source of Formal credit. The body theorem's subject is the
pre-register-allocation ISel stream, so the credit covers
instruction selection and says nothing proved about register allocation, the
frame or the encoded bytes. Its source is the LIR instruction selection
receives. In a compile that claims proofs that is the adapter's LIR, because
neither shared LIR pass runs there (OD-225, under
[Correctness and proof scope](#correctness-and-proof-scope)). Its machine
side is the stream after the x86 machine passes of the opt level
(`run_x86_optimization_passes`; at O2 about twenty of them, BlockMerge,
LoopRotate, IfConvert and the SIB folds among them). A Valid theorem
therefore covers what those passes did to that function. After the theorem,
at O1 and above, the post-allocation `MovRR` coalescer
(`coalesce_x86_redundant_movrr_copies`) rewrites register copies under no
enforced check. In the default `Warn` mode with `TCG_POST_RA_SPEC` unset, its
captured-spec value-flow check is not even evaluated. The rustc bridge
cannot set that variable, because trustc refuses `TCG_*` variables. The
coalescer is inside the allocation boundary above (nothing proved about
register allocation), but it is an O1+ value-routing rewrite that runs
downstream of the theorem, which no O2 credit covers. The compiler supplies the calling convention (the
target spec for AOT, the host for JIT); it is bound into the verifier-input
digest and the JIT certificate cache key, and Windows x64 is outside the lane.
A recognized body that disagrees with its admitted source is rejected by name
(`[TCG-SOURCE-BOUND-X86-MISMATCH]`). A refuted body theorem fails its covered
rows. Without an independently checked proof (no admitted AY or capable Clean,
`TCG_REFINE_SOLVER=0`, tier-0 recording, an uncertified UNSAT, an AY `unknown`
or timeout) the covered rows stay unverified. Either way promotion is refused.

An `f16` formal parameter on x86-64 is refused by name (`[TCG-X86-F16-ABI]`);
it used to panic in the XMM copy selection. How x86-64 passes `f16` call
arguments and return values has not been checked against a C compiler.

A 128-bit integer argument follows the System V psABI: two consecutive integer
registers, or, when fewer than two remain, wholly on the stack at a 16-byte
boundary, with a later eightbyte still taking the register it left free. GCC 16
and the LLVM 22 in `trustc` do the same, so Rust code built by `trustc`'s LLVM
agrees with this backend (`m149_x86_i128_stack_arg_xback`, all four rlib x bin
cells, after 0-7 `u64`s). C built by an older LLVM-based compiler does not:
Apple clang 14.0.3 (LLVM 15) splits such a value between R9 and the stack and
aligns a stack `__int128` to 8. A `__int128` passed after five or seven integer
arguments therefore does not cross between that compiler's code and either
this backend or `trustc`'s LLVM. `e2e_x86_64_i128_stack_abi` checks the
psABI placement against C written as `u64` eightbytes, not against the host
compiler's `__int128`
(record). This is execution
on chosen values, not a proof of the convention.

A TrustIR function with more independent scalar results than System V's C
return file holds (RAX,RDX / XMM0,XMM1) returns the rest in TrustCG's internal
multi-result registers (`X86_INTERNAL_RET_GPRS` / `X86_INTERNAL_RET_XMMS`:
RCX,RSI,RDI,R8,R9 and XMM2-XMM7), the counterpart of AArch64's X0-X7 / V0-V7.
It is not a C ABI, so it is admitted only on a `Fast` or `Cold` edge; a `C`,
`Rust` or other foreign-convention edge of that shape is refused by name
(`[TCG-X86-MULTI-RESULT]`), and Windows x64 defines no extension. R10/R11 and
XMM14/XMM15 are excluded (post-RA scratch), so the file holds seven integer and
eight FP results; an eighth integer result is refused. Evidence is execution on
chosen inputs (`e2e_x86_64_internal_multi_result`: a native x86-64 or Rosetta
link-run lane and an x86-64 JIT lane, both skipped where no x86-64 executor
exists; the 2026-09-28 record ran the objects under the Unicorn emulator), not a
proof of the convention. The x86-64 object path cannot yet reference an
`Internal` function (`AotDirectModuleFunctionBindingUnsupported`), so an AOT
object uses the convention only between non-internal functions; the JIT has no
such restriction.
Exception handling is emitted for Mach-O and ELF modules; a COFF module
carrying EH, and a RawBytes or SINGLE-FUNCTION emission of any format other
than Mach-O, are refused by name. The ELF lane emits `.gcc_except_table`, a
zPLR `.eh_frame` giving EVERY function of an EH-bearing module an FDE (a real
LSDA for an EH function, an all-filler one for the rest), and the
`DW.ref.<personality>` slot the CIE's indirect personality encoding names —
weak, hidden and COMDAT for an external personality, object-local for one the
module defines `STB_LOCAL`, as on AArch64 ELF. Its pointers are
`R_X86_64_PC32` against local `.text` and `.gcc_except_table` section anchors,
emitted in ascending `r_offset` order because GNU ld walks `.eh_frame` with one
monotonic relocation cursor. A function the lane cannot describe — no frame
lowering, an empty body, or a second personality in the same module — is
refused rather than emitted without unwind tables. `e2e_x86_64_eh_catch`,
`e2e_x86_64_eh_invoke_trust_ir_run` and `e2e_x86_64_eh_resume_trust_ir` link
their objects with the host `c++` and run them on an x86-64 Linux GNU or macOS
host; they first ran on x86-64 Linux GNU on 2026-09-24. GNU `readelf` reads the
CIE, the FDE, the ascending `R_X86_64_PC32` records and the slot's binding back
out of an emitted object, the one image `link_objects` stages is checked for
`PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` (the fixtures that link by other routes are not),
and four controls bound what a passing run shows: dropping the covering LSDA
call-site row's landing pad loses the catch, so does turning the CIE personality
encoding from indirect (`0x9b`) to direct (`0x1b`), two independent objects each
carrying their own COMDAT slot both catch in one link, and the object links as a
shared object while the same object with its personality record retargeted at
the personality symbol directly is refused by GNU ld. That is native execution
and readback evidence for those three fixtures (a catch-all pad, the trust-ir
`Invoke`/`LandingPad` path at O0-O3, and a cleanup pad whose `_Unwind_Resume`
must reach an enclosing handler), all with the C++ personality; it is not a proof
of LSDA or personality correctness. Typed catches, filters and mixed
personalities remain refused. Unlike the AArch64 Linux lane, the two
`X86ISelFunction`-level fixtures exercise one lowering each rather than O0-O3, no
`llvm-dwarfdump --eh-frame` leg compares their rows with the disassembled
prologue, and no fixture runs the RUST personality against libstd natively on
this lane.

The x86-64 certificate path applies a non-vacuous rule the AArch64 path does
not: a function with no genuinely discharged instruction proof is refused
(`non_vacuous_function_evidence`), because covered-elsewhere and skipped rows
alone establish no value semantics. Bodies with no value-semantics row at all
are exempt. WHICH bodies is decided by ONE rule; a second, independent rule
decides only whether the exemption gets an AUDIT NAME.

THE EXEMPTION DECISION is the ANONYMOUS opcode-shape escape
(`x86_64_report_is_empty_body`), unchanged. It reads OPCODES, never a row's
disposition: the exact row sets `[Ret]`, `[Push, MovRR, Pop, Ret]`, `[Ud2]` and
`[Push, MovRR, Ud2]`, plus `Jmp* ; Call ; Ud2` against a source that is a
zero-argument direct call and a trap. On this pipeline the frame envelope is
inserted by the encoder after instruction selection and is never a report row,
so the two frame-enveloped shapes are reachable only from a synthetic report —
but they are admitted with no source and with no row disposition, which means a
`MovRR` that copied a value, a trap with a different skip reason, and a row the
verifier FAILED are admitted with them. A failed row still fails the function
closed through its own certificate. Nothing narrows or widens this rule, because
that would change which functions may be published.

THE AUDIT NAME is the `call_only_body` certificate, issued for a body the rule
above already exempts when TWO further independent facts both hold. (1) Every
report row is either the trap skip (`UD2`) or a
`CALL`/`CALLR`/`CALLM`/`JMP`/`JMPR`/`RET` the verifier leaves unverified by
design — keyed on those exact verifier dispositions, not on opcodes — and at
least one row is that trap skip, because the certificate claims the body traps.
(2) The
LIR source handed to instruction selection, flattened in layout order, is a
bare DIVERGING transfer: `Jump* ; Trap`, or `Jump* ; Call (direct, no
arguments, no results) ; Trap`. A report with no source is refused outright.
The population is the measured one — on `core` at O0 with `-Cpanic=abort`, the
`call abort; ud2` body of the cold panic helpers and the trap-only body of
`abort_immediate`. The source requirement is what keeps it there: a body that
RETURNS to its caller (`call f; ret`), a chain of calls, and a call whose
arguments happened to need no reconstructed `MOV` are all refused, because
nothing in a transfer-only row set proves what a callee received. (`call f; ret`
is refused twice over: its rows carry no trap, which (1) requires, and its
source returns, which (2) refuses.) `trust-cg --emit-proofs` writes the
certificate as an `eval-only` per-rule `.cert` audit file and no lowering
sidecar, because it has no `ProofDatabase` obligation. It carries the function's
name, so the certificate BUNDLE a compile returns — what the promotion gate
reads and what `proof_bundle_sha256` covers — names every function that promoted
on this exemption; the per-rule `.cert` is one file per rule and names the first
of them.

THE NAME BUYS NO PROMOTION. The certificate is issued `verified`, because what
it states is true, but it is excluded from every gate that asks whether any
obligation was discharged (`proof_evidence::certificate_is_discharge_evidence`):
from the verifying JIT's per-function verdict
(`x86_certificates_show_verified_semantics`, and so from
`every_function_semantics_verified`), from the JIT's module-level gate
(`gate_jit_proofs_promotable`), and from the rustc bridge's independent
non-empty-bundle re-check. The same predicate excludes the `covered_elsewhere`
certificate that each CALL, JMP and RET row of such a body carries, because it
too discharges nothing. The verifying JIT (`CachedVerified`, `AlwaysVerify`)
therefore refuses to publish every body this exemption admits: a trap-only
body, a `call f; ud2` body, and an empty `ret` body. Until 2026-09-28 the
predicate excluded only the exemption, and the verifying JIT's certification
step returned Ok with per-function `verified = true` for the `call f; ud2` body
and the empty `ret` body on their `covered_elsewhere` certificates alone, with
no discharged obligation behind either
(`x86_verifying_jit_still_refuses_a_call_only_body` measures all of them at the
certification boundary). That was measured on an arm64 host, through the
uncached path only, with no x86-64 code executed; that an Ok there is what
publishes the code is known by reading the JIT, not by a run. On
the AOT object lane these bodies still promote, and a CGU of only such bodies
is admitted by its object relocation inventory certificate, which is what
admitted it before this category existed too.

COVERED-ELSEWHERE ROWS THAT CITE A DECODE CHECK (X-OPCODES-P13, 2026-10-12).
Two covered-elsewhere opcodes rest their credit on a per-compile decode check
of their own emitted bytes rather than on a structural argument: x86-64
`MovRI`, whose encoding half is ENC-3's run of
`x86_encoding_proofs::mov_imm_check_for_preg`, and AArch64 `AlignNop`, whose
byte exactness is ENC-5's decode of the NOP word
(`compiler::covered_elsewhere_cited_decode_check`, pinned to exactly these
two). Their certificate is `verified: true` (`covered_elsewhere`) only when the
compile's backing for that check is ENFORCED: ENC-3 in its default `enforce`
mode for x86-64, read from the same environment the encode funnel resolves;
ENC-5 at proof grade (the verifying JIT, the address-free route) or in the
compatibility policy's `enforce` mode for AArch64. Under
`TCG_DECODE_CHECK=warn|off`, `TCG_DECODE_CHECK_A64=warn|off` on a
compatibility route, or `TCG_NO_DECODE_CHECK=1`, the row is a `verified: false`
`covered_elsewhere_withheld` certificate naming the check and why it did not
back the bytes; it blocks promotion and counts as evidence, so a per-function
verdict that needs every evidence row verified fails on it. The x86-64 verifying
JIT also bypasses its outer certificate cache unless ENC-3 is enforced, so a
certificate cached under an enforced check is never served for unchecked
bytes. Until this change both rows were positive whether or not their check
ran. Under the default `enforce` mode the x86-64 `MovRI` row's text now names
ENC-3, so the proof-bundle digest of every x86-64 compile with a `MovRI` row
changed once; emitted code did not. Evidence strength: unit tests, two kinds.
Through the real x86-64 encode funnel, a test-only fault seam
(`TCG_TEST_DECODE_CHECK_FORCE_MISMATCH`, compiled only into trust-cg-codegen's
own unit tests) forces ENC-3 to refute the `MovRI`: under enforce the compile is
refused before any certificate exists, under warn the encode passes and the row
is withheld. Through each production certificate lane
(`compiler_decode_backing_lane_tests`: x86-64 AOT, the x86-64 JIT's cached and
uncached modes, the AArch64 JIT verifying and emitting proofs under the
`Unchecked` override, AArch64 AOT), a test-only hook
(`decode_check::lane_probe`) records the decode-check mode every encode of a
probe function ran and the backing the lane handed the certificate builder, and
the tests require them to agree, with the cited row following, under the
default, warn, off and `TCG_NO_DECODE_CHECK=1` environments. A fixed `Enforced`
at the x86-64 AOT, x86-64 JIT or AArch64 JIT lane fails them. What it does not
cover: the AArch64 AOT lane builds certificates only for a proof-requesting
compile, which is also proof grade, so a fixed `Enforced` there is equal by
construction and no test can tell them apart; an AArch64 JIT compile that the
promotion gate refuses never reaches its encode, and there the backing is
checked against the policy alone; through the public AOT compiler a warn-mode
compile is still refused by an earlier row in every fixture tried (the
selector's `MovRR` copy blocks first when the source-bound replay is off), so
the withheld row is observed at the lane's certificate builder, not in a
returned refusal; ENC-3 still covers the ENCODING only, not the lowerer's choice
of constant; and the other covered-elsewhere opcodes (CALL/JMP/RET targets,
`BLR`, `BR`, `CBZ`/`CBNZ`/`TBZ`/`TBNZ`, AArch64 `RET`) cite no check a mode can
switch off and are unchanged.

THE ABI ENVELOPE (JIT ONLY). In a verifying JIT mode an empty `ret` body and a
zero-argument `call f; ud2` panic entry are now judged by one more certificate,
`x86_abi_envelope`, which IS discharge evidence: a System V envelope theorem
(`trust_cg_verify::x86_source_bound_envelope`) over the function's FINAL
pre-relocation bytes and its symbolic fixup manifest. For the void return it
states that the RET's target is the caller's return address, RSP after the RET
is `rsp0 + 8`, every callee-saved GPR the bytes write is restored, and memory at
or above `rsp0` is unchanged. For the panic entry it states that `RSP + 8` is
16-byte aligned at callee entry (RSP after the CALL's push), the return slot
holds `code_base` plus the offset at which the byte recognizer found the `ud2`
(stated against that offset, not against the address the CALL pushes; in
production the two are always equal, because the Rust walk refuses every body
with an instruction between the CALL and the `ud2` before a theorem is built,
so for every body the owner admits this item is a read-back of that push; only
a test-only builder without the walk's refusals shows the item falsified for
such a body), every callee-saved GPR other than RBP is unchanged,
and memory at or above `rsp0` is unchanged. Memory is byte-granular and
array-free (Ackermann-reduced). The theorem is replayed in PARTS, each under
the full premise set: one per item, and one per byte of an item that compares
a 64-bit memory read (18 parts for the pinned void return, 10 for the panic
entry). The certificate is `verified` only when EVERY part has a Valid replay
(an AY proof that Clean independently accepted); then the function carries one
verified certificate per part. Otherwise it is a named `verified: false`
refusal (`X86_ENVELOPE_NEEDS_REPLAY` naming the first part without a Valid
replay, a refutation naming the refuted part, or a mismatch). So the JIT admits
these two shapes ONLY on a replayed theorem. Trap-only bodies get no envelope
and stay refused, and so do profile-counter spellings, whose trampoline and
counter-patch bytes are outside the envelope's closed byte set.

What this is measured to do, on the arm64 macOS development host only, with no
x86-64 code executed:
- Replay refused (`TCG_REFINE_SOLVER=0`): the JIT refuses both shapes by the
  envelope's name.
- Every mutant theorem is refuted: for each, AY answers a counterexample to a
  part of an item the Rust evaluator says the defect breaks. The mutants are a
  missing POP, an extra POP, POP RBX for POP RBP, PUSH RBX then POP R12, a
  write above `rsp0`, a partial overwrite of the return slot, a frameless
  (misaligned) call, an extra push before the call, an instruction between the
  CALL and the `ud2`, and a CALL whose push lands on the caller's return
  address. Measured with both AYs below. These theorems come from a test-only
  builder without the Rust walk's refusals: in production the walk refuses
  every one of these bodies by name before any theorem is built, so the AY
  refutations show that the theorem would catch each defect, not that the
  solver is what refuses it.
- The Trust pack 9192 toolchain AY (`ay 0.26.0 build 9624`, Clean store pack
  8606) certifies no part of a correct envelope: the first part's certificate
  carries an unproved step, or AY's own strict check rejects a hole step. Under
  it the JIT refuses both shapes, naming the first part.
- A local overlay AY (`ay 0.27.0 build 11378`, commit `0b670d840`, with Clean
  `5390f432b`; assembled locally, not a published pack) certifies every part
  of the void return, the panic entry and a framed void body with saves (34
  parts), and Clean fully verifies each proof. Under it the x86-64 JIT compile
  of the empty body, the panic entry and the panic entry behind a jump returns
  Ok in `AlwaysVerify` and `CachedVerified`, each function carrying one
  verified `Formal` certificate per part.
- Under that overlay AY the whole conjunction is not certified: AY answers
  `unknown` with `incomplete self-check-rejected` for the void return and
  `incomplete proof-trusted` for the panic entry, and times out (30 s) on the
  framed void body with saves. A 64-bit memory-read equation proved as one
  goal is not certified either, while each byte equation certifies. That is
  why the theorem is replayed in parts.
- `CachedVerified` never serves these functions from the certificate cache:
  the store also requires the function's x86 body report to be reusable, and
  these bodies have no genuinely verified row, so every call re-verifies.

Execution on an x86-64 host is not measured, and the toolchain the project
pins (build 9624) still refuses both shapes.

The envelope's trusted base:
- the verify-owned byte recognizer and the x86-64 semantics of its closed set
  (PUSH/POP r other than RSP, `mov rbp, rsp`, `sub/add rsp, imm8`,
  `call rel32`, `ret`, `ud2`);
- the manifest parser and the Rust fixup pairing (exactly the judged holes:
  callee name and binding, hole offset, zero placeholder);
- the System V entry premises (`rsp0 + 8` 16-byte aligned, `rsp0` above the
  stack depth);
- the Ackermann transcription;
- the SMT-LIB serializer.

Outside the theorem:
- the JIT's rel32 patching and the absolute-jump veneers it appends after
  certification;
- the identity of pre-relocation and published bytes;
- what the callee does.

Windows x64 is not admitted. The AOT object lane does not run the envelope
(its `emit_proofs` export is refused as JIT-only).

NEITHER RULE CONTAINS THE OTHER, which is why the order is load-bearing. The
allowlist admits the frame-enveloped and source-less shapes listed above, which
the conjunction refuses: those promote with no audit name, as they did. The
conjunction admits `Jump* ; Trap` — the O0 two-block `-> !` body whose rows are
`[Jmp, Ud2]` — which the allowlist does not enumerate; because the allowlist
decides, that class keeps its `non_vacuous_function_evidence` refusal and is
published by neither lane, and it is given no name because a refused function
promotes nothing to audit. Consulting the conjunction first would have promoted
it: that is a widening of the publication boundary, and this exemption naming
does not take it.

A body with one register write (`MOV r, imm` included), load, store, address
computation or ALU row keeps the rule, and neither exemption supplies evidence
for such a row. The frame envelope, the call and branch edges and their
relocations rest on frame lowering's validators, the CFG model and the
relocation inventory, not on an instruction proof. The AArch64 JIT applies no
vacuity rule at all.

### RISC-V 64

RISC-V 64 is experimental. It has real lowering and encoding infrastructure,
but does not have the semantic breadth, proof emission, ABI/object maturity,
or validation depth of the primary targets.

### WebAssembly (wasm32)

`--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (alias `wasm32`) routes to the wasm lane. It
never constructs a register target and runs no register allocation. Its two
optimizations, the trust-ir mid-end and the local emission pass described
below, run at O1 and above, and each keeps a rewrite only when its checker
accepts it. The CLI's wasm routes compile at `-O` (default `-O2`): `-O0`
emits each function's baseline body, and `-O1` to `-O3` run both passes. One
input without `-c` becomes a closed module that owns
its memory and imports nothing. `-c` writes each input as a relocatable object
in the tool-conventions format (`env.__linear_memory`, `env.__stack_pointer`,
`env.__indirect_function_table`, a `linking` symbol table, relocations); several
inputs are compiled to objects and linked by an external `wasm-ld`, which
exports every default-visibility definition and gets `-L`, `-l` and `-Wl`.
trust-cg does not ship `wasm-ld`. WASI and emscripten imports are not
accepted, and `-g`, `--panic-unwind`, `--emit-proofs`,
`--profile-generate`, `--profile-use`, `--cegis-superopt`,
`--compile-artifact-cache`, `--trace`, or `--metrics` is refused by name rather
than silently dropped. `wasm64` is not matched.

The lowering covers the trust-ir value domain: integers of every width (narrow
ones canonicalized; 128-bit ones in memory at O0 and, at O1 and above, in two
`i64` locals, low and high half, unless a definition or use of the value has
only a memory lowering: for example the 128-bit atomics, a 128-bit constant
spelled as bytes, a 128-bit value used as the aggregate of an `extractfield`
or `insertfield`, or a call whose callee type is unknown, and any other use
without a pair lowering, together with every value a block argument, `copy`
or `select` ties to such a value, keep the memory form; library-free inline
multiply and shift sequences, where at O1 and above a pair-carried value
shifted or rotated by an integer constant uses that amount's constant half
shifts, and division and remainder through one
trust-ir helper that the closed module or object carries itself), floats (IEEE
`min`/`max`/`copysign`, `FRem` through `fmod`), overflow and checked
arithmetic, `select`, aggregates, tuples, enums (direct, niche and untagged),
fat pointers, atomics (single-threaded, including 128-bit read-modify-write
and compare-exchange) and bulk memory. Irreducible control flow lowers as a
dispatch loop, and an `Alloca` with a runtime count is carved from the shadow
stack. Calls follow the WebAssembly BasicCABI: an unpadded single-lane
aggregate is passed and returned directly, `i128` splits into two `i64`, and
every other aggregate (including a padded or over-aligned singleton) is passed
by address and returned through `sret`, as clang does without the multivalue
feature. Choosing the `i64` pair is a lowering decision and is not separately
proved: the differential tests and structural gates that cover the rest of
the lane cover it. It does not change the C ABI: an `i128` argument is two
`i64` halves, and an `i128` result returns through `sret` (into a transient
scratch slot of the caller's frame, as the 128-bit division helper's result
does).

In a relocatable object at O1 and above, the lane uses an internal ABI for a
strong, hidden function under a crate-private name
(`<symbol>.tcg.crate.<16 hex digits>`, the rustc bridge's name for a
codegen-unit-private item placed once) whose C form returns through `sret`
only scalars or 128-bit integers, at most four wasm values. Such a function
is defined as an internal entry `<name>.tcg.mv` that returns them as wasm
multi-value results (a 128-bit one as its two `i64` halves), plus a C-form
entry under its own name that forwards to it; the object then declares the
`multivalue` feature. Direct calls in every object of the crate call the
internal entry; function pointers, static data, vtables, exports and other
backends' code see only the C form. The decision reads only the function's
name, linkage, visibility and signature, which the bridge gives a
declaration as its definition has them, so every object of the crate decides
it alike. A session that does not admit `multivalue` (a CPU other than
`generic`, `lime1` or `bleeding-edge` without a later `+multivalue` target
feature, or a last `multivalue` target feature of `-multivalue`; the CPU is
read first, then the target spec's features, then `-C target-feature`) keeps
the C form everywhere (the bridge sets `WasmInlineHints::without_multivalue`),
as do closed modules and O0. Every object the lane emits passes a structural
boundary gate (`trust_cg_verify::wasm_internal_abi`, run on each object
before it is written, and over a fixed corpus at O0-O3 with byte-mutation and
hand-built negative controls by the soundness-gate target
`wasm_internal_abi_gate`). The gate refuses, as `[TCG-WASM-INTERNAL-ABI]`, an
object in which a multi-value function is exported, in an element segment,
weak, default-visibility, misnamed, or referenced other than by a direct
call relocation at a `call`, or in which a relocated `call_indirect` type is
multi-value, or whose forwarding entries do not store each result exactly
once at the BasicCABI offset and width trust-ir's layout gives the
signature. Before linking, the bridge refuses a crate whose objects
disagree about an internal entry (one called but not defined exactly once,
or imported at another type). These are structural checks, not a proof
that an internal entry computes its function, and the gate cannot see
objects trust-cg did not compile. Functions rustc places in another codegen
unit keep rustc's own symbol and therefore the C form, as do link-once,
weak, default-visibility, aggregate-result and `PassMode::Indirect`
functions; a call through a function pointer to a planned function pays one
more call, through the forwarding entry. A link with `--export-all`, or an
explicit `--export` of a `.tcg.mv` symbol, would export an internal entry.
The lane still uses `sign-ext` and `nontrapping-fptoint` whatever
`-C target-cpu` says.

At O1 and above an object's `name` section shows a crate-private function
under its Rust symbol, without the `.tcg.crate.<tag>` mark and the
`.tcg.mv` suffix (an argument-promotion clone keeps `.tcg.ap<h>`), and
`wasm-ld` copies those names into the linked module. Two functions may
then share a debug name: a C-form entry and its internal entry, or two
crates' copies of an upstream function. Symbols, exports and imports are
unchanged. Among an object's C-ABI definitions (never an internal entry,
its C-form entry or a lane helper), bodies of at least 128 code bytes whose
type, locals, code and relocations are equal are folded: one non-weak
member keeps its body and another becomes a one-call forwarder to it, so
every function keeps its index, symbol, exports and table entries and no
two addresses become equal. A member is folded only when it is not
reachable from the kept member in the object's call graph (every function
a body's relocation names, and from a body with an indirect call every
function whose address the object takes and every function whose symbol
is not local, since another object or the host can take that one's
address), so no forwarder lies on a cycle of calls among its object's
functions, an indirect call included whichever object took the address it
calls. `trust_cg_verify::wasm_body_fold` checks every
fold against the object's bytes with its own reader, this rule included,
and a refusal keeps the unfolded object, never the compile. A forwarder
adds one call frame to each call entering it; a recursion that passes
through another object's function or the host and re-enters a folded
function pays one extra frame per level. In the rustc bridge at O1 and
above on wasm32, constant allocations with equal contents share one global,
so one address, within a codegen unit: the global is named by a 128-bit
hash of the image's length, alignment, bytes and pointers, the CGU merge
compares every same-named copy field by field and falls back to
per-function objects on any difference, and a hash collision or an image
that points at the allocation's own reservation keeps the per-allocation
name. Rust gives constants no address identity; statics and the allocations
a static's image reaches are not shared, and at O0 each function keeps its
own copy (OD-153).

A body-less Rust-convention declaration is refused when an aggregate
crosses it (`[TCG-WASM-RUST-ABI-LINK]`), because rustc's wasm32 Rust ABI is
not modeled at an object boundary. A source `Assert` is refused by its panic
kind (`[TCG-ASSERT-PANIC]`); the lane no longer lowers it to a bare trap.
Variadic definitions, thread-locals, exception handling (the lane needs
`panic=abort`), SIMD, first-class closure values and `f16`/`f128` are refused
by name. `Neg`, `Not` and `CtPop` are admitted only at an integer scalar type,
as in the native adapter, so `not bool` (trust-ir's `UnOpNotOnScalarBool`, the
must-refuse row `unop_not_scalar_bool`) is refused by name on every wasm entry.
Output bytes are deterministic.

The wasm lanes share the native path's admission. Every module, object and
single-function entry runs trust-ir's codegen admission
(`trust_cg_lower::validate_codegen_prerequisites`, which no policy widens) and
then the codegen license. The license is the caller's `CodegenLicensePolicy`
on the `*_license` entries (and the `*_license_optimized` entries, which also
take the optimization level) and the default policy on every other entry. The
CLI's wasm path honors `--recognize-authority` and `--refuse-unlicensed`, and
the rustc bridge passes the policy its native arm uses.

The lane also refuses the following by name, with the native reasons:
- a `RegionHavocStore` marker;
- an `Undef` carrying proof annotations, or whose type is outside the native
  scalar carrier set (aggregate and vector poison is unmodelled);
- an `ArraySplat` at a non-array type;
- a pointer op at a non-pointer type or with a result arity other than one;
- a `PtrMetadata` or `PtrFromParts` whose declared metadata type is not the
  pointer's metadata at 32-bit pointers;
- an `AlwaysMemory` module, and an `Unclassified` module once an aggregate
  crosses a call edge by value. `wasm32_target_info` stamps `NativeC`, the
  Basic C ABI classification the lane applies, and the bridge keeps its own
  claim;
- a C-convention declaration whose narrow parameter has a recorded
  `ParamAttrs` slot with no recorded extension. The Basic C ABI, like
  DarwinPCS, makes the caller extend; the tree carries no external citation
  for that reading.

The rustc bridge declares every `extern "rust-call"` callable with its
argument tuple's elements on wasm32 as on the native targets
(`rust_call_spread`, round 10), so its former `[TCG-RUST-CALL-ABI]` refusal of
calls a tupled declaration could not place is gone. Measured before that
refusal (2026-10-03, O0 and O2), a pointer to a reified `Fn::call` of a
closure trapped with `function signature mismatch` where LLVM returns a value
(441 of 3522 checks). The corpus crate `r10-bridge-rust-call.rs` and its
LLVM-built library compare, in `wasm32_differential`, `rust-call` fn pointers
in both directions (`[f32; 4]`, `(u32, u64)`, `(f64, f64)` and `(bool, u64)`
elements), a user `rust-call` trait method through `&dyn` in both directions,
