a foreign `rust-call` item, and a reified `Fn::call` body address made by one
backend and called by the other. Measured 2026-10-08 (`targo --unverified`, no
proof claim, with rustup stable's `rust-lld` 22.1.6 as `wasm-ld`, a local
measurement aid): every export agrees with LLVM at the default level, at O2
and at O3 with four codegen units. In the same run 12 of the target's 13 tests
pass; `wasm32_corpus_agrees_with_llvm` keeps the known `r5-bridge-iter-frames`
failure (OD-167: 17,397 disagreements at O2, as recorded for `origin/main`).

Both lanes are full lanes of both `must_refuse_corpus` targets at `8a0d54c0`,
with every artifact row retargeted to wasm32, and they run at the library
entries' default level, O2, so the trust-ir mid-end and the local emission
pass are on. The mid-end only ever sees a module the admission accepted, and
its output must pass that admission again. A row that
declares no target or the canonical one takes the wasm32 shape and keeps its
`struct_passing`; the i686 row stays pinned and is refused as such. The object
lane accepts `import_backed_summary_unauthenticated`, as the native strict
adapter does and for the same reason. The closed module refuses that row only
because its one declaration is unbound under the closed import policy.
`sequence_element_op` is refused by the lane's missing `Sequence` carrier,
before its element op is reached.

trust-ir's dominator computation inside that admission is quadratic on a deep
chain of blocks that all branch to one shared block: about 228 s per admission
for 20,000 blocks in a debug build. The native entries pay the same cost.

In an object the 128-bit division helper is a weak hidden
`__tcg_divmod128_<digest>` definition, whose name is pinned to the helper's
text. The lane has two helper texts: the baseline at O0
(`__tcg_divmod128_7b90c2514708d153`) and, at O1 and above, one that
estimates a wide divisor's quotient (`__tcg_divmod128_5af6f467d6747164`), so
objects of both levels link side by side (OD-152). `wasm-ld` keeps one
copy of each and does not export it. Every object the lane compiles
refuses a module that names any `__tcg_divmod128_` symbol (defined or
declared, function or global, any linkage) as `[TCG-WASM-SYMBOL]`, whether
or not that module divides, so a crate that defines the name fails to compile
even when the bridge's per-function fallback puts the definition and the
division into different objects. trust-cg cannot check objects it did not
compile: a STRONG definition of the reserved name in a C or LLVM-built object
of the same link would replace the helper unchecked. On a zero divisor or
`MIN / -1`,
which trust-ir leaves undefined, the lane returns a value and does not trap:
for a zero divisor an all-ones quotient and the dividend as remainder (the
signed forms compute that over the magnitudes, then apply the signs), and
`MIN` with remainder 0 for `MIN / -1`. The helper's fast paths (64-bit
operands, a 64-bit divisor and, for a wider divisor, a normalized
shift-subtract at O0 and at O1 and above a quotient estimated by one
128-by-64 division and corrected once) are checked by execution against the
reference interpreter and Rust's operators, not by a solver proof.

General TrustIR source `Inst::Assert` remains refused by the shared v52
admission floor and the Wasm lowering backstop. The Rust bridge's separately
implemented Wasm MIR-assert route below emits conditional branches and genuine
panic calls; it does not admit general source-Assert instructions.

Each framed function gets a shadow-stack frame. Home slots and fixed allocas
share frame bytes by liveness, but only while no address can be observed: an
address that reaches memory, a callee, control flow or any operation that may
trap on its bits pins its allocation, and so does an access through a pointer
rebuilt with integer arithmetic (`ptrtoint`/`add`/`inttoptr`) at a
displacement the lane cannot bound inside its allocation. A bound comes from
constants, from a remainder or mask, or from a dominating unsigned bounds
check against a constant or a length parameter. A length parameter counts only
in a function whose entry block no branch re-enters, and a displacement
carried around a loop back edge is never bounded by a check of the loop's
rebound index. Under trust-ir's `inttoptr` such a pointer may resolve into a
neighbouring allocation. The C library's `memset`, `memcpy` and `memmove`,
when declared bodiless with their exact C shapes, are trusted to keep no
pointer argument. A pointer stored into a local cell, as slice iterators and
range-indexed subslices do, still pins its allocation, so such frames remain
larger than LLVM's and can exhaust the shadow stack where LLVM's do not
(`a.iter().take(64)` and `iter_mut().take(n)` over a large local array trap at
`-O2` where LLVM's module runs). A zero-sized `Alloca` occupies one byte, so
distinct live allocations never share an address. Weak or link-once
definitions are treated as replaceable at link time. A frame is still often
larger than LLVM's. In particular a callee copies a by-value aggregate
argument rather than reusing the caller's copy, so deep recursion can exhaust
the 1 MiB stack where LLVM's code does not; that fails closed with a trap. An
`Alloca` whose earlier pointer may still be observed is carved per execution,
as trust-ir defines it, so a long loop that keeps such pointers live grows the
stack. A closed module checks each new stack pointer against its static data.
Functions over an engine limit (50,000 locals, 1,000 parameters or results, a
7,654,321-byte body) are refused with `WasmLowerError::ImplementationLimit`.

The lane emits no proof certificates. Before a module or object is written it
passes the CFG structural checker and a frame-bounds guard that refuses a
constant-offset frame access outside the allocated frame; an object also
passes the internal-ABI boundary gate described above. Its other evidence
is the encoding, CFG-structural, memory/call-ABI, bulk-memory and value-domain
obligation families; the coverage gate credits all 128 value-bearing wasm
opcode rows the lane can emit (never-selected rows are excluded and checked
absent from live-compiled code). The float and bulk-memory credits are
battery and corpus evidence rather than proofs over all inputs, the
`min`/`max` credit relies on trust-ir leaving the ±0 tie unpinned, and the
addresses and sizes of aggregate moves, and of a `memcopy` with a constant
count of 1 to 32 bytes (emitted at O1 and above as `memory.copy` of that
constant without the zero-count guard, which the emission pass expands into
loads and stores when its addresses are locals or relocation-free
expressions), rest on the differentials; every
`memset` and every longer or run-time-count copy keeps the guard. Two
execution differentials complete it: the trust-ir interpreter against
compiled wasm on a 180-function value-domain corpus (as a closed module and
as a relocatable object linked by `wasm-ld`), and the Rust-level corpus
below. Relooper bisimulation and a source-to-wasm translation-validation
verdict remain named deferrals, and the structural invariants are necessary
conditions, not a proof that a module computes what its trust-ir computes.

At O1 and above (the library entries without a level, the CLI at `-O1` to
`-O3`, and the rustc bridge when `-C opt-level` or its `opt-level` knob asks
for it) the trust-ir mid-end (`crates/trust-cg-irmid`, profile `Wasm32`,
wired by `wasm/mid.rs`) rewrites the module before it is lowered. It runs
ninety-two enabled passes in this order, with both fill-call slots withheld
under OD-155 and both comparison-call slots under OD-164:
- the copy respelling (`retype_copy`, `passes/simplify.rs`): a `copy T x`
  whose operand is an integer of another type of the same width (the
  bridge's sign-reinterpreting copy, which trust-ir's validator reports)
  becomes `bitcast` of `x` to `T`, the reading the lane and the
  differential's view give it, so the inliner copies no such finding into
  a caller. A `copy` of a thin pointer as another thin pointer type
  becomes `ptrtoptr` the same way. Checker rule
  `SimplifyRule::ReinterpretCopy`; a refinement (OD-151, OD-163);
- the operand respelling (`respell`, `passes/simplify.rs`, checker
  `rebuild_respell` in `trust_ir_mid_tv_fold.rs`): an `icmp` at a typed
  thin pointer (a slice iterator's position against its end) compares its
  operands cast to `ptr` by fresh `ptrtoptr`s, and a `memcopy` or `memset`
  whose byte count is a pointer-width unsigned integer other than `usize`
  (the bridge's `u32`) takes a fresh `usize` of it (a `const usize` of a
  constant count, else a `zext`). trust-ir's validator reports both
  spellings; the lane and the differential's view read them alike either
  way. Exact (OD-163);
- copy propagation of same-type copies;
- field-access lowering (`passes/field_access.rs`): the rustc bridge's
  `extractfield`/`insertfield` through a pointer becomes the load or store the
  lane emits for it, at a `gep u8` of the lane's byte offset from trust-ir's
  layout, when every use of a read reads its result as the lane's type (or,
  for a pointer lane, as the pointer of a load or `gep`) and a write's result
  is unused and its value of the lane's type. trust-ir's validator reports the
  pointer forms (`FieldAccessInvalid`) and its interpreter refuses them, so
  the rewrite is exact only relative to the lane's and the differential view's
  reading of them (OD-121). A pointer lane may also be read by a `copy` as
  another thin pointer type, which the copy respelling then makes a
  `ptrtoptr`;
- the copy respelling again;
- the pointer-chain rewrite: `inttoptr(ptrtoint(p) + k)` to `gep u8, p, [k]`,
  and the round trip `inttoptr(ptrtoint(p))` to a copy of `p`, only when `p`
  lies `d` bytes into an `alloca` of known size (count-free, or counted by an
  integer constant of at least 1) as the `alloca` itself or a pointer derived
  from it by copies, `ptrtoptr`s and `gep`s by non-negative constants, every
  step inside it, the integer is at least pointer-wide, and `k` is a constant
  with `0 <= d + k <` that size. `k` may be a constant expression (an integer
  constant, a same-width `bitcast` of one, or an `add` or `mul` of two such,
  every step in `[0, 2^(bits-1))`), which is folded into a fresh constant;
- copy propagation again;
- constant folding (`passes/const_fold.rs`): an integer or `bool` instruction
  of at most 64 bits whose operands are all constants of the width it
  declares, and that raises nothing on them (no division by zero, no
  overflowing signed division, no shift by the width or more), becomes the
  constant it computes: `add`, `sub`, `mul`, bitwise operations, rotates,
  shifts, divisions, remainders, `neg`, `not`, `icmp`, the boolean connectives
  and integer `zext`, `sext`, `trunc` and same-width `bitcast`. A `bool`
  constant the bridge spells as the integer 0 or 1 is respelled `const bool`.
  Exact (OD-120);
- the memory-call rewrite (`passes/mem_call.rs`): a call of a function the
  module only declares, named `memmove`, `memcpy` or `memset`, with the C
  prototype becomes `memcopy overlap`, `memcopy` or `memset` of a fresh
  `const usize` of the count (a `memset` fill truncated to `u8` by a fresh
  `trunc`). The C prototype here means three parameters, not variadic, and
  one pointer-like result; a pointer-like destination; a pointer-like source
  or an integer fill of 9 to 32 bits; and an unsigned count of pointer
  width. The call's pointer arguments must be pointer-like, its fill and
  count must have their parameter's types, its count must be an integer
  constant and its result must be unused. Its checker
  (`trust_ir_mid_tv_memcall.rs`) re-derives each of these on the source.
  Exact under the premise that such a call performs the C library's
  operation (OD-141), the open debt OD-143 records: a module import or an
  undefined object symbol may link another implementation under the name.
  A function the module defines under one of those names keeps its call,
  and so does any call of a run-time count. Round 17's widening to a
  `memmove` or `memcpy` of a run-time count (OD-165: the count `zext`ed to
  `usize`, the lane's guarded `memory.copy`) is **withheld** from the
  default pipeline at its merge with OD-155 (OD-165's merge boundary):
  it extends the open premise to more calls. The pass keeps it for its
  tests, and its checker still re-derives such a witness under the
  premise. The interpreter differential's view gives such declarations
  the C library's bodies;
- the comparison-call rewrite (`mem_cmp`, `passes/mem_cmp.rs`, checker
  `trust_ir_mid_tv_memcmp.rs`) is **withheld** from the default pipeline
  (OD-164): it would read a declaration named `memcmp` or `bcmp` with the
  C prototype as C's comparison, a new name-based premise of the kind
  OD-143 and OD-155 leave unauthenticated. The call stays and
  `passes_withheld` names `mem_cmp`. What the pass does when a test runs
  it: a direct call of such a declaration (two pointer-like parameters, an
  unsigned integer count of pointer width, a 32-bit integer result), both
  compared operands pointer-like and the count an integer constant `k <=
  16`, becomes the constant 0 (`k = 0`), the difference of the two bytes
  read as unsigned chars (`k = 1`), or, only when every use of the result
  is an `icmp eq` or `ne` with the constant 0, the xors of the operands'
  8-, 4-, 2- and 1-byte chunks or-ed together and `zext` of that being
  nonzero (`k >= 2`). Exact under the premise that such a call performs
  C's comparison over the `k` bytes C requires to exist (OD-164). The
  differential's view gives such a declaration no body; only the
  checker's tests run in a view that gives it one comparing every byte
  pair and returning the first difference;
- the fill-call rewrite is **withheld** (OD-155). A declaration named
  `__trustcg_array_fill_iW` with the bridge's helper prototype is not
  authority for its implementation: ordinary module imports and object
  undefined symbols may link a different host function. Every nonempty
  `FillCallWitness` refuses without source-bound helper custody; the default
  pipeline retains the call and reports the missing contract. The
  differential no longer invents a helper loop for these declarations.
  Restore this optimization through authenticated producer bulk operations
  or a checked original owned helper body, not a name/prefix allowlist;

The bridge's frame-sharing prepass also retains external byte-fill calls;
its former name-only replacement ran even at O0 and supplied no helper
custody. Private-slot forwarding and allocation sinking are retained. A
retained fill call captures its array's address, so arrays in disjoint
scopes that a repeat expression fills no longer share frame bytes: the
bridge differential corpus's `fr_two_scopes` exhausts the 1 MiB stack at
`-Copt-level=1` and above, and `wasm32_differential` fails on
`r5-bridge-iter-frames` until fill custody is restored (OD-167).

- the byte-copy rewrite (`passes/byte_copy.rs`, checker
  `trust_ir_mid_tv_bytecopy.rs`), two steps in one witness (OD-149). A run
  of at least two byte loads and stores in one block that copies
  consecutive bytes of one allocation to the same offsets of another, with
  only `const`, `copy`, cast, `gep` and integer arithmetic between them,
  becomes one `memcopy` at its last store. Allocations are an `alloca`, an
  entry parameter or a global's address, through copies, `ptrtoptr`s and
  `gep`s by non-negative constants; two ranges are disjoint only when they
  lie in different `alloca`s, in an `alloca` and a parameter or global, in
  different globals, or in disjoint bytes of one base, so two parameters
  are never assumed disjoint. A refinement: a byte load of part of a
  pointer drops its provenance where `memcopy` keeps it. Then a `memcopy`
  of a constant count out of an `alloca` that does not escape, whose copied
  bytes earlier stores of the same block cover exactly with no other write
  into the slot since the first of them, becomes those stores made into
  the destination at the same offsets (alignment 1); exact. Overlap,
  effects inside the run, escaping slots and partial coverage leave the
  code alone;
- constant-branch folding with unreachable-block removal;
- dead-code elimination of an allowlist that excludes every instruction whose
  definedness depends on its operands' values and the bridge's write-through
  `insertfield` (a load or `gep` is on it only when its address is a fresh
  allocation or a global, directly or through `gep`s by constants, `ptrtoptr`s
  and copies), except that a dead `inttoptr` from `isize`, `usize` or an
  integer of at most 32 bits, and a dead shift by a constant below the width
  or division or remainder by a constant that cannot fault (nonzero, and for a
  signed one not all ones, read at the operation's width) at a fixed integer
  width other than `isize`/`usize`, are removed as refinements (OD-117);
- the memory cleanup before inlining: store forwarding, removal of dead
  slot stores and scalar replacement (as described below), copy propagation
  and dead-code elimination over every function before any callee is
  spliced, so a callee whose only `alloca` is a temporary it promotes is
  spliced as a frameless body, also into a caller's loop (OD-150);
- call-site inlining (the OPT-4 inliner ported to trust-ir), visiting callees
  before callers. A direct `call` of a function defined in the module with
  `external`, `internal` or `private` linkage becomes a renamed copy of its
  body: the entry parameters are bound to the arguments (a thin pointer of
  another pointer type through `ptrtoptr`), and the returns are joined into
  the call's results. An array parameter (of scalars) that the bridge
  passes by the address of its bytes is bound to a fresh `load` of the
  array from that thin pointer, and a thin pointer a callee's `ret`
  returns for an array result is read by a fresh `load` of it at the call,
  the differential's view's own reading of both (OD-162); policy: only when
  every use of the parameter or of the call's result reads a lane. Never
  spliced: a recursive callee; a declaration; one
  another definition may replace at link time (`weak`, `linkonce`, their ODR
  forms, `extern_weak`, `available_externally`); a naked, variadic or
  feature-stating one; one with a parameter passed by copy; one carrying
  proof annotations, call-site proof context, a summary, source provenance
  or a body gate, or named by a module obligation; one with
  exception-handling, coroutine, ownership, binding-frame or dialect
  instructions. A spliced `alloca` is a slot of the caller's frame for its
  whole activation, so an allocating callee is never spliced when one of its
  `alloca`s lies on a cycle of its own, into a block on a cycle of the
  caller (unless every `alloca` of the callee is a return slot, returned by
  address and otherwise only the address of plain loads and stores,
  directly or through constant `gep`s: no pointer to it outlives the
  iteration, so the lane keeps one frame slot and the interpreter allocates
  it per iteration as the source did per call; OD-162), or into a caller on
  a cycle of direct calls, and the slots spliced
  into one caller total at most 1,024 bytes; a recursion
  through calls the module does not show (a vtable, another crate) can
  therefore hold up to 1,024 more stack bytes per level than the source.
  `#[inline(never)]` and `#[cold]` functions stay calls; they come from the
  rustc bridge's side table (`WasmInlineHints`), so another producer's
  callees have no such hint, though a trust-ir `cold` attribute is honoured.
  A callee still using the bridge's field access through a pointer (one
  field-access lowering left in place) also stays a call. The size budget,
  in trust-ir instructions: at most 12 and no
  `alloca`, inlined at every call; a single call site of a non-exported,
  never address-taken callee, up to 400; otherwise loop-free callees up to
  40, while the caller grows by at most its own size (at least 256) and the
  module by at most 25% (at least 256). A single-call-site callee another
  object references (another codegen unit) keeps its out-of-line copy, so
  the linked module grows by the copy;
- copy propagation, then lane-load scalarization (`lane_load`,
  `passes/lane_load.rs`, checker `trust_ir_mid_tv_lanes.rs`): a
  non-volatile `load` of an array of scalars (integers, floats, `bool`,
  `char`, thin pointers) whose result is read by `extractfield` at the
  array's type gains, right after it, a `load` of each lane read (alignment
  1, at a fresh `gep u8` of the lane's offset from the interpreter's
  layout), and each read becomes a `copy` of its lane's load; exact
  (OD-162). Then field-access lowering and the copy respelling again, the
  pointer-chain GEP rewrite, copy propagation and dead-code elimination,
  over the spliced bodies;
- single-dominating-store forwarding: a load from a frame slot used only by
  plain loads and stores (directly or at a constant byte offset) becomes the
  stored value when one store is, on every path, the last write of exactly
  its bytes. Only integer, `bool`, `char` and float values of the load's own
  type are forwarded; pointers, partial overlaps, mixed widths, undefined
  reads and irreducible CFGs are left alone;
- removal of the stores of such a slot that nothing reads any more;
- scalar replacement: a frame slot (an `alloca` count-free or counted by an
  integer constant of at least 1) reached only through plain loads and
  stores, `gep`s by constants, `ptrtoptr`s to thin pointers, copies and the
  rustc bridge's field access through a pointer (a write-through
  `insertfield` only when its result is unused, a read-through
  `extractfield` only when its result is read as the lane's type) becomes
  one SSA value per field, joined by new block parameters. A field is a
  maximal run of overlapping access ranges. A run of one range of at most 8
  bytes, or of 16 bytes accessed only as 128-bit integers, is carried as its
  access type when it has one, else as an integer of its width, and an
  access of another type of the same width is a `bitcast`, or for a pointer
  a `ptrtoint`/`inttoptr` through `ptr`, applied only to values that can
  never be the poison image of uninitialized bytes. A one-byte field
  accessed as `bool` and as a one-byte integer is carried as the integer: a
  `bool` store is its `zext`, a `bool` load the nonzero test `icmp ne c, 0`
  against a fresh zero (the reference interpreter reads a `bool` byte as
  nonzero), and no store of the field may leave it poison. A field read
  and written only as thin pointers, every store writing an address
  strictly inside a fresh allocation, is carried as the pointer itself (the
  interpreter's allocations never overlap and are never reused), so the
  pointee can be promoted next. A run of several ranges of 2, 4 or 8 bytes
  in all (the bridge's word copies over narrower fields) is carried as one
  unsigned integer whose parts are shifted and masked; every value stored
  into it must never be poison. A read of the slot itself counts as never
  poison when every value stored into the slot is (once promoted the read
  is the field's carrier, which holds only the initial zero, the stored
  values and merges of them; OD-150), so a loop that reloads a field, steps
  it and stores it back keeps the field promotable. A read only the
  `alloca` reaches gives an integer field an initial zero, a refinement of
  the source's poison, not an exact rewrite. Slots whose address reaches
  a call, is indexed by a variable, is observed as an integer or is copied
  by bulk memory, volatile and atomic accesses, other fields wider than 8
  bytes, other partial overlaps, conversions of values that may be poison,
  undefined reads of non-integer fields, a stored `undef`, joins at the
  entry or behind an unwind edge, unreachable blocks and irreducible CFGs
  leave the slot or the function alone. Its checker re-derives the slot, the
  fields, the conversions and the parts on the source and proves each read's
  value by walking every backward CFG path to the store or join that defines
  it; each rewritten access counts as a refinement;
- constant-table promotion: a local table written only with integer or `bool`
  constants, read within proven bounds, whose address is never observed or
  passed on, becomes a new internal read-only global. A byte read before its
  store reads the table's byte (undefined bytes become 0), a refinement. It
  and the CRC-table rewrite below are the passes that add static data, so
  they run only where the memory layout
  follows the module emitted: objects (the linker places data apart from the
  stack) and the sized closed module of the CLI's route, whose owned pages
  grow so that the optimized module keeps at least the input's shadow stack.
  Under a caller's fixed module policy (a page count, or a host-reserved data
  region) they are withheld and named in the report's `passes_withheld`;
- copy propagation;
- by-address cloning (`byaddr`, `passes/byaddr.rs`, checker
  `trust_ir_mid_tv_byaddr.rs`): a plain `call` passing a thin pointer for
  an array parameter (of scalars) of a callee under the bridge's
  crate-private name, strong and hidden, without proof material, whose
  every entry parameter has exactly its declared type and whose every use
  of the parameter is a lane read in its prologue, calls a clone that
  takes `ptr` and loads the lanes. The prologue is the longest prefix of
  the entry block made only of count-free `alloca`s, `const`, `gep`,
  casts, `copy`, `binop`, `unop`, `icmp`, `select`, plain loads,
  `extractfield`s of the parameters the clone promotes, and `insertfield`s
  and plain stores into an `alloca` of that prefix (or a `gep` of one by
  constant indices); any other form ends it, even one that writes no
  memory (`globaladdr`, `overflow`, `fcmp`, `nullptr`, `undef`) or only
  the callee's own slot (a `memset` of it), so a callee with such a form
  ahead of its lane copies gets no by-address clone. A slot the prologue
  fills lane by lane from the parameter, read afterwards only by loads, is
  replaced by the parameter, and its copies go, only when every
  instruction of the callee is on an allowlist: value-only forms, plain
  non-volatile loads, count-free `alloca`s, `br`, `condbr`, `switch` and
  `ret`, and stores, write-through `insertfield`s, `memcopy`s and
  `memset`s into its own slots. An `insertfield` is otherwise admitted
  only over an operand typed (a block parameter, copy, load, constant or
  cast) as an aggregate value (a struct, tuple, array, record or enum),
  never over a pointer carrier (a thin pointer, or the wasm32 lane's
  `i64`/`u64` address), a type not named or an untyped value (a `select`,
  an `undef`, another `insertfield`'s result, so a chained value
  `insertfield` keeps the slot). `dealloc`, `drop`, `retain`, `release`,
  every call and every form not named keep the slot. The argument must be
  typed a thin pointer by the same rule. The pass reads a callee by its
  own copy of the checker's prologue and typing, which a test of the
  checker compares with the checker's over a corpus of shapes, and
  refuses, as the checker does, a clone that would keep a thin-pointer
  parameter entered as another pointer type than declared, so it proposes
  no clone the checker refuses on any of these. A refinement: the clone
  reads the bytes the call saw (OD-166). Policy: only parameters with such
  a slot and more than eight lanes or read wider than a lane (a packed
  struct's bytes read as an `f64`); the clone carries argument promotion's
  name mark, counts toward its sixteen clones and is withheld with it
  (`passes_withheld` key `byaddr`); it runs before argument promotion,
  which would otherwise pass the lanes as values into a clone that still
  copies them;
- argument promotion, visiting callees first. A frame slot (an `alloca`
  count-free or counted by an integer constant of at least 1) whose address,
  through copies, `ptrtoptr`s, `gep`s by constants and the bridge's integer
  address chains, reaches nothing but plain loads and stores, the bridge's
  field access through a pointer and arguments of plain `call`s of functions
  defined in the module with `external`, `internal` or `private` linkage, at
  parameters those callees use only that way at constant offsets, is passed
  to a clone of one such callee as the values of the scalar fields
  (integers, floats, `bool`, `char`, thin pointers) the callee reads through
  the parameter, and the clone returns the fields it writes after its own
  results, which the caller stores back. A parameter of an aggregate type
  the bridge passes by address is promoted to the lanes the callee reads,
  under the same slot premises. Only a callee under the bridge's
  crate-private name (`<symbol>.tcg.crate.<tag>`), strong and hidden, not
  variadic, naked or feature-stating, with no parameter passed by copy, no
  proof material and at most 400 instructions, is cloned, and only when
  every parameter the clone keeps is of exactly its declared type at the
  callee's entry (a kept thin pointer of another pointer type would copy
  the callee's `EntryParamsMismatch`). The clone is a strong hidden
  function `<symbol>.tcg.ap<h>.tcg.crate.<tag>` in the same object, so the
  internal multi-value ABI returns its results in registers when the
  session allows the `multivalue` feature. With the feature withheld
  (`-C target-cpu=mvp`, or `-multivalue` last) the clone keeps its C form
  and its extra results come back through that form's `sret` buffer in
  memory; the mid-end is not told the session's choice and makes such
  clones anyway. The original callee stays for every other caller. No other argument of the
  call may be derived from the slot, and a call carrying a proof annotation
  or proof context is not promoted. Every byte copied in at the call (an
  aggregate's lanes included: the lane reads an aggregate passed by address
  where the callee extracts each lane, and `[MaybeUninit<T>; N]` reaches
  trust-ir as `[T x N]`), and every byte copied out at a `ret` of the clone,
  must be last written on every path by a value that is never poison, so a
  lane written from a load, or one that covers padding, stays in memory.
  Policy: at most four wasm results (one for a Rust-convention callee), no
  copied-out field beside an aggregate result, eight fields and 64 bytes
  per parameter, sixteen parameters per clone and sixteen clones per
  module, and no clone that keeps the bridge's field access through a
  pointer parameter. Its checker (`trust_ir_mid_tv_argpromo.rs`) shares
  only the clone-name function with the pass: it re-derives each site's
  admission, fields, slot containment and never-poison bytes by its own
  backward walks, mints the clone's fresh values itself, and rebuilds the
  clone and the call exactly. Each promoted call is checked as a refinement
  of the reference interpreter's semantics, not as an exact rewrite (the
  clone allocates its own copy of the bytes on every call, and for an
  aggregate passed by address the argument reads lanes that nothing else
  can write during the call);
- the pointer-chain rewrite, copy propagation and dead-code elimination
  again, over the clones and the rewritten callers;
- scalar replacement again, and copy propagation;
- constant folding, the memory-call and byte-copy rewrites again
  (on the counts inlining and argument promotion made constant, and the
  copies inlining brought together), algebraic simplification
  (`passes/simplify.rs`) and copy propagation. Simplification turns into a
  `copy` (or a `trunc` of the low
  part) an operation by its identity element (`x + 0`, `x | 0`, `x >> 0`, a
  rotate by 0, `x * 1`, `x & ~0`), a mask over an extension's bits, a
  truncation of an extension back to its source, a bitcast round trip, and the
  low and high parts of a pair scalar replacement packed (`trunc c` and `trunc
  (c >> 32)` of `c = (zext a) | (zext b << 32)`). It also turns a `rotl x, c`
  with `0 < c < width`, whose every use in the function is an `and` of its
  type with a constant below `2^c`, into `lshr x, width - c` by a fresh
  constant (V8's Liftoff calls out of line for a rotate; OD-124). It also
  turns `sub a, b` at the pointer width, where `a` is `add r, x` and `b` is
  `r` behind address-preserving casts (`copy`, `ptrtoptr`, pointer-width
  `ptrtoint`/`inttoptr`/`bitcast`), into `copy x` (a slice's end minus its
  start is its length; `SimplifyRule::PointerDifference`, OD-160). Each
  rewrite is a refinement: the source's operation inspects its operands
  where a `copy` does not;
- the select-branch rules (`select_branch`, `passes/select_branch.rs`,
  checker `trust_ir_mid_tv_selbr.rs`; OD-160): a `switch` or `condbr` whose
  scrutinee the checker's evaluator decides under each value of a `bool` of
  its operand chain becomes `condbr` on that `bool` (or `br` when both
  values take one edge), provided the block defining the `bool` dominates
  it; a refinement. The blocks the rewrite leaves unreachable are removed.
  The evaluator reads constants, `null`, selects on known conditions,
  casts, compares and integer arithmetic, and the value an equality pins
  (`p == 0` assumed true makes `p` zero). It also assumes that an `alloca`
  of known size plus a constant offset at most that size is not the
  address 0. Under an edge that fixes the `bool`, an operand that is a
  `select` on it behind at most four casts (the pass forwards through at
  most two) reads its arm through fresh copies of the casts placed before
  its use (exact). The edge is the `then` or `else` edge of a `condbr` with
  two different targets, and it fixes the `bool` when that `condbr` is on
  the `bool` itself, or when the evaluator decides its condition against
  the edge if the `bool` takes the other value. The edge must enter a block
  other than the function's entry (the call enters the entry too) that no
  other edge enters, and that block must dominate the use's block.
  Policy: only edge arguments and addresses (a pointer cast, a `gep` base,
  a load's or store's pointer) are forwarded, and a terminator whose `then`
  edge would lead to a block ending in `unreachable` while its `else` edge
  does not is left alone. They run again after each unrolling and in the
  late round below;
- the range rules (the native lanes' LIR unsigned-range simplification,
  `lir_unsigned_range`, ported to trust-ir, with path and loop facts). A
  value's fact is an interval of its raw bits derived from its definition
  (constants, `and` masks, `zext`/`trunc`/`sext`/same-width `bitcast`,
  non-wrapping `add`/`sub`/`mul`, `lshr`/`urem` by a known amount,
  `select`, and decided compares and overflow flags, narrowed where
  trust-ir's `propagate` derives a fact), with two narrowings. In a block
  entered by a single edge (every edge of every terminator counted), the
  `then` or `else` edge of a `condbr` with distinct targets on an integer
  `icmp`, and in every block that edge's target dominates, the compared
  values are narrowed to the hull of their values that satisfy the
  compare, and a later compare of the same two values that the dominating
  one decides is folded (`icmp_implied`). A block parameter may carry an
  interval that holds on every incoming edge (a loop induction range: the
  initial value lies in it, and the step stays in it under the dominating
  exit test). Nothing flows across a join another edge reaches, and
  nothing comes from loads, calls or `switch` edges; a value derived before
  a guard (`zext i` above a check of `i`) is not narrowed; two block
  parameters that always carry equal values are not related; and signed
  intervals that cross zero are not represented, so a possibly negative
  signed counter keeps its overflow check. A compare the intervals or a
  dominating compare decide becomes a constant (signed predicates only when
  each interval stays on one side of the sign boundary). An
  `add`/`sub`/`mul.overflow` that cannot overflow (unsigned, or signed over
  non-negative operands) becomes the plain arithmetic and a `false` flag. A
  `select`, `assert` or `condbr` on a decided condition becomes a copy of
  its arm, nothing, or a branch. A `switch` drops the cases outside its
  value's interval, takes a remaining case as its default when the cases
  cover the interval (and no longer claims exhaustiveness), and becomes a
  branch when one edge is left. The blocks a folded branch leaves
  unreachable are removed. Each rewrite names its rule and one interval
  premise per operand, in the rewrite's block; the witness also lists the
  claimed block-parameter intervals. The checker computes its own reverse
  postorder and dominator tree and finds each single-edge guard and its
  condition itself; it assumes the claimed intervals and checks each on
  every edge from a reachable block (entry and step), accepts a premise
  only when it contains the interval it derives, decides the rule from the
  premises alone and rebuilds the target exactly, so each rewrite is exact.
  The pass and the checker each index the guarded blocks by
  dominator-tree preorder, so a deep guard chain is folded and checked in
  time linear in its size. The compare, narrowing, implication and overflow
  decisions are checked against brute force only at widths up to 4 bits;
  35 solver lemmas (fact rows, overflow and compare decisions, guard
  narrowings, the induction step and three implications) are checked by
  tests, never per compile. On the measuring host `ay` answered UNSAT for
  31 of them at 8 bits, none with a certified proof, and `unknown` for the
  multiplication and remainder ones; no overflow rewrite obligation has a
  solver answer;
- closed-form induction (`passes/loop_cf.rs`, the native lanes'
  `loop_iv` counted-loop recognizer lifted to trust-ir). Every loop pass
  of this list and its checker (closed-form induction, full and
  interval-bounded unrolling, invariant code motion, strength reduction)
  takes a natural loop only when its header is not the function's entry
  block and its preheader is reachable: the call enters the entry with
  any arguments, so an unreachable block branching to an entry header
  would otherwise pass for the preheader and lend its arguments as the
  start values (round 17's final review found this accepted by full,
  interval-bounded and closed-form rewrites through the CLI, OD-159). A
  natural loop qualifies for the closed form when all of the following
  hold. Its header is entered from outside by exactly one edge, from a
  preheader ending in `br` to the header, and from inside by exactly one
  back edge. The header ends in the
  loop's only exit, a `condbr` on an `icmp` defined in the header that
  continues while `i <u n`, `i <s n` or `i != n` (either operand order,
  either edge), where `i` is a header parameter stepping by exactly `+ 1`
  and `n` is a bound of `i`'s type defined outside the loop (or passed back
  unchanged). Its other blocks form no cycle, end in `br`, `condbr` or
  `switch` within the loop and hold only instructions on the dead-code
  table, and their values are not used after the loop. Its other header
  parameters are passed back unchanged or are accumulators `p + t`,
  `t + p` or `p - t` (also the value of an `add.overflow`/`sub.overflow`
  whose flag nothing reads), with `t` a constant or invariant `b`, or
  `x`, `a * x` or `x * a` where `x` is the induction variable at its own
  type, its `zext` under `<u` or its `sext` under `<s` (the accumulator at
  least as wide). Such a loop is replaced by its trip count and each
  accumulator's final value `p0 +- (a * (N * x0 + T(N)) + b * N)`,
  computed at the end of the preheader modulo the accumulator's width,
  with `T(N) = N (N - 1) / 2` computed by halving the even factor first;
  the trip count at each wider type and the induction sum at each type and
  extension are computed once and shared. The header then runs once, on
  the source's last values, and branches to the exit; the loop's other
  blocks go. A closed loop can leave its enclosing loop closable, so the
  pass looks again (at most 64 times). Initial values and value
  coefficients must have the accumulator's type, the bound the induction
  variable's, and all of them must be never poison by the checker's
  greatest fixed point (entry parameters; constants; integer, float,
  compare, cast and overflow results; copies, selects and block
  parameters of such values), since the loop may run zero times. The
  algebra (trip count per exit, the non-wrapping extension, the triangular
  step, the accumulator's induction step) is eight lemmas, checked
  exhaustively at 3 and 4 bits and handed to `ay` at 8 bits by tests
  (seven UNSAT, uncertified; `acc:step` times out and proves nothing);
  it is not a per-compile proof. The rewrite is exact when every removed
  instruction is in the dead-code table's exact class, else a refinement
  (a removed instruction that inspects a value may raise undefined
  behaviour the source loop would have raised);
- full unrolling (`passes/unroll.rs`, the native lanes' constant-trip unroll
  lifted to trust-ir), inner loops first and repeated until nothing changes. A
  natural loop qualifies when it has a dedicated preheader and one back edge,
  its other blocks form no cycle, its header ends in a `condbr` on an `icmp`
  it computes with one edge leaving the loop, and its blocks end in `br`,
  `condbr`, `switch`, `ret` or `unreachable`. The compare must be decided on
  every visit: each operand reads as a constant, a value from before the loop
  or a header parameter, plus a constant offset, through `copy`, same-width
  `bitcast`, the address casts at pointer width, `add` and `sub` of a
  constant, `mul` of constants and `gep u8` by a constant, where a header
  parameter whose back-edge argument reads as itself plus `s` holds `init + k
  * s` on visit `k`; equality compares are decided on a shared root, ordered
  ones on constants. Other exits are kept (OD-118): a block entered by one
  side exit alone that leaves without re-entering the loop, and whose values
  nothing else reads, is copied with each iteration; other code after the loop
  may use only the header's values. Policy (OD-122): at most 16 trips (the
  checker accepts 32) and at most 1,024 copied instructions (the checker's own
  bound), of which at most 256 are estimated to survive constant folding
  (constants and frame-slot addresses propagated over the whole function, an
  induction variable starting at a slot address included); no copy that
  would keep a call or a 128-bit arithmetic operation, compare, select, load
  or store, other than a load or store through a frame slot at a constant
  offset (OD-142; extensions and truncations do not count); no
  `alloca` in the loop; every copied instruction one trust-ir's validator
  reads without a finding. Its checker (`trust_ir_mid_tv_unroll.rs`)
  recomputes the trip count from the source and rebuilds every copy. Every
  visit of the source loop is a copy executing the same instructions on the
  same values; a dropped copy of the exit compare makes the rewrite a
  refinement (an `icmp` faults on poison operands);
- interval-bounded unrolling (`bounded_unroll`, `passes/bounded_unroll.rs`,
  checker `trust_ir_mid_tv_bounded.rs`; OD-159): a loop of full unrolling's
  shape whose header ends in `condbr` or `switch` and leaves the loop on
  visit `B` becomes `B` copies of its iterations that keep their exit
  tests, and a last header visit that branches along the proven exit. The
  checker evaluates the header on visit `B` itself: its induction variables
  are constant there, and values from before the loop are read by
  intervals the checker derives from their definitions (constants, masks,
  remainders and quotients by constants, non-wrapping `add` and `mul`,
  casts, `select` hulls, a block parameter as the hull of its incoming
  arguments, and a parameter of the function's entry block as its type's
  whole range, since the call enters the entry too). Values of the loop
  are read outside it only by exit blocks, which each copy takes along.
  Exact. Policy: `B <= 8` (the checker admits 16) and full unrolling's
  cost model. Full and interval-bounded unrolling type an overflow
  operation's value and flag for their copies' substitution check (an
  `enumerate` counter is an `add.overflow`'s value);
- their cleanup: constant folding, the select-branch rules (on the copies'
  exit tests), simplification, copy propagation and constant-branch
  folding; address folding (`passes/addr_fold.rs`: an
  `inttoptr` to `ptr` whose integer reads, through the bridge's address casts
  and constant offsets, as an `alloca` (count-free or counted by a positive
  constant) or global of known size that dominates it, plus a constant inside
  it, becomes `gep inbounds u8` of that allocation, or a `copy` at offset
  zero; exact); copy propagation and dead-code elimination; dead block
  parameters (`passes/dead_param.rs`: the greatest set of non-entry block
  parameters that no instruction reads, at most passed on to another such
  parameter, goes with their arguments when every entering edge is a `br`,
  `condbr` or `switch` passing the parameter's type; exact); dead-code
  elimination; block merging (`passes/merge.rs`: a block one edge enters takes
  that edge's arguments for its parameters, and when the edge is its
  predecessor's `br` the two become one, only when every argument has its
  parameter's type and trust-ir's validator reads every moved instruction
  without a finding; exact); store forwarding, dead-slot removal, scalar
  replacement and copy propagation, then scalar replacement and copy
  propagation again (a slot whose stored values were reads of a slot the one
  before promoted, an iterator adapter's state copied out of its
  constructor's, is promotable only then);
- a late round: the select-branch rules, the range rules and
  interval-bounded unrolling again (a `Zip`'s state is in values only
  now, and its index steps through a `select` the rules forward under the
  loop's branch), with the same cleanup once (constant folding, the
  select-branch rules, simplification, copy propagation, branch and
  address folding, dead-code elimination, dead block parameters, block
  merging, store forwarding, dead-slot removal, scalar replacement and copy
  propagation);
- constant folding, the select-branch rules and the range rules again (a
  second range run folds the `Err` flag switches the first one's folds
  expose), then block merging;
- the CRC-table rewrite (`crc_table`, `passes/crc_table.rs`, checker
  `trust_ir_mid_tv_crctable.rs`; OD-161): a pure acyclic region of integer
  operations (a block's tail ending in `condbr` or `switch` and the blocks
  it reaches before a join with one parameter, entered only from inside)
  becomes `global_addr`, the input as `i32`, a multiply by the entry size,
  an in-bounds `gep` and one load from a fresh read-only internal global of
  the region's 256 results, each computed by the checker running the region
  (exhaustive; exact). The region must have one non-constant input, which
  the checker bounds below 256 from its definition (an `and` with a
  constant, a `zext` of a byte, a `urem` or `lshr` by a constant), no value
  read outside it, and its xors with a constant must all name one
  polynomial. Equal tables of a function share one global. Policy: at
  least four xors of the polynomial and sixteen instructions, and a result
  of one, two, four or eight bytes. Like constant-table promotion it adds
  static data, so a caller's fixed module policy withholds it
  (`passes_withheld` key `crc_table`); then block merging again;
- loop-invariant code motion (`passes/licm.rs`, the tiers of the native
  lanes' `licm` restated over trust-ir's poison semantics and operand
  types), per loop with such a preheader, innermost first. A header
  parameter every back edge passes back unchanged becomes the preheader's
  argument, which must have the parameter's type. An instruction whose
  operands are defined outside the loop (or by an instruction already
  moved) moves to the end of the preheader in either of two cases. Case
  one: it is speculatable on operands that are never poison and have the
  types its form declares, by the checker's own typing (a value it cannot
  type, such as a call result, is refused). The speculatable forms are
  constants at their own type (an integer, `bool`, `u128` or float
  constant, a null `ptr`, and the bridge's global-address stub of a module
  global at offset zero at a pointer type; a stub with an offset, which
  the differential reads through a `gep`, and an integer constant at any
  other type stay in the loop), null pointers and global addresses;
  integer `add`, `sub`, `mul`, bitwise operations and rotates; float `add`,
  `sub`, `mul` and `div`; shifts by a constant below the width; unsigned
  division and remainder by a nonzero constant and signed ones by a
  constant other than 0 and -1 (an amount or divisor is the bits the
  constant holds at the operation's width, read signed by a signed
  division whatever the type's signedness, as the interpreter reads it:
  `sdiv u32 x, 4294967295` divides by -1 and is not speculatable, nor is a
  `usize` division by 4294967296 at wasm32's 32-bit width); compares of
  integers, `bool`s and floats;
  `zext`, `sext`, `trunc`, integer and float `bitcast`s, `uitofp`,
  `sitofp`, `fpext` and `fptrunc` (no float-to-int conversion, raw or
  saturating, although the saturating ones are total), and
  `ptrtoptr`; `ptrtoint`; `inttoptr` of an integer at most pointer-wide in
  a loop that allocates, frees and calls nothing; `select` on a `bool`,
  `copy` and overflow operations. Case two: it is in the header after only
  quiet instructions (no call, `assert`, store, allocation or atomic); this
  also admits a division, remainder or shift of any operands, a `gep`, an
  `inttoptr` of any integer width in a loop that allocates, frees and calls
  nothing, and a non-volatile load only when every instruction of the loop is
  quiet (tier (a)) or its only other instructions are quiet ones and
  non-volatile stores to other bytes (tier (b)): the load and every store at
  an address that reads as an `alloca` or `global_addr` plus an in-bounds
  constant, each store to another allocation or to disjoint bytes of the same
  one, where an allocation is identified by its `alloca` instruction or by its
  global's name (every `global_addr` of one global, and two module globals
  sharing a symbol name, are the same allocation; OD-123). A load beside a
  call, an atomic, a store through any other address, overlapping bytes or a
  store past its allocation stays in the loop.
  Only instructions that cost a wasm operation move (arithmetic, compares,
  selects, loads, `gep`s, widening and narrowing casts), with the free
  instructions and constants they read, and never a constant expression
  (operands all constants), which the local emission pass folds or
  rematerializes where it is used. Every move is exact: the moved
  instruction computes the same value from the same operands and raises
  only where the source does;
- strength reduction (`passes/iv_sr.rs`, the native lanes' `strength_reduce`
  and `ptr_iv_sr` lifted to trust-ir), per loop with a dedicated preheader and
  one back edge. The induction variables are header parameters stepping by a
  constant `s` from a never-poison initial value of their integer type. A loop
  value of an integer type that wide, read (through constants, copies,
  same-width casts, the address casts, `add`, `sub`, and `mul` and `shl` by
  constants) as `A * i + R + c` with `A` not 0, 1 or -1 and `R` a never-poison
  value from before the loop (a pointer or an integer of the width) or none,
  becomes `q + c` for a new header parameter `q` that starts at `A * i0 + R`
  and steps by `A * s`, when some use of it is not itself replaced; values
  sharing `(i, A, R, type)` share one parameter. Its checker
  (`trust_ir_mid_tv_ivsr.rs`) reads every value again with its own code,
  rebuilds the rewrite and proves `q`'s invariant by induction over the
  header's edges, modulo the width. Exact;
- copy propagation and dead-code elimination again.

At O0, or with the bridge knob `no-wasm-irmid`, none of them runs; at O1, O2
and O3 the same ninety-two run. There is no constant CSE; no if-conversion
of a branch whose arms only compute (measured slower on the harness, OD-150);
no rewrite of unauthenticated array-fill helper calls (OD-155) or of
`memcmp`/`bcmp` calls (OD-164); no unrolling of a
loop with a run-time trip count that no derived interval bounds by eight
trips; no closed form of `RangeInclusive`'s exhausted flag (the
select-branch rules remove the `switch` on its `select`, not the flag); an
unrolling cost model without a
profile, which refuses only copies that keep a call or a 128-bit operation
(an unrolled loop's code still grows where the loop pays, `inline_machine`
147 -> 672 code bytes on the harness, and also in loops the workload seldom
runs, `it_sum` +252 bytes for 0.4% fewer executed instructions); no scalar
replacement of a field read through another type, except a `bool` read as a
one-byte integer; no rewrite of a memory call with a run-time count by
default (OD-165's merge boundary), of a `memcmp` or `bcmp` call at all by
default (the comparison-call rewrite is
withheld, OD-164; run by a test, it leaves a run-time count, more than 16
bytes or a multi-byte comparison whose sign is read alone); no
specialization of a callee for a constant argument (so no harness
program's `memcmp` has a constant count when the mid-end runs); no forwarding of a `memcopy` out of a
read-only global; and no folding of loads from a read-only table's
initializer. For each pass
and each
function, the rewrite is kept only when `trust_cg_verify::trust_ir_mid_tv`
accepts its witness and the
reference interpreter finds no disagreement on its seeded inputs (eight,
plus two aliasing inputs for a function with two or more pointer or slice
parameters); otherwise
that function keeps its body from before the pass (a rollback, never a
refusal). The witness checker rebuilds the rewritten function from the source
and the claimed rewrites and re-derives slots and tables on the source with
trust-ir's layout; it is structural, shares trust-ir's layout and operand
walk, and is not an SMT proof. An inline splice is checked by rebuilding the
caller and by OPT-4's self-checks (well-formed CFG, single definitions,
opcode and effect conservation), and its checker re-derives admission, the
argument binding, freshness and the stack bound. A splice is counted as a
refinement, because a call's own checks (no poison argument or result,
exact argument types) go away with the call. The stack bound is a resource
condition the interpreter differential cannot observe, since the
interpreter never frees an `alloca`.

The differential builds inputs for scalar, pointer, slice and by-value
aggregate parameters. Memory for a pointer is planned from the function's
own accesses (followed four calls and three pointer slots deep) and the
interpreter's layout, filled with seeded small values, and passed by a
driver function. Each pointer parameter gets its own objects, except in two
extra inputs drawn for a function with two or more pointer or slice
parameters: one binds all of them to one address, and one binds the second
part-way into the first's object. No other aliasing arrangement is
exercised. Module callees run through the call. A function-pointer,
closure, trait-object or handle parameter gets no input. The differential
compares return values, panics, and the bytes of the memory the input
provided that the source left initialised. Bytes the source left
uninitialised are not compared. Other memory a run leaves behind, such as a
global, is observed only through those. Globals the function and its
callees name (up to 64 beyond its own) are allocated before the call, so a
pointer to one keeps its identity. A global the module only declares (the
bridge declares a static another codegen unit defines at the placeholder
type `ptr`) gets a 1 MiB interpreter object when its declared type is
smaller, so an access past its declared size reads no other allocation of
the run. The interpreter zero-fills a global without an initializer, so
the static reads as zero, in the source and the target alike, until the
run writes it: its real contents are unknown, and a comparison is under
that stand-in. An access more than 1 MiB past such a global's address is
not covered and can still land in another of the run's allocations. Pointers to allocations made during the
call, including a global only the rewrite names, are compared up to
renaming. An input on which both sides return with nothing to compare is not
counted as a comparison. The differential excludes inputs on which the
source raises undefined behaviour. It never counts a run the interpreter
cannot finish (a call to a declaration, an unsupported construct, exhausted
fuel) as agreement; a candidate that does not finish, raises undefined
behaviour or leaves uninitialised a byte the source's reading reads is a
disagreement, and that function is rolled
back. It sizes a run's fuel from the function and its loops: at most
262,144 steps, or 65,536 when a loop allocates. It stops at a per-module
step budget, past which a rewrite rests on its witness alone. It interprets
a view of the module that spells, in typed forms with the lane's meaning,
the rustc bridge's lane idioms the interpreter refuses: sign-reinterpreting
copies, mixed-width shift amounts, pointer comparisons, integer-spelled
`bool` and global-address constants, write-through and read-through field
access over pointers, and relocated global initializers. It gives a
`memmove`, `memcpy` or `memset` the module declares with the C prototype the
C library's body (the count read as `usize`, the fill truncated to `u8`, the
operation, the destination returned), so a comparison through one rests on
OD-141's premise, still open generic-import debt under OD-143. It gives a
`memcmp` or `bcmp` declaration no body (OD-164's merge boundary), and it
no longer gives a `__trustcg_array_fill_iW` declaration an invented helper
body (OD-155); such an unsupported foreign call receives no differential
execution credit. The view also
reads plain loads and stores with alignment 1, as wasm executes them, and
reads an aggregate argument the bridge passes by address as the pointee's
bytes at the call, while the lane reads each lane where the callee extracts
it: the two differ when something else writes those bytes during the call
(aliasing), a shape on which the differential's agreement says nothing
about the lane. A
mistake in that view would weaken the differential, never the emitted code,
which it does not change. Every candidate rewrite is counted once in the
report, either as compared or under one reason. Coverage is never implied.
On the 144-program harness corpus at O2 (section 0.31 of
`docs/wasm32_perf_roadmap.md`, round 16's bridge) it compared 8,015 of the
sixty-four-pass pipeline's 9,958 candidate rewrites (80.5%; the copy
respelling 83 of 96, the fill-call rewrite 7 of 7, the byte-copy rewrite 19
of 22, the memory-call rewrite 16 of 17, scalar replacement 331 of 467,
inlining 167 of 214, full unrolling 50 of 61, strength reduction 50 of 66,
invariant code motion 75 of 108, field-access lowering 74 of 119, address
folding 78 of 113, constant folding 533 of 617, simplification 329 of 402,
block merging 803 of 992, dead block parameters 146 of 176, argument
promotion 32 of 41, the range rules 168 of 208, closed-form induction 3 of
3); the others were not compared because the step budget ran out (828),
the function calls a declaration (406), every input was undefined (298),
the interpreter refused a typing (205) or a cast (197) or ran out of fuel
(5), or nothing was observed (4). Those rewrites
rest on their witness checks alone. A miscompile both a pass and its checker
accept, on inputs the seeded samples miss, passes this check: round 14's
first invariant code motion tier (b) did (OD-123), and the bridge corpus row
that found it is in the wasm32 differential below.
Each pass's proof table goes through a validated
`ProofTableTransformTransaction` in which every obligation is `Preserved`; a
transaction trust-ir rejects rolls that pass back on every function it
changed. Functions carrying proofs, summaries, call-site proof context,
source provenance or a body gate, or named by a module obligation, are
skipped. A module with a function over 4,096 blocks is not optimized. The
memory passes rest on the premise the lane's frame layout already uses: an
allocation whose address is never observed or passed on is reached only
through values computed from it. The select-branch rules' evaluator rests
on one more: trust-ir's memory model places no allocation at address 0
(the reference interpreter allocates from 1024, and the wasm32 lane carves
frame slots below the stack pointer, above static data), so a frame-slot
address at an in-bounds constant offset is taken to be non-zero (OD-160).

Some of these rewrites make a program slower under one V8 tier while it
executes fewer instructions (interleaved re-times on a loaded host, not
evidence; sections 0.32 and 0.33 of `docs/wasm32_perf_roadmap.md`): the
pointer difference makes `chunked_sum`'s `chunks_exact(4)` chunk length a
constant and Liftoff runs the shorter loop slower (1.58x -> 2.15x B1;
TurboFan and default tiering unchanged); the select-branch rules make
`k06_vm` about 5% slower under default tiering and 2% under TurboFan, and
`drop_reassign` 2-8% slower under TurboFan (the new branch keeps the
`bool`'s arm order, which can reverse the source's; the cause inside V8 is
not measured); and splicing `narrow_i8`'s `overflowing_pow` leaves a
return slot filled by a `memcopy` out of a constant global, which no pass
forwards, so the spliced loop keeps a frame (Liftoff 1.54x -> 2.38x B1,
TurboFan 1.28x -> 1.12x).

The optimized module is emitted only when all of the following hold;
otherwise the input is emitted:
- trust-ir's validator reports no finding kind more often than on the input;
- when it reports any finding, trust-ir's function-local validation of each
  changed function reports no finding (by full text) that the function's
  input lacks; finding kinds only module validation produces are compared by
  module-wide count;
- the input's admission accepts it;
- its static data is no larger than the input's under a caller's fixed
  module policy, so it neither shortens the stack the input had nor writes
  past a host-reserved region;
- the lane lowers it, and the CFG structural invariant is not refuted on its
  bytes.

A function the mid-end appends (argument promotion's and by-address
cloning's clones) has no input to compare with, so the second condition requires that function-local
validation reports no finding in it at all. When the first two conditions
or the admission refuse an output, the mid-end runs again, each step at
most once and in this order (OD-119):
1. if the output has clones, with the callees left unpromoted of every
   clone whose own body carries a finding (function-local, or module-level
   with every other body removed) or that a function with a new
   function-local finding calls; the step is skipped when no clone is
   blamed;
2. if the inliner spliced any call (a splice copies its callee's validation
   findings, but the refusal need not come from a splice), with every
   spliced callee whose input body carries a finding left called; the step
   is skipped when no such callee exists;
3. if closed-form induction, full or interval-bounded unrolling,
   invariant code motion, strength reduction, block merging, field-access
   lowering or the select-branch rules changed a function (they copy
   instructions, move them to another block or retype a result, validation
   findings included), once without all eight (`MidConfig::loop_passes`):
   that output is emitted when it passes, and
   otherwise the steps below go on from the refused output that has them,
   with them kept;
4. if the inliner still spliced a call, without the inliner;
5. if the output still has clones, without argument promotion and
   by-address cloning.

A refusal no clone is blamed for therefore withdraws the inliner's splices
before the whole of argument promotion. The final report names every
withdrawal made in `passes_withheld` (`loop_passes`, `argpromo_callees`,
`inline_callees`, `inline`, `argpromo` with `byaddr`). The mid-end thus runs at most six
times. Only the last output's refusal emits the input. No step withdraws
constant folding, the memory-call rewrite, the operand
respelling, lane-load scalarization, simplification, address folding or dead
block parameters alone, so a validation finding one of them introduces
is withdrawn only if a
step above happens to remove it; otherwise the unit emits its input and loses
the whole mid-end.

When the mid-end changed something the input is lowered as well (its
baseline bodies, without the local emission pass), and its admission or
lowering refusal is the compile's, so those refusals are exactly the ones
without the mid-end. An entry that reports the CFG structural invariant (the
evidence entries and every object compile) also checks it on that lowering of
the input when it emits the optimized module, and fails the compile when it
is refuted there; without the mid-end the invariant is checked on the
emitted bytes, which include the local emission pass. A pass's
`functions_changed` in the report counts function-passes, summed over every
run of that pass (copy propagation runs twelve times, dead-code elimination
six times, constant folding four times, the GEP rewrite and scalar replacement
three times each, constant-branch folding, store forwarding, dead-slot
removal, the memory-call rewrite, simplification, the range rules and block
merging twice each, and field-access lowering, the inliner, constant-table
promotion, argument promotion, closed-form induction, full unrolling, address
folding, dead block parameters, invariant code motion and strength reduction
once), and its `refinements` count dead UB-raising instructions removed, the
stores of unread slots removed, tables promoted, the loads and stores scalar
replacement rewrote, inline sites, promoted calls, closed loops whose removed
instructions include one that inspects a value, simplifications, and unrolled
loops that drop a copy of their exit compare; the rewrites of constant
folding, the memory-call rewrite (under OD-141's premise), field-access
lowering, address folding, dead block parameters, block merging, the range
rules, invariant code motion and strength reduction are all exact. The
report's `functions_changed` also counts the functions argument promotion
appended, and `allocas_after` counts their `alloca`s. For the range rules alone the report also counts
kept and rolled-back rewrites per rule (`rules`, `rules_rolled_back`, with
the claimed block-parameter intervals under `param_interval`; additive
fields, pending the owner's sign-off). A function left with no
`alloca`, home, staging or call-scratch slot has no shadow-stack frame: no
prologue, epilogue, `__stack_pointer` update or stack guard, and nothing for
the frame-bounds guard to check. The bridge knob `no-wasm-irmid` switches
the mid-end off alone and `trace-wasm-irmid` prints its report.
`WasmCompileEvidence::mid_end` reports what ran (an additive field; the
schema name is unchanged); the compile verdict stays `missing_evidence`. At
O1 and above the lane adds a one-byte GEP index unscaled.

Then the local emission
pass (`wasm/opt.rs`, `wasm/opt/control.rs`, `wasm/opt/rewrite.rs`) rewrites
each function. First a control cleanup, in up to four rounds, deletes the
`br`s and `return`s that falling through already performs (no `loop` label
crossed, no value moved or discarded), code after a transfer or after a
construct no path leaves (keeping an `unreachable` where the next `end`
needs it to validate), and `block`s and `loop`s no branch names
(renumbering the branches), deletes empty `else` arms and turns one-branch
`if; br d; end` arms into `br_if`. Only the empty block type is cleaned; a
body the cleanup cannot account for (another block type, an instruction or
call without a known arity, a dead instruction carrying a relocation) is
left as it is. A cleanup is used only when
`trust_cg_verify::wasm_local_tv::validate_control` accepts it: a lockstep
simulation of the two bodies over pairs of program points, with its own
decoder and arity table and stacks of value tokens, that pairs
conditionals, `br_table`s and returns, checks frame heights and requires
every post instruction to be reached or (an `end`, `else` or filler
`unreachable`) to validate on its own. Only the empty block type is
modelled; a relocation is accepted only on a non-control instruction the
simulation paired with a twin carrying the same relocations; an empty
control cycle such as a panic handler's `loop {}` is refused, and so is a
function past 2^24 steps. A refused cleanup is counted by reason in
`local_emission.control_refusals` and the function continues from its
uncleaned body; it never refuses a compile. An accepted cleaned body is
the body the rest of the pass is validated against. Then:
single-use stackify with `local.tee`, dead-definition removal, narrow-mask and
sign-extension elimination, memarg offset folding, loads and stores in place
of a `memory.copy` of at most 32 constant bytes, and copy-affinity colouring,
self-copy deletion, reordering and constant rematerialization of locals, and
removal of dead `local.tee`/`local.set` writes before and after colouring.
Stackify may not move a definition where that would raise the number of
same-type locals live at a local write above the input's peak for that type;
where that kept a definition in place, the unlimited candidate is built too
and the pass picks between the two candidates by code bytes (then declared
locals), or, at a cost of at most 4 code bytes, by V8 Liftoff's limit of 12
cached declared locals (measured on arm64 V8 14.6, applied only when every declared
local is i32 or i64; other engines and x64 are not modelled). A candidate the
validator refuses after dead-write removal is rebuilt once without it, and
the first refusal is counted in `local_emission.dead_write_retries`. Because
the pass shrinks callers as well as callees, V8 TurboFan's caller-relative
inlining budget can inline less than for the baseline bodies. At O0, or with
the bridge knob `no-wasm-local-opt` (which compiles at O0), neither the
mid-end nor this pass runs and every function is emitted as the lane's own
body, unchanged from before either pass. A rewrite is emitted only
when `trust_cg_verify::wasm_local_tv` validates it against the lane's body of
the same function (its control-cleaned body, when the cleanup was
accepted), per straight-line segment: identical control; equal
ordered effects, with addresses compared as base plus offset and an offset
folded only under a no-wrap bound the validator re-derives, or under the
no-wrap premise of a single-index GEP's address addition (OD-125).
trust-ir's reference interpreter makes a GEP result past `2^32 - 1` undefined
behaviour on wasm32 (WS2.16). `trust_cg_verify::wasm_nowrap_premise`
re-derives the premise from the trust-ir function and the lane's
value-to-local map (checked to be a function and injective, not derived), and
binds it to that function's name and the body it was derived on; it reaches a
control-cleaned body only through an accepted lockstep control validation
(`validate_control_with_premises`). The validator re-checks the premise on the
body (the GEP's local written once, with the sum of what its base and index
hold) and applies it only to accesses after the GEP. This makes that
function's emission equivalence conditional on its premised GEPs being
defined. It rests on the reference interpreter's semantics, not the Lean model
(wasm32 is outside the proven subset), and reads trust-ir allocation placement
as unspecified, with the wasm execution's addresses as one admissible
placement, which trust-ir does not yet state normatively. In rustc bridge
output on wasm32 at O1 and above (the level the lane runs at: `-C
opt-level`, or the bridge's `opt-level` knob when set, which overrides it
for the GEPs as for the lane), the bridge itself emits `gep inbounds u8
base, [k]`, with a constant `0 < k <= i32::MAX`, for the constant-offset
addresses Rust guarantees in bounds (OD-140,
`rustc-codegen-trust-cg/src/wasm32_inbounds.rs`): field and
front-`ConstantIndex` projections of a place through a local, a reference or
a raw pointer, the bytes of a place a statement copies whole, and the vtable
method slot of a call through a `dyn` reference. Their premises rest on
Rust's in-bounds and dangling-place rules as the bridge's lowering states
them, not on a check; execution differentials against LLVM are their
evidence. The bridge knob `no-wasm32-place-gep` withdraws them. Every other
GEP is the mid-end's. Every other address the bridge forms on wasm32 is an
integer chain (`ptrtoint`/`add`/`inttoptr`), carries no premise and is never
folded: `ptr::add`/`offset`, `wrapping_add`/`arith_offset`, integer
arithmetic, a runtime index, a slice pattern's elements of a `&[T]`, the
`Box<dyn Fn>` call's vtable slot, the bridge's library models, and every
address at that level O0 (including `-C opt-level=2` with the knob
`opt-level=0`). Neither is a scaled constant index, a GEP result read more
than once or in another segment, or an index constant several GEPs share.
The rest of each segment's check: equal end
stacks
and live-out locals; claimed local bounds re-checked at every boundary; one
term per evaluation of a float operation whose NaN result is
nondeterministic; typed `global.get` results; and its own stack accounting
re-checked against wasm typing. Otherwise the function keeps the lane's
uncleaned body (or the cleaned one, when only the cleanup changed it).
Every syntactically unequal residual is refused, so no solver runs while
compiling and the emitted bytes do not depend on the host. Only memory 0 is
modelled. This relates two wasm bodies of one function, given the module's
call signatures, and where a GEP premise was used, only on executions in
which those GEPs are defined; it is not a source-to-wasm proof and moves no
compile
verdict (`WasmCompileEvidence::local_emission` reports what ran, with the
premises admitted and the folds made on one). Apart from a premised GEP's
addition, which folds in objects too, frame-relative
offsets fold only where the prologue's stack guard (closed modules with static
data) proves the frame did not wrap, never in relocatable objects, so never in
rustc bridge output. The frame-bounds guard checks the lowering's own body,
and the wasm ABI evidence family checks the O0 bytes; at O1 and above the
emitted bytes are related to those only through the validator.

`benchmarks/wasm-vs-llvm` measures the lane's output against rustc+LLVM at
`-C opt-level=2` on 144 small `no_std` programs. Its rows record sizes,
wasm-level instruction counts, shadow-stack use in linear memory and V8
timings for a stamped revision, host and measuring-code digest. They are
compiled with `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=no-proof-certs` (the lane emits no
certificates), so they carry no proof claim. Agreement with LLVM on the input
grid (up to the sign of zero on the exports the corpus manifest lists, and
NaN payloads, which are not observed) is a differential test, not a proof.

## Rust integration

The `crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg` bridge pins the custom `trust` toolchain and
is not part of the root workspace. It requires a coherent Trust compiler,
build tool, sysroot and matching private compiler libraries. Its differential
tests explicitly disable frontend verification; a passing diagnostic build is
not Trust-verified compilation or self-hosting. It accepts a bounded
MIR/layout/ABI subset and deliberately rejects many Rust programs. Missing
areas include complete MIR statements and terminators, `TyAndLayout`/`FnAbi`,
mono items, statics and
vtables, aggregates and DSTs, runtime/lang items, panic/unwind, drop semantics,
inline assembly, debug/profiling hooks, and broad ecosystem validation.

**Coroutines and drop glue on Linux AArch64 (2026-10-24).** The Linux
runtime twins of the Darwin static-data, drop/heap and coroutine fixtures
(`static_data_linux`, `drop_heap_linux`, `coroutine_generator_linux`;
[record](reports/perf/2026-10-24-linux-bridge-runtime-twins/README.md)) met
these bridge refusals, each by name and fail-closed. Until `5d37f4cf1` the
Darwin generator `ay_gen_seq` (`yield 10; yield 20; return 30`), like the
other five- and six-state coroutines measured, was refused at O2 and O3 at object
emission (`[TCG-A64-SWITCH-BIND] ... jump-table bounds constant constant
register x9 is not materialized by a move-wide chain: no producer in the
block`), because `const-trip-guard-normalize` hoisted the resume loop's
jump-table bound out of its dispatch block; the normalizer now leaves a
dispatch header alone, and the switch binder still refuses, rather than
follows, a bound produced outside its dispatch block.
At every level a coroutine whose locals live across a `yield` is refused at
its drop glue (`StatementKind::Nop`), one dropped while it holds user-`Drop`
state is refused (`Ty::Coroutine(..)`), and a coroutine closure that borrows
a captured scalar is refused ("borrowed scalar reference used without
deref"); `Vec<Box<T>>` and a struct of `Box<T>` fields whose `T` has a `Drop`
impl are refused ("per-element drop glue not lowered", "recursive drop glue
not lowered"). These are certificates-off native measurements on Linux; the
Darwin coroutine fixture runs at O0 only, so its O2/O3 behaviour on Darwin is
unmeasured.

**Codegen options, linkage and debug information (ledger L06-P7,
2026-10-01).** Every codegen option the bridge reads is decided before it
lowers anything (the matrix is in the bridge README). Not implemented, and
refused by a `[TCG-OPT-*]` code instead of ignored: cross-crate and
linker-plugin LTO, PGO (`profile-generate`/`profile-use`/
`-Z profile-sample-use`), coverage instrumentation, sanitizers, stack
protectors, AArch64 branch protection, mcount/XRay/patchable-function-entry
hooks, a `-Z min-function-alignment` above the four bytes every AArch64
function has, code models other than small, `-C jump-tables=no`,
`-C debuginfo=full` (variables and types) and every debuginfo level off
aarch64-apple-darwin. Per-function attributes with the same effect
(`#[patchable_function_entry]`, a function alignment attribute) are not
inspected. Frame pointers in frameless leaves and
`-C link-dead-code` for executables are warned as not honoured. Debug
information is line tables only: on aarch64-apple-darwin
`-C debuginfo=line-tables-only` (and `line-directives-only`/`limited`, with a
note) emits a DWARF 4 line program and one subprogram DIE per function from
MIR spans. Inlined and macro-expanded code is attributed to its call site in
the function's own file (no `DW_TAG_inlined_subroutine` or namespace DIEs),
a subprogram is named by its crate-qualified def-path rather than its object
symbol, and a debug build is a proofs-off build: with certificates on the request is
refused, because the certified relocation inventory refuses DWARF sections.
Spans are claim metadata, but they are not code-neutral: a spanned compare is
not fused by the bounds-assert pass, so a `-g` object can differ from the
default one in more than its `__DWARF` segment. A codegen unit whose
