cell agrees or is refused by name, the controls included. Re-measured
2026-09-29 with the same driver at O0-O3: at trust-cg `8328b1068`, with and
without the argument-verdict change, 622 of the 624 non-oracle cells equal
LLVM x LLVM and 2 are refused by name (O0 `w1_a16_home_dyn`,
`[TCG-SCALAR-CELL-LAYOUT]`); at `0d0257f58` (after `8048ee383` lowered those
two), with and without the change, all 624 are equal. None is wrong in any
run, and every run reports the same 42 control refusals at O1 / O3, levels
the controls' `refused_at` lists do not name (a driver expectation, not a
wrong value). What remains there is
what remains on x86-64 (above); in particular a padded scalar newtype RETURNED
by value (`-> #[repr(align(16))] struct Wide(i64)`, which rustc returns through
the hidden `x8` buffer) is refused by name (`[TCG-RET-ABI]`) rather than lowered
— before, an LLVM callee's result was read out of `x0` (a bus error). Since
round 10 an AArch64 Darwin host also runs the x86-64 lane of `m145` (and of
`m140`, `m141`, `m144`, `m146`) under Rosetta, as `#![no_std]` programs
against a `core` the build compiler builds from its own library source
(`tests/support/x86_rosetta.rs`); a Rosetta run qualifies Rosetta's execution
of the x86-64 code, and no run on one target stands in for the other.

**Register exhaustion: every argument's placement is compared per
signature** (measured 2026-09-29/30 on aarch64-apple-darwin natively and on
x86_64-apple-darwin under Rosetta, `targo --unverified`, no proof claim). The
per-argument gate (`check_param_abi_lanes`) compares each by-value argument in
isolation — class, count, per-lane extent and value offset — and decides its
MODE; register numbering, exhaustion and stack offsets are decided by the
whole-signature placement check (`check_signature_placement`, see §17 under
aggregate passing above), which compares every byte of every argument of every
declaration the bridge emits. Families, each a row of
`tests/signature_placement_families_xback.rs` (one callee crate per row, all
four rlib x bin cells, O0-O3 on both targets, each row bounded by its own
level range; `SIGFAM_LEVELS` narrows it; a required target of
`scripts/check_darwin_aarch64_bridge.py`):

| Family | Before (origin/main `47f63ec1d`), O0 | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Pair` at the last register: `(u64, u64)`, `Option<u64>`, `&[u8]` at x7 / R9, `(f64, f64)` / `(f32, f32)` at d7 / xmm7 | agrees (the pair lane, `ab0b74ce0`) | agrees; with the lane disabled the check refuses exactly these rows (mutation run) |
| Rust-ABI narrow `Cast` (1-4 bytes) after eight integers: `[u8; 1]`, `[u8; 2]`, `[u16; 1]`, `{u8, u8, u8}`, `[u8; 4]`, `[f32; 1]`, two casts back to back, a `fn` pointer and a `dyn` method (aarch64) | WRONG in both mixed cells: e.g. `[u8; 4]` 197 / 210 against 63, the `dyn` method 27 / 162 against 144 | agrees: declared as the one integer rustc passes (`narrow_cast_param_plan`); with that plan disabled the check refuses all nine rows, and with the check also disabled they are wrong again |
| A closure body's `Pair` argument, the body exported (`-Zshare-generics`) and called by the other backend: at x7 / R9, `&[u8]`, `Option<u64>`, a narrow cast, and `(u32, u32)` / `(f32, f32)` a whole slot would put in one register; in-crate `(u32, u32)`, `Option<u32>` + `(u16, u8)` through a generic `F: Fn` | REFUSED at O0 (`closure_pair_boundary_disagreement` / the per-slot gate), and on x86-64 `ka` / `ks` / `ko` refused although they agree; the narrow-cast closure WRONG (52 / 38 against 169) | agrees: closure bodies take the pair / narrow-cast lanes and every closure call site builds its arguments through ONE builder (`closure_call_arg_values`) |
| A by-value (`FnOnce`) closure environment exported and called by the other backend: a `Pair` (two `u64`, a captured slice), one scalar, a narrow `Cast` (3 bytes), a pointer to a copy (12 bytes); in-crate two references | REFUSED at O0 (`refuse_by_value_closure_env_shared_symbol`) | agrees: the environment is argument 0 by rustc's own mode |
| Iterator intercepts: `enumerate().map(..)`, `enumerate().filter(..).map(..)`, `fold` | agrees (bridge rlib cells) | agrees, now through the builder |
| `extern "rust-call"` callables: an exported `rust-call` fn whose untupled elements put a pair at x7 / R9, an `i128` element, a `dyn Fn` whose `i128` element crosses both ways, a `dyn Fn` over a closure with a pair and a narrow cast (`dyn_fn_pair`) | REFUSED by name (`refuse_tupled_rust_call_*`; the dispatch spread's `i128` refusal) | agrees: declared with the tuple's elements as rustc's `FnAbi` lists them (`rust_call_spread`, F2); on the pre-F2 build the same rows are refused in 17 cells per target |
| `rust-call` fn POINTERS crossing both ways and a user `rust-call` trait method through `&dyn` (`rc_fnptr_rev`, `rc_fnptr_fwd`, `rc_trait_dyn`) | WRONG, silently, in 16 of 24 cells per direction (the tupled declaration against rustc's untupled call) | agrees (F2) |
| A closure environment that is ONE `f64` / `f32` through every by-value crossing (`env_f*`, `fn_env_f*`, `fn_env_f32_stack`, `dyn_env_f*`, `fnmut_env_f64`) | REFUSED `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` / `[TCG-RET-ABI]` (an integer slot) | agrees: a one-lane float slot (`closure_slot_ty`, F1), copied at its own type (`slot_lane_value_ty`; before that, x86-64 `env_f*` were WRONG, see "Closure calls returning a float pair") |

Standalone `core` from the compiler's own library source, `no-proof-certs`:
the same failed-root sets before and after on both targets (measured against
origin/main c84d39e93: 21 at O0 and 5 at O3 on aarch64 and on x86-64; against
47f63ec1d, aarch64 21 / 5 and x86-64 22 / 6), and no `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` line —
the 16 closure bodies with a by-value `ScalarPair` environment that a check
alone would have refused now declare it as rustc does. Measured again before
and after F2 (the `rust-call` untupling) on the branch merged with origin/main
`3b0797875`: the same sets, 21 at O0 and 5 at O3 on each target, and no
`[TCG-ARG-ABI]` line.

**Closure function-pointer row requalified 2026-11-09.** `clo_fnptr`, a
non-capturing closure coerced to a `fn` pointer with a pair at the last integer
register and calls crossing both ways, now compiles and matches the existing
LLVM oracle on both targets at O0-O3. The stale x86-64 object-identity refusal
exception has been removed: all four combinations of library and caller
backends must compile and run at every level. The full three-method signature-family
target passed on Trust 16387, with AArch64 executed natively and x86-64 under
Rosetta. These are the existing `no-proof-certs` runtime diagnostics, not
formal-proof credit or native x86-64 hardware qualification. The older dated
measurements retain the refusal that existed when they were recorded.

Named, not closed:

- The check's trusted base (§17 above): the classifier and the
  `PassMode` -> value model are shared by both sides, so their correctness is
  the family matrix's (test rung). Recording rustc's placement as trust-ir
  `ParamAttrs.pass` would state the rule once on the consumer side.
- An element of a call's argument tuple that is read from the tuple's bytes
  (a by-value aggregate, a fat pointer, a `&dyn`) needs the tuple in memory.
  Every untupling call's tuple that carries a by-value aggregate is given a
  slot (rule (3c) of `compute_memory_backed_locals`, keyed on the callee's
  `rust-call` ABI since F2, which closed the `&dyn Fn(T12)` "needs a
  byte-backed tuple" refusal). The refusal itself remains, by name
  (`[TCG-ARG-ABI] Fn-trait tuple element N ... needs a byte-backed tuple`), for
  a tuple the lowering keeps in registers although an element must be read
  from bytes, a case rule (3c) does not key on (it keys on a by-value
  aggregate element); no program measured in round 10 reaches it after F2.
- The x86-64 RETURN placement still reads `abi_reg_lanes`' mirror of the
  selector's return classification (the selector exposes no return placement
  function yet). Variadic anonymous arguments are the variadic lane's.

**`rust-call` calls and closure bodies across the backend boundary: one rule
(since round 10 met `main`'s refusals, 2026-10-08).** From 2026-10-02 until
this merge, `main` kept the bridge's TUPLED declaration of `extern
"rust-call"` callables, its pointer-declared closure environments and its
whole-slot closure pairs, and refused by name each crossing where they could
disagree with rustc (`[TCG-RUST-CALL-ABI]`, and `[TCG-ARG-ABI]` from
`refuse_tupled_rust_call_escape`, `refuse_closure_pair_escape`,
`refuse_by_value_closure_env_*` and `closure_defining_copy_reaches_body`).
What it measured before those refusals, on AArch64 Linux (at `13a7b0ad9`,
`5e0696862`, `65fc9aaf3` and `fd6f7475f`): a scratch matrix of 23 tuple kinds
over 15 call routes had 291 of 3105 cells wrong (249 wrong values, 42
SIGSEGV), all on the `fn`-pointer, method-pointer, generic-pointer-caller,
non-`Fn*` `dyn` and foreign routes; a `(bool, u64)` tuple whose padding was
nonzero read `false` as `true` (961 against 41 at O2 and O3); the address of a
`FnOnce` closure body SIGSEGV'd; a by-value closure body reached through
another crate's copy of its `#[inline(always)]` defining function SIGSEGV'd or
printed pointer-like values; and a `Fn` closure body's address, with a `&str`
after six `u64` (or after a `u128` and three `u64`) and handed out through a
constant or a static, SIGSEGV'd. The merge takes round 10's rule instead:
every callable is declared as rustc's `FnAbi` lists it (a `rust-call` tuple's
elements, `rust_call_spread`; a closure body's `Pair` arguments and by-value
environment by rustc's own modes) and judged per signature
(`check_signature_placement`), so none of those shapes has a disagreement left
to refuse, and every program those refusals pinned is a row that must COMPILE
and print LLVM's value in all four library x binary pairings at O0-O3:
`tests/support/rust_call_pointer_calls.rs` (the reproducer pointer, a `(f64,
f64)` pointer, the non-`Fn*` `dyn` method, the foreign item, `(bool, u64)`
through a pointer and as a linked item, a reified `FnOnce` body, a `Fn` body's
address reified, read from an inline `const` and stored in a static, after six
`u64` and after a `u128`, a library calling the pointers, and a library's
`(bool, u64)` item) and `tests/support/inlined_closure_bodies.rs` (moved and
borrowed environments through an `#[inline(always)]` defining function, and
two controls). Measured 2026-10-08 on aarch64-apple-darwin with this merge's
backend (`rust_call_boundary_aarch64`, the backend's `no-proof-certs` knob,
`targo --unverified`, no proof claim): 232 native runs of the first module and
64 of the second over the four pairings at O0-O3 print LLVM's value, and none
is refused. The Linux AArch64 host,
whose `aarch64_c_fnabi_aggregate_linux` runs the same two modules, was not run
for this merge. The three shapes `main` listed as KNOWN OPEN WRONG CODE on its
refusal route (a closure body this crate links, taking a whole-slot `Pair`
that holds a `bool`; an `#[inline(never)]` closure in an exported generic
parent that another crate also copies, with a `&str` at register exhaustion;
a by-value closure type reaching another crate through a field typed by a
`type_alias_impl_trait` alias) are family-matrix rows (`bool_pair_body`,
`inline_never_parent`, `tait_field`). Measured 2026-10-08 on
aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-apple-darwin under Rosetta: every cell of
`bool_pair_body` and of `inline_never_parent` with both crates at one level
agrees with LLVM at O0-O3. `tait_field` holds an `#[inline(never)]` `FnOnce`
closure whose by-value environment is a `Pair` in a field typed by the
alias, and every caller links its body from the library at O0-O3; the row
checks that import itself (`crosses`, `nm -u` of the caller's object), so a

O2 or O3), so the row also runs every pair of two different levels on
AArch64 (`mixed_levels`). Measured 2026-10-10 on aarch64-apple-darwin
(`signature_placement_families_agree_aarch64`): every cell of `tait_field`
at O0-O3 and of `inline_never_parent`'s 12 mixed pairs agrees with LLVM,
while `main`'s pre-merge bridge (`65e816a73`, through `SIGFAM_DYLIB`)
SIGSEGVs in `tait_field`'s bridge-library x LLVM-binary cell at every level
and gives `inline_never_parent` a wrong value at library O0 with binary O2
and O3. Not covered: the x86-64 lane builds each level against its own

**The `p09_sieve` miscompile at O2/O3 was trust-cg-opt, not the bridge (found
2026-09-29, root-caused and fixed 2026-09-30).** The shared corpus guest
`p09_sieve` (`tests/real_program_corpus/corpus_guests.rs`: a `[bool; 1000]`
sieve whose count-if arm also runs `sum += i`) exited 192 where LLVM exits 198,
at O2 and O3, through the bridge at `3235a8d81`. `neon_bytesum`'s count-if
kernel ran its vector loop over `i` in [2, 962) and added only to the count
register; `sum` was updated by the scalar remainder alone, so it held only the
six primes in [962, 1000). A later bool-load lowering (`bb4bbac08`: `ldrb; tst
#0xff`) stopped the matcher firing on `[bool]`, so the guest agrees at
`47f63ec1d` (198 at O0-O3, remeasured), but the defect was the class, not the
guest: whole programs over `[u8]`, `[u32]` and `[i32]` at `47f63ec1d`, bridge
against LLVM, were wrong in 21 of 144 rows per level at O2 and O3 on aarch64
(fill and zero-fill with a second carried register; the count-if-with-sum arm;
byte-sum, byte-count, popcount, fill and zero-fill whose only extra register is
`last = i`, at N a multiple of the vector block (16, 64, 1024), where the
vector loop takes every iteration and the remainder that writes `last` never
runs) and in 37 of 144 on x86-64 under Rosetta (byte-sum, byte-count,
popcount-sum, fill, zero-fill and i32-sum with a second carried register, and
the count-if-with-sum arm). Fixed by the loop-state contract under
**Optimization and performance**: every row agrees on both targets at both
levels, and so does `p09_sieve`
(`crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg/tests/opt_loop_state_run.rs`, x86-64 under
Rosetta). That is test-rung evidence over the rows it runs.
`real_program_corpus_a64` still cannot see a row of this kind: it runs with
proof certificates on, under which every row is refused (`[TCG-PROOF-465]`,
with `[TCG-MIR-UNSUPPORTED]`; 0 of 26 rows compiled at `c84d39e93`, below
its 69.2% floor, so that target is red), and it only compiles, never runs.
The run lane is `opt_loop_state_run`'s corpus test: every guest at O0, O2
and O3, proofs off, linked and run against LLVM. All 39 rows agree since
2026-10-03; `p13_sort_std` at O2 and O3 was refused by name
(`[TCG-MIR-UNSUPPORTED]`, `&raw (*v)[k of n]` in `core::slice::sort`) until

**Layout images the bridge used to derive from declared fields** (fixed
2026-09-28, measured on AArch64 across a real rlib x bin boundary): a
single-variant enum whose `#[repr(C)]` / `#[repr(uN)]` keeps a TAG (`#[repr(C)]
enum TagC { V(i64) }` is 16 bytes, tag at 0, payload at 8) was typed as its
payload scalar, dropping the tag — `&TagC::V(-51)` read by LLVM answered 0 at O0
and O3 — and is now declined by the scalar type mapper
(`single_variant_enum_keeps_tag`) and modeled as a Direct-tagged memory enum; a
write to the one SIZED field of a single-scalar newtype whose ZERO-SIZED field
comes first (`struct ZstLead((), u64)`, `z.1 = v`) was bound under the MIR field
index no whole-local read consults and LOST (8738 against 4242). The earlier
`binding_shape_and_field` repair routes that sole sized MIR field to the whole
local for SSA reads and writes. The September 30 frozen Linux campaign exposed
an additional allocated-cell refusal: `checked_scalar_cell_projection` counted
both declared fields. Its subsequent checked-layout repair counts fields
occupying storage, requires the selected field to be the sole non-ZST field at
offset zero, and retains exact extent, alignment, leaf-type and exclusive-cell
checks. The unchanged `zst_lead_write` matrix passes with separate source/backend
provenance; the earlier eight compile refusals remain recorded. Through a REFERENCE, the pointee
lanes of a tagged single-variant enum and of a single-variant enum whose fields
rustc reordered (`enum Reord { V(u8, i64) }`, the `i64` at 0) were declaration
order — a bridge-built `fn(v: &TagC)` read the tag as the payload, and `fn(v:
&Reord)` read garbage even with both sides bridge-built — and both now take the
memory-enum pointee lane (`single_variant_enum_lanes_match_rustc_offsets`). All
are rows of the `m145` matrix (`tag_c_*`, `tag_u8`, `zst_lead_write`,
`reorder_ref`). A reordered multi-field STRUCT by reference was measured correct
before and after (its field reads already use rustc's offsets).

A `wasm32-unknown-unknown` session routes each codegen unit to the wasm
object lane, and rustc links the objects with `wasm-ld` (`-C linker=`). It
requires `-C panic=abort` and `-Ztrust-ir-cg-args=no-proof-certs`, since the
lane emits no certificates. Under `panic=abort` a failed MIR assert calls
core's panic entry with rustc's caller location, so the `#[panic_handler]`
runs before the abort. A bounds check calls the genuine `panic_bounds_check`
with its `index` and `len`, so the handler sees rustc's payload and location.
The other MIR assert kinds take the native route described under **MIR
assertion panic runtime** above: they call rustc's kind-specific panic entry
(`panic_const_add_overflow`, `panic_const_div_by_zero`, ...) with the caller
location, and a recording `#[panic_handler]` at O0 agrees with LLVM's.
Only a panic CALL whose payload the bridge cannot model (a formatted
`panic_fmt`, for example) still raises a message the bridge synthesizes naming
the original entry, which a handler that inspects the message can tell from
LLVM's. General TrustIR `Inst::Assert` still refuses as `[TCG-ASSERT-PANIC]`;
the Wasm route does not establish native qualification. The Trust
toolchain ships no wasm32 standard library;
`scripts/build_wasm32_sysroot.sh` builds `core` and `compiler_builtins` from
the compiler's own library sources, and only `no_std` crates without `alloc`
have been exercised.

The MIR lowering computes addresses, lengths and indices in a native 64-bit
word. A wasm32 session narrows that word to 32 bits before emission
(`src/wasm32_words.rs`): values joined by the word operations are partitioned,
and a class that touches a pointer-width fact is retyped to `i32`. A class
that is also a Rust-typed `i64` is refused as `[TCG-WASM32-WORD]` rather than
guessed. Data images, vtables, virtual calls, the slice and `Chars` cursor
models, the slice stride iterators (`Windows`, `Chunks`, `ChunksExact`,
`RChunks`, `RChunksExact`, kept in std's own `{ v, size }` /
`{ v, chunk_size }` / `{ v, rem, chunk_size }` state) and the
`array::IntoIter` model follow the session's pointer width. The stride
iterators' field offsets and the `array::IntoIter` `alive` indices are read
through `layout_of`. On wasm32, the following run over an `array::IntoIter`:
- its constructor and identity `into_iter`;
- `next`;
- the modeled chain terminals;
- core's own `size_hint`, `next_back`, `nth`, `advance_by` and `rfold`
  bodies;
- the `IndexRange::try_fold` that rustc's -O2 inliner exposes, driven as a
  `Range<usize>` source.

Every other callee whose first argument is an `array::IntoIter`, or a
reference to one, is refused by `[TCG-OWNING-ITER-METHOD]`. This includes user
and generic functions that receive the iterator, `by_ref()` and `for x in
&mut it` at -O0, `len`, `clone`, `as_slice`, `peekable`, `eq`, `skip_while`,
`rposition` and `find_map` at -O0. Other shapes are refused by name by the
iterator-chain models. Examples, not a complete list: a capturing closure in
a fold or short-circuit drive (`.map(|x| x * k).sum()`, `.position(..)` at
-O2, `.enumerate().fold(..)`), `.zip()`, `chain` with an adapter sub-source,
`flat_map`, `step_by` above -O0, a user `try_fold` returning `ControlFlow`,
`rfind`, `rev().fold` over `f64`, and a constant-array argument. `max`/`min`
at -O0 are refused for slices as well.

The `Vec` header carrier (`[TCG-COLLECTION-LAYOUT]`), the
`vec::IntoIter`/`Drain` models and the BTreeMap, `vec_*` and `slice_repeat`
helper families still assume 64-bit layouts and are refused
(`[TCG-WASM32-MODEL]`, `[TCG-WASM32-HELPER]`); so is a decoded `print!`, whose
std-sink lowering builds `fmt::Arguments` from 8-byte words only
(`[TCG-PRINT-SINK]`). Function definitions carry
rustc's per-codegen-unit linkage (CGU-private copies become hidden link-once
definitions under a crate-private name), so crates built with several
codegen units link. Calls follow rustc's wasm32 `FnAbi`, including
`PassMode::Cast` and `Indirect` arguments, `sret` returns, by-memory C unions
and over-aligned aggregates, and `#[track_caller]`'s hidden location. A
Rust-ABI union, one-lane value or padded over-aligned newtype reaching a
`fn` pointer or another backend's code is refused as `[TCG-WASM32-BYVAL-ABI]`,
LLVM intrinsic imports (`memory_grow`) as `[TCG-WASM32-LLVM-INTRINSIC]`, and
`#[thread_local]` compiles as a plain static only without the `atomics`
feature. A `#[repr(C)]` struct around one `i128`/`u128` crosses `extern "C"`
as rustc's cast, two `i64` halves (a return goes through the caller's
buffer). C-ABI 8- and 16-bit integer scalars that the bridge holds in a
one-lane memory slot (`Option<NonZeroU8>`, `(u8,)`, `Option<#[repr(u8)]
enum>`, ...) are passed and returned with rustc's zero or sign extension on
every target, and a declaration that cannot carry the extension is refused
by name (`[TCG-ARG-ABI]`/`[TCG-RET-ABI]`); the x86-64 side of that plan is
not execution-checked on the Darwin AArch64 host. Two `extern` items sharing
a `#[link_name]` whose signatures lower to different value shapes are
refused (`[TCG-ARG-ABI]`) or kept out of a merged module. A constant
aggregate of two bytes or more is read from its read-only data global:
directly when the local is stored once from the constant and only read as
scalars (never moved, borrowed or address-compared), otherwise copied with
one `memcopy`. Nothing guards those bytes at run time (wasm has no
read-only memory), so the direct read rests on that classification.

On wasm32, a `count()` (or a debug-build `position()`) that passes
`usize::MAX` (2^32 - 1) items panics as core does, and so does a `chain`
count whose total passes it with overflow checks on. The bridge reaches that
result by visiting every item, where LLVM computes `Range::count` in O(1); a
range of at most 32-bit items (16-bit for `..=`), which cannot pass the
limit, is counted without the per-item check.
`.enumerate()`'s own index still wraps past 2^32 items where an
overflow-checked LLVM build panics. `flat_map(..).count()` is refused by
name, as is a `chain(..).count()` whose half can itself exceed `u32::MAX`
or is neither a range nor a slice. On every target, `.cloned()` over an
element whose `clone` is not the builtin derive's (a `#[automatically_derived]`
attribute alone does not count) runs the real `Cloned` bodies: `any`/`all`/
`find`/`find_map` compile, while `count`, `position` and `fold`/`sum` over
such chains are refused by name. `iter().rev().take(n)` reductions over
non-scalar slice elements are refused on every target. `Take` over a
user-defined iterator is refused at O2/O3 when its `spec_fold` is not
inlined. `Cycle` sources stay unmodeled and refused.

Apart from those refusals, the bridge accepts nearly the same Rust it
accepts natively. Natively compiling every audit-replay compile that wasm32
refused (2,059 of about 10,300 compiles of about 5,100 programs at O0 and
O2) found nine, in seven programs, refused only on wasm32: a crate defining
`__wasm_call_ctors`, which `wasm-ld` synthesizes (`[TCG-WASM-SYMBOL]`); an
`extern "C"` function taking a `#[repr(C)]` wrapper of `u128` by value; and,
at `-O2` only, `iter::from_fn`, `repeat_with` and `successors` under
`take(n).sum()`, `<[T]>::swap` over 24-byte or 4-aligned 16-byte elements,
and `rev().count()` over a slice of `()`. Of those, only the
`__wasm_call_ctors` crate is still refused; the others now compile and
agree with LLVM in the differential corpus. Its own frontend
limits apply unchanged: loops
that rotate or swap loop-carried values, or thread a memory read through
the back edge, are refused as `[TCG-SSA-071]`; a deref through a pointer
local whose own address may be kept is refused as `[TCG-RETAINED-ADDR]`;
`#[track_caller]` closures called from a modeled iterator lane are refused
as `[TCG-TRACK-CALLER-ABI]`. `tests/wasm32_differential.rs` compiles 37
`no_std` corpus crates (about 760 exports, 6 of the crates against
dependency crates built by either backend) with this lane and with LLVM, at
debug and in 81 further optimization and codegen-unit configurations, and
runs both in node; every export must agree, traps included. Its
`wasm32_bounds_check_panic_runs_the_handler_like_llvm` case compares what a
recording `#[panic_handler]` observes of an out-of-bounds index (its
location, the message's kind and a hash of the formatted text) with LLVM at
`-O0` to `-O3`. Its `wasm32_in_bounds_addresses_are_geps_only_at_o1_and_above`
case reads the lane's input module of `r15-bridge-place-projections.rs`: no
GEP at O0, with `no-wasm32-place-gep` or with `-Copt-level=2` and the
bridge knob `opt-level=0`, and at O1 to O3 (also `-Copt-level=0` with
`opt-level=2`) only `inbounds u8`
GEPs by a constant in `1..=i32::MAX`, one in each projection kind's function
and none in the negative controls (OD-140); the projection crate, like
`r15-bridge-mem-intrinsics.rs` (constant-count `memmove`/`memcpy`/`memset`
through `ptr::swap`, `ptr::copy`, `copy_nonoverlapping` and `write_bytes`),
is also compared against LLVM at `-O0` to `-O3`. It skips without a wasm32
sysroot, `wasm-ld` or `node`. That corpus, the audit replays and the native
execution differentials are the evidence for the Rust lane; none is a proof.

It is not a general Rust codegen backend.

## Optimization and performance

- O0 is the conservative evaluation baseline. O1–O3 exist and are actively
  tested, but confidence and coverage vary by pass, target, and input shape.
- Per-pass translation validation (`L10-P3`,
  [`pass_validation`](crates/trust-cg-opt/src/pass_validation/mod.rs)) covers
  seven AArch64 passes (the default diagnostic runs only the first two):
  both list schedulers (dependence preservation, also
  for the codegen pipeline's final scheduling), `mem-pair-formation`,
  `if-convert`, `late-boolean-diamond` and `tiny-loop-diamond` (symbolic
  equivalence of each changed acyclic single-entry region) and `licm`
  (code-motion side conditions). Every other scheduled AArch64 pass has no
  dedicated validator. In the default and proof-grade modes its changed runs
  are recorded as uncovered, not refused, and its unchanged runs are not
  checked: the unchanged-claim check runs on every pass only under
  `TRUST_CG_PASS_VALIDATION_SCOPE=all`. The same holds for the extended loop
  rotation (outside the pass manager), the post-allocation branch layout and
  the opt-in CEGIS superoptimizer, recorded as `branch-layout` and
  `cegis-superopt`.
  The ledger row asks proof-required modes to refuse a MISSING validation;
  they do not. Proof-grade publication and certified pass execution refuse a
  failed covered run but not an uncovered one, and only the explicit
  `require-coverage` policy refuses uncovered runs. As things stand it would
  refuse nearly every optimized compile: on 20 Darwin floor targets, 5,805
  changed runs were uncovered against 798 validated.
  Under `TRUST_CG_PASS_VALIDATION_SCOPE=all` a generic region check runs on
  every pass. On the compile corpus it validated 57% of the other passes'
  changed runs: nearly all of `dce`, `cfg-simplify`, `declarative-rewrite`,
  `addr-mode` and `cmp-branch-fusion`, and few of `copy-prop`, `cse`, `gvn`
  and `sroa`, whose cross-block value equalities it does not model. It
  validated none of the loop restructuring and vectorizer passes.
  What a verdict is not: it is translation validation of
  one run under the validators' machine model, which shares the operand-role
  and memory-effect tables with the passes, interprets only an integer
  subset (moves, add/sub/logic/shift/multiply/divide, extends, bitfields,
  selects, compares, base-plus-immediate and pair loads and stores) and
  treats every other instruction as an uninterpreted deterministic value or
  an observable effect. Equal normalized terms are the only acceptance, so
  it is incomplete. Regions with loops, jump tables, invoke blocks or
  indirect branches are not modeled. Exception edges are followed: a
  landing pad is a region of its own, and liveness flows through the edge.
  LICM's hoists are shown either as loop-preheader moves or, for pure
  values, as moves to any dominating block that no reader can tell apart.
  In an invoke block, a call's exception edge counts as an exit: a move
  placed after the call must not be skippable on a path to its source, and
  one placed ahead of it must not be read by a landing pad. A hoisted load
  passes an in-loop store only when both are bounded direct accesses to
  different fixed stack slots. Distinct symbols are not disjoint memory to
  the validator (OD-127). A hoisted register no other instruction writes is
  exempt from the liveness checks only when the preheader lies on no cycle.
  Only the dependence and unchanged-claim checks report `refuted`. The
  region and hoist checks report every failure as `unproved`, a genuine
  violation included: the guarded mem-pair miscompile was found as
  `unproved`.
  In proof-grade publication and certified pass execution, a covered run the
  validator cannot show refuses the compile even when the rewrite is correct.
  Measured at `ec6c90504`, and again at `c48a01e49` after merging main, no
  covered run failed on the compile corpus's 247 modules
  ([report](reports/perf/2026-10-01-l10p3-pass-validation/README.md)).
  The whole Darwin floor (292 targets) at `ec6c90504`, run under `enforce`
  with the dedicated scope, had no compile refused by validation. The first
  such run, at `63a8ea224`, refused three targets on correct rewrites: LICM
  guard-preheader and cross-loop hoists, and mem-pair formation in a
  landing pad. The validators then learned dominating moves and exception
  edges.
  The default diagnostic refuses nothing. It records the verdicts in
  `PreparationMetrics::pass_validation` and the compile result's
  `CompilationMetrics::pass_validation`, and prints a `trust-cg: warning:`
  line on standard error for each refuted or unproved run.
  Cost, in instructions retired on the compile corpus with emitted bytes
  unchanged: the default tier runs only the schedulers' validator, at +0.47%
  to +0.80%. The dedicated tier costs +5.0% to +8.0%. The rustc bridge's
  default route is proof grade, because it emits proof certificates unless
  told not to, so every default bridge compile pays the dedicated tier:
  +8.56% on the corpus's 98 bridge pairs, measured at `bc4be093d` with a
  probe build that skipped only the proof-grade raise.
  A validated pass's certified-pass-chain record travels in the chain's
  existing `lean5` checker envelope (`checker.kind = "lean5"`, placeholder
  transport). Its evidence class is the record's `local_checker.kind`
  (`trust-cg-opt-translation-validation`), not a Lean check.
  The native target's Linux arm has not run.
- Rewrites that run new code INSTEAD OF some of a scalar loop's iterations (a
  vector loop, an unrolled body, a closed form, a nest replacement, a deleted
  loop) are admitted by one rule with three clauses, stated once in
  `crates/trust-cg-opt/src/loop_contract.rs` over both machine IRs.
  CONTROL: every way the scalar loop can leave must be the plan's loop test,
  an exit the new code reproduces (`neon_find`'s match), or an exit the pass
  proves no replaced iteration takes. The contract enumerates the exits
  itself (edges and fall-throughs out of the loop, trap carriers, returns,
  indirect branches), not the pass. It admits on its own terms an unsigned
  bounds check of the induction against a bound at least the loop test's,
  when the check runs only in iterations the test admitted and before the
  induction's advance, so `a[i]` over an array of the loop's length still
  vectorizes. Any other proved-untaken claim is a pre-guard the pass checks
  before its new code (`swap_range_guard`, `mac_row_unroll`,
  `mac_reg_block`, the x86 saxpy-Q runtime obligations and window scan),
  which the contract takes on the pass's word. REGISTERS: every register the
  loop carries across its back edge or leaves live at an exit must be one the
  new code reproduces. NZCV / EFLAGS count as a register; a call, a phi, a
  physical-register operand or an implicit register effect in the loop
  refuses. Each such pass builds its plan only through the sealed
  `LoopLocality` token, and the private statements it replaced were deleted
  (the register scans, and the exit checks of `strided_store_unroll`,
  `mac_row_unroll` and `dead_loop`): `neon_array`, `neon_bytesum`,
  `neon_fill`, `vectorize` (two idioms and the in-place path),
  `neon_iota_fill`, `neon_stencil`, `neon_reduce`, `neon_minmax`,
  `neon_predsum`, `neon_farray`, `neon_fpred`, `neon_fmap`, `neon_condstore`,
  `neon_find`, `neon_bitrev`, `neon_map`, `neon_butterfly`, `scalar_unroll`,
  `strided_store_unroll`, `mac_row_unroll`, `swap_range_guard`,
  `mac_reg_block`, `reduction_split` (split and closed form), `dead_loop` and
  every `x86_vectorize` plan. What the rule does NOT decide: memory (each
  pass's own alias and bounds obligation); whether the new code really
  reproduces the registers and exits a pass names, and whether the loop test
  a plan names is the one its trip count comes from (the recognizer); and
  whether a pre-guard really proves its exits untaken. ITERATIONS: the new
  code and the scalar remainder together must run exactly the iterations
  the scalar loop runs. The first two clauses read the loop before the
  rewrite and cannot see what the new code computes: `vectorize` passed
  them and still divided its own induction's trip bound (16 of 64 lanes,
  `4b1fb93c7`) and left remainder lanes in blocks nothing branched to and
  ran an undivided bound past an odd trip count, a nonzero start and an
  inclusive test (`a0603f3bc`), each fixed by a private check. The third
  clause (`loop_contract/coverage.rs`) runs the rewritten code before it is
  published: the TRIP SLICE of the original and the rewritten function
  (every register a branch or trap condition depends on, and of a trap
  whose test the model does not compute, the operands it names; a loaded
  value, or one an unmodeled instruction wrote, is unknown, and a branch or
  conditional trap on it that leaves the loop is taken as not taken in the
  scalar loop, whose exits the control clause accounts for, and in the
  rewritten code only at an instruction tied to such a scalar exit taken
  as not taken on the same inputs: the same instruction in the same loop
  block, kept or rewritten in place, or in a block the rewrite names as a
  copy of it, leaving to the same block, one for one (in each such block
  the instructions of one text stand in order for the scalar block's of
  that text, and only when there are equally many, so a new exit of the
  text of the scalar loop's own ties neither); a trap whose test the model
  does not compute is never taken as not taken in the rewritten code when
  the run knows every operand it names; any other refuses, and that a tied
  exit's undecided value is the scalar exit's, whatever computes it (for a
  flag reader, the compare its text does not name), so that it fires in
  the iteration the scalar one would, is the pass's premise) from the
  loop's preheader, for every input
  it samples (0, 1, one short of, at and one past every power of two up to
  1024, 48, 100, 1000, and the 32- and 64-bit edges; every pair of up to two
  inputs, and a fixed sparser selection of three or more, in which an
  input only the operands a carrier names make one (no modeled branch or
  trap condition reads it) does not count: the other inputs take the
  combinations they take without it, each run once for every combination
  of such inputs over 0, 1, 17, 64, 1000 and the maximum, the combinations
  of all the inputs counted together run as well, and past 12,000 crossed
  combinations the clause refuses; a value an unmodeled preheader
  instruction writes is one input
  for both functions only when the rewritten preheader agrees with the
  scalar one instruction for instruction up to it, else the rewritten code
  runs with it unknown), counting each entry into a block the rewrite names
  as the iterations it claims and each entry into a kept scalar loop's
  header by the scalar loop's rule (a top-tested loop's final, exiting
  entry is not an iteration), so a kept scalar loop must be unchanged (the
  same instructions and layout successors) and entered from new code only
  at its header, or the clause refuses; the counts, the exit (a return, a
  trap, an indirect branch and a tail call are four outcomes) and the

  as not taken, the new code's own included; modeled every AArch64 and x86

  return and a trap into one outcome; and read AArch64 `MOVWrr` as a 64-bit

  *Correction (2026-10-10, review of `f2788e9ab`; recorded 2026-10-11):*

  `e2e_aarch64_udot_popcount`, `e2e_aarch64_vec_len_guard_differential`
  and `wasm_p8_loops`) and `trust-cg-llvm-import`'s
  `bitreverse_intrinsics` reach 791 coverage verdicts outside the clause's

  *Correction (2026-10-11, review of `23ed4a3e0`):* "Each is refused now"

  Measured at `fbdb55042` against `23ed4a3e0` over the same suites: 804

  *Correction (2026-10-11, review of `fbdb55042`, merged at `27aeaa0df`):*
  "every pair of up to two inputs" stopped holding there, and the sampled
  carrier operands newly admitted a rewrite. An operand live into the loop
  that only a carrier names was an input counted with the ones the branches

  A long loop is advanced in one step only where an affine re-execution of
  its iteration proves the path and every decision exactly (linear compares
  within their no-wrap range, equality modulo the width), so a
  16777216-iteration loop is decided
  exactly; anything else is stepped within a budget, and an exhausted budget
  refuses. Runs that reach a block in the same state are merged, so a
  region with a cycle that passes no counted block is refused undecided: a
  run around it never leaves, and before this rule the merge dropped it and
  a rewrite that hung was admitted (a unit row, red before the rule). It is
  a decision for the inputs it runs, not a proof for all
  inputs, and two inputs the program can only hold together are sampled
  independently (refusing, never admitting). `vectorize`'s in-place rewrite,
  `neon_fill` and `loop_unroll`'s bounded-early-exit tier publish through it
  (`publish_covered`, `candidate::commit_covered`); the private `vectorize`
  checks the clause subsumes, and its unreachable scalar epilogue, are
  deleted, and its plain (no induction) path, whose test fixtures are not
  counted loops, no longer publishes on them. Three checks stay beside the
  clause (`clause_gap`; each was measured wrong without it on 2026-10-10).
  Two of them `95660b90e` deleted and 2026-10-10 restored. The header must
  run only its exit test, because the clause does not count a top-tested
  loop's final, exiting header entry and the rewrite counts latch entries,
  so work on that entry ran once in the scalar loop and on two lanes in the
  vector one. A plan's trip must be fixed at compile time, an induction
  plan's and a plain (no induction) plan's alike: a header constant bound
  tested against a counter that enters the loop as a constant and changes
  only by one step in the latch that reads the counter and constants alone,
  every other in-loop definition of the counter a copy of the step's result
  after it. A trip that depends on a run-time value is decided only at the
  sampled values: `(argc == 6) ? 13 : 2 * argc` ran one extra lane at `argc
  == 6`, and a start entering through a header copy of the step's result ran
  one on MachIR. The third is the unplanned-effect rule: every instruction
  of the loop that the plan does not account for (its vectorized
  instructions, reduction bridges, the induction's step and the header's
  exit branch) must only compute registers, because the rewrite leaves it
  scalar and runs it once per vector iteration, so a store of the induction
  in the latch or the body ran on every second value (revertBits printed
  `last=16777214` for 16777215 at O2), and a load, call, trap or other
  conditional branch is refused the same way. With the three, no run-time
  value reaches the trip slice of a published plan, and the clause's one run
  decides its iteration count exactly. It decides the count only. What the
  planned instructions read is checked beside it, and what each lane
  computes from that stays the pass's premise. Review on 2026-10-11 found
  those reads broken on MachIR, each rewrite published with a wrong value,
  and the recognizers refuse each shape found first: an ordered-sub bridge
  address with any definition in the loop (a copy in the latch moved it to
  another slot, and both lanes accumulated into the slot the first lane
  saw); an induction alias or sign extension with a second definition, or a
  sign extension that reads neither the induction nor a register with one
  definition (the vectorized `rbit` read the lanes where the scalar loop
  read 5); and lanes that do not reach every reader (built at the first
  reader the plan lists, after a reader in an earlier block or ahead of the
  first direct reader of the induction, or after the latch's write-back,
  where they hold the induction advanced by `vf`). The final review of
  `27aeaa0df` found the class still open: register work resetting the
  bridge's loaded accumulator between its load and its reducer (kept once
  per vector iteration, so both lanes were subtracted from 0), or the
  `rbit` result between it and its bridge (ignored for the lanes), a
  compare idiom reading the induction ahead of its lanes, and reads given
  lanes of registers the rewrite builds none for (a header copy, a constant
  set in the loop, a loop invariant, the previous iteration's value), where
  the rewrite read a SIMD register nothing writes. `clause_gap` now checks
  every read of the planned instructions over the loop's paths
  (`planned_input_gap`): no in-loop definition the plan does not make may
  reach it, and a read given lanes, other than of the induction, must see
  on every path a value its iteration computes by a planned lane producer;
  the lane check counts compare idioms among the induction's readers. A
  plain (no induction) plan has no lanes to start from, so none is
  published. These checks decide what the planned instructions read, on
  register identities, and are not a proof that each lane computes the
  scalar iteration's value. Of the in-tree plans these checks drop one, a
  test fixture's: with every `clause_gap` refusal logged across
  `trust-cg-opt`'s targets, two `trust-cg-llvm-import` programs and 37
  `trust-cg-codegen` NEON, unroll and vectorizer targets, the refusals added
  on 2026-10-10 fired only on rows built for them, and revertBits' O2 loop
  still vectorizes; with every plan, `clause_gap` verdict and publication
  logged over the same targets, the first 2026-10-11 checks changed none,
  and the final review's changed only that fixture's plain plan
  (`test_plain_plan_with_a_run_time_counter_start_declines`), refused where
  it was published reading lanes nothing builds. Every other rewrite above
  still admits through the first two clauses only, listed by file in
  `crates/trust-cg-opt/src/loop_contract/coverage_routes.txt`, which a unit
  test recounts; `vectorize`'s two idioms stay there because a stack-slot
  induction needs a memory model the clause does not have. A
  pass whose rewrite resumes only at the scalar header, or only at named
  blocks, says so and a test checks that premise. The x86 CRC-table and
  window-scan recognizers go through the contract but have no fixture
  anywhere, so no row exercises them. Passes that run every iteration and
  replace none (`loop_unroll` and `x86_loop_unroll` full unrolling,
  `x86_licm`, `loop_unswitch`, `alias_hoist`, `recurrence_store_forward`,
  `resid_collapse`, `x86_latch_dup`'s latch tail duplication and
  `x86_loop_simplify`'s preheader insertion) are outside the rule, as is
  `loop_dead_pure_sink`, which removes only a slice whose definitions have no
  use outside it. A full unroll deletes register work it judges dead (each
  copy's trip test); the contract states that rule once too
  (`DeadWork::check`: nothing kept reads what a deleted instruction wrote,
  flags included, on any path), and `loop_unroll`'s copy-counted,
  bounded-early-exit and diamond tiers ask it, their private scans deleted.
  The bounded-early-exit address fold asks it for the `Madd` it deletes but
  also re-points loads, and the rule walks forward from the deleted
  instruction: a load ahead of the `Madd` of an address the loop carries
  reads the previous iteration's value, and from `95660b90e` until
  2026-10-10 the last iteration's fold re-pointed it to the next element (a
  unit row, interpreted). The fold again requires every operand naming the
  address to be a load or store it re-points in that iteration, and, from
  2026-10-10, a base the unrolled loop does not define: `[base, #off]` is
  the `Madd`'s address only while the base holds what the `Madd` read, and
  a base bumped between the `Madd` and its load had every iteration load
  the element past its own (a unit row, interpreted; the scan before
  `95660b90e` did not check the base either). That rule refused no fold
  in the logged suites but that row. The
  bounded-early-exit tier
  dropped a trip test an exit still read and folded away an address a store
  at the exit used until `e6dbb93df`; the diamond tier's scan covered only
  the trip boolean, so an exit reading the dropped compare's flags unrolled
  anyway (a unit fixture of each diamond variant, red before the rule).
  `x86_loop_unroll` and `loop_unroll`'s legacy Phi tier do not ask it. An x86 recognizer with a bail trace names the escape (a
  register or an exit) when the contract refuses. The evidence is tests:
  per-pass unit rows over both IRs and the whole-program rows of
  `crates/rustc-codegen-trust-cg/tests/opt_loop_state_run.rs` (aarch64
  natively, x86-64 under Rosetta), not a proof. The parts are not equally
  evidenced. Without the register clause 21 (aarch64) and 37 (x86-64)
  whole-program rows per level are wrong; with its header half alone (the
  exit half removed) every row agrees, and only 15 unit rows fail. Every
  measured live-out row is also live into the header, and the shape only
  the exit half sees (a bottom-tested loop that writes the register first)
  is vectorized by no pass today. Without the control clause (measured on
  aarch64 at O2 and O3, the same at `c84d39e93`) 30 early-exit rows per level
  are wrong (`neon_fill` ran its vector loop past a `break` or `return`
  inside the vector prefix), and three canary programs per level go wrong: a
  `break` at 64 over a 64-byte raw buffer (the call returned 1000 and wrote
  over 900 bytes past it), a fill of a 64-byte slice to 1000 (896 to 903
  bytes written past the slice before its bounds-check panic), and a
  stride-3 marking loop to 1024 over a 64-byte slice
  (`strided_store_unroll`: SIGSEGV where LLVM panics). x86-64 was right on
  all of them. With the clause every row agrees on both targets. On a
  131-kernel probe (aarch64 and x86-64, O2 and O3, 522 cells) the clause
  changed exactly the 20 cells that were wrong and no other, and the 18
  beat-llvm programs keep their exit codes and vector-instruction counts.
  Dropping the clause again fails 12 unit tests, brings back the three
  canary programs' wrong exits, and stops the aarch64 loop-state program
  compiling (`strided_store_unroll` then unrolls the `strided_brk` kernel
  past its `break`, and the AArch64 spill-slot check refuses the result), so
  the early-exit rows' own failure under that mutant is not observed; it is
  observed on the code before the clause, above.
- JIT compiles that claim no proof run the module inliner at O1+
  (`prepare_jit_lir_module`), and a bodied trust-ir `AvailableExternally`
  function is an inline-only template there and at the AOT inliner seam
  (`Compiler::compile`). Splicing one rests on the one-definition rule (the
  body computes what the extern- or linker-bound definition computes), which
  nothing checks. Every body spliced is disclosed in `inline_only_bodies` (on
  `JitCompilationResult` and `CompilationResult`). A body authenticated
  against caller-supplied dependencies
  (`Compiler::with_inline_only_dependencies`: an import row `verify_import`
  accepts, a definition whose translation is the same LIR) is recorded as a
  discharged premise instead. A compile that makes a proof claim
  (`emit_proofs`, or a verifying JIT validation mode such as x86-64's default
  `CachedVerified`) runs no LIR inliner at all (OD-225). It splices no body,
  authenticated or not, and lists every inline-only body in `withheld`.
  The Core JIT plan does not take inline-only bodies; the CompileService
  install records (as opposed to its payloads) do not name the premises; a
  module's own one-block
  definition with a load or store is not an inlining template (one-block
  inline-only bodies with memory operations are). The
  x86-64 JIT half of this is unexecuted on the Apple Silicon host that
  measured it (`docs/jit-inline-only-bodies.md`).
- `CompilerConfig::never_inline` names functions the module inliner never
  splices (rustc's `#[inline(never)]`; trust-ir carries no such attribute, so
  a producer supplies the names). The set is unioned into the names OPT-4
  already withholds, at the AOT seam (every target) and in the JIT module
  step, so a call to a named function stays a call; a named inline-only body
  is not spliced either. OPT-4 is the only inliner a compile runs (the
  machine-level `inline` pass has no callee registered). The set controls
  splicing only, not what other passes do to a call (a sibling call in tail
  position may still become a `b` at O2/O3). The set is part of
  the compile policy's Artifact projection and the artifact-cache identity
  when non-empty, and the Core JIT proof-grade boundary refuses a non-empty
  set.
- Integer-array reductions now use checked candidate construction across all
  five builders. Native controls cover selected signed/unsigned index domains,
  narrow/widening reductions, top-tested and rotated EQ/GE loops, and scalar
  fallbacks, captured widened bounds and mixed-width comparisons. They exposed
  repaired entry/index-domain and stale-source substitution defects; they are not
  exhaustive vector equivalence, arbitrary malformed-IR safety, frontend
  coverage or a benchmark for whole-function cloning. Wider indices outside
  the i32 address domain stay scalar, as do 64-bit compared bounds that differ
  from their i32 projection. Extreme wraparound ranges remain outside the
  bounded native evidence; DotProd still requires target support.
- The conditional-store vectorizer's private builder shares the checked
  candidate-construction helpers, but its public pass stays disabled pending
  typed writable/single-owner range authority.
- FP array vectorization leaves in-loop negation and repeated stores through
  one base scalar. Zero-minus-value is not exact FP negation, and a shared
  post-increment pointer cannot represent two stores to the same element.
  Widening reductions and iota fills run by default; pure-f64 reductions remain
  opt-in. Candidate/alias-guard regressions and native fill controls (executed
  on macOS ARM64; the Linux GNU arm awaits a Linux run) provide bounded
  evidence, not a complete native or formal vectorization
  campaign. The native controls use a post-pass iteration observer and a platform
  C caller; they are not frontend coverage or a benchmark.
- The matmul register-blocking pass `mac-reg-block` runs by default at O2
  and O3 on one shape only: the three-deep square i64 nest
  `c[i*N+j] += a[i*N+k] * b[k*N+j]` in `i, k, j` order over three distinct
  stack-local arrays, with `N` a constant multiple of 12 or 8 (a 12- or
  8-accumulator tile) no larger than 504 and every index bounds-checked. The
  recognizer accepts a check as a compare and branch, or as a trapping
  `TrapBoundsCheckExact` carrier with a constant length. The rustc bridge
  emits a MIR bounds check as a compare and branch to a block that calls the
  real `panic_bounds_check` and then `unreachable`. Before TrustIR v52 it
  emitted a constant-length check as a `const` + `icmp ult` + `assert`
  triple, which lowered to the carrier; the shared admission floor now
  refuses that triple as a kindless source `assert`, so the bridge no longer
  produces carriers. The recognizer refuses by name the publication review
  items: 32-bit or other non-64-bit values in 8-byte cells, any bounds
  check, carrier or backing slot shorter than `N*N`, a carrier with a
  register length or on a value that is not a recognized index, a check of
  an index that is not the current iteration's (computed in a loop header,
  or checked after its loop exits), any conditional branch other than the
  loop tests and those checks (early exits, conditional stores), work other
  than copies and the counter test in a loop header, an access outside the
  body of its own loop, a read that its single definition does not dominate,
  a loop counter read outside its loop or after its latch step, a counter
  not reset once per parent iteration, and any value the nest writes that is
  live after it, unless the nest only copies that value out and back (the
  bridge threads outer-loop values through inner loops that way). Until
  2026-09-28 six such shapes were admitted and miscompiled at O2 and O3, and
  the bridge's own nests were all refused (its checks were carriers).
  Rectangular nests, other `N`, other loop orders, arrays reached through
  pointer parameters or held in a `Vec` (a length known only at run time),
  and i32 or f64 elements are left as scalar loops; `mac-row-unroll`, which
  unrolls the inner loop of a nest this pass leaves alone, still refuses the
  carrier form. The release gate `e2e_aarch64_mac_reg_block_differential`
  (nine tests) compiles, with compare-and-branch checks whose failure
  returns -1, 16 kernels in the modeled shape (11 must be rewritten exactly
  once, with the 12-lane tile exactly when 12 divides `N`, and the 5 whose
  `N` is neither a multiple of 8 nor of 12 must not be), 17 kernels that
  must stay unrewritten (13 of them negative controls), and a 28-kernel
  fixed-seed sweep. Each is built at O2 and O3 with the pass on and off, and
  all four builds run in forked children against a C reference. It also
  compiles the `p4_matmul` nest the current bridge emits (captured from the
  bridge of 25f0d2efc), whose failed checks call `panic_bounds_check`: the
  pass must rewrite it exactly once at O2 and O3, and all four builds, run
  through the unchecked JIT with the panic entry bound to a stub that
  records its arguments, must equal a C transcription over nine repetition
  counts. A copy with one check a single element short must stay unrewritten
  and, in every build, make the reference's `panic_bounds_check` call with
  the check's source location. The same 61 kernels in the pre-v52 bridge
  triple, and the `p4_matmul` nest as the bridge emitted it before v52, are
  admission fixtures only: each must be refused at the shared floor
  (`require_assert_panic_kinds`) at O2 and O3, on the object path and the
  JIT. The pass's carrier-form recognition therefore has no native evidence.
  The gate has run on macOS ARM64; the Linux GNU arm awaits a Linux run. It
  is a bounded differential over the listed shapes, sizes, seeds and
  repetition counts, not a proof: the recognizer's guards are checked by
  unit tests on hand-built machine IR, and the rewrite has no certificate or
  translation validation of its own.
- Two AArch64 O2/O3 transforms remove the bounds check of `while k <
  v.len() { .. v[k] .. }` over a `Vec` whose header stays in a stack slot.
  LICM hoists a loop-invariant plain load that is not guaranteed to run
  (it sits behind the loop's exit test) only when its address resolves,
  through copies, immediate offsets and constant-index GEPs, to one
  fixed-size stack slot and the accessed bytes lie inside it; the loop must
  still write no memory, or only bounded direct accesses in distinct fixed
  stack slots. Name-only global and stack-versus-global alias permission was
  withdrawn; the shared memory-motion floor
  retains its lost capabilities and regression qualification. A
  pointer loaded from memory, a parameter, a runtime-sized slot or a second
  value-changing definition of the base keeps the load in the loop.
  aarch64-bounds-check-elim folds an explicit `cmp idx, len ; b.hs trap`
  whose failing successor only executes `BRK` when a dominating strict
  unsigned guard tests the same index root against the same length root, or
  against an equal load of the same bytes in the same block with no write
  between. It declines non-strict and signed guards, proof-annotated
  checks, other failing successors, and every function with a volatile
  access (the volatile-trace check would refuse the lost path). The release
  gate `e2e_aarch64_vec_len_guard_differential` compiles the Vec and boxed
  sum shapes and four negative controls at O2 and O3 with both transforms on
  and off, and runs them against a C reference over 15 lengths, 3 pass
  counts and 2 seeds; the two negative controls whose check must fire have
  to die by SIGTRAP exactly where the reference traps. Its preheader-writer
  rows run four kernels whose preheader stores to the slot the loop reads
  (after a mid-block `TrapBoundsCheckExact` carrier, or as its last
  instruction) over 12 `x` values and 6 trip counts; they pin LICM's
  insertion point after every preheader store, call and trap guard. It has
  run on macOS ARM64; the Linux GNU arm awaits a Linux run. It is a bounded
  differential, not a proof; neither transform has a certificate or
  translation validation of its own.
- NEON LD1/ST1 post-index words are executed natively through three
  emitters. `neon_ld1_st1_post_execution` decodes `neon_fmap`'s one-vector
  remainder loop in the final object and runs it against a C oracle at O2
  and O3 for f32/f64 in-place maps and rotated two- and three-array maps.
  `neon_butterfly_writeback_execution` does the same for `neon_butterfly`'s
  vector body in three f32 FFT butterfly loops. The ST1 of `vectorize.rs`'s
  i32 induction-store rewrite runs in the default O2, Os and O3 pipelines.
  `ary3_init_o2_e2e` links and runs its two imported-O0 fixtures natively
  for the host's triple (executed on macOS ARM64, and on Linux AArch64 GNU
  on 2026-10-23 with LD-96's repair, which restored
  the MADD address the rewrite reads). Their own checks cover every stored
  element and sentinel for entry indices that are zero, nonzero, negative
  and next to `i32::MAX`.
  Runs of two or more vector iterations advance the store base only through
  the ST1 post-index writeback. That target requires the ST1 to be present
  but does not decode or isolate its words. Other emitters are not covered,
  and most cannot run in the default pipelines:
  - the `vectorize.rs` contains4 LD1 needs an opt-in environment switch;
  - the trailing ST1 of `neon_map` and `neon_stencil` cannot occur with
    their even unroll factor;
  - `neon_condstore` is unscheduled.

  The `neon_iota_fill` LD1/ST1 uses are not exercised. The two targets run
  the shapes and inputs they name, and this is not a proof of either
  transform.

  In `neon_ld1_st1_post_execution` the executed LD1/ST1 words observe the
  transfer (address, width, arrangement and data) but not the post-index
  base-register update. `neon_fmap` recomputes every remainder-loop pointer
  with MADD, so the `#16` writeback of all 20 executed words is dead. That
  target enforces this: each word rewritten to the no-writeback `[Xn]` form
  or to the register post-index `[Xn], X1` form must still pass the C
  oracle, and the decode gate must refuse it.

  `neon_butterfly` walks one pointer per stream and nothing recomputes it,
  so its 12 executed writebacks are live. A walk over the decoded control
  flow shows each is read as a base on the next iteration before any
  redefinition. Each word rewritten to `[Xn]`, or to a register post-index
  by a register the decoded stream proves holds 8, fails the oracle, and
  only in calls that run two or more vector pairs. The limits of that
  evidence:
  - the kernels are one butterfly shape with strict `llvm.fma.f32` and
    twiddle offsets 0 and 8. A 4,088-byte offset, which the matcher admits,
    did not vectorize in an exploratory O2 compile: the `+4092` address of
    the second twiddle field was hoisted out of the loop instead of folded
    into its load, so the two twiddle loads no longer share a base. Clang's
    `llvm.fmuladd` form is not run;
  - Os schedules the pass but is not reachable through `Compiler`, whose
    `OptLevel` stops at O3;
  - the oracle performs each operation with the host's scalar instruction
    (inline assembly, in the loop's operand order), so it checks agreement
    with scalar execution on that host, not IEEE conformance.
- CEGIS, PGO, vectorization, compute-graph/dispatch planning, Metal emission,
  CoreML MIL construction and ONNX-to-VNN import include real implementations.
  Dispatch plans do not supply an accelerator runtime, and production CoreML
  graph emission refuses without an exact tensor recipe. ONNX emits standalone
  tensor JSON rather than TrustIR. These boundaries remain after removal of the
  separate GPU runtime crate.
- The AArch64 CEGIS budget (`--cegis-superopt=<SECS>`) is wall-clock time,
  not deterministic fuel. Its clock starts at a function's first
  solver-backed verification, and no further verification starts after it
  has elapsed. A function with at most one such candidate gets the same
  outcome at any machine load only if that query finishes within the
  per-query limit (`per_query_ms`, 5 s in the compiler pipeline). That limit
  is also wall-clock time. It covers the whole exchange, including waiting
  for the solver and the Clean replay, and a query that exceeds it ends as
  `QueryIncomplete`. With two or more candidates, a slow or loaded machine can
  also refuse a later query. Either way the compile fails with
  `CegisIncomplete` instead of emitting a partial result. The first
  proof-bearing query in a process also content-hashes the Clean checker,
  which takes about 1.9 s in an unoptimized build on the Linux AArch64 host.
- The walk that finds AArch64 CEGIS candidates is linear in the function and
  the budget does not bound it. Replaying a cached CEGIS result is not
  linear: each recorded rewrite is revalidated by scanning the function, so a
  cache hit costs time proportional to the recorded rewrites times the
  function size. A release build took about 11 s to replay 24,000 rewrites in
  one 72,000-instruction block. Each recorded rewrite needed an admitted
  verification, but the process proof cache can answer repeated identical
  obligations, so the budget does not bound how many a search records.
- An AArch64 CEGIS obligation states that the rewritten instruction's
  destination holds the same value after the original window as after the
  replacement. The original side runs the materializer (`Movz`, `Movn`,
  `Movk`, read from its `imm16` and `hw` fields) and the `MulRR`, `AddRR` or
  `AndRR` it feeds; the replacement's immediate is first encoded as the
  codegen encoder encodes it and then decoded (`ZeroExtend(imm12)`, or the
  Arm ARM `DecodeBitMasks`). A replacement with a wrong immediate, source
  register or operation is refuted, no obligation is `X == X`, and AY must
  produce an Alethe proof that the identity-pinned Clean checker accepts.
  Outside the proof: that the removed materializer is the reaching
  definition of its register and that nothing else reads it (structural
  checks over the shared operand-role model and the whole instruction arena,
  checked against the register allocator's partition for every opcode but
  not proven); the window interpreter itself, whose semantics for its eight
  opcodes are transcribed and whose encoder mirrors are checked against the
  real encoder's words, but which no independent decoder checks; and cache
  replay, which does not repeat the proof (next item).
- The AArch64 CEGIS cache is integrity-checked against the matcher, not
  signed. Its entries carry no MAC and the codec checks only their format.
  A cache hit applies a recorded rewrite only where the search's matcher,
  run on the current body, admits the recorded window and rebuilds exactly
  the recorded body (opcode, register ids and classes, immediates). Any
  other entry is stale: the function is searched again and a complete
  search rewrites the entry. Replay does not re-run the solver, so a writer
  of the cache root can still make the pass apply a matcher candidate
  without its proof, or drop rewrites and lose optimization. The root is
  `TRUST_CG_CEGIS_CACHE`, else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/trust-cg-cegis`, else
  `~/.cache/trust-cg-cegis`, else the host-shared
  `<temp dir>/.trust-cg-cegis-cache`. On Unix it is used only if the
  directory it resolves to is owned by the current user and not group- or
  world-writable. Otherwise the process warns once (`refusing untrusted
  shared cache root`) and uses an in-memory cache. The cache creates
  directories `0700` and entries `0600`, and it is not opened by a compile
  without CEGIS. A root an earlier build created under a permissive umask
  (`0775`, as on the Linux host) is refused until its owner runs `chmod 700`
  on it. The root's ancestors are not checked. A user who can write a parent
  directory without the sticky bit could replace the root after the check.
  A function whose block schedule lists an instruction id more than once is
  not optimized, because an in-place rewrite would change every copy.
- The x86-64 CEGIS pass (`TCG_CEGIS_X86=<SECS>`) still checks a wall-clock
  deadline before each block and each candidate. It commits the rewrites
  proven before the deadline, so its output can depend on machine load, and
  it has none of the AArch64 pass's all-or-nothing transaction. Its
  immediate-fusion obligation is still `op(x, k) == op(x, k)`, built from the
  opcode alone, so its rewrites rest entirely on its matcher.
- The LLVM IR importer carries function and global linkage, visibility and
  `section` and admits only the self-keyed `any` COMDATs the backend emits
  itself (L02-P13). It refuses by name what trust-ir or the backend cannot
  express: `common`, `appending` (other than the `@llvm.used` arrays),
  `thread_local`, `externally_initialized`, DLL storage classes,
  `partition`, function `prefix`/`prologue` data, multi-member or
  non-`any` COMDATs, and every `alias` and `ifunc`, refused by its keyword
  (before the L02-P13 second closure-audit repair they were refused only by
  the generic "without `global`/`constant` storage class" message). So C built with `-fcommon` (clang before 11, and Apple
  clang for Darwin targets, which still defaults to it) and C++ with guard
  variables or static-initializer COMDATs do not import; the IntMM
  end-to-end test pins the `common` refusal for Apple clang's default IR and
  imports the same program built with `-fno-common`. An ODR or link-once
  definition written without a `comdat` clause is in no group in LLVM, and
  llc emits it as a plain weak symbol, so the importer carries it as the
  backend's ungrouped weak definition: a function's `linkonce_odr` as
  `LinkOnce` and `weak_odr` as `Weak`, and a global's `linkonce`,
  `linkonce_odr` and `weak_odr` as `Weak`. That gives up only what ODR lets
  an optimizer assume (the backend no longer inlines such a function).
  Before, every such definition went alone into a COMDAT group named after
  it, so an AArch64 ELF object linked before an LLVM object whose
  same-named group has a second member (clang's shape for an inline
  variable's guard) made GNU ld and LLD discard that group: its members
  became undefined weak and the program crashed, and gold refused the
  link. A function definition listed in `@llvm.used` is refused by name:
  LLVM retains its section (`SHF_GNU_RETAIN`), the backend does not admit
  trust-ir's `Function::retained`, and LLD `--gc-sections` removed the
  imported one. The array's names are matched as LLVM names symbols, so
  `@"reg"` and `@reg` (and `@"\72eg"`) are one: every quoted name is now
  read in its decoded spelling (L02-P15); before, the importer kept a
  quoted name's quotes, and a function listed in one spelling and defined
  in the other escaped the refusal. A global in `@llvm.used` is retained, under
  either spelling; one only in `@llvm.compiler.used` no longer is, because
  llc retains nothing for it (the retained section survived a
  `--gc-sections` link that dropped llc's). On AArch64 ELF a retained
  global is retained alone, as llc places it: in a section of its own
  (`.data.<symbol>`, `.bss.<symbol>`, `.rodata.<symbol>`,
  `.data.rel.ro.<symbol>`, or another section of its explicit name),
  flagged `SHF_GNU_RETAIN`. Before the second closure-audit repair the flag
  was set on the whole shared section the global was packed into, so every
  unlisted neighbour survived `--gc-sections` with it: an unlisted
  `.data` global whose pointer named an undefined function made the link
  fail where llc's linked (24 of 24 runs: O0-O3, static and PIE, GNU ld,
  gold and LLD), and LLD's
  `__start_`/`__stop_` walk of a named section saw three members where
  llc's saw one. The own section's name differs from llc's for a private
  global (`.data.p`; llc names its `.L` label, `.data..Lp`), an
  `unnamed_addr` constant whose mergeable section the importer gives up
  with `unnamed_addr` (`.rodata.c`; llc `.rodata.cst<N>.c`, or
  `.rodata.str<W>.<A>.c` for a string) and a relocated constant under the
  `static` model
  (`.data.rel.ro.c`; llc `.rodata.c`): the shared sections differ the same
  way without retention. Linkers place the relocated constant's sections
  alike, but they fold llc's mergeable ones: two equal `unnamed_addr`
  `i64` constants and two equal C strings in their implicit sections got
  one address each in llc's linked image and two in the import's (24 of 24
  runs: O0-O3, static and PIE, GNU ld, gold and LLD), which `unnamed_addr`
  permits either way (it lets equal constants share an address and does
  not require it). In an explicit section the same merge also moves the
  member a `__start_`/`__stop_` walk reads: LLVM gives a mergeable member
  a section of its own flags and entry size (`SHF_MERGE`), apart from the
  section's other members, and linkers fold its equal entries. Three
  `unnamed_addr` `i64` constants (5, 5 and 9) in one named section were
  walked as 2 entries with llc's object and 3 with the import's in 24 of 24
  runs, and llc wrote the eight members of a set mixing such constants with
  ordinary ones in five sections of that name (one per flags and entry
  size), where the import writes one in declaration order. Since the
  second verifier round of the L02-P13 second closure-audit repair the
  importer refuses by name an `unnamed_addr`
  constant with a `section` clause exactly when LLVM 22 makes it mergeable
  (`getKindForGlobal`: no relocation, and a null-terminated array of `i8`,
  `i16` or `i32` or 4, 8, 16 or 32 bytes; not in a section LLVM classifies
  by name, such as `.bss.*`). In a sweep of 1,050 one-global modules (35
  shapes, 6 section names, 5 prefixes) llc wrote `SHF_MERGE` for 200: the
  importer refuses 180 of them by this name and 20 for their literal
  struct type, which it does not import, and refuses none of the other 850
  by this name. `local_unnamed_addr` permits no such merge and is not
  refused. A hidden,
  protected or `extern_weak` declaration is written as an undefined symbol
  with that binding and visibility even when nothing references it, as llc
  writes it (an `available_externally` global and a default declaration
  are not); before, the AArch64 ELF emitters wrote an undefined symbol only
  for a referenced name, so an unreferenced hidden declaration no longer
  hid the C definition a `pic` shared object linked: the library exported
  it and an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer rebound the library's own call (1005
  where llc's library returned 12). GNU ld now refuses an executable that
  leaves such a hidden declaration undefined, as it refuses llc's object;
  gold and LLD link it. The same rule applies to every module the AArch64
  ELF emitters compile, the Rust bridge's included: a hidden declaration
  whose last reference the optimizer removed is still written. The four
  coverage-mapping section names LLVM makes non-allocated are refused by
  name (see the explicit-section paragraph). The floor target
  `symbol_linkage_elf` now carries host-neutral rows for every symbol fact
  the importer decides (its lib unit tests are not a floor lane) and native
  llc-twin rows for the retention and declaration facts. The audit's 51
  importer mutants, rerun at this repair's base, left 30 passing all
  sixteen floor importer targets; at the repair, `symbol_linkage_elf` alone
  fails 50 of them and 10 of the repair's own 11 (codegen retention,
  declaration and section mutants and the alias refusal). The two
  survivors are equivalent: one drops a decode `canonicalize` already did,
  and one adds `available_externally` to a set that already excludes every
  global with an initializer (L02-P13 second closure-audit repair). The
  repair's verifier round: a global declaration listed in `@llvm.used` (an
  `external` or `extern_weak` one, or a default `available_externally`
  global) is marked retained too and compiles on AArch64 and x86-64 ELF
  with llc's symbols for it (an undefined symbol when something references
  it or its visibility or weakness puts it in the table, none for an
  unreferenced default one), where every object path refused it; the
  Mach-O paths refuse it by name, because llc's Mach-O writer gives every
  listed declaration an `N_NO_DEAD_STRIP` undefined symbol, referenced or
  not, and so does the x86-64 COFF path, for llc's `/INCLUDE:` directive.
  That round also admitted a listed hidden or protected
  `available_externally` global, with a symbol llc does not write (below).
  The sections of a named set are emitted in llc's creation order
  whichever kinds its members are, where llc keeps module order (see the
  explicit-section paragraph). In that round `symbol_linkage_elf` gained
  three host-neutral and three native rows for these facts and for the x86-64
  ELF per-global retention (which only a lib unit test had pinned), and
  `aarch64_elf_symbol_binding` a row for the declared-undefined set through
  the Pipeline API; each of the round's 13 mutants (among them the
  verifier's three that the floor passed: COMDAT sections after the others,
  x86-64 retention per shared section, the declared-undefined validation
  switched off) fails one of those two floor targets. The second verifier
  round refuses by name an `available_externally` global with hidden or
  protected visibility,
  listed or not. llc 22 states no visibility for an `available_externally`
  global (`AsmPrinter::emitSpecialLLVMGlobal` skips it), so a reference to
  one is a `STV_DEFAULT` undefined symbol, which llc addresses PC-relative
  as a dso-local one; the import wrote the stated visibility on its
  undefined symbol (since L02-P6 for an unlisted one). Linked against a
  library that defines the symbol, the import's executables failed in 72
  of 72 configurations (a plain hidden, a listed hidden and a listed
  protected global; O0-O3; `-no-pie` and PIE executables; GNU ld, gold and
  LLD) where llc's linked and ran in 60, and a shared object linking the
  definition hid it (the hidden forms) where llc's, under gold, exported it
  (GNU ld and LLD refuse llc's PC-relative reference there). Writing a
  default symbol instead would keep the import's GOT reference to a symbol that is then
  preemptible, which llc's direct reference is not (that form, linked into
  a shared object with the definition, linked under all three linkers and
  read an `LD_PRELOAD` interposer's 1005 at O0-O3, where llc's linked under
  gold alone and read the definition's 12), so the global is
  refused; an `available_externally` function's visibility is written by
  llc and the import alike and stays admitted. A function declaration
  listed in `@llvm.used` is now admitted only when the compile target's
  object format is ELF and refused by name otherwise, with no target known
  too: llc's Mach-O writer writes the listing as an `N_NO_DEAD_STRIP`
  undefined symbol, its COFF writer (for an MSVC environment) as a
  `/INCLUDE:` directive and its Wasm writer as a no-strip undefined symbol
  (measured with llc 22.1.2), and no emitter here writes any of them for a
  function. Before, only a Mach-O triple was refused, so a module without a
  triple compiled for an Apple target dropped the listing (the object had
  no `_fd` where llc's has an `N_NO_DEAD_STRIP` one). The branch read a
  module's own triple as ELF only for a Linux OS or an `elf` environment;
  on its port onto L02-P15 (LD-23) the object format is the compile
  target's, read by `src/triple.rs` as LLVM 22.1.2's `Triple` reads it
  (the triple a caller passes to `import_text_for_target`, as the
  `trust-cg-ws2-import` driver does, else the module's), so every triple
  LLVM reads as ELF is admitted (FreeBSD, bare-metal, a bare architecture;
  llc wrote nothing for the listing for each AArch64 and x86-64 one
  measured) and an explicit `-macho` ending is refused as Mach-O. MinGW
  COFF (`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`), for which llc also writes nothing, is
  refused: only the ELF form was compared with this backend's. A module
  imported through `import_text`, without a compile target, whose triple
  names ELF but which is compiled for another object format still loses
  the listing: the backend does not compare the module's triple with the
  target it compiles for. `symbol_linkage_elf`
  gained two host-neutral rows for the two refusals (the first also pins
  the backend's own contract for a hidden `AvailableExternally` import that
  another trust-ir producer states: a hidden undefined symbol when
  referenced, none when not) and extended the listed-declaration row; each
  of the round's 19 mutants fails it. Of the two earlier mutants whose
  witness this round moved, the one that writes an unreferenced hidden
  `available_externally` global as an undefined symbol had been killed only
  through the importer's hidden form, which is now refused, and is killed
  by the trust-ir check; the other stays equivalent (`available_externally`
  added to a set that excludes every global with an initializer). The verifier's 160 order and
  constructor fuzz modules compile to byte-identical objects (1,920 at
  O0-O3 under every model) at the round-1 head and at this round's.

  `dso_local` (LD-31). `dso_local` lets llc assume the symbol is in the
  linked image, and llc 22.1.2 then addresses a default-visibility one that
  is not `extern_weak` PC-relative under `static`, PIE and `pic` alike,
  where the backend addresses every declaration through the GOT and, under
